question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool show a probability of 20% or higher for a cumulative 75+ bps cut (from the current 4.00%-4.25% level) by the January 2026 FOMC meeting, as of October 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 17, 2025, the FOMC cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00%–4.25%. This was the first cut since December 2024. One dissenter, Stephen Miran, voted for a 50 bps cut. The FOMC's median economic projections suggest another 50 bps of cuts could occur in 2025, potentially bringing rates to around 3.50%–3.75%. CME FedWatch data as of mid-September indicated a 93.2% probability of a 25 bps cut at the November meeting and a 92.7% probability of a further 25 bps cut at the December meeting.

For the ultimate question to resolve Yes (a 50+ bps cut at the January 2026 meeting specifically), the Fed would need to be in an aggressive easing mode by that point. If market-implied probabilities shift toward expecting cumulative cuts of 75+ bps between now and January 2026 (i.e., the fed funds rate falling to 3.25%–3.50% or lower by January 28, 2026), this would signal that the market sees a scenario where substantial easing—including possibly a 50 bps cut at the January meeting—is plausible. The CME FedWatch tool derives probabilities from 30-Day Fed Fund futures prices and is widely used to gauge market expectations for FOMC rate decisions.

Currently, with the rate at 4.00%–4.25% and median projections suggesting rates could fall to ~3.50%–3.75% by year-end, a cumulative 75+ bps cut by January 2026 would imply rates at or below 3.25%–3.50%, which is more aggressive than current median projections.

Sources:
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- FOMC September 2025 Statement: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
- Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on October 17, 2025, the CME FedWatch tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) shows an implied probability of 20% or higher that the federal funds target range will be at or below 3.25%–3.50% (i.e., a cumulative 75+ basis points of cuts from the current 4.00%–4.25% level) following the January 2026 FOMC meeting (scheduled for January 27–28, 2026). The probability is calculated by summing the probabilities assigned to all target rate ranges at or below 3.25%–3.50% for the January 2026 meeting date on the CME FedWatch tool. If the CME FedWatch tool is unavailable on October 17, 2025, resolution will be based on the closest available prior date between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17. If the tool is discontinued entirely during this period, the question resolves as ambiguous. The resolution window is from 2025-09-18 to 2025-10-17, with the reading taken on October 17, 2025 (or the closest prior available date).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will cut rates by 50+ bps at the January 2026 meeting specifically. A 50 bps cut at a single meeting is unusual and typically occurs only when economic conditions deteriorate significantly or when the Fed is in an aggressive easing cycle. If by mid-October market-implied probabilities show expectations for cumulative cuts of 75+ bps through January 2026 (more aggressive than current median projections), this would indicate that economic data or geopolitical developments are pushing expectations toward a faster easing pace. Such a shift would significantly increase the probability of a large single-meeting cut (50+ bps) at the January meeting, as the Fed might need to front-load cuts. Conversely, if market expectations remain anchored at 25 bps per meeting with a modest total cutting cycle, a 50+ bps cut at the January meeting becomes very unlikely. This subquestion captures a near-term observable signal—market pricing—that directly informs the ultimate question without merely restating it.

question: Trump declassifies UFO files in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump administration declassifies any previously classified files pertaining to extraterrestrial life and/or unexplained arial phenomena by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements of declassifications that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not count.

The primary resolution source for declassification will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hold a public hearing or publish an official report recommending UFO/UAP file declassification between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Rep. Anna Paulina Luna chairs the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, which was established to push for public access to classified government information, including UAP-related files. Luna has been vocal about her belief that the government holds significant classified information about unidentified aerial phenomena, making bombshell claims on The Joe Rogan Experience podcast in August 2025 about 'interdimensional beings' and classified photographs of objects 'not created by mankind' (https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/trump-insider-makes-bombshell-claim-on-ufo-and-aliens-very-credible-people-have-101723548123456.html). Separately, Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard has acknowledged the possibility of extraterrestrial life and pledged future public updates (https://thepoliticalinsider.com/tulsi-gabbard-acknowledges-possibility-of-aliens-pledges-public-updates/). The Pentagon's AARO has been releasing more unclassified investigation reports in 2025, and Congress passed reforms compelling cooperation from agencies and protecting whistleblowers (https://medium.com/@author/pentagons-2025-ufo-shift-inside-the-year-the-walls-began-to-talk). The UAP Transparency Act, proposed by Rep. Tim Burchett, aims to declassify all UFO-related documents within 270 days (https://medium.com/@author/the-pentagons-ufo-secret-crashed-saucers-nitinol). As of September 2025, the Task Force has not yet held a formal public hearing or released a comprehensive report, though Luna has indicated she plans to continue seeking answers and pushing for public access to previously hidden information.

Sources:
- Hindustan Times, "Trump insider makes bombshell claim on UFO and aliens": https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/
- The Political Insider, "Tulsi Gabbard Acknowledges Possibility of Aliens": https://thepoliticalinsider.com/tulsi-gabbard-acknowledges-possibility-of-aliens-pledges-public-updates/
- ABC News, "UFO sleuths want fewer secrets in Trump-era investigations": https://abcnews.go.com/US/ufo-sleuths-fewer-secrets-trump-era-investigations/story
- Medium, "Pentagon's 2025 UFO Shift": https://medium.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets (chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna or any successor chair) either (a) holds a publicly announced hearing (open to the public or publicly streamed/recorded) that specifically addresses the declassification of UFO/UAP-related government files, OR (b) publishes an official report or formal recommendation calling for the Trump administration to declassify UFO/UAP files. Evidence must come from official congressional records (https://www.congress.gov/), the Task Force's official communications, or C-SPAN recordings (https://www.c-span.org/). A consensus of at least two credible news sources (e.g., AP, Reuters, major US newspapers) reporting on the event will also suffice. Closed/classified-only sessions do not count. If the Task Force is dissolved or renamed before the end date, the question resolves No. If a hearing or report is announced but not actually conducted/published within the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The House Task Force on Declassification of Federal Secrets is one of the primary congressional mechanisms pushing the Trump administration toward UFO/UAP file declassification. A public hearing or formal recommendation from this body would be a strong leading indicator that actual declassification is forthcoming before December 2025. If the Task Force remains inactive or fails to produce public action in September 2025, it suggests less congressional pressure on the administration, making a declassification announcement by year-end less likely. Conversely, a public hearing with specific recommendations would signal political momentum and institutional readiness for declassification, substantially updating the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics for August 2025 be 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. unemployment rate is a key labor market indicator closely watched by economists assessing recession risk. As of the most recent data, the unemployment rate stood at 4.2% for July 2025 (released August 1, 2025). A rising unemployment rate is one of the primary signals the NBER considers when determining whether the economy is in a recession, since recessions involve broad declines in economic activity including employment. The Sahm Rule, a well-known recession indicator, triggers when the three-month moving average of the unemployment rate rises 0.5 percentage points above its low over the prior 12 months. As of mid-2025, the Sahm indicator was approximately 0.3 percentage points, meaning additional increases in unemployment could push it toward the 0.5 threshold. A jump to 4.4% or above in August would represent a meaningful deterioration in the labor market and would bring the Sahm indicator closer to the recession threshold, significantly increasing the probability of a recession being declared.

The BLS Employment Situation report for August 2025 is scheduled for release on Friday, September 5, 2025.

Sources:
- BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
- BLS Economic News Release Schedule: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm
- The Orange County Register, 'Is a 2025 recession a myth or reality?': https://www.ocregister.com/2025/05/14/is-a-2025-recession-a-myth-or-reality-in-this-age-of-uncertainty/
- Sahm Rule Recession Indicator (FRED): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports a seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate of 4.4% or higher for August 2025 in its Employment Situation report released between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. The primary resolution source is the BLS Employment Situation Summary available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm. The relevant release is the one scheduled for September 5, 2025. If the BLS release is delayed beyond 2025-10-01, the question resolves as ambiguous/unresolvable. Only the initial release figure for August 2025 counts; subsequent revisions are not considered. The unemployment rate must be reported as 4.4% or higher (i.e., ≥4.4%, including 4.4% exactly) to resolve Yes. Otherwise, it resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The unemployment rate is one of the most important indicators the NBER examines when determining recessions. A significant rise to 4.4% or above would represent a notable labor market weakening and would bring the Sahm Rule recession indicator very close to its trigger threshold. This would substantially update forecasters' views on whether a 2025 recession will ultimately be declared. Q1 2025 GDP was already negative (-0.2%), so the recession question now hinges partly on whether the labor market deteriorates meaningfully in the second half of 2025. By contrast, Q2 GDP rebounded to 3.3%, making a consecutive-negative-quarters trigger less likely unless a sharp downturn materializes — which would likely show up first in employment data. Knowing the August unemployment rate by early September provides an actionable near-term signal.

question: Will Max Verstappen be the 2025 Drivers Champion?
description:
This market will resolve according to the driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2025 F1 season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

As soon as the results for the final scheduled race of the 2025 F1 season are known this market will resolve.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2025 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), this market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen's points deficit to the Drivers' Championship leader be 50 or fewer after the United States Grand Prix (Round 19, October 19, 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, Max Verstappen sits third in the 2025 Drivers' Championship standings, approximately 69 points behind leader Oscar Piastri with seven rounds remaining. Verstappen has won the last two races (Monza and Baku), suggesting Red Bull has made significant progress with car upgrades. However, both McLaren drivers — Piastri and Lando Norris — remain well ahead in the standings. The maximum points available per race weekend (including sprint) is approximately 34 points (25 for a win + 1 for fastest lap + 8 for sprint win), so Verstappen would need to consistently outscore the leader by a large margin over multiple races to close the gap. The next races in October include the Singapore GP (October 5), the Japanese GP (October 12, a sprint weekend), and the United States GP (October 19, also a sprint weekend). Red Bull adviser Helmut Marko has acknowledged that Singapore — a high-downforce, hot circuit — will be a key benchmark for whether Red Bull's recent resurgence is real (Motorsport.com, September 21, 2025). If Verstappen can keep the deficit within striking distance (50 points or fewer) through three races in October, he remains a plausible title contender for the final stretch of the season.

Sources:
- Motorsport.com: "After Baku brilliance, here's why Singapore GP is key for Max Verstappen's F1 title hopes" (Sep 21, 2025) https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/singapore-gp-key-max-verstappen-f1-title-hopes/10680000/
- Formula 1 official standings: https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2025/drivers
- Sportskeeda: "Max Verstappen outlines his target with Red Bull for the second half of the 2025 F1 season" (Aug 11, 2025) https://www.sportskeeda.com/f1/max-verstappen-outlines-target-red-bull-second-half-2025-f1-season
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, after the conclusion of the 2025 United States Grand Prix (scheduled for October 19, 2025, at Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas), the official FIA/Formula 1 Drivers' Championship standings show Max Verstappen within 50 points (inclusive) of the championship leader. This question resolves No if Verstappen's deficit to the leader exceeds 50 points after the US GP results are finalized, or if Verstappen has been mathematically eliminated from the championship by that date. If the United States Grand Prix is postponed beyond October 31, 2025, or canceled, this question resolves based on the standings after the last completed race before October 31, 2025. The resolution window is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. The primary resolution source is the official Formula 1 Drivers' Championship standings at https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2025/drivers.
subquestions.rationale: Verstappen's points deficit to the championship leader is the single most important observable metric for determining whether he can win the 2025 title. If after three October race weekends (including two sprint weekends offering extra points), Verstappen has closed the gap to 50 points or fewer, he remains a serious contender with approximately 4-5 races remaining. If the gap has grown beyond 50 points, the title becomes extremely unlikely or mathematically impossible. This question measures Verstappen's trajectory and Red Bull's competitiveness in a crucial stretch that includes different circuit types (street circuit in Singapore, high-speed Suzuka, and mixed-character COTA), providing a robust indicator. Forecasters who disagree on whether Verstappen will be champion are likely to have different expectations about whether Red Bull's recent Monza/Baku resurgence will hold across varied circuits.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Iran fail to reach or maintain a diplomatic agreement (nuclear deal or framework) between December 23, 2025 and January 22, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Diplomatic relations between the U.S. and Iran are a key indicator of the likelihood of military conflict. Following the June 2025 12-day war between Israel and Iran—during which the U.S. struck three Iranian nuclear facilities on June 22, 2025, and Iran retaliated by striking a U.S. base in Qatar on June 23—a ceasefire was brokered by President Trump on June 24, 2025. Since then, tensions have remained elevated. Iran's parliament passed a law in July 2025 suspending IAEA cooperation and barring inspectors until the Supreme National Security Council confirms the safety of nuclear facilities (https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3963456.html). Britain, France, and Germany have warned they may activate the UN 'snapback' mechanism to reimpose sanctions due to Iran's non-compliance with the JCPOA (https://www.meforum.org/articles/2025/iran-flexes-muscle-in-persian-gulf-while-sanctions). Iran conducted major military exercises in December 2025, firing ballistic and cruise missiles in the Persian Gulf (https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets). Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi has demanded the suspension of some sanctions as a condition for any deal, a demand repeated in every round of talks. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson warned in December 2025 that radioactive leaks from the U.S. strikes make IAEA inspections impossible (https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3982543.html). The absence of a diplomatic framework substantially increases the risk of renewed military confrontation.

Sources:
- Trend News Agency, Iran condemns military strikes: https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3979836.html
- Trend News Agency, Radioactive leak inspections: https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3982543.html
- MEF, Iran Flexes Muscle: https://www.meforum.org/articles/2025/iran-flexes-muscle-in-persian-gulf-while-sanctions
- Straits Times, Iran holds drills: https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
- Trend News Agency, Iranian MFA on IAEA: https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3963456.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between December 23, 2025 and January 22, 2026 (inclusive), no new nuclear deal, diplomatic framework agreement, or formal written understanding between the United States and Iran is publicly announced by both the U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov/) and Iran's Foreign Ministry (https://en.mfa.gov.ir/). The agreement must be described by both parties as a binding or framework agreement covering Iran's nuclear program. Informal talks, expressions of willingness to negotiate, or unilateral statements do not count. If the existing June 24, 2025 ceasefire collapses (i.e., either side publicly declares the ceasefire void or conducts a qualifying military strike against the other), this also resolves Yes. The question resolves No if such a deal or framework is announced by both parties within the resolution window. Resolution will be based on official government communications and credible reporting from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), and the U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov/).
subquestions.rationale: The presence or absence of a diplomatic channel between the U.S. and Iran is one of the strongest leading indicators of whether the U.S. might strike Iran. The June 2025 ceasefire paused hostilities, but Iran's suspension of IAEA cooperation, ongoing military exercises, European threats of snapback sanctions, and unresolved nuclear issues all suggest the diplomatic situation is fragile. If no diplomatic agreement materializes in the near term—or if the ceasefire collapses—the probability of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran before February 28, 2026, increases significantly. Conversely, a new diplomatic framework would strongly decrease that probability. This subquestion tracks a different observable (diplomatic outcomes) rather than restating the military strike question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Trump meet with Xi Jinping by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping between July 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US and China extend their tariff truce (originally set to expire around August 12, 2025) through at least September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In May 2025, the US and China reached a 90-day tariff truce in Geneva, temporarily setting US duties on Chinese goods at 30% and Chinese levies on US goods at 10%. This truce was due to expire around August 12, 2025. In late July 2025, senior US and Chinese negotiators met in Stockholm to discuss extending the truce. President Trump expressed optimism, saying 'We're very close to a deal with China.' Analysts widely expected the truce to be extended by another 90 days, which would push the new deadline to approximately early November 2025. Multiple analysts noted that a truce extension would 'set the stage for a Trump–Xi handshake later this year,' as continued diplomatic engagement and avoidance of tariff escalation are seen as necessary preconditions for a leader-level meeting. As of late August 2025, the outcome of the Stockholm talks and any truce extension details are the key near-term indicators for whether the diplomatic trajectory supports an in-person Trump-Xi meeting before October 31.

Sources:
- Firstpost, 'Very close to China deal': Trump hopeful as trade negotiators meet in Stockholm (2025-07-28): https://www.firstpost.com/world/very-close-to-china-deal-trump-hopeful-as-trade-negotiators-meet-in-stockholm-13842362.html
- Market Screener, US-China trade truce extension seen, may ease way for Trump-Xi meet (2025-07-28): https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/US-China-trade-truce-extension-seen-may-ease-way-for-Trump-Xi-meet--49364219/
- Fairfield Sun Times, Chinese, US officials meet for 2nd day of trade talks in Stockholm (2025-07-29): https://www.fairfieldsuntimes.com/news/national/chinese-us-officials-meet-for-2nd-day-of-trade-talks-in-stockholm/article_e6b2e504-0df2-5eb3-9632-7b3b3f35a8c3.html
- India Today, Trump to meet Xi? US, China to resume talks in effort to extend trade truce (2025-07-28): https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/trump-to-meet-xi-us-china-to-resume-talks-in-effort-to-extend-trade-truce-2734567-2025-07-28
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, credible reporting (from sources such as Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, or official US/Chinese government statements) confirms that the US-China tariff truce that was originally agreed in Geneva in May 2025 remains in effect through at least September 30, 2025 — meaning neither side has reimposed the higher pre-truce tariff rates (i.e., the US has not raised tariffs on Chinese goods above the truce-level 30%, and China has not raised tariffs on US goods above the truce-level 10%). If the truce has expired or either side has reimposed higher tariff rates before September 30, 2025, this resolves No. Minor adjustments to tariff rates on specific product categories do not count as a truce collapse, but a broad reimposition of pre-truce tariff levels does. Resolution sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), and official US Trade Representative announcements (https://ustr.gov).
subquestions.rationale: The continuation of the US-China tariff truce is a critical precondition for a Trump-Xi meeting. Analysts have explicitly stated that a truce extension 'could set the stage for a Trump-Xi handshake later this year.' If the truce collapses and tariffs escalate sharply, the diplomatic environment would become far too hostile for a leader-level meeting. Conversely, if the truce holds and trade negotiations continue, it creates the diplomatic runway needed for scheduling and executing a Trump-Xi summit before October 31. This subquestion measures the health of the US-China diplomatic relationship in a concrete, observable way that is distinct from (but highly informative about) whether the leaders will actually meet.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

subquestions.question: Will TIME magazine publish a major cover story or feature specifically focused on artificial intelligence (as a broad topic, not just an individual AI leader) between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME's Person of the Year selection, typically announced in December, is heavily influenced by the cultural and news dominance of a person or concept throughout the year. In recent years, AI has been a leading candidate for the honor. TIME has shown increasing editorial attention to AI: it launched the TIME100 AI list in 2023 and continued it in 2024 and 2025, most recently publishing its TIME100 AI 2025 list in late August 2025 (https://time.com/collection/time100-ai-2025/). In 2023, TIME did not select AI as Person of the Year despite widespread speculation, instead choosing Taylor Swift. However, AI's cultural prominence has only grown since then, with President Trump hosting an AI summit in July 2025 and calling AI 'pure genius' (https://www.wion.com/world/us-news/i-dont-like-anything-artificial-trump-wants-to-rename-ai-calls-it-pure-genius-mocks-authors-over-copyright-complaints-843939). The question of whether TIME dedicates a major cover story to AI as a phenomenon (rather than just profiling individual AI leaders) in the fall would be a strong editorial signal that AI-as-concept is being elevated to Person of the Year contention. TIME's cover stories are listed at https://time.com/vault/. Past Person of the Year selections that were concepts rather than individuals include 'The Computer' (1982), 'You' (2006), and 'Ebola Fighters' (2014).

Sources:
- TIME100 AI 2025: https://time.com/collection/time100-ai-2025/
- WION on Trump AI summit remarks: https://www.wion.com/world/us-news/i-dont-like-anything-artificial-trump-wants-to-rename-ai-calls-it-pure-genius-mocks-authors-over-copyright-complaints-843939
- TIME Vault (covers archive): https://time.com/vault/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), TIME magazine publishes at least one cover story (print or digital cover featured on time.com) whose primary subject is artificial intelligence as a broad topic or phenomenon — not merely a profile of an individual person who works in AI. The cover must use terms such as 'Artificial Intelligence,' 'AI,' or closely synonymous phrasing (e.g., 'The Age of AI,' 'The AI Revolution') in the cover headline or subheadline. A cover story that profiles a specific individual (e.g., 'Sam Altman') with AI mentioned only in passing does not count. Resolution will be determined by checking TIME's cover archive at https://time.com/vault/ and the TIME homepage at https://time.com/ for covers dated or published within this window. If TIME's website is unavailable, archived versions on the Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/) may be used as a fallback. If no qualifying cover story is published by October 1, 2025, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: TIME's editorial choices in the months leading up to the Person of the Year announcement are strong indicators of what the magazine's editors consider the dominant story of the year. If TIME runs a major AI-themed cover story in September, it signals that the editorial team views AI as a defining narrative of 2025 — making it more likely AI could be selected as Person of the Year. Conversely, if TIME's September covers focus on other subjects (political figures, cultural events, geopolitical crises), it suggests AI may not be the magazine's top editorial priority for 2025. This is a genuinely different observable event from the ultimate question: it asks about editorial attention to AI in a specific month, not about the December selection itself. Two forecasters who disagree on whether AI will be Person of the Year would likely update their forecasts in the same direction upon learning whether TIME devoted a cover to AI-as-concept in this period.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. deploy additional major naval combatants (beyond those already announced as of September 1, 2025) to the Caribbean region near Venezuela between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, the United States has built up a significant naval presence in the Caribbean near Venezuela, including three Arleigh Burke-class destroyers, the guided-missile cruiser USS Lake Erie, an amphibious assault ship, two landing-dock ships, a littoral combat ship, and the nuclear-powered fast-attack submarine USS Newport News. In total, more than 4,500 U.S. personnel are deployed in the Southern Caribbean. The stated mission is counter-narcotics interdiction, but it coincides with escalating political pressure on the Maduro regime, including a $50 million bounty on Maduro's capture. Venezuela has responded by deploying warships, drones, and mobilizing 4.5 million members of its Bolivarian Militia. Analysts such as Phil Gunson of the International Crisis Group have characterized the buildup as an attempt to pressure Maduro into negotiation rather than a precursor to invasion. However, the continued expansion of the naval task force would signal an escalation trajectory that could increase the risk of an incident or confrontation. The question tracks whether the U.S. continues to add warships — a leading indicator that tensions are intensifying rather than plateauing.

Sources:
- Newsweek, 'USS Lake Erie crosses Panama Canal as Trump's Caribbean buildup continues' (Aug 30, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2039089
- AFP via France24, 'Venezuela deploys warships, drones as US destroyers draw near' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250826-venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near
- The Telegraph, 'We should take Trump's sabre-rattling against Venezuela seriously' (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/08/31/trump-sabre-rattling-venezuela-navy-task-force-caribbean/
- The Inquisitr, 'Trump Hit With Venezuela's Significant Threat Over $50M Maduro Reward' (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.inquisitr.com/trump-venezuela-military-threat-maduro-bounty/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting (from sources such as Reuters, AP, AFP, Newsweek, the U.S. Department of Defense, or USNI News) confirms that at least one additional major U.S. naval combatant — defined as a destroyer, cruiser, frigate, aircraft carrier, amphibious assault ship (LHD/LHA), or submarine — not previously reported as deployed or en route to the Caribbean region near Venezuela as of August 31, 2025, has been ordered to or has arrived in the Caribbean theater (defined as the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico south of 25°N, or western Atlantic east of Venezuela within 500 nautical miles of Venezuelan territory). Ships merely transiting the Panama Canal without being assigned to the Venezuela-related mission do not count. Routine port calls unrelated to the Venezuela deployment do not count. If reporting is ambiguous about whether a vessel is 'additional' versus a replacement for a departing ship, a net increase in major combatant count in the theater qualifies. If no credible reporting confirms such a deployment by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- USNI News Fleet Tracker: https://news.usni.org/category/fleet-tracker
- U.S. Southern Command press releases: https://www.southcom.mil/Media/Press-Releases/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- AP News: https://apnews.com
subquestions.rationale: The scale and trajectory of the U.S. naval buildup near Venezuela is one of the strongest leading indicators of whether a military engagement might occur. A continued expansion of the task force beyond the already substantial deployment would signal that the Trump administration is escalating pressure and accepting higher risk of a confrontation, increasing the probability of an incident. Conversely, if the naval presence stabilizes or shrinks, it suggests the buildup was primarily coercive diplomacy rather than a precursor to kinetic action. Forecasters who disagree about whether a US-Venezuela military engagement will happen by October 31 are likely to update their views based on whether the U.S. continues adding firepower to the theater during September.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla's Austin Robotaxi service begin accepting ride requests from the general public (non-invite-only) by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla launched an invite-only Robotaxi pilot in Austin, Texas on June 22, 2025, operating a small fleet of 10–20 vehicles with a human safety monitor seated in the passenger seat. As of late August 2025, the service remains limited to select testers. Elon Musk has repeatedly stated that the Austin Robotaxi service will open to the general public in September 2025. Barclays analysts noted that Tesla has secured all required permits and regulatory approvals to expand operations across Texas and will operate as a licensed transportation network company until August 2026. However, even with a public launch, the Austin service currently uses safety monitors in the passenger seat — not in the driver's seat — meaning Tesla could argue the monitor is not 'positioned to take control' of the vehicle. Whether this configuration meets the ultimate question's criteria for 'fully driverless' is a separate matter, but a public launch in Austin would be the most likely first step toward a service that could qualify.

Sources:
- NewsBytes, 'Musk confirms Tesla robotaxi rollout for the public in September' (2025-08-18): https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/tesla-robotaxis-set-for-public-rollout-in-september/story
- GuruFocus, 'Barclays Expects Long Approval Process for Tesla's Robotaxi' (2025-08-22): https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2748890/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi
- The Munich Eye, 'Tesla Launches Robotaxi Service with Limitations' (2025-08-16): https://themunicheye.com/Tesla-Launches-Robotaxi-Service-with-Limitations-11612
- Tesla North, 'Tesla Hints at Chicago Robotaxi Launch with New Job Listings' (2025-08-21): https://teslanorth.com/2025/08/21/tesla-hints-at-chicago-robotaxi-launch-with-new-job-listings/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), Tesla's Austin, Texas Robotaxi service becomes available to the general public — meaning any member of the public can request a ride through the Tesla app or website without needing a prior invitation, employee status, or closed-beta enrollment. Evidence must come from an official Tesla announcement (e.g., Tesla blog, press release, or verified Tesla social media account), credible major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, TechCrunch), or the Tesla app itself showing open availability. If the service opens to a broader but still restricted group (e.g., a waitlist that only some people are accepted from, or a specific geographic sub-area of Austin), this still counts as Yes provided any member of the public within the service area can sign up and request a ride without a specific invitation. If the public launch is announced but explicitly scheduled for a date after September 8, 2025, this resolves No. If no credible reporting confirms a public launch by end of day September 8, 2025 (UTC), this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The Austin public launch is the most likely near-term precursor to Tesla achieving a fully driverless Robotaxi service. Musk has specifically targeted September for this milestone. However, even opening to the public in Austin would likely still involve safety monitors in the passenger seat, which may or may not satisfy the ultimate question's 'fully driverless' criteria. This subquestion tracks whether Tesla hits even its most basic public-launch timeline — if Tesla cannot open Austin to the public in early September, it becomes extremely unlikely that it will achieve a fully driverless (no safety monitor positioned to take control) service by October 31. Conversely, if the Austin public launch happens quickly, it signals Tesla is on an aggressive trajectory that could potentially lead to removing safety monitors or launching a qualifying driverless service in another jurisdiction before the October deadline.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will a credible report emerge between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 that OpenAI is actively developing or testing a standalone web browser product (not merely a browser extension or plugin)?
subquestions.background_information:
Multiple reports in mid-to-late 2025 have referenced OpenAI's rumored standalone browser project. A Windows Central article from August 30, 2025 noted OpenAI's 'rumored project' alongside other AI browsers like Perplexity's Comet and the Browser Company's Dia (https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you). The competitive landscape for AI-powered browsers is heating up: Perplexity launched Comet in July 2025 at $200/month (https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you), and Anthropic released a Chrome browser extension in closed beta in August 2025 (https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/). OpenAI has been expanding its product surface area rapidly—launching GPT-5, upgrading Codex, and releasing speech-to-speech models—suggesting the company is actively broadening beyond ChatGPT into adjacent product categories. However, as of September 1, 2025, no official confirmation from OpenAI about a standalone browser has been made public. The existence of concrete development evidence (e.g., job postings, leaked builds, partnership announcements with browser engine providers, or credible journalist reports citing insider sources) would be a strong leading indicator that an October 2025 launch is plausible.

Sources:
- Windows Central, 'Let me scam that for you' (2025-08-30): https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you
- ZDNet, 'Anthropic's Claude Chrome browser extension rolls out' (2025-08-28): https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/
- The Information (subscription), OpenAI browser reports: https://www.theinformation.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), at least one credible report is published (by outlets such as The Information, Bloomberg, The Verge, TechCrunch, Reuters, or equivalent) OR an official OpenAI communication (blog post, job listing, press release, or public statement by an OpenAI executive) confirms that OpenAI is actively developing or internally testing a standalone web browser application intended for general web browsing. Reports must specifically describe a standalone browser product—not a browser extension, plugin, ChatGPT browsing feature, or integration within a third-party browser. If the only references are vague 'rumors' without any sourcing to people familiar with the matter or concrete evidence (such as code repositories, job postings, or product screenshots), the question resolves No. Resolution sources include:
- OpenAI official blog: https://openai.com/blog
- The Verge: https://www.theverge.com/
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
- Bloomberg Technology: https://www.bloomberg.com/technology
- The Information: https://www.theinformation.com/
subquestions.rationale: A standalone browser is a major product undertaking. If no credible reports of active development or testing emerge by October 1, it becomes very unlikely that OpenAI could publicly launch such a product by October 31. Conversely, if concrete development evidence surfaces—such as insider reports, leaked builds, or official hiring for browser teams—this would significantly raise the probability of an October launch. This subquestion tracks observable precursor signals rather than simply asking the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Supreme National Security Council officially order the closure or blockade of the Strait of Hormuz between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06?
subquestions.background_information:
In June 2025, Iran's parliament voted to approve a measure to close the Strait of Hormuz following US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites. However, the final decision on whether to actually implement a closure rests with Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), which is the ultimate decision-making body on national security matters in Iran. As of the articles available through late June 2025, the SNSC had not yet made a final decision. Iranian lawmaker Esmail Kosari stated, 'The closure of the strait is on the agenda and will be done whenever necessary,' but the Supreme National Security Council had not formally ordered it. Meanwhile, tanker traffic through the strait had begun to reduce due to rising tensions, with some operators halting transits. Commodore Alireza Tangsiri, head of Iran's IRGC naval forces, stated that Iran has the option of disrupting traffic but chooses not to. The strait handles approximately 20 million barrels of oil per day, about 20% of global oil consumption, making any closure decision enormously consequential for both global markets and Iran's own economy (as it would also prevent Iran from exporting its petroleum and antagonize China, its biggest oil buyer).

Sources:
- India Today: Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2741123-2025-06-22
- Times of India: US strikes on Iran: Tehran's top security council to decide on Strait of Hormuz closure: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122051671.cms
- The Straits Times: What if Iran tries to close the Strait of Hormuz?: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/what-if-iran-tries-to-close-the-strait-of-hormuz
- Ship & Bunker: Crude Futures Jump After Iranian Threats: https://shipandbunker.com/news/world/471380-crude-futures-jump-after-iranian-threats-to-strait-of-hormuz-ship-traffic
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), Iran's Supreme National Security Council (or an equivalent top-level Iranian governmental authority such as the Supreme Leader) officially orders or publicly announces a decision to close, blockade, or severely restrict international maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Evidence must come from at least two credible international news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, or official Iranian state media such as IRNA or Press TV). A parliamentary vote alone does not count; the decision must come from the executive/security authority empowered to implement such an order. If no such announcement or order is confirmed by credible reporting by 2025-12-06 23:59 UTC, the question resolves No. If reports are ambiguous or contradictory, a consensus of at least three major international news outlets will be required for Yes resolution.

Sources for resolution:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- IRNA (Islamic Republic News Agency): https://en.irna.ir/
- Press TV: https://www.presstv.ir/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Iran will close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027 (with the market end date in March 2026). A formal order from Iran's Supreme National Security Council is the critical prerequisite step before any actual closure could occur. Iran's parliament already voted to approve closure in June 2025, but the SNSC has the final say. Monitoring whether the SNSC makes this decision in the near term is the most direct leading indicator of whether an actual closure will follow. If the SNSC orders closure, the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes increases dramatically. If no such order materializes despite ongoing tensions, it suggests Iran is maintaining its historical pattern of threatening but not following through, which would significantly decrease the probability of a closure before March 2026.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses shows 'Wicked: For Good' (2025) as the film with the highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will any single movie's 2025 domestic cumulative gross exceed $500 million on Box Office Mojo by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
For Wicked: For Good to be the top-grossing domestic film of 2025, it would need to outperform all other 2025 releases. As of late August 2025, the top domestic grossers of the year include several major releases from the first eight months. Key competitors include sequels and franchise films released in the summer season. If any film has already crossed $500 million domestically before Wicked: For Good even opens on November 21, 2025, that would represent a very high bar for the musical sequel to clear in roughly five and a half weeks of release (November 21 – December 31). For context, the original Wicked earned approximately $468 million domestically during its full theatrical run spanning late 2024 into early 2025. Only a handful of films in history have earned over $500 million domestically in a single calendar year. If a competitor has already reached this level by the end of September, it would significantly reduce the probability that Wicked: For Good finishes as the #1 domestic grosser for the 2025 calendar year. Current 2025 domestic box office standings can be tracked at Box Office Mojo.

Sources:
- Box Office Mojo 2025 yearly domestic grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- Wicked worldwide gross data: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/
- Wicked: For Good release info: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt15360024/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of September 30, 2025, any single movie's 2025 calendar-year domestic gross listed on Box Office Mojo's 2025 yearly domestic chart (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses) equals or exceeds $500,000,000. Only domestic (U.S.) gross accumulated between January 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025, counts. The data must be checked on or after October 1, 2025, when September 30 figures are available. If Box Office Mojo is unavailable, The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/market/2025/top-grossing-movies) may be used as a fallback source. This question covers the period from 2025-09-01 (the question's start date) to 2025-09-30 (the end date), but the gross figures considered are cumulative 2025 calendar-year totals as of September 30, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a meaningful early indicator because it measures how dominant the competition already is before Wicked: For Good even releases on November 21. If a film has already crossed $500 million domestically by the end of September, Wicked: For Good would face an extremely difficult task to overtake it in just ~5.5 weeks of 2025 calendar-year release. Conversely, if no film has reached that threshold, the race remains more open and Wicked: For Good's chances improve. This is a genuine crux for disagreement: forecasters who believe a summer blockbuster will dominate would expect 'Yes,' while those who think the field is weak enough for a late-year musical sequel to win would expect 'No.'

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially announce the establishment of diplomatic relations between Janaury 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Israel publicly commit to a pathway toward Palestinian statehood (e.g., endorsing a two-state framework or presenting a plan for an independent Palestinian state) between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has repeatedly and explicitly stated that normalization with Israel is contingent on the establishment of a Palestinian state and the end of the war in Gaza. On July 28, 2025, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan stated: 'For the kingdom, recognition is very much tied to the establishment of the Palestinian state' and that 'there's no reason, even, or no credibility, to have a conversation about normalization with constant death and suffering and destruction in Gaza' (Anadolu Agency, July 28, 2025). On August 17, 2025, former Saudi intelligence chief Prince Turki al-Faisal called Netanyahu a 'genocidal maniac' and stated Saudi Arabia would not normalize under his leadership (The Siasat Daily, August 17, 2025). Meanwhile, Israel's current coalition government under PM Netanyahu has consistently opposed the creation of a Palestinian state. Experts cited by The Wall Street Journal and TASS (July 7, 2025) assessed that Israel's unwillingness to meet Saudi conditions makes normalization unlikely. A June 2025 UN conference co-chaired by Saudi Arabia and France produced a roadmap focused on Palestinian statehood, international recognition, and normalization with Israel (Asharq Al-Awsat, May 24, 2025). Whether Israel shifts its position on Palestinian statehood is the single most critical precondition for Saudi normalization.

Sources:
- Anadolu Agency, July 28, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3350123
- The Siasat Daily, August 17, 2025: https://www.siasat.com/saudi-arabia-will-not-normalise-relations-with-a-genocidal-maniac-says-prince-turki-al-faisal-3166892/
- TASS, July 7, 2025: https://tass.com/world/1945789
- Asharq Al-Awsat, May 24, 2025: https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5268351
- The Jerusalem Post, April 16, 2025: https://www.jpost.com/opinion/article-852133
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the Israeli government—through the Prime Minister, Foreign Minister, or an official government statement—publicly endorses, commits to, or presents a concrete plan or framework for the establishment of an independent Palestinian state as part of a two-state solution. A vague reference to 'future negotiations' or 'discussing options' does not qualify; there must be an explicit acknowledgment that the goal is Palestinian statehood. Resolution will be based on official Israeli government communications (e.g., statements from the Prime Minister's Office at https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office), as well as credible international news sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com), and Haaretz (https://www.haaretz.com). If no such commitment is made by September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia has made Palestinian statehood the non-negotiable precondition for normalization with Israel. Israel's current government under Netanyahu has firmly opposed this condition. If Israel were to shift its stance and publicly commit to a pathway toward Palestinian statehood in September 2025, it would dramatically increase the likelihood of normalization by year-end. Conversely, continued Israeli opposition to Palestinian statehood would strongly signal that normalization in 2025 is essentially impossible. This is the core crux on which forecasters disagreeing about normalization are most likely to disagree: whether Israel will budge on the Palestinian state issue in time.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire before 2026?
description:
On March 17, Israel announced extensive strikes on terror targets belonging to the Hamas terrorist organization in the Gaza Strip ending a previous ceasefire agreement which had been agreed on January 15 (See: https://x.com/IDF/status/1901802698237935705).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Israel and Hamas between March 19, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterwards.

An announced agreement to reinstate the previous agreed upon January 15th ceasefire deal will qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Israel and Hamas, however a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Israel formally respond to or engage in active negotiations on the Hamas-accepted 60-day ceasefire proposal (or any new ceasefire proposal) between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 18, 2025, Hamas approved a 60-day ceasefire proposal mediated by Egypt and Qatar, based on a framework put forth by US envoy Steve Witkoff. The proposal includes Hamas releasing ten Israeli hostages and the remains of 18 others in exchange for Palestinian prisoners, with Israeli forces redeploying closer to the Gaza border to facilitate humanitarian aid. As of August 31, 2025, Israel has not formally responded to Hamas's acceptance. Netanyahu's office insists any agreement must involve the simultaneous release of all hostages, and senior Israeli officials have indicated that Netanyahu does not intend to prioritize ceasefire negotiations. Instead, Israel's security cabinet is focused on plans for a Gaza City offensive. CNN reported on August 31 that 'the fact that the deal isn't formally on the agenda indicates how low the proposal is on Netanyahu's priority list.' However, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and parts of the Israeli security establishment have urged the cabinet to discuss negotiations before escalating military operations. The US and Israel shifted in late July 2025 toward seeking a comprehensive deal that ends the war entirely rather than partial ceasefires. Hundreds of thousands of Israelis have protested demanding an end to the war and the safe return of hostages.

Sources:
- "Hamas Approves 60-Day Ceasefire Proposal, Awaiting Israel's Response" (Egyptian Streets, August 19, 2025): https://egyptianstreets.com
- "Ceasefire deal not on agenda with Israel's security cabinet set to discuss looming Gaza City offensive" (ABC17NEWS/CNN, August 31, 2025): https://abc17news.com/news/national-world/cnn-world/2025/08/31/ceasefire-deal-not-on-agenda-with-israels-security-cabinet-set-to-discuss-looming-gaza-city-offensive/
- "'No more partial deals': Official says Israel, US now back comprehensive plan to end war" (Times of Israel, July 31, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com/no-more-partial-deals-official-says-israel-us-now-back-comprehensive-plan-to-end-war/
- "Top Israeli officials meeting to discuss ceasefire after Hamas's 'positive' response" (Washington Examiner, July 5, 2025): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/policy/defense/3100000/top-israeli-officials-meeting-ceasefire-hamas-positive-response/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), Israel's government (Prime Minister's Office, security cabinet, or authorized negotiating team) formally responds to the existing Hamas-accepted 60-day ceasefire proposal OR enters into active, acknowledged negotiations on any ceasefire proposal with Hamas through mediators (Egypt, Qatar, US, or others). 'Formally responds' means an official Israeli government statement accepting, rejecting with a counter-proposal, or presenting modified terms in response to the Hamas-accepted proposal. 'Active negotiations' means at least one round of talks (direct or through mediators) in which Israeli representatives participate with the stated purpose of reaching a ceasefire agreement, as reported by at least two credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, Times of Israel, Al Jazeera). Mere informal comments by unnamed officials, background briefings without concrete engagement, or unilateral Israeli statements about preconditions without direct engagement with mediators do not count. If no credible media reports confirm such formal engagement by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Israel engages with the existing ceasefire proposal or enters negotiations in September is a strong leading indicator of whether a ceasefire deal can be reached before the ultimate question's October 9, 2025 deadline. As of late August, Israel has not responded to Hamas's August 18 acceptance, and negotiations are not on the cabinet's agenda. A shift toward active engagement would dramatically increase the probability of a deal, while continued refusal to negotiate would make a ceasefire before the deadline very unlikely. This is a genuine crux: forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely disagree on whether Netanyahu will pivot toward negotiations under domestic, military, and international pressure, or continue prioritizing the Gaza City offensive.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett file to run in the 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary by December 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Jasmine Crockett of Dallas has publicly stated she is considering entering the race, with her decision reportedly hinging on polling results. As of early November 2025, Crockett's supporters have been conducting text polls to gauge her viability. The Texas candidate filing period for the 2026 primary runs from November 8 to December 8, 2025, meaning any candidate must file by that deadline to appear on the ballot.

Crockett is a high-profile Democratic congresswoman representing Dallas, and her entry could significantly reshape the primary. She would draw from a similar base of Black and urban voters as Allred, potentially splitting the Dallas-area vote and benefiting Talarico. Conversely, if she does not enter, the race remains a two-person contest between Allred and Talarico, where Allred's higher name recognition and 2024 Senate campaign experience may give him an advantage.

A CBS News report from November 2, 2025, noted that Crockett was actively considering the race and that her decision would be based on polling data. Talarico welcomed potential competition, while Allred expressed respect for Crockett.

Sources:
- CBS News, "Democrats Colin Allred, James Talarico tout endorsements as Jasmine Crockett eyes Texas Senate race" (Nov 2, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/democrats-colin-allred-james-talarico-tout-endorsements-as-jasmine-crockett-eyes-texas-senate-race/
- The Dallas Morning News, "James Talarico targets rival Colin Allred's home turf in Senate primary fight" (Oct 28, 2025): https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett files as a candidate in the 2026 Texas Democratic Senate primary between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-08 (the filing deadline). It resolves No if, by December 8, 2025, Crockett has not filed to run in the Democratic Senate primary. Resolution will be based on the Texas Secretary of State's candidate filing records (https://www.sos.state.tx.us/elections/index.shtml) or credible news reporting from outlets such as the Texas Tribune (https://www.texastribune.org/), Dallas Morning News, or CBS News confirming or denying her filing. If the filing deadline is extended beyond December 8, 2025, this question resolves based on whether Crockett has filed by the original December 8 deadline. The resolution window is 2025-11-13 to 2025-12-13, with the key event (filing) needing to occur by December 8, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: Jasmine Crockett's entry into the Democratic primary would be one of the most consequential developments affecting whether Talarico wins the nomination. As a sitting congresswoman from Dallas—Allred's home base—Crockett would likely split the moderate and Black voter base that Allred relies on, potentially creating a path for Talarico to win a plurality in a three-way race. Conversely, if she stays out, Talarico faces a more straightforward one-on-one contest against Allred, who has higher statewide name recognition and fundraising infrastructure from his 2024 campaign. The filing deadline falls within our resolution window, making this a concrete, observable indicator that would meaningfully update forecasts on the ultimate question.

question: Will Gemini 3.0 be released by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) Google's Gemini 3.0 model is made available to the general public. 

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Gemini 3.0 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Google as being accessible to the general public.

Gemini 3.0 refers to a product explicitly named Gemini 3.0 (e.g. Gemini 3.0 pro would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Gemini 2.0, similar to the progression from Gemini 1.0 to Gemini 2.0. Products labeled as Gemini 2.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Google officially announce or preview a model explicitly named 'Gemini 3.0' (or widely recognized as the direct successor to Gemini 2.x) at a public event or blog post between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Google's Gemini model family has progressed from Gemini 1.0 (launched December 2023) through Gemini 1.5 and then to Gemini 2.0 (launched in late 2024/early 2025). As of September 2025, the latest publicly available models are in the Gemini 2.5 series, including Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash (with its recent image generation variant). There has been no public mention or leak from Google regarding a 'Gemini 3.0' model as of September 1, 2025.

Google typically announces major model releases at its annual developer conference (Google I/O, usually in May) or at dedicated Made by Google hardware events (often in August-October). The August 2025 Made by Google event focused on Pixel 10 hardware and Gemini for Home integration, with no mention of Gemini 3.0. Google's recent focus has been on iterating within the 2.x line (2.0, 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash).

For Gemini 3.0 to be publicly released by October 31, 2025, it would almost certainly need to be announced or previewed before October 1. Major AI model releases from Google are typically preceded by blog posts, research papers, or event announcements weeks before general availability.

Sources:
- Digital Trends, 'Google Gemini: everything you need to know' (2025-08-22): https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-everything-you-need-to-know/
- Telangana Today, 'Google unveils Gemini 2.5 Flash Image' (2025-08-28): https://telanganatoday.com/google-unveils-gemini-2-5-flash-image-with-advanced-ai-powered-editing-and-generation
- Google AI Blog: https://blog.google/technology/ai/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), Google publicly announces, previews, or reveals a model explicitly named 'Gemini 3.0' (including variants such as 'Gemini 3.0 Pro', 'Gemini 3.0 Flash', etc.) or a model that is officially described by Google as the successor to the Gemini 2.x family (not merely an incremental update like 2.5 or 2.7). The announcement must appear on an official Google channel such as the Google AI Blog (https://blog.google/technology/ai/), the Google DeepMind blog (https://deepmind.google/), a keynote presentation at a Google event, or an official Google social media account. Alternatively, if a credible consensus of major tech outlets (e.g., The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica) reports such an announcement based on official Google communications, that also suffices. A leak or rumor without official confirmation does not count. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Gemini 3.0 to be publicly released by October 31, 2025, Google would almost certainly need to announce or preview the model before October 1. Google's pattern with major model releases involves public announcements (blog posts, event keynotes, developer previews) weeks before general availability. The absence of any mention of Gemini 3.0 in recent events (including the August 2025 Made by Google event) and the continued focus on the 2.5 line suggest a 3.0 release by October 31 is unlikely — but tracking whether an announcement materializes in September is the strongest leading indicator. If no announcement appears by October 1, forecasters should significantly lower their probability for the ultimate question.

question: Will the U.S. invade Venezuela by December 31, 2025?
description:
