subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Congress vote on or pass a War Powers Resolution to restrict U.S. military operations against Venezuela-linked targets by November 6, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 3, 2025, the Trump administration sent a memo to Congress declaring a 'non-international armed conflict' with Latin American 'terrorist organisations' linked to Venezuelan drug cartels, granting wartime powers to strike, kill, and detain cartel fighters without trial. Democrats in Congress, including Senator Jack Reed, criticized the move as lacking legal justification and began drafting a War Powers Resolution to block further unilateral military action. Senator Adam Schiff also warned that 'lawless killings may lead to war.' The War Powers Resolution process is a key congressional check on presidential military authority. If Congress moves to block or restrict operations, it would signal strong domestic political resistance to escalation, making a full invasion far less likely. Conversely, if no such resolution advances, it may indicate tacit acceptance of the administration's military posture, leaving the door open for further escalation. As of early October 2025, the Pentagon has deployed the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit (2,200 Marines), ten F-35 stealth jets, Navy warships, a nuclear submarine, and special operations forces to the Caribbean near Venezuela. Three lethal strikes on suspected narcotrafficking boats in September 2025 killed at least 17 people.

Sources:
- The US Sun, 'US prepares to seize ports in Venezuela as Trump declares war on cartels' (Oct 3, 2025): https://www.the-sun.com/news/13671234/us-prepares-seize-ports-venezuela-trump-declares-war-cartels/
- TASS, 'Trump declares war on drug cartels — media' (Oct 3, 2025): https://tass.com/world/1879451
- Vanguard, 'Venezuela wants peace, but will fight US if invaded' (Sep 19, 2025): https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/09/venezuela-wants-peace-but-will-fight-us-if-invaded-ambassador-padilla/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 (inclusive), either chamber of the U.S. Congress (House or Senate) holds a floor vote on a War Powers Resolution or similar joint resolution specifically aimed at restricting, limiting, or terminating U.S. military operations related to Venezuela or Venezuela-linked cartel targets. The resolution does not need to pass; a floor vote in either chamber is sufficient. Resolution will be determined by official congressional records available at https://www.congress.gov/ or credible news reporting from sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), or The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com). If no such vote occurs by November 6, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Congressional action on a War Powers Resolution is a critical leading indicator of whether the U.S. will escalate to a full military invasion of Venezuela. If Congress actively moves to restrain the President's military authority, it significantly reduces the probability of an invasion by December 31, 2025, as it would create legal and political barriers. If Congress does not act, it signals acquiescence to the administration's escalating military posture, which could enable further steps toward invasion. This subquestion captures a concrete, observable institutional action that is distinct from the invasion itself but highly informative about its likelihood.

question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”  if, Ukraine signs any written instrument (e.g., treaty, ceasefire/armistice, framework/“roadmap,” exchange of letters, or mediated agreement text) that: (i) includes both Ukraine and the Russian Federation as parties, and (ii) either ends hostilities/establishes a ceasefire or commits both sides to a defined process toward ending the war (i.e., stated objective of peace/normalization plus principles, steps, and/or a timetable) by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold direct, officially acknowledged bilateral or multilateral negotiations (with both delegations physically present) between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, Ukraine and Russia have not held direct face-to-face peace negotiations since the early rounds of talks in Istanbul in spring 2022. Although diplomatic activity has increased—with the U.S. hosting a Trump-Putin summit in Alaska in August 2025 and Trump publicly proposing a meeting between Putin and Zelensky—no direct Ukraine-Russia negotiating session has been confirmed. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov stated on August 21, 2025 that Putin is 'ready to meet' Zelensky but only after issues are 'well worked out' at expert and ministerial levels, and he raised questions about Zelensky's legitimacy since his term expired in May 2024 (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/PUTIN-PREPARED-TO-MEET-ZEL-148234567/). Ukraine has insisted on a ceasefire as a first step and has rejected territorial concessions as preconditions (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/18/). The G7 foreign ministers on September 24, 2025 reaffirmed support for Ukraine and pledged to work with the U.S. on 'robust and credible security guarantees' (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/). European allies have outlined five requirements for a peace deal, including a ceasefire as the starting point (various sources from August 2025). The significant gap between the two sides' preconditions—Russia demanding recognition of territorial changes and Ukrainian neutrality, Ukraine demanding a full ceasefire first—means that the initiation of direct talks would be a major leading indicator that a signed peace deal before year-end 2025 is plausible.

Sources:
- Market Screener, 'Putin prepared to meet Zelenskiy but legitimacy an issue, Lavrov says' (Aug 21, 2025): https://www.marketscreener.com
- Ukrainska Pravda, 'Ukraine Rejects Territorial Concessions in Deal with Russia' (Aug 18, 2025): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/
- Anadolu Agency, 'G7 vows continued support for Ukraine' (Sep 24, 2025): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/
- WION, 'Russia says Putin ready to meet Zelensky' (Aug 21, 2025): https://www.wionews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), credible international news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, or official government statements from Ukraine or Russia) report that official representatives of both Ukraine and the Russian Federation participated in the same direct negotiation session—whether bilateral or multilateral (e.g., mediated by a third party such as the U.S., Turkey, or the UN). The session must involve both Ukrainian and Russian delegations physically or virtually co-present at the same meeting (not merely parallel or shuttle diplomacy conducted through intermediaries). The meeting must be officially acknowledged by at least one of the two governments (Ukraine or Russia) as a negotiation or peace talk. Informal backchannel contacts, prisoner exchange discussions, or meetings solely between one party and a mediator do not count. If no such meeting is reported by credible sources by November 2, 2025 (allowing two days for reporting lag), this question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Official Ukrainian presidential website: https://www.president.gov.ua/en
- Official Russian government statements via TASS: https://tass.com/politics
subquestions.rationale: A signed peace deal by December 31, 2025 is virtually impossible without direct negotiations between Ukraine and Russia taking place first. As of October 2025, no such talks have occurred since early 2022, and both sides have significant preconditions. If direct negotiations begin in October, it would dramatically increase the probability of a signed agreement by year-end. Conversely, if October passes without any direct talks, the window for negotiating, drafting, and signing a peace deal by December 31 becomes extremely narrow. This subquestion thus serves as a strong leading indicator: forecasters who believe a 2025 peace deal is likely should assign higher probability to October talks, while skeptics would assign low probability to both.

question: Will Eric Adams drop out?

subquestions.question: Will Andrew Cuomo officially withdraw from the 2025 New York City mayoral race by September 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 NYC mayoral race features a crowded field of non-Democratic candidates competing against Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani. The key non-Democratic candidates include incumbent Mayor Eric Adams (running as an independent), former Governor Andrew Cuomo (also running as an independent), Republican Curtis Sliwa, and attorney Jim Walden. Both Cuomo and Walden pledged in late July 2025 to drop out if they were not leading in polls by early September, in order to avoid splitting the anti-Mamdani vote (https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall). As of early August, Adams and Cuomo were calling on each other to drop out, with Cuomo's camp calling Adams 'unelectable' and Adams insisting Cuomo should rally behind him as the sitting mayor (https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/2025/07/18/adams-cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out). Recent polling has generally shown Mamdani with a significant lead, with Adams and Cuomo splitting the moderate/independent vote. If Cuomo drops out and consolidates support behind Adams (or vice versa), it dramatically changes Adams' calculus about whether to remain in the race. Conversely, if Cuomo stays in, the continued vote-splitting may increase pressure on Adams to drop out — or may embolden Adams to stay in, hoping Cuomo eventually exits.

Sources:
- Donald J. Trump site: https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/andrew-cuomo-jim-walden-pledge-to-drop-independent-bids-in-nyc-mayoral-race-if-not-leading-come-fall
- NY State of Politics: https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/2025/07/18/adams-cuomo-call-on-each-other-to-drop-out
- WBAP 820 AM: https://www.wbap.com/2025/08/06/adams-cuomo-refuse-to-drop-out-of-nyc-mayoral-race/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Andrew Cuomo officially withdraws from, suspends, or announces his withdrawal/suspension from the 2025 New York City mayoral race between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-20 (inclusive). Resolution will be based on an official statement from Cuomo or his campaign, or a consensus of credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., New York Times, Politico, NY1, New York Post, Daily News). If Cuomo merely signals he might drop out without making a definitive announcement, or if he endorses another candidate but does not formally withdraw, this resolves No. If no credible reports of a withdrawal emerge by end of day September 20, 2025 (ET), this resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- Politico New York: https://www.politico.com/states/new-york
- NY1: https://www.ny1.com
- New York Post: https://www.nypost.com
- New York Daily News: https://www.nydailynews.com
subquestions.rationale: Cuomo's decision to stay in or drop out is one of the most important factors affecting Adams' own calculus. Both Cuomo and Walden pledged to exit by early September if not leading in polls. If Cuomo drops out and endorses Adams, Adams gains a much more viable path to victory and is far less likely to drop out himself. If Cuomo drops out and does NOT endorse Adams (or endorses someone else), this could also shift the race dynamics. If Cuomo stays in despite his earlier pledge, the continued vote-splitting makes both candidates less competitive against Mamdani, potentially increasing pressure on Adams to exit. This is a genuine crux: two forecasters who disagree on whether Adams will drop out likely disagree in part based on what they expect Cuomo to do.

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl' achieve at least 300 million Spotify streams on its first day of release (October 3, 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' is scheduled for release on October 3, 2025. It has already broken Spotify's record for the most pre-saved album Countdown Page, surpassing her own previous record set by 'The Tortured Poets Department' (TTPD) in 2024. TTPD achieved 300 million streams on its first day and one billion streams within five days, making it the most-streamed album in a single day on Spotify (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-04-22/the-tortured-poets-department-taylor-swift-album-record/). Swift was Spotify's most-streamed artist of 2024, with over 26.6 billion global streams (https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-12-04/top-songs-artists-podcasts-audiobooks-trends-2024/). She currently holds the all-time record as the most-streamed artist on Spotify with over 108.9 billion lead-artist streams (https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/music/most-streamed-us-musician-how-taylor-swift-overtook-bad-bunny-drake-and-more-101726694000670.html). The new album features 12 tracks, including a collaboration with Sabrina Carpenter on the title track. A massive first-day streaming performance would add billions of streams to Swift's 2025 total, significantly boosting her chances of finishing as Spotify's top artist for the year.

Sources:
- Spotify Newsroom, TTPD records: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-04-22/the-tortured-poets-department-taylor-swift-album-record/
- Spotify Wrapped 2024: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2024-12-04/top-songs-artists-podcasts-audiobooks-trends-2024/
- Hindustan Times, Swift streaming milestones: https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/music/most-streamed-us-musician-how-taylor-swift-overtook-bad-bunny-drake-and-more-101726694000670.html
- Euronews, pre-save record: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album
- RouteNote, album details: https://routenote.com/blog/taylor-swift-breaks-spotify-pre-save-record-life-of-a-showgirl/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible reports from Spotify or major music industry outlets (e.g., Billboard, Variety, Digital Music News, or Spotify's official newsroom at https://newsroom.spotify.com/) confirm that Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' achieved at least 300 million Spotify streams on its first day of availability (October 3, 2025). The resolution window is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. If no official or credible third-party reporting on the album's first-day streaming total is available by October 31, 2025, or if the album's release is delayed beyond October 31, 2025, the question resolves No. Streams are counted globally across all tracks on the album, consistent with how Spotify reported first-day figures for 'The Tortured Poets Department.' The primary resolution source is Spotify's official newsroom (https://newsroom.spotify.com/) or official Spotify social media accounts. If Spotify does not publish exact figures, credible music industry reporting (e.g., Billboard at https://www.billboard.com/ or Chart Data at https://x.com/chartdata) may be used.
subquestions.rationale: A blockbuster first-day performance for 'The Life of a Showgirl' would generate a massive spike in Swift's cumulative 2025 streams, reinforcing her lead over competitors for Spotify's top artist of the year. Her previous album TTPD's 300 million first-day streams were instrumental in her securing the #1 spot in 2024. If the new album matches or exceeds this benchmark, it signals enormous listener engagement that would likely persist through the remainder of 2025, making it very difficult for any other artist to surpass her total streams. Conversely, if the album underperforms relative to TTPD, it could indicate waning momentum that might allow a competitor to overtake her. This is a concrete, measurable early indicator that directly impacts the annual streaming totals Spotify uses to determine its top artist.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House Oversight Committee issue a subpoena to the Walz administration or Minnesota state agencies in connection with the Minnesota fraud probe between December 29, 2025, and January 21, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
House Oversight Chairman James Comer has been leading an expanding federal investigation into fraud in Minnesota, reportedly involving billions of dollars in misused federal funds across welfare, education, housing, and nutrition programs. As of late December 2025, Comer warned that 'the walls are caving in on Tim Walz' and indicated the probe was incorporating whistleblower testimony, subpoenas, and federal agency coordination (Fox News, Dec 23, 2025). Comer had previously threatened subpoenas for withheld information (Redstate, Dec 12, 2025). Multiple Trump cabinet officials, including Education Secretary Linda McMahon and SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler, have publicly called for Walz to resign or accused him of obstructing investigations. Governor Walz has acknowledged responsibility but questioned the scope of claimed fraud figures, calling them politically motivated. Whether the congressional investigation escalates through formal subpoena power could significantly increase political pressure on Walz and signal whether the scandal reaches a level that could force a resignation.

Sources:
- Fox News (Dec 23, 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/comer-warns-walls-caving-tim-walz-minnesota-fraud-probe-widens
- Redstate (Dec 12, 2025): https://redstate.com/bonchie/2025/12/12/watch-walz-serves-up-stunning-word-salad-on-minnesota-fraud-n2184123
- Fox News (Dec 16, 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-cabinet-official-calls-walz-resign-over-massive-fraud-scandal-scathing-letter-shame-on-you
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between December 29, 2025, and January 21, 2026 (inclusive), the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Accountability issues at least one formal subpoena directed at the Walz administration, any Minnesota state agency (e.g., Minnesota Department of Human Services, Minnesota Department of Education), or any current or former official of these entities in connection with the Minnesota fraud investigations. Evidence of a subpoena may come from official committee press releases (https://oversight.house.gov/), congressional records, or a consensus of credible news reporting (e.g., from outlets such as Fox News, CNN, AP, Reuters, the Washington Post, or the Star Tribune). If no such subpoena is publicly confirmed by January 21, 2026, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The escalation of the congressional investigation is a key leading indicator of whether political pressure on Walz intensifies to the point where resignation becomes more likely. A formal subpoena would signal that the probe is producing actionable findings and that Congress is willing to use compulsory process against Walz's administration—substantially increasing the political and legal pressure on him. Forecasters who believe Walz is likely to resign would probably also expect the investigation to escalate rapidly, while those who think he will ride out the storm would expect the probe to stall or remain at the rhetorical level. This makes it a meaningful crux for disagreements about the ultimate question.

question: Ukraine recognizes Russian sovereignty over its territory by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement. 

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory for any amount of time will count.

An agreement by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995, “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia, which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement, is an example of a qualifying agreement.

An official unilateral pledge by Ukraine formally recognizing Russian sovereignty over any UN-recognized Ukrainian territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution even if not part of an agreement with Russia.

The April 19, 2013, Brussels Agreement between Serbia and Kosovo, in which Serbia recognized Kosovo’s de facto administration but did not formally grant de jure recognition, would not be considered a qualifying agreement under this market, as this market requires formal recognition of sovereignty rather than acknowledgment of administrative control.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold direct, officially acknowledged bilateral negotiations (in person or via videoconference) between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, Ukraine and Russia have not engaged in direct bilateral peace negotiations. Most diplomatic activity has been mediated through third parties, primarily the United States and various European actors. In April–May 2025, the Trump administration presented proposals that included US recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea and de facto acceptance of Russian control over other occupied territories, but Ukraine firmly rejected formal cession of any territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that formally surrendering land is a constitutional red line, and Ukrainian lawmakers have been nearly unanimous in opposing de jure recognition of Russian sovereignty over any Ukrainian territory (https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/). Russia, for its part, has demanded preconditions such as Ukraine halting mobilization and ceasing acceptance of foreign military aid before agreeing to a full ceasefire (https://www.rt.com/news/616089-ukraine-cede-land-russia-trump-envoy/). The European Union has also rejected US proposals to recognize Crimea as Russian (https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief). Without direct talks between Kyiv and Moscow, any agreement — let alone one involving territorial recognition — remains extremely unlikely. The initiation of direct negotiations would therefore be a critical early indicator of whether a deal recognizing Russian sovereignty over Ukrainian territory could materialize by end of 2025.

Sources:
- Kyiv Independent: https://kyivindependent.com/dangerous-and-cruel-trumps-reported-crimea-proposal-sparks-horror-among-ukraines-lawmakers/
- RT (Trump envoy report): https://www.rt.com/news/616089-ukraine-cede-land-russia-trump-envoy/
- Euronews (Brussels rejects Crimea recognition): https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/04/23/brussels-rejects-russian-recognition-of-crimea-and-sanctions-relief
- Yahoo News (Ukrainians reject Crimea surrender): https://www.yahoo.com/news/shocked-us-peace-proposal-ukrainians-090028498.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia hold or publicly announce they have scheduled direct bilateral negotiations (whether in person, via videoconference, or through formally designated bilateral negotiating teams meeting face to face). The negotiations must be officially acknowledged by both the Ukrainian government and the Russian government (e.g., through statements from the respective presidents, foreign ministries, or official spokespeople). Talks mediated solely through a third party (e.g., US shuttle diplomacy, or UN-mediated discussions where Ukrainian and Russian delegations do not directly engage with each other) do not count. The primary resolution sources will be official statements from the Ukrainian President's Office (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) and the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mid.ru/en/). If official statements are unavailable, resolution may rely on an overwhelming consensus of credible international media reporting (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com/, Associated Press https://apnews.com/, BBC https://www.bbc.com/news) confirming that direct bilateral negotiations took place or were formally scheduled. If the event is announced but postponed beyond October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to formally recognize Russian sovereignty over any of its territory by December 31, 2025, a necessary precondition is that Ukraine and Russia are actually engaged in direct negotiations. As of September 2025, no such direct talks have occurred; all diplomatic channels have been indirect. The commencement of direct bilateral negotiations within the next month would be a strong early signal that a deal — including potentially one involving territorial recognition — could be reached within the ultimate question's timeframe. Conversely, the absence of any direct talks would strongly suggest that the ultimate question will resolve No, since there would be insufficient diplomatic runway to negotiate and announce such a monumental agreement by year's end.

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift cancel, postpone, or visibly skip any previously scheduled public appearances or professional commitments in October 2025, with speculation about a pregnancy being cited as a possible reason by at least two major entertainment news outlets?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce announced their engagement in late August 2025, fueling ongoing speculation about the couple's family plans. Multiple AI-generated hoax pregnancy announcements circulated on social media in September 2025 and were debunked by Snopes and Yahoo Fact Check, indicating strong public interest in the topic. Swift is currently in a period of album promotion for her upcoming 'New Heights' collaboration album, which typically involves a packed schedule of appearances, interviews, and promotional events. Celebrity pregnancies are often first suspected by the public when stars unexpectedly withdraw from scheduled events or alter their public appearance patterns. Travis Kelce mentioned in a September 2025 interview that no wedding date has been set yet, but the couple's engagement keeps them in the spotlight. As of October 2025, Swift has various professional commitments related to album promotion and potential award-season events.

Sources:
- Yahoo Fact Check on AI pregnancy hoax: https://www.yahoo.com/news/fact-check-taylor-swift-travis-kelce-didnt-announce-pregnancy-seriously-194455498.html
- Snopes debunk of pregnancy rumor: https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/taylor-swift-travis-kelce-pregnancy/
- Covers.com on Swift-Kelce engagement and wedding odds: https://www.covers.com/sport/taylor-swift-travis-kelce-wedding-odds

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), Taylor Swift cancels, postpones, or is notably absent from at least one previously scheduled or widely expected public appearance or professional commitment (e.g., a concert, award show, TV appearance, press event, or promotional obligation), AND at least two major entertainment news outlets (e.g., People, TMZ, E! News, Entertainment Weekly, Us Weekly, Page Six, Billboard, Variety, or equivalent) publish articles speculating that a pregnancy could be a reason for the change. The speculation does not need to be confirmed — it only needs to appear in the reporting of at least two distinct major outlets. If Swift does not cancel or skip any appearances, or if no major outlet links any absence to pregnancy speculation, this resolves No. Resolution will be determined by searching Google News for relevant coverage from the listed outlets on or before 2025-11-03 to account for articles published on October 31.
subquestions.rationale: A key early indicator of a pregnancy announcement is a change in the public behavior of the celebrity — particularly cancellations or unexplained absences from scheduled events. If Swift were pregnant, she might reduce public appearances before making an official announcement, and entertainment media would likely speculate about the reason. This subquestion captures a different observable event (schedule changes + media speculation) rather than simply asking about the pregnancy announcement itself with an earlier deadline. If this resolves Yes, it would significantly increase the probability of a pregnancy announcement before year-end; if No, it modestly decreases the probability since it suggests business-as-usual.

question: Will Russia capture Kupiansk by October 31?
description:

An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the railroad station, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW map show Russian-controlled territory (shaded red) within the built-up area of Kupiansk east of the Oskil River expanding to cover at least 15% of that built-up area by October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-September 2025, satellite imagery and open-source analysis indicate that Russia controls only about 6.3% of the built-up areas of Kupiansk, far less than the 'half the city' that Russian officials have claimed (The Moscow Times, September 17, 2025). Russian forces have been infiltrating the eastern outskirts of Kupiansk using unconventional routes, including gas pipelines crossing the Oskil River, and have established positions in the southern outskirts and near the railway (Ukrainska Pravda, September 12, 2025). However, Ukrainian forces deny significant Russian advances and maintain that they control Kupiansk and surrounding areas (Ukrainska Pravda, September 17, 2025). The Kup'yans'k-Pivdennyi railroad station — the target in the ultimate question — is located within the city, meaning Russia would need to substantially expand its control of Kupiansk's built-up area beyond the current ~6.3% to reach it. DeepState's war blog has characterized the Russian presence in Kupiansk as a contested 'grey zone' with small units moving through forests rather than a consolidated occupation (The Moscow Times, September 17, 2025). The ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) is the primary tool for tracking territorial control.

Sources:
- The Moscow Times (2025-09-17): https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive-a86638
- Ukrainska Pravda (2025-09-12): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/12/7431234/
- Ukrainska Pravda (2025-09-17): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/17/7431456/
- ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-20 (inclusive), the ISW Ukraine interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian-controlled territory (shaded red) covering approximately 15% or more of the built-up area of Kupiansk that lies east of the Oskil River. The built-up area of Kupiansk east of the Oskil is defined as the urbanized zone visible on satellite imagery roughly bounded by the river to the west and the city limits to the east, north, and south. Assessment will be made by visual comparison of the red-shaded area on the ISW map against the total built-up area east of the Oskil, using standard mapping tools or visual estimation. If the ISW map becomes unavailable, DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as a fallback. If both are permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible open-source conflict-tracking analysts (e.g., reporting from credible OSINT accounts or news outlets) may be used. Temporary map glitches do not count. The question resolves No if the 15% threshold is not reached at any point during the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: To capture the Kup'yans'k-Pivdennyi railroad station, Russia must significantly expand its territorial control within Kupiansk's built-up area from the current ~6.3%. Tracking whether Russian-held territory doubles or more (reaching ~15%) within the city east of the Oskil River by October 20 serves as a leading indicator: if Russia cannot substantially expand its footprint in Kupiansk by that date, it is very unlikely to reach the railroad station by October 31. Conversely, if territorial control is expanding rapidly, it signals momentum toward the station. This subquestion measures the rate of advance — a fundamentally different observable from the binary 'station captured or not' — and provides an early signal about the trajectory of the battle.

question: Israel strikes Iran by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly announce a repositioning or deployment of additional military assets (e.g., carrier strike groups, THAAD batteries, or bomber task forces) to the Middle East between October 1, 2025 and October 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Historically, U.S. military deployments to the Middle East have served as both a deterrent and an enabler of Israeli military action against Iran. Before Israel's October 2024 strikes on Iran, the U.S. deployed a THAAD battery and additional personnel to Israel (https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3938919/). During the June 2025 12-day conflict referenced by CSIS, Israel expended more than 150 THAAD interceptors — nearly a quarter of the U.S. stockpile — highlighting the critical role U.S. air-defense assets play in enabling Israeli offensive operations against Iranian targets (https://www.csis.org/analysis/enduring-role-fires-modern-battlefield). The deployment of a carrier strike group or additional missile-defense assets to the region is often a precursor to or concurrent with major Israeli military operations, as it provides both defensive cover and a signal of U.S. political backing. As of late September 2025, the USS Harry S. Truman Carrier Strike Group is operating in the Mediterranean, and the U.S. maintains CENTCOM assets in the Gulf region. Any significant additional deployment would signal heightened expectations of escalation between Israel and Iran.

Sources:
- U.S. Department of Defense, THAAD deployment to Israel (Oct 2024): https://www.defense.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/3938919/
- CSIS, 'The Enduring Role of Fires on the Modern Battlefield' (Sep 2025): https://www.csis.org/analysis/enduring-role-fires-modern-battlefield
- Times of Israel, Houthi missile and drone attacks and Israeli retaliatory strikes: https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-intercepts-yemen-ballistic-missile-houthis-say-it-had-cluster-bomb-warhead/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 22, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Defense, CENTCOM, or senior U.S. administration officials publicly announce or confirm the deployment, repositioning, or surging of additional major military assets to the Middle East region (defined as the CENTCOM area of responsibility, including the Eastern Mediterranean). Qualifying assets include: a carrier strike group, an amphibious ready group, a THAAD or Patriot battery, a bomber task force, or a squadron of fighter aircraft. Routine rotations that were previously scheduled and publicly announced before October 1, 2025 do not count; the deployment must be described as a new or additional movement. Resolution will be based on official DoD/CENTCOM press releases (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/) or credible reporting from at least two of the following: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), or The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com). If no such announcement is made by October 22, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: U.S. military force posture in the Middle East is one of the strongest leading indicators of whether Israel will undertake a major strike on Iran. Israeli strikes on Iranian territory require extensive air-defense coverage and political coordination with the United States, both of which are signaled by new U.S. deployments. If the U.S. surges additional assets to the region, it substantially increases the probability that Israel is preparing or has received a green light for strikes on Iran. Conversely, the absence of new deployments suggests the status quo is holding. This subquestion is observable well before the ultimate question's deadline and measures a different but highly correlated variable — U.S. military posture rather than the Israeli strike itself.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and Iran reach a nuclear deal or formal diplomatic agreement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?

If the US and Iran reach a nuclear agreement or significant diplomatic understanding, it would dramatically reduce the likelihood of an Israeli strike on Iran, as Israel would face enormous US pressure not to undermine a deal. Conversely, if talks collapse, Israel may feel compelled to act militarily.

question: Apple Vision Pro 2 released by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will Apple officially announce a new Vision Pro headset (successor to the original Vision Pro) at its September 2025 event?

Note: This question is about announcement only, not retail availability. If the event is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether a Vision Pro successor will be released (available for purchase) by December 31, 2025. An official announcement in September is a necessary precursor to a retail release by year-end. If Apple does not announce a successor Vision Pro at or shortly after its September 2025 event, it becomes highly unlikely that the product could be available for purchase by December 31. Conversely, if Apple does announce a successor at the September event, the product would very likely ship within weeks or months, dramatically increasing the probability of a year-end release. This makes the September announcement a strong early indicator for the ultimate question, without simply being the same question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will TIME's Person of the Year for 2025 be a woman?

subquestions.question: Will a woman appear on TIME Magazine's November 2025 shortlist or 'Person of the Year' speculation coverage as a leading candidate?
subquestions.background_information:
Each year, TIME Magazine announces its Person of the Year in early-to-mid December. In the weeks leading up to the announcement, TIME and other media outlets publish shortlists, reader polls, and speculative coverage about likely candidates. In 2024, TIME's shortlist included figures such as Donald Trump (who won), Kamala Harris, Kate Middleton, and others. In 2023, Taylor Swift won the award. Recent reporting from Showbiz411 (October 10, 2025) suggested TIME may be distancing itself from awarding Donald Trump again, with an editorial criticizing his Nobel Peace Prize campaign. Meanwhile, a Just Jared article from September 30, 2025, cited reports that Trump was 'reportedly set to be named' Person of the Year for a second time. The mixed signals make the identity of the 2025 honoree uncertain. Historically, women have won the individual Person of the Year award relatively rarely — notable recent winners include Taylor Swift (2023), Greta Thunberg (2019), and Angela Merkel (2015). Whether a woman features prominently in the pre-announcement speculation and shortlist coverage can serve as an early indicator of the final selection.

Sources:
- Showbiz411: TIME Magazine Seems To Shut the Door on Trump Getting Person of the Year (October 10, 2025): https://www.showbiz411.com/2025/10/10/time-magazine-seems-to-shut-the-door-on-trump-getting-person-of-the-year-with-damning-nobel-peace-prize-editorial

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), TIME Magazine publishes an official shortlist, reader poll, or equivalent 'Person of the Year' candidates feature for 2025 that includes at least one woman as a named candidate, OR if at least three major English-language news outlets (e.g., CNN, BBC, The New York Times, The Washington Post, Reuters, AP, The Guardian) publish articles between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 identifying a specific woman as a leading or frontrunner candidate for TIME's 2025 Person of the Year. The woman must be identified by name, and the coverage must specifically discuss her as a serious contender (not merely listed among dozens of possibilities). If TIME does not publish a shortlist or poll by November 30, 2025, resolution relies solely on the three-major-outlet criterion. If neither condition is met by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary sources for resolution:

subquestions.rationale: TIME's Person of the Year announcement in December is typically preceded by weeks of shortlist speculation and official reader polls in November. If a woman features prominently as a leading candidate in this pre-announcement coverage, it significantly raises the probability that a woman will ultimately be selected. Conversely, if November speculation is dominated entirely by male candidates (e.g., Trump, Zelensky, or other male world leaders), it would be a strong indicator that the final pick is unlikely to be a woman. This subquestion captures an observable early signal — the composition of the speculative shortlist — that is distinct from the final announcement itself but highly correlated with the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Eric Adams endorse Cuomo?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams publicly call on Andrew Cuomo to drop out of the NYC mayoral race (or vice versa, Cuomo call on Adams to drop out) between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 NYC mayoral general election features Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani leading in polls with ~44% support, followed by Andrew Cuomo running as an independent (~25%), Republican Curtis Sliwa (~12%), and incumbent Mayor Eric Adams (~7%). There has been widespread discussion among business leaders and political figures about the need for either Adams or Cuomo to drop out to consolidate the anti-Mamdani vote. Former Gov. David Paterson, who previously supported Cuomo in the primary, switched to endorsing Adams in August 2025, and has suggested one of the two should step aside. Attorney Jim Walden has proposed a ranked-choice poll pledge to determine which non-Democratic candidate should face Mamdani one-on-one, with Cuomo signing on but Adams not yet agreeing. Cuomo has previously urged other candidates to coalesce behind the strongest opponent, but Adams has refused to drop out. As of late August 2025, there is no indication that Adams plans to endorse Cuomo or vice versa; instead, both camps appear to be competing for the same lane of moderate/centrist voters opposed to Mamdani.

Sources:
- NewsMax, "Fmr N.Y. Gov. Paterson to Endorse Adams in Mayoral Race" (2025-08-13): https://www.newsmax.com
- The Hill, "Former NY governor endorsing Eric Adams for NYC mayor" (2025-08-13): https://thehill.com
- CBS News, "Former Gov. David Paterson endorsing Eric Adams for reelection" (2025-08-13): https://www.cbsnews.com
- NewsMax, "Mamdani Leaves NY Business Leaders Divided on Opposition Strategy" (2025-07-22): https://www.newsmax.com
- The Wave, "Editorial: Jim Walden To The Rescue?" (2025-07-18): https://rockawave.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), Eric Adams publicly calls on Andrew Cuomo to withdraw from the mayoral race, OR Andrew Cuomo publicly calls on Eric Adams to withdraw from the mayoral race. A 'public call' must be a direct, on-the-record statement (e.g., in a press conference, interview, official social media post, or campaign statement) explicitly urging the other candidate to drop out or step aside. Vague suggestions that 'someone' should consolidate do not count — the statement must specifically name the other candidate. Resolution will be based on credible reporting from major news outlets such as the New York Times, New York Post, Politico New York, or NY1, or official statements from the Adams or Cuomo campaigns. If no such public call occurs by September 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Adams and Cuomo are publicly pressuring each other to drop out is a key indicator of whether an endorsement could follow. If Adams publicly calls on Cuomo to drop out, it signals he views the race as competitive and himself as the stronger candidate — making an Adams-endorses-Cuomo outcome very unlikely. Conversely, if Cuomo publicly calls on Adams to drop out (and Adams's poll numbers remain very low), this increases pressure on Adams to exit the race and potentially endorse Cuomo. The absence of any such public calls would suggest the status quo continues — both running independently with no endorsement forthcoming. This is a different observable event from the endorsement itself, but it directly tracks the political dynamics that would precede or preclude an endorsement.

question: Will tariffs generate >$250b in 2025?
description:
The U.S. government collected $82.2b in customs duties in FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/reports-statements/financial-report/2024/notes-to-the-financial-statements19.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes"  if the value of costumes duties collected in FY 2025 according to the Financial Report of the United States Government published by the Treasury Department for FY 2025 (See: https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/financial-report/) is greater than $250b. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No". 

If the Treasury Department does not publish relevant data  for FY 2025 by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be the Treasury Department.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Treasury report cumulative gross customs duties of at least $200 billion for FY 2025 through August 2025 in the Monthly Treasury Statement?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. fiscal year 2025 runs from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2025. For the ultimate question of whether tariffs generate more than $250 billion in FY 2025, the trajectory of customs duty collections through the penultimate month (August) is a critical leading indicator. As of the end of July 2025, cumulative customs duties reached approximately $150 billion on a gross basis, with monthly collections hitting records of $27.2 billion in June and $28 billion in July. Higher 'reciprocal' tariffs on U.S. trading partners took effect on August 1, 2025, which President Trump and Treasury Secretary Bessent indicated would significantly increase collections further. Bessent has predicted tariffs may generate more than $300 billion in revenue for the full fiscal year. If cumulative collections through August reach $200 billion, that would mean September would need to generate approximately $50 billion to cross the $250 billion threshold — a plausible amount given recent monthly trends. If collections fall well short of $200 billion through August, reaching $250 billion for the full year becomes much harder. The Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for August is typically published in mid-September and reports customs duties as a line item under government receipts.

Sources:
- Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement: https://fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/
- July tariff revenues break monthly record: https://trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov/articles/july-tariff-revenues-break-monthly-record/
- US customs duties top $100B for first time: https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/us-customs-duties-top-100-billion-first-time-fiscal-year-2025-07-11/
- Benzinga report on customs duties exceeding $100B: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/07/45709858/amid-trump-tariffs-us-customs-duty-collection-exceeds-100-billion-in-a-fiscal-year-for-the-first-time
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Treasury Department's Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) for August 2025, published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, reports cumulative gross customs duties collected during FY 2025 (October 2024 through August 2025) of at least $200 billion. The relevant data can be found in the MTS 'Receipts' table under 'Customs duties' (gross basis, before refunds). The MTS is available at https://fiscal.treasury.gov/reports-statements/mts/. If the August 2025 MTS is not published by 2025-10-01, or if it does not contain customs duty data, this question resolves No. For avoidance of doubt, the $200 billion threshold refers to the 'fiscal year-to-date' gross customs duties figure reported in the August 2025 MTS.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks the cumulative customs duty trajectory through August 2025 — the second-to-last month of FY 2025. If cumulative collections reach $200 billion through August, then September would need only ~$50 billion to hit $250 billion for the full year, which is very plausible given June ($27B) and July ($28B) collections, especially with reciprocal tariffs in effect since August 1. If collections are well below $200 billion, reaching $250 billion becomes much harder. This makes the $200 billion threshold a meaningful crux: forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question are likely to find that the August cumulative figure substantially updates their beliefs about whether $250 billion will be reached for the full fiscal year.

question: Macron out in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will French Prime Minister François Bayrou lose a confidence vote in the National Assembly between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A confidence vote on Prime Minister François Bayrou's budget plan is scheduled for September 8, 2025. Bayrou has proposed approximately €44 billion in spending cuts and tax increases, including scrapping two public holidays and freezing spending increases. Opposition from both the far-right National Rally (led by Marine Le Pen) and the far-left France Unbowed (led by Jean-Luc Mélenchon) makes his survival uncertain. Bayrou's predecessor, Michel Barnier, was ousted after only three months via a similar no-confidence motion in late 2024. If Bayrou loses, he must resign along with his government, leaving Macron to either reappoint him, choose a seventh prime minister since 2017, or call new elections. The hard-left has explicitly called on Macron to resign if the government falls, with Mélenchon stating 'Macron is chaos... He must go.' However, Macron has repeatedly and firmly stated he will serve out his term until 2027, saying on August 29, 2025: 'The mandate which has been given to me by the French people, and by no-one else, is a mandate that will be carried out through to the end of its term.' The Paris stock exchange fell roughly 2% amid the political uncertainty, and French sovereign bond yields have risen.

Sources:
- France 24: https://www.france24.com
- The Straits Times, 'France's Macron vows to serve out term despite budget crisis' (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.straitstimes.com
- Hurriyet Daily News, 'Fears of new political crisis grip France' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com
- Yahoo News, 'Macron rules out resigning if he loses sixth prime minister' (Aug 30, 2025): https://news.yahoo.com
- Court House News Service, 'Macron vows to serve out term despite budget crisis' (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.courthousenews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), the French National Assembly passes a motion of no confidence (motion de censure) against Prime Minister François Bayrou's government, OR if Bayrou loses a vote of confidence (vote de confiance) that he himself initiated. The question resolves No if no such vote occurs or if Bayrou survives all confidence/no-confidence votes held during this period. Resolution will be based on official records of the French National Assembly (https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/) or a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as France 24 (https://www.france24.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), and Le Monde (https://www.lemonde.fr). If the scheduled September 8 vote is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The fall of Bayrou's government would be the most significant near-term catalyst that could increase pressure on Macron to resign. While Macron has firmly stated he will serve out his term, losing a sixth prime minister would deepen France's political crisis dramatically. If Bayrou survives, the political pressure on Macron eases substantially, making his departure in 2025 extremely unlikely. If Bayrou falls, it creates the chaotic political environment in which opposition calls for Macron's resignation intensify, parliament could be dissolved again, and the scenario for Macron's departure — while still unlikely given his stated intentions — becomes more plausible. This is the key observable near-term event that would most update forecasters on the ultimate question.

question: Will Hezbollah disarm in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hezbollah officially announces it will disarm in Lebanon by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only announcements supported by the Secretary-General of Hezbollah (currently Naim Qassem), a direct successor, or, if the position of Secretary-General of Hezbollah is vacant, the widely acknowledged leadership of Hezbollah will qualify. 

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in Lebanon.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hezbollah leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Israel withdraw from all five of its military positions in southern Lebanon by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since the November 2024 ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, Israel has maintained troops at five strategic positions inside southern Lebanon. A key reason Hezbollah has given for refusing to disarm is Israel's continued occupation of Lebanese territory and ongoing military strikes. Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem has repeatedly stated that 'the resistance will not hand over its weapons as long as aggression and occupation continue' (Middle East Eye, 2025-09-09). Israel has conditioned its withdrawal on Lebanese efforts to disarm Hezbollah, with PM Netanyahu offering a 'phased' pullout only if Lebanon follows through on disarmament plans (BSS, 2025-08-25). Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich has stated that 'the IDF isn't withdrawing — and with God's help, won't withdraw — from the five positions' (The Duran, 2025-08-03). Lebanese officials have insisted that Israel must first commit to a full cessation of hostilities and withdrawal before disarmament can proceed. This creates a deadlock: Hezbollah won't disarm while Israel occupies Lebanese territory, and Israel won't withdraw until Hezbollah disarms. An Israeli withdrawal would remove one of Hezbollah's primary justifications for retaining its weapons, potentially shifting internal Lebanese political dynamics toward disarmament.

Sources:
- Middle East Eye, 'Lebanon: What will it take to disarm Hezbollah?', 2025-09-09: https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/lebanon-what-will-it-take-disarm-hezbollah
- BSS, 'Israel PM offers phased withdrawal if Lebanon disarms Hezbollah', 2025-08-25: https://www.bssnews.net/news/international/189273
- The Duran, 'Beirut walks a political tightrope without a safety net', 2025-08-03: https://theduran.com/beirut-walks-a-political-tightrope-without-a-safety-net/
- The Express Tribune, 'Hezbollah refuses to be disarmed', 2025-09-27: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2506789/hezbollah-refuses-to-be-disarmed
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera) confirms that Israel has fully withdrawn its military forces from all five positions it has maintained inside southern Lebanon since the November 2024 ceasefire. 'Fully withdrawn' means no Israeli military personnel remain stationed at any of the five positions. Temporary cross-border incursions or patrols that do not constitute permanent or semi-permanent stationing do not prevent resolution as Yes, provided the five fixed positions are vacated. If Israel withdraws from some but not all five positions, or if withdrawal is announced but not completed by 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. If reporting is ambiguous or contradictory, the question resolves based on UNIFIL situation reports (https://unifil.unmissions.org/) and official Israeli Defense Forces statements (https://www.idf.il/en/).
subquestions.rationale: Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon is a critical precondition that Hezbollah has explicitly cited for any discussion of disarmament. If Israel withdraws, it removes Hezbollah's primary stated justification for retaining weapons, which could shift the political calculus in Lebanon and make a formal disarmament announcement more plausible before year-end. Conversely, continued Israeli occupation makes Hezbollah disarmament in 2025 virtually impossible, as it gives the group both political cover and genuine security rationale for maintaining its arsenal. This is a genuine crux: forecasters who believe Hezbollah might disarm likely expect some movement on the Israeli withdrawal front, while those who see disarmament as near-impossible likely expect the occupation to persist.

question: Israel x Iran ceasefire broken by March 31, 2026?

subquestions.question: Will Israel's Prime Minister publicly announce or confirm plans for a new military strike on Iran during his visit to Washington, D.C. before February 5, 2026?

Reports indicate that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu plans to present proposals for a new attack on Iran to President Trump during an upcoming visit to Washington. Israel is particularly concerned about Iran rebuilding and expanding its ballistic missile production capacity, with estimates of up to 3,000 missiles per year if unchecked. Meanwhile, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed on December 21, 2025, that all damaged strategic facilities have been 'fully reconstructed,' asserting Iran's readiness for renewed conflict. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stated on January 5, 2026, that Iran is 'intensifying efforts to safeguard its territorial integrity' and does not trust external statements. A public Israeli commitment to new strikes on Iran would be a strong leading indicator that the ceasefire could break before March 31, 2026.

Conversely, if the visit occurs without such an announcement—or if diplomatic language prevails—it suggests the ceasefire may hold. question: Will 'Wicked: For Good' have the best domestic opening weekend in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will any movie released in 2025 before November 21 have a 3-day domestic opening weekend gross of $150 million or more, as reported by The Numbers?
