question: Starmer out in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Keir Starmer ceases to be the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for any period of time between February 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of Keir Starmer's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The resolution source for this market will be the government of the UK, however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will a formal Labour leadership challenge or a no-confidence motion against Keir Starmer as Labour leader be publicly initiated between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Keir Starmer has faced growing discontent within the Labour Party throughout 2025. His personal approval ratings have cratered, with an Ipsos survey showing 73% of UK adults unsatisfied with his performance — the lowest score the polling company has ever recorded for a prime minister's first-year performance. Reform UK has overtaken Labour in some polls, and senior Labour MPs have openly discussed the possibility of Starmer being forced out. Sky News deputy political editor Sam Coates reported in July 2025 that 'I am hearing from ministers in government that Starmer might have to go in months.' A LabourList poll of party members found that former leader Ed Miliband topped favourability rankings among potential replacements, with a net favourability of +68.6.

Under Labour Party rules, a leadership challenge can be triggered if a challenger secures nominations from 20% of Labour MPs and MEPs, or if the leader loses a confidence vote at the party's annual conference. Labour's annual conference is scheduled for late September 2025, which could provide a natural focal point for any organised challenge. The July 2025 bond market sell-off, prompted by Starmer's perceived failure to back Chancellor Rachel Reeves, further damaged confidence in his leadership.

Sources:
- Sky News report on Starmer's position: https://www.rt.com/news/601234-starmer-could-be-on-way-out/
- Economic Times on Labour leadership speculation: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/uk/keir-starmer-on-the-way-out-this-surprise-contender-could-be-the-uks-next-prime-minister/articleshow/111510234.cms
- Labour Party rulebook on leadership challenges: https://labour.org.uk/rulebook/
- Starmer bond market crisis: https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2025/07/03/starmer-crisis-shows-uk-still-lives-at-mercy-of-the-bond-market
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), any of the following occur: (1) A Labour MP or group of Labour MPs publicly announces they are formally challenging Keir Starmer for the Labour leadership, including by declaring candidacy and/or submitting nomination papers; OR (2) A formal no-confidence motion in Starmer as Labour leader is tabled or voted upon at Labour's annual conference or through any other official Labour Party mechanism; OR (3) Starmer himself announces he will face a leadership contest. This does not include informal media speculation, anonymous briefings, or opinion polls about leadership preferences. The event must be confirmed by official Labour Party communications (https://labour.org.uk/) or reported by at least two of the following: BBC News (https://www.bbc.co.uk/news), Sky News (https://news.sky.com/), The Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/), or Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/). If no such formal challenge or no-confidence motion is publicly initiated within this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The most plausible mechanism for Starmer to leave office in 2025 is through internal Labour Party pressure — either a formal leadership challenge or a no-confidence motion that forces his resignation. Labour's annual conference in late September 2025 is a natural flashpoint where such a challenge could crystallize. If a formal challenge is initiated in September, it dramatically increases the probability that Starmer ceases to be PM before year-end. Conversely, if Starmer survives the conference period without a formal challenge, it suggests the party establishment is not yet ready to move against him, making his departure by December 2025 less likely. This subquestion captures an observable, near-term event that is a strong leading indicator of the ultimate outcome without merely restating it.

question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The Statement on Monetary Policy for the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy meeting for January is scheduled to be released on January 23, 2026 (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Japan's January 2026 meeting.

If the short-term policy interest rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Bank of Japan (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Japan's statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will Japan's core consumer price index (CPI, excluding fresh food) year-over-year increase exceed 3.0% for the October 2025 reading (released in November 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Japan's core CPI (excluding fresh food) has remained at or above the BOJ's 2% target for over three years. In September 2025, core CPI year-over-year growth was reported at around 2.4-2.8%, with some measures of underlying inflation running above 3%. The persistence and trajectory of inflation is a key factor in whether the BOJ will raise rates at its January 2026 meeting. If inflation accelerates further above 3%, it increases pressure on the BOJ to hike rather than cut rates, making a rate decrease even less likely. Conversely, a sharp deceleration in inflation could open the door to a more dovish stance. The October 2025 CPI data is scheduled for release by the Statistics Bureau of Japan on November 21, 2025.

At the BOJ's October 2025 meeting, the board voted 7-2 to hold rates at 0.5%, with two members dissenting in favor of a hike to 0.75% due to ongoing inflationary pressures (bne IntelliNews, 2025-10-30: https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-348841/). ING analysts noted core inflation remaining above 3% as a reason a December 2025 hike was possible (Investing.com, 2025-10-29: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-93CH-3942567). The IMF urged the BOJ to proceed 'very gradually' with hikes given trade uncertainties (Yahoo Finance, 2025-10-15: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/imf-urges-bank-japan-move-040124407.html).

Sources:
- Statistics Bureau of Japan CPI release: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html
- bne IntelliNews, BOJ holds rate (2025-10-30): https://www.intellinews.com/bank-of-japan-keeps-key-rate-unchanged-as-takaichi-takes-office-348841/
- Investing.com, BOJ preview Oct (2025-10-29): https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/boj-preview-oct-rates-to-remain-on-hold-outlook-in-focus-amid-sticky-inflation-93CH-3942567
- Yahoo Finance, IMF urges gradual hikes (2025-10-15): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/imf-urges-bank-japan-move-040124407.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Japan's core consumer price index (CPI, excluding fresh food, as reported by the Statistics Bureau of Japan at https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html) for October 2025 shows a year-over-year increase exceeding 3.0% (i.e., strictly greater than 3.0%). The relevant data release is expected on or around November 21, 2025. If the October 2025 CPI data is not released by December 8, 2025, this question resolves No. The resolution window is between 2025-11-08 and 2025-12-08. The primary resolution source is the Statistics Bureau of Japan's CPI release page: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/index.html. If this source is unavailable, a consensus of credible financial news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, NHK) reporting the official figure may be used.
subquestions.rationale: The trajectory of Japan's core inflation is one of the most critical inputs to the BOJ's rate decision. If core CPI exceeds 3.0% year-over-year, it strongly signals persistent inflationary pressure, which makes a rate cut at the January 2026 meeting extremely unlikely and instead increases the probability of a rate hike. Conversely, if inflation decelerates meaningfully, it could shift expectations toward a more dovish BOJ stance. This inflation reading will be available well before the January meeting and is a key data point the BOJ will consider, making it a highly informative early indicator of whether the BOJ would decrease rates.

question: Will Trump's approval rating hit 40% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump’s approval rating according to Silver Bulletin is equal to or below the listed value for any date between April 14 and December 31 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Note that the approval ratings for this date must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely once the next data point is available, the previous one is finalized).

This market's resolution source will be Silver Bulletin' approval rating poll aggregator, https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin, specifically the approval rating indicated by the green trend line for the resolution date. Changes in the methodology by which Silver Bulletin calculates the approval rating will have no bearing on the resolution of this market. If Silver Bulletin's approval rating becomes permanently unavailable, RealClearPolitics will be used.

If the approval rating for December 31 is not published by January 4, 2026, 12:00 PM ET (noon), this market will resolve according to all previous datapoints.

subquestions.question: Will Trump's Silver Bulletin approval rating trend line fall below 44% at any point between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-August 2025, Nate Silver described Trump's approval rating numbers as 'very boring,' with his net approval fluctuating between -8.5 and -8.9 percentage points since August 1 (https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-numbers-very-boring-nate-silver-1939558). This implies an approval rating of roughly 45-46% and disapproval of roughly 54-55%. Earlier in 2025, Trump's approval dipped as low as roughly 44.5-45% on the Silver Bulletin trend line during the tariff-driven decline in late April (net approval hit -9.7). To reach 40% approval — the threshold in the ultimate question — Trump would need a significant further decline from his current ~45-46% level. Whether his approval drops below 44% in September would be a meaningful intermediate signal, as it would indicate the kind of accelerating decline needed to eventually reach 40%. Silver Bulletin publishes daily approval trend line data at https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin. The approval rating has been relatively stable since mid-July at around 45-46% approve / 54-55% disapprove, so a drop below 44% would represent a notable shift.

Sources:
- Newsweek, "Donald Trump approval rating numbers have become 'very boring' -- Nate Silver" (Aug 11, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-numbers-very-boring-nate-silver-1939558
- Silver Bulletin approval rating tracker: https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin
- Newsweek, "Trump's approval rating has 'started to drop more quickly' -- Nate Silver" (Jul 21, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/trump-approval-rating-drop-nate-silver-2025-1936821
- NYMag, "At 100 Days, Trump Approval Rating Is As Low As First Term" (Apr 28, 2025): https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/at-100-days-trump-approval-rating-is-as-low-as-first-term.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between September 1, 2025, and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the green trend line on Silver Bulletin's approval rating tracker (https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin) shows Trump's approval rating at or below 44.0%. The relevant data point is the 'approve' percentage on the green trend line (not individual polls). A data point is considered finalized once the next day's data point is published. If Silver Bulletin's tracker becomes permanently unavailable during this period, RealClearPolitics' approval average (https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/approval/donald-trump/approve) will be used as a fallback. If neither source is available, the question resolves as ambiguous. The question resolves No if, for every finalized data point between September 1 and September 30, 2025, the approval trend line remains above 44.0%.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump's approval to reach 40% by the end of 2025 (the ultimate question), it would need to decline roughly 5-6 percentage points from its current ~45-46% level. A drop below 44% in September would represent a meaningful downward break from the stable range observed since mid-July, signaling the kind of erosion trajectory that could plausibly continue to 40% by year-end. Conversely, if approval stays above 44% through September — maintaining the 'very boring' stability Silver noted — it becomes significantly less likely that approval will plunge all the way to 40% in the remaining three months of 2025. This subquestion thus serves as an early warning indicator: forecasters who disagree on whether 40% will be reached should update substantially based on whether a sub-44% reading materializes in September.

question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hamas officially announces it will disarm in the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only credible announcements, for example by the widely acknowledged leadership of Hamas, will qualify.

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in the Gaza Strip.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hamas leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Hamas publicly reject disarmament as a precondition for advancing to the second phase of the Trump peace plan between November 30 and December 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Hamas has consistently resisted demands to disarm as part of the US-backed 20-point Trump peace plan, which took effect with a ceasefire on October 10, 2025. The plan's second phase requires Hamas to relinquish its military capabilities and governance role in Gaza under international supervision. However, Hamas has only agreed to the first phase (ceasefire and hostage exchange) and has publicly stated that the remaining phases are 'up for negotiation.' On November 26, 2025, Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem reiterated that the organization will not disarm unless the issue is resolved through 'internal Palestinian dialogue' and linked to a broader political process culminating in an independent Palestinian state with Jerusalem as its capital. Senior Hamas official Osama Hamdan has stated that Hamas rejects disarmament, international forces inside Gaza, and non-Palestinian governance, and that weapons would only be handed over to a future Palestinian state. Meanwhile, Qatar's Prime Minister has indicated that Qatar is pressuring Hamas to accept disarmament, and Arab mediators have suggested Hamas might be open to partial disarmament. Despite this, Hamas has been reasserting power in Gaza, carrying out retribution executions and rebuilding infrastructure, signaling it intends to maintain its military and political position. A fresh formal rejection of disarmament by Hamas leadership in December would be a strong signal that the ultimate question (agreement to disarm by December 31) will resolve No.

Sources:
- Arutz Sheva: "Hamas continues steadfast refusal to disarm" (Nov 26, 2025) https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/404567
- Gatestone Institute: "How Hamas Is Planning to Deceive the Trump Administration" (Nov 13, 2025) https://www.gatestoneinstitute.org/21529/hamas-deceive-trump-administration
- The Hill: "Hamas reasserts power in Gaza with retribution campaign" (Oct 14, 2025) https://thehill.com/policy/international/5043210-hamas-reasserts-power-gaza-retribution/
- The Boston Globe: "Arab mediators believe Hamas could be open to partially disarming" (Oct 8, 2025) https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/10/08/world/arab-mediators-believe-hamas-could-be-open-partially-disarming/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 25, 2025 (inclusive), a senior Hamas official (e.g., a member of the politburo, a recognized spokesman such as Hazem Qassem or Osama Hamdan, or a leader such as Khalil al-Hayya) makes a public statement—reported by at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Al Jazeera, BBC, CNN)—explicitly rejecting disarmament as a precondition for proceeding to the second phase of the Trump peace plan or explicitly stating that Hamas will not agree to disarm. Statements that condition disarmament solely on future Palestinian statehood or 'internal Palestinian dialogue' without agreeing to a concrete disarmament process count as rejections. The question resolves No if no such public rejection is reported during this period, or if Hamas makes statements indicating openness to disarmament without preconditions. Resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news).
subquestions.rationale: Hamas's public stance on disarmament in the weeks leading up to December 31 is the most direct observable indicator of whether they will formally agree to disarm by the deadline. As of late November 2025, Hamas has been consistently rejecting disarmament demands, but the situation is fluid with ongoing mediation. If Hamas issues another explicit rejection in December, it would strongly suggest the ultimate question resolves No. Conversely, a notable absence of rejection statements—or signals of openness—could indicate movement toward agreement. This subquestion captures a concrete, observable indicator (public statements by Hamas leadership) that directly informs the probability of the ultimate outcome.

question: Elon no longer world's richest before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Elon Musk is any rank other than #1 on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index at any point between June 30, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bloomberg Billionaires Index (https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/). If this source becomes permanently unavailable in that time period, the Forbes Real-Time Billionaires List will be used (https://www.forbes.com/real-time-billionaires/#6aa3f0213d78). If both sources become permanently unavailable, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will Tesla's stock price decline by 15% or more from its closing price on September 1, 2025, at any point between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Elon Musk's net worth is heavily tied to Tesla stock. As of late August 2025, Musk's net worth was approximately $407-410 billion according to Forbes' real-time tracker, with a substantial lead over the second-richest person, Larry Ellison (~$278-280 billion). However, Musk's wealth has been highly volatile in 2025 — he lost over $71 billion earlier in the year due to Tesla stock declines triggered by trade war fears and political controversies (Benzinga, July 5, 2025: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/07/45678-elon-musks-71-billion-wealth-wipeout). As of August 22, 2025, Forbes listed Musk at $407.9 billion and Ellison at $277.9 billion, a gap of roughly $130 billion (townflex.com: https://townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/). Tesla stock is the primary driver of Musk's wealth; a sharp decline in Tesla shares could significantly narrow or eliminate his lead. Musk holds approximately 506 million Tesla shares after his recent pay package approval (Morningstar, August 4, 2025: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/2025080411148/elon-musk-to-get-29-billion-richer-as-his-pay-package-is-approved-teslas-stock-jumps). A 15% decline in Tesla stock would wipe roughly $23 billion from his stake, though this alone might not close the gap. However, a significant Tesla decline often coincides with market conditions that could boost competitors' wealth (e.g., Oracle stock rising for Ellison). Tesla's stock has been volatile throughout 2025 due to EV market competition, Musk's political activities, and trade policy uncertainty.

Sources:
- Benzinga (July 5, 2025): https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/07/45678-elon-musks-71-billion-wealth-wipeout
- Townflex (August 22, 2025): https://townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/
- Morningstar (August 4, 2025): https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/2025080411148/elon-musk-to-get-29-billion-richer-as-his-pay-package-is-approved-teslas-stock-jumps
- TEMPO.CO (August 25, 2025): https://en.tempo.co/read/1966217/10-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-elon-musk-lost-billions
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Tesla's stock price (TSLA on NASDAQ) closes at or below 85% of its closing price on September 1, 2025 (i.e., a 15% or greater decline from the September 1 close), on any trading day between September 2, 2025, and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). The closing price is defined as the official NASDAQ closing price. If September 1, 2025 is not a trading day, the closing price from the most recent prior trading day will be used as the reference. Resolution will be based on publicly available historical stock data from Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/history/) or NASDAQ's official records (https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/tsla/historical). If both sources are unavailable, Google Finance may be used as a fallback. The question resolves No if no trading day in the specified window sees a closing price at or below the 85% threshold.
subquestions.rationale: Tesla stock is the single largest driver of Elon Musk's wealth. A sharp Tesla decline is the most plausible near-term mechanism by which Musk could lose the #1 ranking on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. While Musk's current lead (~$130 billion over Ellison) means a 15% Tesla drop alone wouldn't dethrone him, such a decline would signal heightened volatility and negative momentum that could compound into a larger wealth erosion over the remaining months of 2025. Additionally, sharp Tesla declines have historically coincided with broader conditions (e.g., tariff fears, political controversies) that could simultaneously boost competitors' wealth. A Yes resolution here would meaningfully increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes before year-end, while a No resolution (Tesla staying relatively stable) would suggest Musk's lead remains robust.

question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will the USA be favored (odds of 50% or higher implied probability) to win the 2025 Ryder Cup in the betting markets as of September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 Ryder Cup is scheduled for September 26-28 at Bethpage Black in Farmingdale, New York. Team USA, captained by Keegan Bradley, features Scottie Scheffler (World No. 1), Xander Schauffele, Bryson DeChambeau, Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay, Sam Burns, Cameron Young, Ben Griffin, Russell Henley, Harris English, and J.J. Spaun. Team Europe, captained by Luke Donald, includes Rory McIlroy, Tommy Fleetwood, Tyrrell Hatton, Robert MacIntyre, Justin Rose, Rasmus Højgaard, and six captain's picks to be finalized.

Historically, the home team has a significant advantage in the Ryder Cup. The USA has won their last two home Ryder Cups (2016 at Hazeltine, 2021 at Whistling Straits — where they won 19-9). However, Europe won the 2023 edition in Rome 16.5-11.5 and are the defending champions. Europe holds a 12-9-1 record against the USA since 1979 overall.

As of late August 2025, betting markets and fan sentiment are divided, with some expecting a strong USA performance at home and others backing Europe's veteran match-play expertise. The final betting odds on the eve of the tournament (September 25) will incorporate the most up-to-date information about player form, captain's picks, practice round observations, course conditions, and any injury news — making them a strong composite indicator of which team is likely to prevail.

Sources:
- Sportskeeda: "USA's gonna destroy Europe," "Europe wins comfortably" - Golf fans divided as the 2025 Ryder Cup gets closer: https://www.sportskeeda.com/golf/usa-gonna-destroy-europe-europe-wins-comfortably-golf-fans-divided-2025-ryder-cup-gets-closer
- Yahoo Sports: 2025 Ryder Cup format, rules: https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/2025-ryder-cup-format-rules-everything-know-us-takes-europe-180048498.html
- talkSPORT: All you need to know about 2025 Ryder Cup: https://talksport.com/sport/golf/3254388/ryder-cup-2025-bethpage-black-everything/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, on September 25, 2025, the consensus of major sportsbook odds (such as those aggregated on OddsChecker, BetMGM, DraftKings, or FanDuel) implies that Team USA has a 50% or higher probability of winning the 2025 Ryder Cup outright (excluding the tie/draw outcome). The implied probability is calculated from the decimal odds as: implied probability = 1 / decimal odds. If multiple major sportsbooks are available, the average implied probability across at least two major books will be used. If odds are only available in American or fractional format, they should be converted to decimal for the calculation.

The resolution window is between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26. Specifically, the odds snapshot should be taken from the latest available odds on September 25, 2025 (the day before play begins). If September 25 odds are not available due to a market closure, the most recent odds available before September 26, 2025 will be used.

If the Ryder Cup is postponed or canceled before September 26, 2025, such that no pre-tournament odds are posted, the question resolves N/A.

Sources for resolution:
- OddsChecker Ryder Cup page: https://www.oddschecker.com/golf/ryder-cup
- DraftKings Sportsbook: https://sportsbook.draftkings.com/
- FanDuel Sportsbook: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/
subquestions.rationale: Pre-tournament betting odds are one of the best composite predictors of sporting event outcomes, as they aggregate expert analysis, player form, course fit, home advantage, and all other relevant factors. If the USA is favored at 50%+ implied probability on the eve of the event, this is a strong (though not conclusive) signal that they will win. Conversely, if Europe is favored, that updates significantly toward a European win. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question of whether USA wins the Ryder Cup are likely to partly ground their disagreement in whether they believe the USA will be the market favorite heading into the competition. This subquestion resolves before the event begins, making it a true leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

question: Nothing Ever Happens: Khamenei
description:
This market will resolve to “No” if any of the following conditions are met between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 ET:

- Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran
- Khamenei leaves Iran

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, is removed from power for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. Khamenei will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Supreme Leader of Iran within this market's timeframe. The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Khamenei leaves Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if it is confirmed that Ali Khamenei has left Iran for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. In cases where Ali Khamenei may have exited Iranian airspace on a plane, he must be confirmed to have exited the plane in a country other than Iran for this market to resolve to "No". If Ali Khamenei exits Iranian maritime territory on a boat to international waters, this market may resolve to "No". The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. carry out a military strike on Iranian territory between February 5, 2026 and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early 2026, the United States has deployed significant naval forces to the Middle East, including the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group, amid escalating tensions with Iran. Former President Trump confirmed a 'massive flotilla' heading toward the region and has repeatedly warned Iran of consequences for its crackdown on protesters. Reports indicate that U.S. Central Command has completed preparations for a potential military operation, though no final decision has been made. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has reportedly moved to a fortified underground bunker in Tehran due to fears of a U.S. strike, with his son Masoud Khamenei managing day-to-day governance. Iranian officials have warned that any attack would be treated as 'all-out war.' International analysts have warned that miscommunication or sudden escalation could trigger broader regional conflict. A U.S. military strike would dramatically increase the probability that Khamenei is either removed from power or forced to flee Iran.

Sources:
- News.com.au (2026-01-25): https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge/news-story

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
