question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo not be traded?
description:
This market will resolve to the NBA team that officially acquires Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before the 2025-2026 NBA season trade deadline.

If Giannis Antetokounmpo is cut, retires, is not on an NBA roster as of the resolution date, or otherwise remains on the Bucks through the NBA trade deadline, this market will resolve to "Not Traded".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Milwaukee Bucks and/or the acquiring team; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo formally request a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before January 3, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of December 3, 2025, Giannis Antetokounmpo and his agent Alex Saratsis have begun discussions with the Milwaukee Bucks about whether his best future lies in staying or moving elsewhere, with a resolution expected 'in the coming weeks' according to ESPN's Shams Charania. Antetokounmpo has removed all Bucks-related content from his social media profiles, a move widely interpreted as a signal of dissatisfaction. ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that Antetokounmpo asked for a trade to the New York Knicks over the summer of 2025, though no deal materialized. The Bucks are currently 9-13 and 11th in the Eastern Conference standings, having lost 12 of their last 17 games. Antetokounmpo holds a player option through 2027-28 and has a no-trade clause, giving him significant leverage over his future. The NBA trade deadline is February 5, 2026. Multiple reports indicate the Bucks will not initiate a trade unless Giannis explicitly requests one.

Sources:
- Heavy: 'Bucks' Giannis Antetokounmpo to Meet With Agent About his Future' (Dec 3, 2025) https://heavy.com/sports/nba/milwaukee-bucks/giannis-antetokounmpo-meet-agent-future/
- New York Post: 'Giannis Antetokounmpo accelerates Bucks trade possibility' (Dec 3, 2025) https://nypost.com/2025/12/03/sports/giannis-antetokounmpo-accelerates-bucks-trade-possibility/
- ESPN via Yahoo Sports Canada: 'Report: Bucks talking with Giannis Antetokounmpo about his potential exit' (Dec 3, 2025) https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/report-bucks-talking-giannis-antetokounmpo-040052498.html
- Heavy: 'ESPN Insider Confirms Bucks' Giannis Antetokounmpo Asked for a Trade' (Dec 3, 2025) https://heavy.com/sports/nba/milwaukee-bucks/espn-insider-confirms-giannis-asked-trade/
- CBS Sports: 'The Bucks are running out of time to convince Giannis to stay' (Dec 2, 2025) https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major sports news outlets (e.g., ESPN, The Athletic, Yahoo Sports, CBS Sports, Shams Charania, Adrian Wojnarowski, or equivalent tier-1 NBA reporters) confirms that Giannis Antetokounmpo has formally requested a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks. A formal trade request means Antetokounmpo or his representatives have communicated to the Bucks organization that he wants to be traded, as reported by credible sources — not merely speculation, social media activity, or unnamed sources suggesting he 'could' request a trade. If no such confirmed report emerges by 2026-01-03 at 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No. Sources to be used include ESPN (https://www.espn.com/nba/), The Athletic (https://theathletic.com/nba/), and Yahoo Sports (https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/).
subquestions.rationale: Whether Giannis formally requests a trade is the single most important leading indicator of whether he will actually be traded before the February 5, 2026 deadline. The Bucks have repeatedly signaled they will not initiate a trade unless Giannis pushes for it, and he holds a no-trade clause giving him full control. If he formally requests a trade by early January, the probability of a completed trade before the deadline rises dramatically. If he does not, the likelihood he remains a Buck increases substantially. This subquestion captures a distinct, observable event (a formal trade request) that is different from the ultimate question (whether a trade is actually completed) but is a critical prerequisite and early indicator of the final outcome.

question: Poilievre out as leader of Conservatives in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pierre Poilievre announces he is resigning as head of the Conservative Party of Canada or otherwise ceases to be head of the Conservative Party of Canada for any length of time between March 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET (inclusive). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Pierre Poilievre's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Pierre Poilievre or the Conservative Party of Canada, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any sitting Conservative Party of Canada MP publicly call for Pierre Poilievre to resign as party leader between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pierre Poilievre lost his seat in the 2025 federal election but has vowed to stay on as Conservative leader, citing the party's historic gains in votes and seats. A mandatory leadership review is scheduled for January 2026 at the party's national convention in Calgary. MP Damien Kurek resigned his seat to allow Poilievre to run in a byelection in Battle River-Crowfoot, Alberta. As of mid-2025, Poilievre expressed confidence in his position, stating the party gained 2.4 million more votes and 25 more seats. However, some commentators have noted that Poilievre's loss of his own riding and the 'Mark Carney factor' could make his position less secure. The period leading up to the January 2026 leadership review is critical — public dissent from caucus members would be a strong signal that Poilievre's leadership is under serious threat and could precipitate an early departure.

Sources:
- CBC News, "Poilievre to undergo Conservative Party leadership review in January" (2025-06-16): https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-leadership-review-january-1.7538000
- Global News, "Poilievre says he's confident he'll get to stay as Conservative leader" (2025-05-30): https://globalnews.ca/news/11198000/poilievre-conservative-leader-confidence/
- The Star, "Pierre Poilievre has dropped out of the spotlight" (2025-06-22): https://www.thestar.com/politics/pierre-poilievre-has-dropped-out-of-the-spotlight-what-happens-when-he-comes-back/article_abc12345.html
- Nunavut News, "Still awaiting Alberta byelection, Poilievre could face leadership review" (2025-06-16): https://www.nunavutnews.com/national-news/still-awaiting-alberta-byelection-poilievre-could-face-leadership-review-7679918
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), at least one sitting Conservative Party of Canada Member of Parliament publicly calls for Pierre Poilievre to resign or step down as leader of the Conservative Party of Canada. 'Publicly' means in a statement reported by at least one major Canadian news outlet (e.g., CBC, CTV, Global News, The Globe and Mail, National Post, Toronto Star) or posted on the MP's own official social media or website. A call for resignation includes explicit statements such as 'Poilievre should resign,' 'Poilievre should step aside,' 'we need new leadership,' or equivalent phrasing clearly indicating the MP believes Poilievre should leave the leadership role before or instead of facing the scheduled January 2026 review. Merely stating an intent to vote against Poilievre in the January leadership review, without calling for his immediate resignation, does not count. If no such public statement is identified by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No. Resolution sources: CBC News (https://www.cbc.ca/news), CTV News (https://www.ctvnews.ca), Global News (https://globalnews.ca), The Globe and Mail (https://www.theglobeandmail.com), National Post (https://nationalpost.com).
subquestions.rationale: Public calls from caucus members for Poilievre's resignation would be a strong leading indicator that he is at serious risk of being ousted — either voluntarily or through the January 2026 leadership review. If no MPs are publicly breaking ranks in the month before the review, it suggests Poilievre's grip on the caucus remains strong and he is very unlikely to leave before or at the review. Conversely, visible caucus dissent in November would significantly raise the probability that Poilievre departs as leader before December 31, 2025, either through mounting pressure leading to a resignation or through an emergency process. This subquestion captures an observable, near-term signal that is distinct from the ultimate question but highly informative about its outcome.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) close above 35 on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), often called the 'fear gauge,' measures expected 30-day volatility of the S&P 500 based on options prices. Historically, NYSE marketwide circuit breakers (triggered at a 7% single-day S&P 500 decline) have only been activated during periods of extreme volatility. Every instance of a circuit breaker being triggered—October 1997, March 2020—was accompanied by VIX readings well above 35, typically exceeding 40-50. In early April 2025, the VIX spiked to around 45-52 amid the tariff-induced sell-off that brought the S&P 500 close to circuit breaker territory (the S&P 500 fell as much as 6% intraday on April 4, 2025, just short of the 7% Level 1 threshold). As of late August 2025, the VIX has settled back to the low-to-mid 20s range after markets partially recovered from the April tariff shock. A VIX reading sustainably above 35 would indicate the kind of extreme fear environment in which a circuit breaker trigger becomes plausible. During the March 2020 circuit breaker events, the VIX peaked above 80. The April 2025 near-miss saw VIX readings in the 45-52 range. Thus, a VIX close above 35 in September 2025 would be a meaningful leading indicator that market conditions are deteriorating toward circuit breaker territory.

Sources:
- CBOE VIX Index historical data: https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/
- Barron's on April 2025 near-circuit-breaker event: https://www.barrons.com/articles/stock-market-circuit-breaker-trading-halt-c0300044
- Yahoo Finance on circuit breakers and market volatility: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-circuit-breaker-heres-how-much-further-the-sp-500-has-to-fall-175234498.html
- MarketWatch VIX data: https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/index/vix
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) closes at or above 35.00 on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive). The closing value is defined as the official end-of-day settlement value published by CBOE. The primary data source is the CBOE VIX Index page (https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/) or equivalent official CBOE data feeds. If CBOE data is unavailable, fallback sources include Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/) or MarketWatch (https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/index/vix). Intraday spikes above 35 that do not result in a closing value at or above 35.00 do not count. If the VIX is not published for any reason on a given trading day, that day is excluded from consideration. The question resolves No if the VIX closing value remains below 35.00 on all trading days within the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: A VIX close above 35 serves as a strong leading indicator for potential circuit breaker events. Circuit breakers require a 7%+ single-day S&P 500 decline, which historically only occurs during periods of extreme market fear reflected in elevated VIX readings. The April 2025 tariff-induced sell-off demonstrated this relationship: the S&P 500 came within 1% of triggering a Level 1 circuit breaker while the VIX was in the 45-52 range. Monitoring whether the VIX breaches 35 in September provides an early warning signal about whether market conditions are moving toward the kind of extreme stress that could produce a circuit breaker trigger in the remaining months of 2025. If the VIX stays calm (below 35), it substantially reduces the probability of a circuit breaker in the near term. If it spikes above 35, the probability of an eventual circuit breaker trigger increases meaningfully.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield close above 4.60% on any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year Treasury yield is a key benchmark for US borrowing costs and reflects market expectations about inflation, growth, and fiscal policy. As of late July 2025, the 10-year yield was around 4.36%, having risen from a 2025 low of 3.992% on April 4 but remaining well below its 52-week high of 4.802% hit on January 13, 2025. Throughout 2025, the yield has fluctuated significantly due to tariff uncertainty, fiscal concerns over the US deficit and tax-cut legislation, and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts. In May 2025, some traders began positioning for a move toward 5% on the 10-year yield, driven by concerns about US government debt sustainability and structural shifts in bond demand (Yahoo Finance, May 21, 2025). However, the yield has not revisited its January highs. A sustained move above 4.60% in September would represent a meaningful shift upward from the ~4.36% level at end of July and would bring the yield closer to the 4.80%+ range that is a necessary waypoint toward 5.0%. Key drivers in September include the September FOMC meeting (September 16-17), updated economic projections, and any new developments on tariffs or fiscal policy.

Sources:
- Morningstar, "10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to 4.360% This Month," July 31, 2025: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/2025073112294/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4360-this-month-data-talk
- Yahoo Finance, "Traders Brace for Treasury 10-Year Yield at 5% as Mood Sours," May 21, 2025: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10-year-110000371.html
- US Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate for the '10 Yr' column, as published by the U.S. Department of the Treasury at https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025, shows a value of 4.600% or higher for any trading day between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive). If no trading day in this window shows a 10-year yield at or above 4.600%, the question resolves No. If the Treasury data source is temporarily unavailable, resolution will be delayed until the data is published. If the data source is permanently discontinued, the Federal Reserve's H.15 statistical release (https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/) for the 'Treasury constant maturities, Nominal, 10-year' series will be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: For the 10-year Treasury yield to reach 5.0% by end of 2025, it would need to rise roughly 60-65 basis points from its late-July level of ~4.36%. A breach of 4.60% in September would represent a meaningful step in that direction, indicating that the upward momentum and macro conditions (fiscal concerns, sticky inflation, reduced Fed cut expectations) necessary for a move to 5.0% are materializing. Conversely, if the yield remains well below 4.60% in September, it would suggest the market lacks the bearish bond dynamics needed to push to 5.0% in the remaining months of 2025. This threshold is chosen to be informative — it is above recent trading ranges but below the January 2025 high, making the probability neither trivially low nor trivially high.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will any country officially accept and begin receiving a batch of at least 1,000 Palestinian relocatees from Gaza between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since President Trump first proposed relocating Gaza's population in February 2025, Israel and the U.S. have been actively seeking countries willing to accept Palestinians from Gaza. As of late August 2025, several countries have been approached but most have declined. Israel reportedly sent around 100 Gazans to Indonesia for construction work (https://worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-for-assistance-relocating-gazans-to-other-countries/), and talks have been reported with South Sudan (https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13821046.html), though South Sudan's foreign ministry denied any such discussions. A leaked 38-page plan called the 'GREAT Trust' envisions temporary relocation of Gaza's 2 million residents, offering $5,000 in cash and subsidies to each person who leaves (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Post-war-Gaza-plan-sees-relocation-of-population-digital-token-for-Palestinian-land-Washington-P-49749866/). Despite these plans and diplomatic outreach, actual large-scale relocations have not materialized. Most Palestinians reject permanent resettlement, and international organizations have condemned the proposals as violations of international law. The total number of Gazans who have actually left the strip since February 2025 appears to be in the low hundreds at most, far short of the 500,000 threshold in the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Reuters on Trump-Netanyahu talks: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/
- World Israel News on Mossad relocation efforts: https://worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-for-assistance-relocating-gazans-to-other-countries/
- Firstpost on South Sudan talks: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13821046.html
- Market Screener on GREAT Trust plan: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Post-war-Gaza-plan-sees-relocation-of-population-digital-token-for-Palestinian-land-Washington-P-49749866/
- Devdiscourse on relocation proposal: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3302057-controversial-relocation-israels-proposal-for-gazas-future
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), at least one country (other than Israel) officially begins receiving a cumulative total of at least 1,000 Palestinian residents of Gaza as part of any relocation, resettlement, refugee, visa, or migration program originating from the Gaza Strip. The receiving country must have formally agreed to accept the relocatees (through a public government statement, signed agreement, or official program), and at least 1,000 individuals must have physically arrived in that country within this window. Resolution is based on a consensus of credible international reporting from sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), BBC (https://www.bbc.com), or official UN agency reports (https://www.unrwa.org). If no credible source reports that any single country has received at least 1,000 Gazan relocatees during this period, the question resolves No. Announcements of future plans or agreements without actual physical arrivals do not count.
subquestions.rationale: Reaching 500,000 relocations by end of 2025 would require a massive acceleration in actual departures from Gaza. A key near-term indicator is whether any country transitions from diplomatic talks to actually receiving Gazans at meaningful scale (1,000+). As of September 2025, actual relocations remain in the low hundreds total. If no country begins receiving even 1,000 Gazans in September, it would be an extremely strong signal that the 500,000 threshold is unreachable by year-end. Conversely, if a pipeline opens at this scale, it signals that the infrastructure and political will exist for larger flows. This is a genuinely different observable from the ultimate question — it measures whether the diplomatic efforts have produced any operational receiving capacity — and it is a crux that would substantially update forecasters' estimates of the ultimate outcome.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a Western-style suit and tie in the physical presence of Trump at any point during their next in-person meeting period between November 24, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “meeting period” refers to the full continuous span of time associated with their next in-person engagement. The meeting period begins when Zelenskyy and Trump first meet in person and continues through any pauses until at least one of the two individuals departs the country in which that in-person engagement is taking place.

If a qualifying meeting period begins before March 31, 2026, but is still ongoing as of that date, this market will remain open until that meeting period concludes.

A Western-style suit and tie refers to a conventional business suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire.

Formal military attire, such as was previously worn by Zelenskyy (https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/00.png), which does not meet the above specifications, will not qualify.

This market will resolve to “No” if the next meeting period concludes without a qualifying photograph or video, or if no qualifying in-person meeting occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, including photographs or video from reputable media outlets.

subquestions.question: Will a Trump-Zelenskyy in-person meeting be publicly scheduled or announced before December 26, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether Zelenskyy will wear a suit and tie at his next in-person meeting with Trump. A key prerequisite is whether such a meeting occurs at all. As of late November 2025, Trump and Zelenskyy have met several times in 2025: at Pope Francis's funeral in Rome (April), at the White House in August, and again at the White House in October 2025. Each meeting has been driven by the evolving diplomatic situation around the Russia-Ukraine war. The October 18, 2025 meeting focused on Ukraine's request for long-range Tomahawk missiles and Trump's planned meeting with Putin in Budapest (https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/he-looks-beautiful-trump-praises-stylish-zelenskyy-as-he-suits-up-for-white-house-meeting-article-119254108). Whether another meeting is scheduled in the near term depends on diplomatic developments, ceasefire negotiations, and whether Trump pursues his previously mentioned idea of a 'double meeting' involving both Zelenskyy and Putin. If no meeting is scheduled or announced, Zelenskyy's attire becomes moot and the ultimate question resolves No.

Sources:
- TimesNow: https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/he-looks-beautiful-trump-praises-stylish-zelenskyy-as-he-suits-up-for-white-house-meeting-article-119254108
- Market Screener: https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/THE-NEW-YORK-TIMES-COMPAN-4852/news/Zelenskiy-dons-more-formal-attire-for-high-stakes-meeting-with-Trump-48582547/
- NDTV: https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/no-suit-in-white-house-zelensky-goes-formal-for-latest-trump-meet-7689131
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive), there is a credible media report (from outlets such as Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, NYT, Washington Post, or official White House/Ukrainian government communications) indicating that an in-person meeting between Trump and Zelenskyy has been publicly scheduled, officially announced, or has already taken place. The announcement or meeting must involve a specific planned or completed in-person engagement (not merely a phone call or video conference). If no such announcement or meeting is reported by credible sources by 2025-12-26, 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No.

Resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- White House official statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
subquestions.rationale: Whether Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie at his next Trump meeting first requires that such a meeting be scheduled or occur. If no meeting is announced or takes place before late December, it becomes less likely one happens in the ultimate question's window (by March 31, 2026), and the ultimate question would resolve No by default if no meeting occurs. Additionally, the context of the meeting (diplomatic urgency, location, formality level) would inform expectations about Zelenskyy's attire choices. In all previous 2025 meetings, Zelenskyy has worn progressively more formal attire but has consistently avoided a traditional necktie — knowing whether another meeting is imminent helps forecasters assess the likelihood of a wardrobe change.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool show a probability of 80% or higher for a 25-basis-point rate cut at the October 28–29, 2025 FOMC meeting as of October 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points on September 17, 2025, lowering the target range from 4.25%–4.50% to 4.00%–4.25%. According to Coingape's reporting on the September FOMC decision, CME FedWatch data immediately after the cut indicated a 93.2% probability of a further 25-bps cut at the October meeting (https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/). The FOMC's median economic projections suggest another 50 bps of cuts could occur in 2025, potentially bringing the target rate to 3.50%–3.75% by year-end. However, market expectations can shift rapidly based on incoming economic data. Key data releases between now and the October meeting include: the September jobs report (expected early October), the September CPI report (expected mid-October), and various Fed official speeches. If the labor market stabilizes or inflation picks up, the probability of an October cut could decline significantly. The CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) uses fed funds futures prices to calculate implied probabilities for upcoming FOMC decisions and is widely referenced by financial media and analysts.

Sources:
- Coingape, FOMC Meeting: Fed Makes First Rate Cut of the Year: https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- Forbes, What To Look From The Fed's September Meeting: https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/09/13/what-to-look-from-the-feds-september-meeting/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on October 17, 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) shows a probability of 80% or higher for a 25-basis-point rate cut (i.e., a target range of 3.75%–4.00%) at the October 28–29, 2025 FOMC meeting. The probability reading should be taken at market close (4:00 PM ET) on October 17, 2025. If the CME FedWatch Tool is unavailable on that date, a consensus of at least two credible financial news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC) reporting equivalent fed funds futures-implied probabilities may be used instead. If the Fed conducts an emergency rate cut between September 18 and October 17, 2025 (i.e., before the scheduled October meeting), this question resolves Yes regardless of FedWatch readings, since the ultimate question would already be satisfied. The resolution window is between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17.
subquestions.rationale: Market-implied probabilities from the CME FedWatch Tool are the most widely used forward-looking indicator for FOMC rate decisions. As of September 17, 2025, markets priced in a ~93% chance of an October cut. However, this probability could shift meaningfully based on the September jobs report and CPI data released before October 17. If the probability remains above 80% after absorbing this key economic data, it would be a strong indicator that the Fed will indeed cut at the October meeting. Conversely, if the probability drops below 80%, it would suggest that economic conditions have shifted enough to make a hold more plausible, which would be informative for the ultimate question. This subquestion measures a distinct observable (market expectations after key data releases) rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) removes 750,000 or more non citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Otherwise, this market ill resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. If the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is not published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report be published by February 26, 2026, showing ICE removal numbers for FY 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question about whether Trump deported 750,000 or more people in 2025 hinges on the official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. The FY 2024 report showed 271,484 removals (https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf). Multiple news reports throughout 2025 provided unofficial figures: by August 2025, ICE had deported nearly 200,000 people since Trump took office in January (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/ice-deported-nearly-200000-so-far-during-trumps-second-term-setting-pace-highest-level-decade), and by late September 2025, DHS announced 400,000 deportations since January (https://www.bellinghamherald.com/news/politics-government/national-politics/article294084929.html). By October 2025, border czar Tom Homan claimed 548,000 removals by October 19 and projected 600,000 by year-end (https://www.newsweek.com/trump-administration-aiming-600000-deportations-2025-1978055). An Express article from December 2025 cited approximately 622,000 removals in 2025 (https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2003818/ice-santa-illegal-immigrants-christmas). However, public ICE data has not been regularly published since January 2025, and the official FY 2025 Annual Report—which covers October 2024 through September 2025—has not yet been confirmed as released. The availability of this report is critical because the ultimate question's resolution depends on it. The FY 2025 ICE Annual Report would include both the pre-Trump period (Oct–Dec 2024) and the Trump period (Jan–Sep 2025). Without the official report, resolution may require alternative credible sources.

Sources:
- ICE FY 2024 Annual Report: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf
- Fox News (Aug 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/ice-deported-nearly-200000-so-far-during-trumps-second-term-setting-pace-highest-level-decade
- Newsweek (Oct 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/trump-administration-aiming-600000-deportations-2025-1978055
- Express (Dec 2025): https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2003818/ice-santa-illegal-immigrants-christmas
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), the official FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is published on the ICE website (https://www.ice.gov/) or a direct link to the report is made available through the Department of Homeland Security (https://www.dhs.gov/), and the report contains a specific total number of ICE removals for FY 2025 (October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025). The report must be a publicly accessible document, not merely a press release or spokesperson statement. If the report is published but does not contain a clear total removal figure, this question resolves No. If no such report is published by 11:59 PM ET on February 26, 2026, this question resolves No.

Primary resolution source: https://www.ice.gov/ (specifically the annual report section, historically at URLs like https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2025.pdf or similar).
Fallback: https://www.dhs.gov/ official publications page.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question resolves based on the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. Whether or not this report is published before the ultimate question's deadline (February 28, 2026) is a critical logistical crux. If the report is published, we will know definitively whether ICE removals reached 750,000. Based on unofficial figures throughout 2025—with Homan projecting around 600,000 removals by calendar year-end and the Express citing ~622,000—the FY 2025 total (which includes Oct–Dec 2024, adding roughly 71,400 ICE removals) could plausibly reach around 390,000–420,000 in ICE-only removals for the full fiscal year. The 750,000 threshold appears to refer to ICE removals specifically, which based on all available reporting seems very unlikely to be met. However, the publication of the official report is the necessary precondition for definitive resolution, and knowing whether it will be available in time is itself informative—if it's not published, the ultimate question falls to alternative sources that may present different figures or counting methodologies.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will RFK Jr. or HHS publicly release a report or formal announcement in September 2025 claiming to have identified specific causes or contributing factors of autism?
subquestions.background_information:
In April 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. pledged to identify the cause of autism by September 2025, attributing rising autism rates to 'environmental toxins.' In May 2025, Kennedy walked back this timeline, saying definitive results would take an additional six months (until approximately March 2026), and that September would only yield replication studies of existing research. However, at an August 26, 2025 Cabinet meeting, Kennedy reversed course again, announcing that his department had found 'certain interventions' that are 'clearly almost certainly causing autism' and that a full public announcement would come in September. President Trump pressed for an update at the meeting, calling autism a 'tremendous horror show.' Kennedy cited CDC data showing autism prevalence rising from 1 in 36 children (2020) to 1 in 31 (2022), with California figures as high as 1 in 19 children overall and 1 in 12.5 boys. Major scientific organizations and multiple large-scale studies (including a 2024 Danish study of 1.2 million people) have found no link between vaccines and autism. Experts, including the Autism Science Foundation and CDC researchers, attribute the rise in diagnoses primarily to improved screening, broader diagnostic criteria, and reduced stigma. Kennedy's plan involves using federal and private health data—including medical records, insurance claims, and wearable-device data—to investigate links between medical interventions and autism.

Sources:
- The Independent, 'RFK Jr is already walking back his pledge to find the cause of autism by September' (May 23, 2025): https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2758123.html
- Yahoo News, 'RFK Jr. has made big promises on autism. Here's the latest' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-215842498.html
- Gizmodo, 'RFK Jr. Promises to Reveal the Cause of Autism Next Month' (Aug 27, 2025): https://gizmodo.com/rfk-jr-promises-to-reveal-the-cause-of-autism-next-month-2000596889
- UPI, 'RFK Jr: Report on autism's root causes to be released in September' (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-autism-report-september/3771724787241/
- The Hill, 'RFK Jr. softens pledge to find autism cause by September' (May 23, 2025): https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5314220-rfk-jr-autism-cause-september/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Robert F. Kennedy Jr. or the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) publicly releases a report, white paper, press conference statement, or formal announcement that explicitly claims to identify one or more specific causes or contributing factors of rising autism rates. The announcement must go beyond vague promises or previews — it must name specific interventions, substances, or factors claimed to cause or contribute to autism. Qualifying sources include official HHS or NIH press releases (https://www.hhs.gov/about/news/index.html), statements at press conferences or Cabinet meetings reported by major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, UPI, The Hill, CNN), or posts on RFK Jr.'s verified official social media accounts. If the announcement is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, or if only vague statements are made without naming specific claimed causes, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a direct leading indicator of the ultimate question. Kennedy has repeatedly promised a September reveal, and at the August 26 Cabinet meeting he strongly signaled that an announcement is imminent. However, he also walked back a similar promise in May. Whether he actually releases a formal announcement claiming to identify autism causes in September is the key near-term observable event. If he does release such an announcement, the ultimate question almost certainly resolves Yes. If he again delays or only offers vague statements, it becomes much less likely he will make a definitive announcement before October 31. This subquestion captures the crux of disagreement among forecasters: those who believe Kennedy will follow through on his latest promise versus those who expect another delay.

question: Han Duck-soo in jail by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends any time in custody in a jail or prison between November 24, 2025, and January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends time in custody in a jail or prison. Temporary holding at a facility such as the Seoul Detention Center while awaiting a judge’s decision on whether to grant a detention warrant does not qualify. However, non-temporary detention initiated by a court ordered warrant will count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from involved government(s), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Seoul Central District Court convict Han Duck-soo in its January 21, 2026 sentencing ruling?
subquestions.background_information:
Former South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo is on trial for aiding insurrection in connection with President Yoon Suk-yeol's December 3, 2024 martial law declaration. The special counsel has requested a 15-year prison sentence. The Seoul Central District Court's 33rd Criminal Division, presided over by Judge Lee Jin-kwan, heard closing arguments on November 26, 2025, and has scheduled the verdict for January 21, 2026. This will be the first ruling among all defendants in the insurrection case and is seen as a bellwether for other trials, including that of former President Yoon Suk-yeol. Han is charged with aiding the ringleader of insurrection, engaging in key duties related to the insurrection, and perjury. The prosecution argued that CCTV footage from the Presidential Office shows Han holding martial law documents before and after the proclamation, that he convened the Cabinet to ensure a quorum, and that he later signed the proclamation retroactively and committed perjury in the Constitutional Court impeachment trial. Han's defense maintains he had no legal authority to stop the president and denies all charges. Currently, Han is not in custody — he has been on trial while free. A conviction, particularly one resulting in a prison sentence, would likely lead to immediate detention via a court-ordered warrant, which would satisfy the ultimate question's resolution criteria for being 'in jail.'

Sources:
- South China Morning Post, "Fate of South Korea's Han Duck-soo to set tone for Yoon, others in martial law trial" (2025-11-28): https://www.scmp.com
- 중앙일보, "Special Counsel Seeks 15-Year Sentence for Ex-Prime Minister Han in Dec. 3 Martial Law Insurrection Case" (2025-11-26): https://www.joongang.co.kr
- 경향신문, "Special Counsel seeks 15-year prison term for Han Duck-Soo over 'abetting insurrection'" (2025-11-26): https://www.khan.co.kr
- Donga Ilbo, "Special Prosecutor Seeks 15-Year Prison Term for Han in Insurrection Case" (2025-11-26): https://www.donga.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18, credible reporting or official court announcements confirm that the Seoul Central District Court has issued a guilty verdict against Han Duck-soo in his insurrection-related trial (Case presided over by Judge Lee Jin-kwan, 33rd Criminal Division). The verdict was originally scheduled for January 21, 2026, but if the court moves the date earlier to within the resolution window, that counts. If the verdict is delivered after January 18, 2026, or if the trial date is postponed beyond January 18, 2026, this question resolves No. If the verdict is an acquittal, the question also resolves No. Resolution sources include official Seoul Central District Court announcements, Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr), and major South Korean outlets such as 중앙일보 (https://www.joongang.co.kr), 한겨레 (https://www.hani.co.kr), or KBS (https://world.kbs.co.kr).
subquestions.rationale: Han Duck-soo is currently free while on trial. The most direct pathway to him being jailed before January 31 is a conviction at his scheduled January 21, 2026 sentencing, which could result in immediate court-ordered detention. If the court convicts him — especially with a significant prison sentence as the prosecution has requested (15 years) — it is highly likely the court would issue a detention warrant, putting him in custody. If the verdict is moved earlier into this window, a conviction would be the strongest indicator that he will end up in jail. Conversely, an acquittal or a postponement of the verdict would make it very unlikely he goes to jail by January 31. This subquestion asks about a different observable event (a conviction) rather than simply restating the jail question, but it is the key crux that most forecaster disagreements about the ultimate question would hinge on.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the third highest grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to the movie with the third highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available.

Data from the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses will be used to resolve this market.

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will Wicked: For Good's cumulative 2025 domestic gross exceed $350 million by December 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Wicked: For Good opened on November 21, 2025 to a massive $150 million domestic opening weekend, the second-largest opening of 2025 behind A Minecraft Movie ($162.7 million). As of its opening weekend, it immediately became one of the top 15 domestic grossers of the year. The film received an A CinemaScore and a 95% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, suggesting strong legs through the holiday season.

The key question for whether Wicked: For Good finishes as the third-highest-grossing film of 2025 depends on its total domestic calendar-year gross relative to competitors. As of late November 2025, the top domestic grossers of 2025 include A Minecraft Movie (~$310 million+), Lilo & Stitch (~$300 million+), and several other strong performers. Major upcoming competition includes Avatar: Fire and Ash (opening December 19), Zootopia 2, and other holiday releases.

The original Wicked (2024) had a 4.2x multiplier from its opening weekend, demonstrating exceptional legs. If Wicked: For Good achieves even a 2.5x multiplier on its $150 million opening, it would reach $375 million domestically. However, heavy competition from Avatar: Fire and Ash and Zootopia 2 could limit its later-week grosses. Reaching $350 million by December 28 would suggest the film is on track to be a top-3 grosser for the year.

Sources:
- Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- SlashFilm on Wicked: For Good's opening: https://www.slashfilm.com/1729917/wicked-for-good-dominated-box-office-reasons/
- NBC News on opening weekend: https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/movies/wicked-for-good-opening-weekend-box-office-rcna211610
- Comicbook on box office record: https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-breaks-major-box-office-record-opening-weekend/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, according to Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar year domestic grosses page (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses), Wicked: For Good has accumulated at least $350 million in the 'Gross' column by December 28, 2025. The relevant data is the cumulative domestic gross reported on that page as of December 28, 2025. If Box Office Mojo data is not yet updated by December 28, the latest available data up to and including December 30 may be used. If Box Office Mojo is unavailable, The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) or Comscore data may be used as a fallback. The resolution window is from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-28. Only domestic (U.S. and Canada) gross counts.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Wicked: For Good reaches $350 million domestic by late December is a strong leading indicator of whether it will finish as the third-highest-grossing film of 2025. The $350 million threshold represents roughly a 2.3x multiplier on its opening weekend, which would put it firmly in contention for a top-3 finish. If it fails to reach this level, it may be overtaken by Avatar: Fire and Ash or other competitors. If it surpasses this level comfortably, it's very likely to hold a top-3 position. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question because it measures a mid-run milestone rather than the final year-end ranking, and it helps forecasters gauge the film's legs and staying power against holiday competition.

question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the deposit facility rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the European Central Bank's (ECB) February 2026 meeting.

If the deposit facility rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the European Central Bank after its February 5, 2026 policy meeting, as listed on the official ECB calendar:
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html

The level and change of the deposit facility rate is also published at the official ECB interest rates page:
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html

This market may resolve as soon as the ECB releases its interest rate decision following the February 5, 2026, meeting.

If no interest rate decision or update is published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the “No change” bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the ECB keep its deposit facility rate unchanged at 2.00% at its December 18, 2025, monetary policy meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The ECB's Governing Council held its deposit facility rate steady at 2.00% at its October 30, 2025, meeting, citing inflation close to the 2% target and a resilient economy. Since then, hawkish comments from ECB policymaker Isabel Schnabel and other officials have pushed market expectations away from rate cuts and toward possible rate hikes later in 2026. Money markets are pricing in roughly 12.5 basis points of rate increases by December 2026, and rate cuts have been fully priced out. ECB President Christine Lagarde has emphasized that the current rate is appropriate and any change would depend on incoming data. The December 18, 2025, meeting will include updated staff macroeconomic projections, which could shape the tone of policy communication going forward. The overwhelming market expectation is for no change at the December meeting, but the outcome and accompanying communication will set the stage for February 2026.

Sources:
- ECB Economic Bulletin Issue 7, 2025: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/economic-bulletin/html/eb202507.en.html
- ECB accounts show no hurry to cut rates (Market Screener, Nov 27, 2025): https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/ECB-accounts-show-no-hurry-to-cut-rates-debate-on-declaring-end-of-easing--49246891/
- Money markets point to ECB rate hikes (Cryptopolitan, Dec 10, 2025): https://www.cryptopolitan.com/money-markets-point-to-ecb-rate-hikes/
- ECB Preview: Driving Home For Christmas (TalkMarkets, Dec 11, 2025): https://www.talkmarkets.com/content/economics--politics/ecb-preview-driving-home-for-christmas?post=641234
- ECB Rate Hike Probability Increases (GuruFocus, Dec 10, 2025): https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2789381/european-central-bank-rate-hike-probability-increases-amid-hawki
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the ECB announces no change to the deposit facility rate at its December 18, 2025, monetary policy meeting, meaning the rate remains at 2.00%. This question resolves No if the ECB changes the deposit facility rate (either up or down) at that meeting. The resolution window is between 2025-12-13 and 2025-12-31. Resolution is based on the official ECB interest rate decision published on or after December 18, 2025, as available at: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html and the ECB press release following the Governing Council meeting listed at: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html. If no decision is published by December 31, 2025, the question resolves Yes (as no change would have been announced).
subquestions.rationale: The December 2025 ECB meeting is the last policy meeting before the February 2026 meeting. If the ECB holds rates in December (as widely expected), it would strongly signal continuity and increase the probability that rates remain unchanged in February as well—particularly since the ECB has emphasized a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach and officials have described the current rate as being in a 'good place.' However, if the ECB were to unexpectedly change rates in December, it would indicate a shift in the policy trajectory that would significantly alter expectations for February. Additionally, the December meeting includes new staff projections and updated risk assessments that will frame the policy debate heading into February. This makes the December decision a high-value early indicator for the February outcome.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire cancelled by December 31?
description:
On October 9, Israel and Hamas signed a deal implementing a ceasefire: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a either Israel or Hamas announce the cancellation of the ongoing ceasefire, or if a consensus of credible reporting confirms that the ceasefire is no longer in effect, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements that one side or another violated the ongoing ceasefire will not be enough to resolve this market to "Yes"; only a definitive announcement by Israel or Hamas, or otherwise a wide consensus of credible reporting that that the ceasefire has been ended, will qualify to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary solution resolution source will be official information from Hamas or the government of Israel, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will all 20 living Israeli hostages held by Hamas be released by October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Under the ceasefire deal signed on October 9, 2025, Hamas committed to releasing all 20 surviving Israeli hostages within 72 hours of the ceasefire taking effect. The ceasefire was approved by the Israeli cabinet on October 10, with the 72-hour window reportedly ending around noon local time on Monday, October 13. As of October 11, no hostages have yet been confirmed released under this deal. The successful release of all living hostages is a core element of Phase 1 of the agreement, and failure to complete this exchange would be a major trigger for Israel to declare the ceasefire void. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has described the hostage return as a 'moral victory,' while Hamas negotiator Khalil al-Hayya stated the group received guarantees the war has ended. However, past hostage negotiations (such as the January 2024 temporary truce) have been fraught with delays and complications. If the hostage release process stalls or breaks down, this would be a strong leading indicator that the ceasefire could collapse before December 31, 2025.

Sources:
- Reuters: Israel-Hamas ceasefire deal, https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/
- Yahoo News: What has to happen next, https://www.yahoo.com/news/israel-hamas-ceasefire-happen-next-end-war-gaza
- ArcaMax: Israel says Gaza ceasefire in effect, https://www.arcamax.com/currentnews/newsheadlines/s-3158291
- The Express Tribune: Fragile peace dawns over Gaza, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2526830/fragile-peace-dawns-over-gaza
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if all 20 living Israeli hostages (as identified by the Israeli government at the time of the ceasefire) are confirmed released from Hamas custody and transferred to Israeli or international (e.g., Red Cross) control between 2025-10-11 and 2025-10-20 (inclusive). It resolves No if, by 11:59 PM UTC on October 20, 2025, one or more of the 20 living hostages have not been confirmed released. Resolution will be based on official statements from the Israeli government (e.g., the Prime Minister's Office or Israeli Defense Forces) or confirmed reporting by at least two major international news agencies (Reuters, AP, AFP). If the number of living hostages is revised downward by the Israeli government before the deadline (e.g., due to confirmed deaths), the question applies to the revised number of living hostages. If the ceasefire is cancelled before October 20 and the hostage release is halted, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The hostage release is the most critical near-term deliverable of the ceasefire agreement. A failure or significant delay in releasing all 20 living hostages would be the single strongest early indicator that the ceasefire could unravel, as Israel has repeatedly stated that the return of hostages is non-negotiable. Conversely, a successful and timely release would significantly reduce the likelihood of ceasefire cancellation by year-end, as it would demonstrate both sides' commitment to the deal and remove one of Israel's primary justifications for resuming military operations. This is a different observable event from the ceasefire itself — it tracks whether a key obligation under the deal is being fulfilled, which is a leading indicator of the deal's durability.

question: Pedro Sánchez out as PM of Spain in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Spain's Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, is removed from power for any length of time between May 28 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation, is dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Prime Minister of Spain within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Spain's 2026 General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) fail to pass an initial congressional vote or be formally withdrawn by the government between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pedro Sánchez leads a fragile minority coalition government that has been unable to pass a budget for two consecutive years, rolling over prior budgets instead. In a September 2, 2025 interview, Sánchez stated he would present a budget and 'fight to get it approved,' while rejecting the idea of resigning if the budget fails (https://www.nzherald.co.nz). Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has urged Sánchez to resign if he cannot secure budget approval. The government's coalition depends on support from a patchwork of smaller parties — including Catalan, Basque, and left-wing groups — making any legislative achievement difficult. Sánchez's Socialists trail the Popular Party significantly in polls (27% vs. 34.4%), and the accumulation of corruption scandals involving his wife, brother, and former aides has further weakened his negotiating position. A budget failure would be a major blow to the government's viability and could intensify calls for snap elections or a resignation. The Spanish government typically presents its budget draft to Congress in the autumn, and early October is a critical window for determining whether a budget vote will proceed or whether the government abandons the effort.

Sources:
- NZ Herald, 'Spanish PM accuses judges of doing politics in graft cases' (2025-09-02): https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/spanish-pm-accuses-judges-of-doing-politics-in-graft-cases/
- AP NEWS, 'Spain's PM refuses to step down and announces anti-graft plan despite corruption inquiries' (2025-07-09): https://apnews.com/article/spain-sanchez-corruption-anti-graft-plan
- Euronews, 'Spain's PM apologises after top aide implicated in corruption scandal' (2025-06-12): https://www.euronews.com/2025/06/12/spains-pm-apologises-after-top-aide-implicated-in-corruption-scandal
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), either: (1) the Spanish government's 2026 General State Budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) is voted down in Spain's Congress of Deputies at any stage (e.g., a vote on the totality or 'enmienda a la totalidad'), OR (2) the Spanish government formally announces it will not present or has withdrawn its 2026 budget proposal. Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Spanish government (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/), the Spanish Congress of Deputies (https://www.congreso.es/), or a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as El País (https://elpais.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), and AP News (https://apnews.com/). If no budget vote occurs and the government has not formally announced withdrawal or non-presentation of the budget during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The budget is the single most important legislative test for Sánchez's minority government. A failure to pass or even present a budget would signal that Sánchez has lost the support of the coalition partners he needs to govern, dramatically increasing the probability of a confidence crisis, snap elections, or resignation before year-end. Conversely, if Sánchez manages to advance a budget, it would indicate his coalition is still functional and reduce the likelihood of him leaving power in 2025. Two forecasters who disagree on whether Sánchez will be out as PM in 2025 would likely update significantly upon learning the fate of the budget effort in October.

subquestions.question: Will Scott Bessent complete second-round interviews with Fed Chair finalists and present a shortlist to Trump before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 27-28, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed aboard Air Force One that the administration has narrowed the Federal Reserve Chair search to five finalists: current Fed Governors Christopher Waller and Michelle Bowman, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett, former Fed Governor Kevin Warsh, and BlackRock executive Rick Rieder. Bessent stated he plans to conduct one more round of interviews and present a 'good slate' to President Trump 'right after Thanksgiving' (Thanksgiving 2025 falls on November 27). Bessent said: 'We're down to five... we hope to present a good slate to the president right after Thanksgiving.... It will ultimately be his choice.' Trump confirmed he expects to name a replacement by year's end. The timing of Bessent's shortlist presentation is a key gating event — it determines whether Trump can announce a pick in December 2025 or whether the process slips into 2026. The composition of that final slate (and whether Waller is prominently featured or has fallen out of favor) would provide strong signal about the likelihood of Waller being the ultimate pick.

Sources:
- Anadolu Agency, October 28, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-treasury-chief-bessent-lists-5-finalists-for-next-fed-chair-as-trump-to-decide-before-years-end/3400052

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), credible news reports confirm that Scott Bessent has (a) completed a second round of interviews or evaluations with Fed Chair candidates AND (b) presented or delivered a final shortlist or recommendation slate to President Trump. Resolution sources include official statements from the White House, Treasury Department, or Bessent himself, as well as credible reporting from outlets such as Fox Business (https://www.foxbusiness.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), or the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com). The question resolves No if, by November 30, 2025, there is no credible reporting that both conditions (a) and (b) have been met. If reporting is ambiguous about whether a formal presentation has occurred (e.g., Bessent says he is 'almost done' but hasn't yet presented to Trump), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Bessent explicitly stated he plans to present finalists to Trump 'right after Thanksgiving' (November 27, 2025). Whether this milestone is met on schedule is a critical gating indicator for whether Trump will announce any Fed Chair pick — including Waller — by year-end 2025. If the process stalls or is delayed past November, it significantly reduces the probability of a December announcement. Conversely, if Bessent delivers the slate on time, it makes a year-end announcement much more likely. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks a process milestone (Bessent's shortlist delivery) rather than Trump's final decision, and it provides signal about the pace and seriousness of the selection process. Forecasters who disagree on whether Trump will pick Waller specifically may update based on whether the process is proceeding on the announced timeline, since delays would change the dynamics of who ultimately gets chosen.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Apple announce a $799 or higher starting price for the base iPhone 17 model at its September 9, 2025 event?

However, some rumors suggest the base iPhone 17 could start at $799 (matching the iPhone 16's price) with 128GB storage, while other sources indicate the price could rise to $849 if Apple bumps the base storage to 256GB. Notably, CNET's roundup of rumors from August 28, 2025 states: 'Analysts predict a $50 price increase across the lineup, potentially raising the base model to $799 from $749.' This is somewhat confusing, as different sources cite different iPhone 16 base prices ($749 vs $799), likely reflecting regional or configuration differences. In the US, the iPhone 16 base model (128GB) launched at $799. The key question is whether Apple will price the standard iPhone 17 above this $799 threshold.

The ultimate question resolves Yes if the iPhone 17 base model is priced higher than $799 (i.e., $800 or more). The September 9 event will be the first official confirmation of pricing.

Sources:
- CNET, "Full iPhone 17 Lineup Specs: Comparing the Latest Rumored Info" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/full-iphone-17-lineup-specs-comparing-the-latest-rumored-info/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10, Apple officially announces or reveals (at its September 9 event or through its official website/press materials) that the base model iPhone 17 (standard edition, lowest storage configuration, US pricing) has a starting price strictly greater than $799 USD (i.e., $800 or more). This question resolves No if: (a) Apple announces a base iPhone 17 price of $799 or less; or (b) Apple does not announce iPhone 17 pricing by 2025-09-10. If Apple announces a price above $799 at this event, the ultimate question will almost certainly resolve Yes (barring an unprecedented price change between announcement and retail availability). If the announced price is $799 or below, the ultimate question resolves No. This subquestion captures the key information-revealing event (the announcement) a few days before the ultimate resolution date, and is directly informative: two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely disagree on what Apple will announce on September 9.

question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt surpasses 38 trillion dollars at any point before December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. national debt exceed $37.5 trillion as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025, according to Treasury Department data. At the time, the debt was growing at roughly $1 trillion every five months — or approximately $6–7 billion per day. As of late September 2025, the debt was already well above $37 trillion and climbing steadily. The Congressional Budget Office estimated a roughly $1.8 trillion deficit for fiscal year 2025 (ending September 30, 2025), with outlays running about 6% higher year-over-year. The fiscal year 2025 deficit, combined with ongoing mandatory spending on Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, and surging net interest payments, continues to push debt higher. If the debt is near or above $37.5 trillion by early October, it would suggest the debt is on a trajectory to reach $38 trillion before the end of 2025 — the threshold in the ultimate question. Conversely, if the debt is significantly below $37.5 trillion, it would indicate a slower pace of accumulation that might make $38 trillion by late October less certain.

Sources:
- U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny: https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/debt-to-the-penny/debt-to-the-penny
- AP News, "US national debt reaches a record $37 trillion" (August 2025): https://apnews.com/article/national-debt-37-trillion-government-spending-a7cf0dce6a2cc9d5b91d36ec4bf9ab9d
- Fortune, "National debt hits a record $37 trillion" (August 2025): https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/national-debt-record-37-trillion/
- CBO, September 2025 Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/publication/61534
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 15, 2025 (inclusive), the total public debt outstanding of the United States as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department exceeds $37,500,000,000,000 (thirty-seven trillion five hundred billion dollars). The primary data source is the Treasury's 'Debt to the Penny' dataset available at https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/debt-to-the-penny/debt-to-the-penny or via the TreasuryDirect API at https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current. If both sources are unavailable, any official U.S. Treasury Department statement or press release confirming the total debt level may be used. The question resolves No if the total public debt outstanding does not exceed $37.5 trillion on any reporting day within the resolution window. Note: The relevant figure is 'Total Public Debt Outstanding,' which includes both debt held by the public and intragovernmental holdings.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion serves as a near-term indicator of the pace of U.S. debt accumulation. If the debt has already crossed $37.5 trillion by mid-October, it would need to grow by only $500 billion more to reach $38 trillion — a pace consistent with or even slower than recent trends, making the ultimate question's $38 trillion threshold very likely to be met. If the debt has not yet reached $37.5 trillion, it would signal an unexpectedly slow rate of borrowing that would make the $38 trillion target less certain. This question measures a different, earlier milestone ($37.5T vs. $38T) and thus is a genuine leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.
