subquestions.question: Will the United States and Russia announce a formal agreement to extend or replace the New START nuclear arms treaty between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11?
subquestions.background_information:
One of the six trigger conditions that would cause the ultimate 'Nothing Ever Happens: Military Edition' market to resolve 'No' is a 'US-Russia nuclear deal.' As of November 2025, the 2010 New START treaty — which limits each country to 1,550 deployed strategic nuclear warheads and 700 deployed missiles and bombers — remains in a precarious state. Russia suspended its participation in the treaty in February 2023, though it has continued to observe its central limits. In October 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed hope for extending New START for another year, and Trump responded that a treaty extension 'sounds like a good idea to me.' Putin warned that if the U.S. declines to extend, Russia will continue strengthening its nuclear arsenal, leaving the world's two largest nuclear powers without any formal arms control framework. Despite positive rhetoric, no formal agreement has been reached. Trump and Putin have held summits (including in Anchorage) and phone calls, and a meeting in Budapest is reportedly being planned. Any formal announcement of a nuclear arms deal between the US and Russia before end of 2025 would trigger the ultimate market's 'No' resolution.

Sources:
- PBS: Putin praises Trump's peace efforts, despite failure to win Nobel prize (2025-10-10): https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/putin-praises-trumps-peace-efforts-despite-failure-to-win-nobel-prize
- Devdiscourse: Trump hosts Zelenskyy at White House following call with Putin (2025-10-17): https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3258619-latest-trump-hosts-zelenskyy-at-white-house-following-call-with-putin
- Face2Face Africa: Putin lauds Trump's peace push as Nobel Prize goes to Venezuelan activist (2025-10-10): https://face2faceafrica.com/article/putin-lauds-trumps-peace-push-as-nobel-prize-goes-to-venezuelan-activist
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 (inclusive), the United States and Russia jointly announce or sign a formal bilateral agreement on nuclear arms control — including but not limited to an extension, renewal, or replacement of the New START treaty, or a new standalone nuclear weapons limitation agreement. The announcement must come from official government sources of both nations (e.g., statements from the White House, U.S. State Department, Kremlin, or Russian Foreign Ministry) and must describe a binding or politically binding commitment, not merely an expression of intent or willingness to negotiate. A joint statement expressing desire to continue talks, without a concrete agreement on terms, does not count. Resolution will be determined by checking official White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov), U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov), and Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru) press releases and statements, as well as major international news sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com). If no such announcement is made by 2025-12-11 at 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A US-Russia nuclear deal is one of the six specific trigger events that would cause the ultimate market to resolve 'No.' Tracking whether such a deal materializes in the near term is a direct early indicator. While both Trump and Putin have expressed positive rhetoric about extending New START, no formal agreement has been reached. If a deal is announced in this window, it would definitively flip the ultimate market to 'No.' Even a near-miss (e.g., a scheduled summit or advanced negotiations) would update forecasters' estimates on whether such a deal could materialize before the December 31, 2025 deadline. The current diplomatic momentum — with planned meetings in Budapest and ongoing discussions — makes this a plausible but far-from-certain outcome, placing forecasts in an informative range rather than near 0% or 100%.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NATO invoke Article 5 (collective defense) in response to a Russian military action between September 24 and October 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 10, 2025, up to 19 Russian drones violated Polish airspace during a massive Russian strike on Ukraine. Polish, Dutch, and Italian fighter jets shot down at least three drones, marking the first time NATO forces directly engaged Russian military assets since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Poland invoked Article 4 of the NATO treaty (consultation), but stopped short of invoking Article 5 (collective defense). Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident brought Europe 'closer to open conflict since World War II,' and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said indications suggest the incursion was intentional. NATO subsequently launched 'Operation Eastern Sentry,' increasing air patrols and deploying ground-based interceptor systems along the alliance's eastern flank. Russia's Zapad-2025 military exercises with Belarus, involving 20,000 troops and advanced weapons systems including Iskander ballistic missiles, ran concurrently. NATO fighter jets also intercepted Russian Su-30 combat aircraft carrying Kh-31 supersonic anti-radar missiles over the Baltic Sea on September 17, 2025. The distinction between Article 4 (consultation) and Article 5 (collective defense, which treats an attack on one member as an attack on all) is crucial: invoking Article 5 would represent a dramatic escalation and would likely precede or accompany a direct NATO-Russia military clash. As of September 24, 2025, Article 5 has not been invoked.

Sources:
- AP News, 'Poland says it shot down Russian drones that violated its airspace during bombardment of Ukraine' (2025-09-10): https://apnews.com/article/poland-russia-drones-airspace-violation
- AP News, 'NATO scrambles jets to shoot down Russian drones in Poland' (2025-09-10): https://apnews.com/article/nato-russia-drones-poland-airspace
- ECFR, 'Hold the line: NATO cannot allow airspace violations to go unchallenged' (2025-09-11): https://ecfr.eu/article/hold-the-line-nato-cannot-allow-airspace-violations-to-go-unchallenged/
- The Mirror, 'NATO scrambles fighter jets to face Russian planes carrying supersonic missiles' (2025-09-17): https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/nato-scrambles-fighter-jets-face-34057891
- The Boston Globe, 'A Polish soldier, an unusual radar dot, and then NATO jets' (2025-09-20): https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/09/20/world/poland-nato-russian-drones/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NATO officially invokes Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty between September 24, 2025 and October 24, 2025 (inclusive). The invocation must be confirmed by an official NATO statement published on nato.int or by a formal communiqué from the North Atlantic Council. Informal references to Article 5 by individual member states, or invocations of Article 4 (consultation), do not qualify. If NATO's official website (https://www.nato.int) is unavailable, resolution may rely on official NATO social media accounts or statements reported by at least two major international wire services (AP, Reuters, AFP). If the invocation is announced but takes effect after October 24, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: An Article 5 invocation would be the clearest institutional precursor to a full NATO-Russia military clash. The September 10 drone incursion into Poland already resulted in NATO forces shooting down Russian drones — but Poland invoked only Article 4 (consultation), not Article 5. Forecasters who believe a NATO-Russia military clash is likely in 2025 would generally assign higher probability to Article 5 being invoked, since Article 5 is the formal mechanism by which NATO would collectively respond to a Russian attack on a member state. Conversely, forecasters who believe the situation will be managed through deterrence and de-escalation would assign low probability to Article 5. This question tracks whether the current escalation spiral — drone incursions, armed interceptions, and military exercises — crosses the threshold from incident management to collective defense posture, which is a strong leading indicator of whether a broader military clash occurs before year-end.

question: Will the EU impose new tariffs on US goods in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union imposes any new or increased tariffs on the United States between July 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

Only tariffs specifically targeting the U.S. will qualify. For example, a global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the EU) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs enacted by EU member states will not count. Only Tariffs imposed by the EU will qualify.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission formally propose or adopt countermeasures (retaliatory tariffs) specifically targeting U.S. goods between October 31, 2025 and November 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The EU and the U.S. reached a framework trade deal in July-August 2025 under which the U.S. imposes a 15% tariff on most EU goods and 27.5% on EU automobiles. The EU agreed to eliminate tariffs on U.S. industrial goods and provide preferential access for U.S. agricultural and seafood products (https://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-u-s-e-u-tariff-deal-is-now-on-paper-and-it-includes-lng-and-ai-chip-purchases-9fba0fa6). However, tensions remain. The U.S. continues to hold elevated tariffs on EU cars as leverage until the EU legislates its promised tariff reductions (https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-dropped/). Meanwhile, the EU has signaled willingness to act independently on trade — for example, proposing a 50% tariff on steel imports exceeding reduced quotas (https://www.bruegel.org/analysis/eu-should-moderate-its-steel-protection-plan), though that measure is framed as a global safeguard rather than a U.S.-specific tariff. EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic has emphasized that EU trade measures must comply with WTO guidelines and require consensus among 27 member states plus European Parliament approval (https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WS67100e6fa310f1265a1d57aa.html). As of late October 2025, the EU has not enacted retaliatory tariffs specifically targeting U.S. goods, though the EU retains a pre-existing legal framework for countermeasures (dating back to the 2018 steel dispute) and has previously adopted rebalancing tariffs on U.S. goods such as bourbon, motorcycles, and jeans.

Sources:
- MarketWatch (2025-08-21): https://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-u-s-e-u-tariff-deal-is-now-on-paper-and-it-includes-lng-and-ai-chip-purchases-9fba0fa6
- New York Post (2025-08-21): https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-dropped/
- Bruegel (2025-10-09): https://www.bruegel.org/analysis/eu-should-moderate-its-steel-protection-plan
- China Daily (2025-10-16): https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WS67100e6fa310f1265a1d57aa.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 29, 2025 (inclusive), the European Commission publishes a formal proposal, or the Council of the European Union adopts a regulation, imposing new or increased tariffs (countermeasures, rebalancing duties, or retaliatory tariffs) that specifically target goods originating from the United States. The measure must explicitly single out U.S.-origin goods; global safeguard measures that apply to all countries equally (such as the proposed steel safeguard) do not count. Resolution will be based on official publications in the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html), European Commission press releases (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en), or a consensus of at least two credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Financial Times, Bloomberg). If no such proposal or adoption occurs during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the EU will impose new tariffs on U.S. goods by the end of 2025. The existence of a formal Commission proposal or Council adoption of U.S.-specific countermeasures during November 2025 would be the most direct leading indicator that such tariffs will be enacted by December 2025. The July-August framework deal reduced immediate tensions, but the deal's implementation depends on both sides following through — the U.S. is withholding auto tariff relief as leverage, and any breakdown in negotiations could trigger EU retaliation. Tracking whether the Commission moves toward formal countermeasures in November provides a strong early signal of the ultimate outcome, since EU legislative processes require formal proposals before enactment. If no such proposal emerges by late November, it becomes much less likely the EU would impose U.S.-specific tariffs by December 2, 2025.

question: Karen Bass out as Mayor of LA in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Karen Bass is no longer serving as Mayor of Los Angeles for any length of time between January 13 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Karen Bass's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

This market's resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Los Angeles City Council initiate a formal motion or hearing related to removing, censuring, or recalling Mayor Karen Bass between September 1 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Karen Bass has faced mounting political pressure throughout 2025. Her approval ratings dropped significantly following her handling of the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, with a UCLA Luskin School Quality of Life Index survey showing a net favorability rating of negative 12 (The Hill, June 2025). She has also faced criticism over her management of a nearly $1 billion budget shortfall, which led to over 1,600 proposed layoffs (CBS News, May 2025). Additional crises have included immigration protests and the deployment of National Guard troops to Los Angeles (The Hill, June 2025). While no formal recall or removal effort has been initiated as of September 1, 2025, political opponents and critics have intensified scrutiny. Under the Los Angeles City Charter (Section 200), the City Council has certain oversight powers, and recall efforts require petition signatures from 15% of registered voters. A formal Council motion targeting Bass's position would be a significant escalation and a strong early indicator that she could leave office before the end of 2025.

Sources:
- The Hill, 'Karen Bass thrust back into hot seat amid LA unrest' (June 12, 2025): https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/4754321-karen-bass-la-unrest/
- CBS News, 'Mayor Bass says she'll take a pay cut as city's budget concerns continue' (May 5, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/mayor-bass-says-shell-take-a-pay-cut-as-citys-budget-concerns-continue/
- Los Angeles City Charter, Section 200 et seq.: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-68898
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), the Los Angeles City Council introduces a formal motion, resolution, or scheduled committee hearing that specifically addresses the removal, censure, or recall of Mayor Karen Bass. Evidence must come from official City Council records (available at https://cityclerk.lacity.org/lacityclerkconnect/) or credible news reporting from outlets such as the Los Angeles Times (https://www.latimes.com/), ABC7 Los Angeles (https://abc7.com/), or CBS News Los Angeles (https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/). Informal public statements by individual Council members calling for resignation, without a formal motion or hearing, do not count. If no such formal action is introduced during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal City Council action targeting Bass's position would be one of the strongest near-term indicators that she could leave office before the end of 2025. While Bass could resign voluntarily or face a recall petition, Council-level action is an observable institutional signal that political dynamics have shifted decisively against her. The absence of such action would suggest that, despite low approval ratings and political criticism, the institutional status quo is holding and Bass is likely to remain in office through year-end.

question: Will US or Israel strike Iran by December 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US or Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US or Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US or Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US or Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran's Supreme Leader or senior Iranian military officials publicly threaten imminent retaliation against the US or Israel in response to a specific provocation between January 20 and February 15, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-January 2026, tensions between Iran, the US, and Israel remain extremely high following the June 2025 military exchanges. In June 2025, Israel conducted airstrikes on Iran killing high-ranking military officials and nuclear scientists, Iran retaliated with Operation True Promise III (hundreds of ballistic missiles and drones targeting Tel Aviv), the US struck three Iranian nuclear facilities on June 22, Iran struck a US base in Qatar on June 23, and a ceasefire was brokered on June 24, 2025 (https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3963684.html). Since then, Iran has conducted military exercises in the Gulf firing ballistic and cruise missiles at simulated targets in December 2025 (https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets). Iran is experiencing its most severe nationwide protests in decades, with nearly 2,600 reported deaths since late December 2025, and President Trump has warned Tehran of 'very strong action' if protesters are executed. Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf has stated that US forces, bases, and Israeli targets would be 'legitimate military objectives' if Washington conducts strikes (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-bases-in-the-line-of-iranian-firepower/articleshow/117229744.cms). Reports indicate the US has been preparing advanced strike capabilities including the GBU-57 bunker buster and stealth bomber platforms for potential 2026 operations (https://www.news18.com/world/missiles-that-think-bombs-that-dig-the-weapons-that-could-define-trumps-next-iran-decision-ws-9196157.html). Explicit public threats from Iran's top leadership citing a specific provocation (such as US support for protesters, new sanctions, or military posturing) would be an important escalation indicator preceding a potential US or Israeli strike.

Sources:
- Trend News Agency: https://en.trend.az/iran/politics/3963684.html
- The Straits Times (Dec 2025): https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
- Economic Times (Jan 2025): https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-bases-in-the-line-of-iranian-firepower/articleshow/117229744.cms
- News18 (Jan 2026): https://www.news18.com/world/missiles-that-think-bombs-that-dig-the-weapons-that-could-define-trumps-next-iran-decision-ws-9196157.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-15, Iran's Supreme Leader (Ali Khamenei), the President of Iran, the Commander of the IRGC, or the Speaker of the Iranian Parliament makes a public statement — reported by at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, Al Jazeera) — explicitly threatening imminent military retaliation or preemptive military action against the United States or Israel in response to a specific, named provocation (such as a specific military deployment, sanctions action, diplomatic action regarding protesters, or territorial incursion). The threat must reference a concrete recent event or action as its trigger, not merely restate long-standing general hostility. General statements of deterrence or reaffirmations of existing policy (e.g., 'we will respond if attacked') do not qualify; the statement must indicate a new, escalated threat tied to a specific provocation occurring on or after January 20, 2026. Resolution sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com). If no qualifying statement is reported by these outlets by 2026-02-15 23:59 UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A specific, escalatory public threat from Iran's top leadership tied to a new provocation is a strong leading indicator of an imminent US or Israeli strike. Historically, the June 2025 exchange was preceded by escalating rhetoric and specific threats. If Iran's leadership issues new specific threats in this period, it signals either that a provocation has already occurred that could trigger strikes, or that the cycle of escalation is intensifying toward military conflict. Conversely, if rhetoric remains at baseline levels, it suggests the ceasefire is holding and a near-term strike is less likely. This is a meaningful crux because forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely diverge on whether the current protest crisis and US posturing will escalate into a new military confrontation — and new specific threats from Iranian leadership would be among the earliest observable indicators of that escalation.

question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:
Proposition 50 is a 2025 legislatively referred constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting, proposed for the statewide special election in California currently set for November 4, 2025.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If by the last legally operative deadline for placing measures on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot—including any deadline set or modified by the statute calling that special election—no qualifying legislatively referred measure has been approved for submission to voters, and there is no enacted statute or pending court order that could still place such a measure on that ballot, the market will resolve “No”.

If the election is officially rescheduled, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines.

The resolution source will be based on the official certified results of the vote as published by  State of California. Subsequent litigation, administrative challenges, or failure of any post-approval triggers will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will a major organized 'No on Proposition 50' campaign committee report raising at least $10 million in total contributions by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Proposition 50 is a legislatively referred constitutional amendment on the November 4, 2025 California special election ballot. It would temporarily allow the state legislature to redraw congressional district maps, bypassing the independent Citizens Redistricting Commission for the 2026, 2028, and 2030 elections. A Berkeley IGS poll from August 11-17, 2025 found 48% support, 32% opposition, and 20% undecided among registered voters (https://medium.com/@bfriedmandc/the-california-redistricting-proposition-50-has-a-very-high-probability-of-passing-d2b5d9ec0cb4). A separate Politico-Citrin Center poll found only 36% of California voters support returning redistricting authority to the legislature versus 64% who favor the independent commission (https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5062670-california-redistricting-special-election/). The opposition includes former Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger, the League of Women Voters, and the California Republican Party. Republicans have filed multiple legal challenges, all denied by the California Supreme Court (https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/). National Republican groups and the Trump administration have also signaled opposition (https://abc7news.com/post/trump-california-republicans-move-block-newsoms-redistricting-ballot-measure/16183052/). Whether the opposition can mount a well-funded campaign is a key indicator of whether Prop 50 could be defeated. California ballot measure campaigns routinely spend tens of millions of dollars. Campaign finance filings are publicly available through the California Secretary of State's Cal-Access system.

Sources:
- Berkeley IGS Poll analysis: https://medium.com/@bfriedmandc/the-california-redistricting-proposition-50-has-a-very-high-probability-of-passing-d2b5d9ec0cb4
- The Hill on 5 things to know: https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/5062670-california-redistricting-special-election/
- Court House News on Supreme Court denial: https://www.courthousenews.com/california-high-court-denies-second-republican-attempt-to-halt-special-redistricting-election/
- ABC7 on Trump/GOP opposition: https://abc7news.com/post/trump-california-republicans-move-block-newsoms-redistricting-ballot-measure/16183052/
- Cal-Access campaign finance database: https://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), any committee registered with the California Secretary of State that is primarily organized to oppose Proposition 50 (the November 4, 2025 redistricting constitutional amendment) reports cumulative total contributions received of at least $10 million, as reflected in filings available through the California Secretary of State's Cal-Access system (https://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/) or the California Fair Political Practices Commission (https://www.fppc.ca.gov/). The committee's name or stated purpose must clearly indicate opposition to Proposition 50 or the redistricting ballot measure. If multiple opposition committees exist, their totals are NOT combined — at least one single committee must meet the $10 million threshold. If Cal-Access data is unavailable, credible news reports citing official filings may be used as a fallback. If no qualifying opposition committee has been registered by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The level of funding behind the 'No on Prop 50' campaign is a critical early indicator of whether Proposition 50 will pass. Despite initial polling showing majority support among decided voters, the Politico-Citrin poll showed 64% of voters prefer the independent commission — suggesting the 'No' side has a persuasion opportunity if it can fund a major campaign. With 20% of voters undecided in August polling, a well-funded opposition campaign ($10M+ by end of September) could significantly shift voter opinion during October. Conversely, if the opposition fails to raise substantial funds, it signals that organized resistance is weak and the measure is very likely to pass. This fundraising threshold is observable well before the election and provides a meaningful signal about the ultimate outcome that goes beyond simply restating the election question.

question: Will Ukraine agree to give up Russian territory in Kursk?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control in Russia’s Kursk Oblast is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. If Russia regains territory in the Kursk Oblast through military action, or if Ukraine unilaterally cedes Russian territory absent of a diplomatic process or agreement, this will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia hold a new formal round of direct peace negotiations between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, direct peace talks between Russia and Ukraine have stalled. The third round of direct negotiations took place on July 23, 2025, in Istanbul, where Russia proposed establishing three online working groups on political, military, and humanitarian issues. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin stated on October 9, 2025, that the 'positive momentum' from the July Alaska summit between Putin and Trump was 'dying out' due to what Russia characterizes as Ukraine's lack of serious commitment. Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky said the decision on a fourth round of negotiations would be made after implementation of agreements from the third round (TASS, October 9, 2025: https://tass.com/). Meanwhile, the U.S. has been pushing Ukraine toward territorial concessions—Steve Witkoff reportedly urged Zelensky to surrender the entire Donetsk region (RedState, October 19, 2025: https://redstate.com/nick-arama/2025/10/19/trumps-top-negotiator-to-ukraine-give-up-the-donetsk-region-n2186540). Zelensky reversed his earlier openness to ceding Russian-occupied territory, stating in September 2025: 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia' (InfoWars, September 26, 2025). The Kursk incursion territory remains a key bargaining chip, and any deal involving Kursk would require active negotiations to be underway. Currently, no fourth round of direct talks has been scheduled.

Sources:
- TASS, October 9, 2025: https://tass.com/politics/1878901
- RedState, October 19, 2025: https://redstate.com/nick-arama/2025/10/19/trumps-top-negotiator-to-ukraine-give-up-the-donetsk-region-n2186540
- InfoWars, September 26, 2025: https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/
- Euractiv, August 10, 2025: https://www.euractiv.com/section/defence-and-security/news/europes-top-leaders-tell-trump-not-to-sell-out-ukraine-at-alaska-summit-with-putin/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia hold a new formal round of direct bilateral peace negotiations (i.e., a fourth round or any subsequent round following the July 23, 2025, Istanbul talks). The negotiations must involve official delegations from both Ukraine and Russia meeting in person (not merely online working group sessions, prisoner exchange logistics, or back-channel communications). Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Ukrainian or Russian governments, or an overwhelming consensus of credible international media sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), or TASS (https://tass.com/). If no such meeting takes place by November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to agree to give up Kursk territory as part of a diplomatic deal by December 31, 2025, active direct negotiations between Ukraine and Russia would need to be underway in the near term. The talks have been stalled since July 2025, and whether a new round of formal negotiations occurs in November would be a strong leading indicator of whether any deal—including one involving Kursk—is achievable by year-end. If no negotiations resume, the probability of a Kursk deal by December 31 drops substantially. Conversely, the resumption of talks would signal momentum toward a broader agreement that could include Kursk territory provisions.

question: Will Polymarket mindshare hit 80%?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Polymarket has at least the specified daily mindshare, as shown on the Kaito Information Markets Arena page (https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets) at any point between November 20, 2025, and March 31, 2026 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only finalized daily results from the Polymarket mindshare percentage shown on the Kaito Info Markets page at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets, specifically the daily values for Polymarket under 'Historical Data', will be used to resolve this market. Values will be considered final once the value for the subsequent day has been released.

The resolution source for this market is the Kaito Info Markets page found at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets. If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the Kaito Info Markets page comes back online and resolve based on the first check after it becomes available. If it becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve based on the latest available data.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the Kaito Info Markets page (https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets), which reports the platform’s mindshare as a percentage to two decimal places (e.g., 66.56%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will Polymarket's daily mindshare on Kaito exceed 72% on any day between December 21, 2025 and January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Polymarket is the leading decentralized prediction market platform, and its 'mindshare' — a metric tracking the share of social/media attention it commands relative to other information/prediction market platforms — is tracked by Kaito on its Information Markets Arena page (https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets). The ultimate question asks whether Polymarket's daily mindshare will reach 80% at any point before March 31, 2026. As of late 2025, Polymarket's mindshare has fluctuated but has been reported in the range of roughly 60–70%, with spikes during high-profile events such as elections or major news-driven markets. The platform has seen enormous growth in 2025: trading volume exceeded $3 billion in October 2025, daily active users grew from ~20,000 to ~58,000, and the platform secured CFTC approval for a regulated U.S. return in November 2025 (https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/polymarket-secures-cftc-approval-for-regulated-u-s-return). The U.S. app launched via waitlist in December 2025 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/polymarket-starts-reopening-us-site-waitlist-members-210000123.html), which could drive further attention. A 72% threshold represents a meaningful step toward the 80% target — if mindshare reaches 72% in the near term, it signals that the platform is on a trajectory where 80% is plausible by March 2026. Conversely, if mindshare remains well below 72%, reaching 80% becomes less likely.

Sources:
- Kaito Info Markets Arena: https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets
- Polymarket CFTC approval: https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/polymarket-secures-cftc-approval-for-regulated-u-s-return
- Polymarket U.S. waitlist launch: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/polymarket-starts-reopening-us-site-waitlist-members-210000123.html
- Polymarket mindshare and ZK data: https://www.okx.com/learn/polymarket-mindshare-data-zk-verifiable-insights
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on any day between December 21, 2025, and January 20, 2026 (inclusive), the finalized daily Polymarket mindshare percentage shown on the Kaito Info Markets page at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets equals or exceeds 72.00%. A daily value is considered finalized once the value for the subsequent day has been released on the same page. The value is read to two decimal places as reported by Kaito (e.g., 72.00% or higher qualifies). If the Kaito Info Markets page is temporarily unavailable, resolution will be based on the first available check after it returns. If the page becomes permanently unavailable before all days in the window can be checked, the question resolves based on the latest available data — Yes if any finalized day in the window showed ≥72.00%, otherwise No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion asks whether Polymarket's mindshare reaches 72% in the near term, which is a meaningful leading indicator for whether it can eventually hit 80%. The 72% threshold is a distinct intermediate milestone — not simply a restatement of the ultimate question with an earlier date or tighter threshold. If Polymarket's mindshare is already approaching 72% during this period (perhaps driven by the U.S. app rollout, new sports markets, or major news-driven prediction markets), that would strongly update forecasters toward believing 80% is achievable by March 2026. If it doesn't reach 72% even during the holiday season and early January — a period when major sports events (NFL playoffs, college football) and potential political developments could drive attention — then reaching 80% becomes substantially harder. This question is informative because it captures the current trajectory of Polymarket's dominance in the prediction market attention space and reflects real-world drivers (U.S. launch, regulatory progress, event-driven engagement) that directly feed into the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Trump try to fire Powell in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve before his term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling or injunction regarding President Trump's authority to remove Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Trump announced the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged mortgage fraud as 'cause' for removal. Cook refused to resign, stating through her attorney Abbe David Lowell that 'the president lacks the authority to fire her' and that she would pursue legal action. The Federal Reserve Act of 1913 permits the president to remove Fed governors only 'for cause,' a power that has never been exercised before. In May 2024, the Supreme Court ruled in Trump v. Wilcox that the president lacks authority to remove Federal Reserve board members without proper cause, reinforcing statutory protections for Fed independence. Cook's legal team has indicated they will pursue 'all necessary actions' to prevent her removal. The case is expected to move quickly through the courts given its constitutional significance and the immediate practical implications for Fed governance. The outcome of this legal battle is widely seen as a critical precedent: if courts permit the removal of a Fed governor on these grounds, it would significantly lower the legal and political barriers to Trump attempting to remove Fed Chair Jerome Powell, whose term runs until May 2026. Conversely, a ruling blocking Cook's removal would reinforce the legal protections shielding Powell.

Sources:
- CBS News, 'Trump says he's fired Federal Reserve board member Lisa Cook' (Aug 26, 2025): https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-fires-federal-reserve-board-member-lisa-cook/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), any U.S. federal court (district court, circuit court, or the Supreme Court) issues a substantive ruling, order, or injunction specifically addressing whether President Trump has the legal authority to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook from her position. This includes temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, or rulings on motions to dismiss related to the Cook removal case. The ruling must be publicly reported by at least two credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg, NYT, Washington Post, or the court's own public docket via PACER at https://pacer.uscourts.gov/). The question resolves No if no such ruling or order is issued during this window. If the case is settled, mooted (e.g., Cook voluntarily resigns or Trump rescinds the removal), or otherwise resolved without a court ruling during the resolution window, the question also resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The Lisa Cook removal case is the most direct near-term legal test of whether Trump can remove Fed officials. A court ruling permitting Cook's removal would dramatically increase the probability that Trump attempts to fire Powell, since it would establish legal precedent that presidential removal power extends to Fed governors. A ruling blocking Cook's removal would reinforce the legal barriers protecting Powell and likely decrease the probability of an attempt. The speed and direction of the court's response in September is a strong leading indicator of whether the legal and political environment will be permissive enough for Trump to escalate to targeting Powell before year-end. This is a genuinely different observable event from the ultimate question — it concerns the Cook legal battle rather than Powell directly — but its outcome is highly informative about the ultimate question.

question: Will Donald Trump visit Germany in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits a listed country between January 15 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET, the relevant market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House officially announce a Trump visit to Germany (or a summit in Germany such as a G7/NATO event) scheduled for October 2025, between October 1 and October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of October 1, 2025, Donald Trump has not made a bilateral visit to Germany during his second term. His only previous visit to Germany was for the 2017 G20 summit in Hamburg during his first term (Statista, September 16, 2025: https://www.statista.com/chart/33648/trumps-international-travels-mapped/). In 2025, Trump's international travel has included a meeting with Putin in Alaska in August (BelTA, August 15, 2025: https://eng.belta.by/world/view/putins-aircraft-lands-in-anchorage-for-historic-meeting-with-trump-168375-2025/) and a state visit to the United Kingdom scheduled for September 17-19 (ProPakistani, July 17, 2025: https://propakistani.pk/2025/07/17/geo-news-and-senior-reporter-admits-to-false-report-of-trumps-visit-to-pakistan/). German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Washington on June 5, 2025, to discuss trade and Ukraine (CFR, June 5, 2025: https://www.cfr.org/blog/germany-chancellor-visits-washington). There are no publicly confirmed plans as of October 1 for Trump to visit Germany before the end of October 2025. Any official announcement of such a visit would be a strong leading indicator that Trump will physically enter Germany before late October.

Sources:
- Statista infographic on Trump's travels: https://www.statista.com/chart/33648/trumps-international-travels-mapped/
- CFR on Merz-Washington visit: https://www.cfr.org/blog/germany-chancellor-visits-washington
- BelTA on Putin-Trump Alaska meeting: https://eng.belta.by/world/view/putins-aircraft-lands-in-anchorage-for-historic-meeting-with-trump-168375-2025/
- ProPakistani on UK state visit schedule: https://propakistani.pk/2025/07/17/geo-news-and-senior-reporter-admits-to-false-report-of-trumps-visit-to-pakistan/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 20, 2025 (inclusive), the White House (via whitehouse.gov, the official @POTUS or @WhiteHouse social media accounts, or official press briefings) announces that President Trump will visit Germany in October 2025, OR if a major international summit (e.g., G7, NATO, EU-US) to be held in Germany in October 2025 is officially confirmed with Trump's attendance. It also resolves Yes if a consensus of at least three credible major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, BBC, CNN) reports such an announcement. If no such announcement is made by end of day (UTC) on October 20, 2025, the question resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- White House official site: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
- @POTUS on X/Twitter: https://twitter.com/POTUS
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
subquestions.rationale: For Trump to physically visit Germany before October 25, an official announcement or scheduling of such a trip would almost certainly need to appear by mid-to-late October. Presidential foreign travel is planned in advance with public announcements typically preceding the trip. If an announcement appears, it is a very strong signal Trump will visit Germany; if no announcement appears by October 20, it becomes extremely unlikely that Trump would make an unannounced visit to Germany within the remaining few days. This subquestion tracks a different observable event (the announcement) rather than the visit itself, and it serves as a leading indicator that would cause forecasters to strongly update their estimates on the ultimate question.

question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31, 2025, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NVIDIA's market capitalization be larger than Apple's market capitalization on November 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early October 2025, NVIDIA (NVDA) is the world's largest company by market capitalization at approximately $4.53 trillion, having surpassed Apple in September 2025. Apple (AAPL) is currently the second-largest company at roughly $3.5–3.9 trillion. Microsoft (MSFT) is the third-largest at roughly $3.4–3.7 trillion. The ultimate question asks whether NVIDIA will be the second-largest company by market cap on December 31, 2025 — meaning another company (likely Apple or Microsoft) would need to overtake NVIDIA but NVIDIA would still need to remain above the third-largest. A key indicator for whether NVIDIA ends the year as #1 or #2 is whether it maintains its lead over Apple in the near term. If NVIDIA falls below Apple in the coming weeks, that is evidence NVIDIA could slide to #2 (or lower) by year-end. Conversely, if NVIDIA maintains a comfortable lead over Apple, it may end the year as #1 rather than #2, which would mean the ultimate question resolves No.

Sources:
- Yahoo Finance: Nvidia Becomes World's Largest Company, Hits $4.5 Trillion Market Cap (Oct 1, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-becomes-world-largest-company-hits-4-5-trillion-market-cap-174512345.html
- Mint: Who's next to touch m-cap of $4 trillion? (July 15, 2025): https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/whos-next-to-touch-m-cap-of-4-trillion-and-can-nvidia-hit-6-trillion-11752557312177.html
- GuruFocus: Nvidia Surges to Second in Global Market Cap (May 16, 2025): https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2876543/nvidia-nvda-surges-to-second-in-global-market-cap-fueling-opt
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of market close on November 10, 2025, NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) has a larger market capitalization than Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL). The resolution window is from 2025-10-14 to 2025-11-10. Market capitalization will be determined using closing share prices on November 10, 2025, multiplied by total shares outstanding, as reported by a consensus of major financial data providers such as Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/), Google Finance (https://www.google.com/finance/), or CompaniesMarketCap (https://companiesmarketcap.com/). If November 10, 2025 is not a trading day (it is a Monday, but if markets are unexpectedly closed), the most recent prior trading day's closing prices will be used. If NVIDIA's market cap is exactly equal to Apple's (extremely unlikely), this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether NVIDIA will be the *second*-largest company by market cap on December 31, 2025. For NVIDIA to be exactly #2, it needs to be below one company and above all others. Currently NVIDIA is #1, ahead of Apple and Microsoft. Tracking whether NVIDIA maintains its lead over Apple in the near term is a meaningful indicator: if NVIDIA stays firmly above Apple, NVIDIA is more likely to end the year as #1 (not #2), which would resolve the ultimate question No. If NVIDIA slips below Apple, that's evidence the competitive landscape is tightening and NVIDIA could plausibly end at #2. This subquestion measures the relative positioning of the two top companies, which is directly relevant to whether NVIDIA will occupy the #2 slot specifically.

question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025 still be ongoing as of November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government shut down on October 1, 2025, after Senate Democrats filibustered the House-passed continuing resolution (CR), preventing it from reaching the 60-vote cloture threshold. As of late October 2025, the shutdown has lasted over three weeks and is tied for the second-longest in U.S. history. The shutdown is the primary political pressure point driving calls from some Republicans—including Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX) and Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA)—to invoke the 'nuclear option' to eliminate the legislative filibuster and pass the CR with a simple majority. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) has so far rejected using the nuclear option for legislation, stating the filibuster 'has protected the country' and 'makes the Senate the Senate.' However, frustration within the GOP caucus is mounting. If the shutdown persists deep into November without resolution, the political pressure on Senate Republicans to use the nuclear option on legislation will intensify significantly, making it more likely they break the legislative filibuster before December 31. Conversely, if the shutdown ends through a bipartisan deal or Democratic concessions, the primary catalyst for the nuclear option on legislation would be removed.

Sources:
- The Hill, 'Chip Roy floats nuclear option on Senate filibuster to end shutdown' (Oct 20, 2025): https://thehill.com/homenews/house/4957890-chip-roy-nuclear-option-filibuster-shutdown/
- Spectrum News, 'Shutdown sparks new conversations on nuclear option' (Oct 21, 2025): https://www.baynews9.com/fl/tampa/politics/2025/10/21/shutdown-sparks-new-conversations-on--nuclear-option-
- Townhall, 'Republican's Not Yet Considering Changing Filibuster Rules To End Government Shutdown' (Oct 9, 2025): https://townhall.com/tipsheet/saraharnold/2025/10/09/republicans-not-yet-considering-changing-filibuster-rules-to-end-government-shutdown-n2649123
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the partial or full federal government shutdown that began on or around October 1, 2025 is still in effect (i.e., at least some federal agencies remain unfunded and non-essential operations are suspended) on November 30, 2025. It resolves No if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025, legislation is enacted (signed into law by the President) that funds all previously unfunded federal agencies, thereby ending the shutdown before November 30, 2025. Resolution will be based on official U.S. government sources, including statements from the Office of Management and Budget (https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/) and reporting from the Congressional Research Service or major wire services (AP, Reuters). If a temporary funding measure (e.g., a short-term CR) is signed but expires before November 30, 2025, causing the government to shut down again, the question resolves Yes. If the shutdown ends but a new, separate shutdown begins before November 30 for unrelated reasons, the question still resolves No (since the original shutdown ended).
subquestions.rationale: The ongoing government shutdown is the single most important driver of the nuclear option debate for legislation. If the shutdown persists through November, political pressure on Senate Republicans to break the legislative filibuster will become extreme—over 60 days without government funding would be historically unprecedented and would test the resolve of senators who have so far opposed changing the rules. A long-running shutdown makes it far more likely that holdout Republican senators relent and support the nuclear option before December 31. Conversely, if the shutdown ends in November through conventional means, the primary impetus for the nuclear option on legislation disappears, making it very unlikely to be invoked by year's end. This subquestion is thus a strong leading indicator of the ultimate question's resolution.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government enter a partial shutdown (lapse in appropriations) on or before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Federal funding for fiscal year 2025 is set to expire at midnight on September 30, 2025. If Congress does not pass new appropriations bills or a continuing resolution (CR) by that deadline, a partial government shutdown would begin on October 1, 2025. As of mid-September 2025, Congress has made limited progress on the 12 required appropriations bills: the House has passed only two (Defense and Military Construction-VA), and the Senate has passed three (Agriculture, Military Construction-VA, and Legislative Branch). Republican leaders hold narrow majorities (219–212 in the House, 53–47 in the Senate), but 60 Senate votes are needed to pass spending legislation, requiring bipartisan cooperation. Senate Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries have urged Republican leadership to negotiate a bipartisan stopgap, while President Trump has expressed skepticism about such talks. Prediction markets as of late August 2025 placed the probability of a shutdown before year-end at over 43%, and multiple news sources have characterized the risk of a shutdown on October 1 as unusually high compared to recent years. Senate Appropriations Chairwoman Susan Collins called a potential October 1 shutdown 'horrendous' and urged passage of a short-term CR.

Sources:
- TheStreet, 'Over 43% chance of U.S. government shutdown in 2025: Polymarket' (2025-08-31): https://www.thestreet.com/crypto/markets/over-43-chance-of-u-s-government-shutdown-in-2025-polymarket
- Military Times, 'Another federal shutdown threat looms as Congress heads back to DC' (2025-08-28): https://www.militarytimes.com/congress/2025/08/28/another-federal-shutdown-threat-looms-as-congress-heads-back-to-dc/
- New Hampshire Bulletin, 'Every fall there's a government shutdown warning. This time it could happen.' (2025-09-03): https://newhampshirebulletin.com/2025/09/03/every-fall-theres-a-government-shutdown-warning-this-time-it-could-happen/
- National Law Review, 'Potential Outcomes If Congress Misses the Federal Funding Deadline' (2025-09-03): https://www.natlawreview.com/article/potential-outcomes-if-congress-misses-federal-funding-deadline
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces a federal government shutdown (full or partial) due to a lapse in appropriations at any point between September 17, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), as indicated by OPM's 'Current Status' page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/). Specifically, a shutdown notice checked at or after 10:00 AM ET on any day in this window that indicates a lapse-in-appropriations shutdown counts. Announcements of closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not count. If no lapse-in-appropriations shutdown notice appears on the OPM status page by 10:00 AM ET on October 1, 2025, this question resolves No. If the OPM website becomes unavailable, credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, CNN, NYT) confirming or denying a federal government shutdown will be used as a fallback resolution source.
subquestions.rationale: Whether a shutdown actually begins on October 1 is a critical prerequisite for the ultimate question about a 10–29 day shutdown in 2025. If Congress passes a CR or other funding measure before the deadline, no shutdown occurs and the ultimate question resolves No. Conversely, if a shutdown begins on October 1, the duration becomes the key variable. This subquestion captures the binary gateway event — does a shutdown start at all — which is the most important early indicator. Two forecasters who disagree on whether the government will be shut down for 10–29 days are very likely to also have differing views on whether Congress can avoid a shutdown entirely by the deadline, making this a strong crux.

question: Taylor Swift holds top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 18th?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Taylor Swift holds the top 10 spots (1-10) on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for the week titled “week of October 18, 2025”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The resolution source will be Billboard.com

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 for the chart week dated October 11, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift's twelfth studio album, 'The Life of a Showgirl', is scheduled for release on October 3, 2025. The album was produced by Max Martin and Shellback and contains 12 tracks. It has already broken Spotify's record for the most pre-saved album countdown page in the platform's history, surpassing her own previous record set by 'The Tortured Poets Department' in 2024 (Forbes, September 3, 2025). Swift has a history of massive debut weeks: 'The Tortured Poets Department' debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and produced ten simultaneous Hot 100 top-10 hits, while 'Midnights' (2022) made her the first artist to occupy all ten top positions on the Hot 100 simultaneously. Billboard named Swift the top artist of the 21st century, citing 14 No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200 and 12 No. 1 songs on the Hot 100 (Hindustan Times, August 30, 2025). The Billboard 200 chart for the week dated October 11, 2025 would reflect first-week sales of the album (tracking period October 3–9). A No. 1 debut on the Billboard 200 would indicate enormous first-week consumption, which strongly correlates with dominating the Hot 100 singles chart as well — a necessary precondition for holding all top 10 spots on the Hot 100 the following week (chart dated October 18).

Sources:
- Forbes: Taylor Swift's New Album Makes History On Spotify: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bryanrolli/2025/09/03/taylor-swifts-new-album-makes-history-on-spotify/
- Euronews: Taylor Swift already breaks Spotify record: https://www.euronews.com/culture/2025/09/02/taylor-swift-already-breaks-spotify-record-before-release-of-new-album

- CinemaBlend: KPop Demon Hunters record vs Taylor Swift: https://www.cinemablend.com/music/kpop-demon-hunters-just-broke-another-big-record-but-i-think-taylor-swift-could-stop-it
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart for the chart week dated October 11, 2025 (or the nearest chart week reflecting tracking data from October 3–9, 2025). The chart is typically published on Billboard.com on the Tuesday following the end of the tracking period. Resolution will be based on the official Billboard 200 chart published at https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/. If Billboard changes its publication schedule or the album release is delayed beyond October 9, 2025, the question resolves No. The resolution window for checking this information is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-11.
subquestions.rationale: A No. 1 debut on the Billboard 200 is a strong leading indicator of whether Taylor Swift can dominate the Hot 100 singles chart the following week. When Swift's previous albums debuted at No. 1 with massive first-week numbers, they also produced multiple simultaneous top-10 Hot 100 hits (e.g., 'Midnights' swept the entire top 10, 'TTPD' held the top 14). If the album fails to debut at No. 1 — perhaps because of unexpectedly strong competition from the KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack or other releases — it would be a strong signal that she is unlikely to hold all 10 top spots on the Hot 100. Conversely, a dominant No. 1 debut with very high streaming/sales numbers would suggest her individual tracks are being consumed at levels consistent with sweeping the Hot 100 top 10. This question resolves before the ultimate question's deadline and measures a different but highly correlated observable outcome.

question: Will Michael Jackson be named in newly released Epstein files?

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice publicly release a batch of previously unreleased Epstein-related documents by December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On November 20, 2025, President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act into law, which mandates the Department of Justice to release all unclassified documents related to Jeffrey Epstein investigations within 30 days — setting a deadline of approximately December 19, 2025. The law requires the release of FBI reports, witness interview transcripts, flight logs, travel records, Epstein's autopsy report, and internal communications, in a searchable and downloadable format. However, there are potential delays: Attorney General Pam Bondi has launched a new investigation into Epstein associates, which could be used to temporarily withhold materials deemed to jeopardize active investigations. Prior to this law, tens of thousands of pages had already been released through lawsuits, FOIA requests, and congressional disclosures, but the bulk of an estimated 100,000+ pages of DOJ/FBI materials remains unreleased. The question is whether the DOJ will begin releasing substantive new documents before the statutory deadline, or whether it will delay until the last moment or invoke exemptions to withhold material.

Sources:
- PBS: '7 things to know about the Justice Department's Epstein files' (Nov 21, 2025): https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/7-things-to-know-about-the-justice-departments-epstein-files
- Global News: 'The Epstein files: What to know ahead of their release' (Nov 21, 2025): https://globalnews.ca/news/10917000/epstein-files-what-to-know/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15, the U.S. Department of Justice publicly releases a batch of previously unreleased documents related to Jeffrey Epstein that contains substantive new material (not merely re-releases, unredactions, or repackaged versions of already-public documents). The release must be confirmed by credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, New York Times, Washington Post, PBS, CNN). If no such release occurs by 11:59 PM ET on December 15, 2025, the question resolves No. If the DOJ announces a delay citing active investigations or national security but has not yet released documents by the deadline, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Michael Jackson is named in 'newly released Epstein files' depends critically on whether the DOJ actually releases a substantial tranche of new documents before the ultimate question's deadline. Michael Jackson has already been mentioned in previously released materials (e.g., flight logs and contact lists referenced in earlier document dumps), so the key question for the ultimate resolution is whether genuinely novel files emerge. If the DOJ delays its release past December 15 or invokes exemptions, it becomes much less likely that Jackson's name will appear in newly released files before December 20. Conversely, if a major document release occurs by mid-December, there is a meaningful chance Jackson is mentioned given his prior appearances in Epstein-adjacent records. This subquestion tracks the necessary precondition — the actual release of new documents — rather than simply restating the ultimate question.

question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S government funding lapse occurs on October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A funding lapse is defined as the President failing to sign the relevant bill(s) extending government funding by September 30, 11:59 PM ET. subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a continuing resolution or full-year appropriations bill funding the government beyond September 30, 2025, by September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Congress returns from its August recess on September 2, 2025, with only about 19 working days before the September 30 funding deadline. As of late August 2025, only two of the twelve regular FY2026 appropriations bills have passed the House, and only three have passed the Senate. Congressional leaders from both parties acknowledge that completing all appropriations bills before the deadline is essentially impossible. Rep. Steve Womack (R-AR) has said the odds of a shutdown are as high as he has seen in recent memory, noting there is 'probably as good a chance right now at a potential shutdown as I have seen in recent memory' (Talk Business & Politics, July 20, 2025). Senate Democrats have urged Republican leaders to begin bipartisan negotiations on a stop-gap funding measure, but as of August 28, no such talks have been announced (The Hill, August 28, 2025). Complicating matters, the White House has submitted a $5 billion rescission package that cancels foreign assistance funding, which Democrats view as an obstacle to bipartisan negotiations (Agri-Pulse, August 31, 2025). For a continuing resolution to be signed into law by September 30, the House would typically need to pass it several days in advance to allow Senate consideration and presidential signature. The March 2025 CR passed with only one Democratic vote in the House, suggesting partisan tensions remain high.

Sources:
- Military Times, August 28, 2025: https://www.militarytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2025/08/28/another-federal-shutdown-threat-looms-as-congress-heads-back-to-dc/
- Talk Business & Politics, July 20, 2025: https://talkbusiness.net/2025/07/womack-sees-potential-for-government-shutdown/
- The Hill, August 28, 2025: https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/4871234-schumer-jeffries-call-on-gop-leaders-to-meet-to-avoid-government-shutdown/
- Agri-Pulse, August 31, 2025: https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/21567-washington-week-ahead-another-possible-shutdown-looms-farm-income-forecast-due
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes (by a recorded floor vote) a continuing resolution, omnibus appropriations bill, or any other legislation that would fund the federal government beyond September 30, 2025, at any point between September 1, 2025 and September 25, 2025 (inclusive). The bill need not have passed the Senate or been signed by the President — only House passage is required. Resolution will be based on official House roll call vote records available at https://clerk.house.gov/Votes and/or reporting from the Congressional Record. If the House passes multiple bills that collectively fund the entire government, this still resolves Yes. If the House passes a bill that only funds a portion of the government (e.g., a defense-only bill) while leaving other agencies unfunded, this still resolves Yes, as any House-passed vehicle extending government funding counts. If no such vote occurs by end of day (11:59 PM ET) on September 25, 2025, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The House passing a continuing resolution or appropriations bill is a necessary precondition for avoiding a funding lapse on October 1. If the House has not passed any funding vehicle by September 25, it becomes extremely unlikely that both chambers can pass a bill and the President can sign it within the remaining five days, making a shutdown near-certain. Conversely, early House passage would be a strong signal that Congress is on track to avoid a lapse. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question (presidential signature by September 30) — it tracks legislative progress in the chamber that historically acts first on spending measures and is where the most significant partisan obstacles currently exist.

question: Paramount x Warner Bros. acquisition announced by June 30?
description:
