Discovery's studios and streaming businesses or only a subset of those businesses (including, for example, HBO / Max, Warner Bros. Pictures, Warner Bros. Television, or related streaming platforms and content libraries).

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from Paramount Global and/or Warner Bros. Discovery; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Warner Bros. Discovery enter exclusive acquisition negotiations with Paramount Skydance by January 8, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) has been actively exploring a sale since October 2025, receiving preliminary buyout offers from Paramount Skydance, Comcast, and Netflix. In late November 2025, WBD requested improved bids by December 1, 2025, after which it was expected to potentially enter exclusive talks with one bidder. Paramount Skydance, backed by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, has been the most persistent suitor, initially offering ~$24/share ($60 billion) in an all-cash bid that WBD's board rejected. However, on December 5, 2025, Netflix announced it was acquiring Warner Bros. in an $82.7 billion deal valued at $27.75 per share, contingent on the spin-off of Discovery Global expected in Q3 2026. This Netflix deal significantly complicates any Paramount-WBD transaction. If WBD has already agreed to sell to Netflix, entering exclusive talks with Paramount becomes far less likely unless the Netflix deal falls apart or WBD negotiates a separate arrangement for assets not included in the Netflix transaction. WBD's stock has surged approximately 83% since September 2025 when Paramount's interest was first reported, closing at $22.96 on November 25, 2025.

Sources:
- Market Screener, "Warner Bros Discovery seeks improved bids by December 1, sources say" (Nov 25, 2025): https://www.marketscreener.com/
- News 9, "Netflix acquires Warner Bros. in a massive $82.7 billion deal" (Dec 5, 2025): https://www.news9live.com/
- Variety, "What Happens if Paramount Acquires Warner Bros. Discovery?" (Oct 22, 2025): https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/what-happens-paramount-acquires-warner-bros-discovery-1236222830/
- CNA, "Warner Bros Discovery rejects Paramount offer, considers full sale" (Oct 21, 2025): https://www.channelnewsasia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major financial or entertainment news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Variety, Wall Street Journal, CNBC) confirms that Warner Bros. Discovery has entered exclusive acquisition or merger negotiations with Paramount Skydance (or Paramount Global). 'Exclusive negotiations' means WBD has agreed to negotiate solely with Paramount Skydance for a defined period regarding the acquisition of all or a subset of WBD's studios and/or streaming businesses. The question resolves No if no such exclusive negotiations are reported by January 8, 2026. If the Netflix-WBD deal announced on December 5, 2025 remains intact and no separate exclusive talks with Paramount are reported, this resolves No. If reporting is ambiguous about whether talks are 'exclusive,' the question resolves No. Primary resolution sources include Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Variety (https://variety.com/), and the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether a Paramount x Warner Bros. acquisition will be announced by June 30, 2026. The Netflix-WBD deal announced on December 5, 2025 represents a major obstacle to a Paramount-WBD deal. Whether WBD enters exclusive talks with Paramount in the near term is a critical leading indicator: if WBD is exclusively negotiating with Paramount (perhaps because the Netflix deal collapsed or was restructured), a formal announcement becomes far more likely. Conversely, if no exclusive Paramount talks materialize by early January 2026—especially given the competing Netflix deal—the probability of a Paramount-WBD announcement by the ultimate deadline drops significantly. This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable intermediate step that would strongly update forecasters' views on the ultimate question.

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 5 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will NASA's CNEOS Fireball database record at least 3 bolide events with impact energy ≥ 1 kiloton of TNT equivalent between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The NASA JPL Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains a publicly available Fireball and Bolide database that logs atmospheric entry events detected primarily by U.S. government sensors, reporting estimated total impact energy in kilotons of TNT equivalent. The frequency of kiloton-class bolide events is a key indicator of whether a ≥5 kt event is plausible within 2025.

Historical data from the CNEOS fireball database shows that events ≥1 kt occur roughly 5–10 times per year on average, meaning roughly 0.4–0.8 per month. In some months, clusters of events occur, while other months have none. A higher-than-average rate of kiloton-class events in September 2025 would indicate elevated bolide activity, which increases the conditional probability of a rare ≥5 kt event occurring before year-end.

Recent notable events include a 1.6 kt fireball observed over southern Japan on August 19, 2025 (https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-august-19-2025/). For broader context, the Chelyabinsk event of February 2013 released ~440 kt, and events ≥5 kt are estimated to occur roughly once every 5–10 years based on the historical record (see Brown et al. 2013, https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12741).

Sources:
- NASA CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
- Watchers.news on 1.6 kt Japan fireball: https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-august-19-2025/
- Brown et al. 2013 on bolide frequency: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12741
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the NASA CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data repository (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) lists 3 or more distinct fireball events with an 'Impact Energy (kt)' value of 1.0 or greater, where the event date falls between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive, using the UTC date recorded in the database). Only natural meteoroid events count; any event confirmed by NASA or credible sources to be artificial debris or reentry of a man-made object is excluded.

If the CNEOS database has not been updated to cover the full September 2025 period by November 30, 2025, resolution may rely on equivalent data published by the European Space Agency (ESA) or reports from the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN). If no authoritative source provides sufficient data by November 30, 2025, the question resolves as ambiguous.

Resolution window: events occurring between 2025-09-01 00:00 UTC and 2025-09-30 23:59 UTC.
subquestions.rationale: The frequency of kiloton-class bolide events in a given month serves as a proxy indicator for overall near-Earth meteoroid flux levels. If September 2025 shows an unusually high rate of ≥1 kt events (3 or more, versus an average of fewer than 1 per month), this would suggest elevated bolide activity, which in turn raises the probability of a rarer ≥5 kt event occurring before year-end. Conversely, a quiet September (resolving No) would be weakly consistent with a lower annual bolide rate, slightly reducing the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it measures a different threshold (1 kt vs. 5 kt) and a different quantity (count of events vs. existence of a single event), providing meaningful intermediate evidence about the current state of Earth's meteoroid environment.

question: Will Gold close between $3900 and $4000 at the end of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the price of the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) as of the final market close price in 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The resolution source will be COMEX trading data for the Gold Continuous Contract (https://www.google.com/finance/quote/GCW00:COMEX).

subquestions.question: Will the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) close above $3,900 on at least 15 trading days during November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Gold has been in a strong uptrend throughout 2025. By late September 2025, front-month COMEX gold was trading around $3,737 per ounce (Morningstar, Sep 25 2025), up over 42% year-to-date. By mid-October 2025, gold broke decisively above $4,000 per ounce on COMEX futures for the first time, with analysts describing $4,000 as a new support floor and projecting targets of $4,400 and higher (TalkMarkets, Oct 14 2025). The ultimate question asks whether gold will close between $3,900 and $4,000 at end of 2025 — a relatively narrow band. Whether gold spends much of November trading above $3,900 is informative about the trajectory and whether the price is likely to settle in the $3,900–$4,000 range or move further away from it by year-end. If gold consistently stays above $3,900 but mostly above $4,000, the ultimate question becomes less likely; if it frequently dips into the $3,900–$4,000 band, it becomes more likely. There are approximately 19–21 trading days in November 2025.

Sources:
- Morningstar, "Comex Gold Settles 0.13% Higher at $3736.90" (Sep 25, 2025): https://www.morningstar.com
- TalkMarkets, "Gold & Silver Smash Through Key Levels" (Oct 14, 2025): https://www.talkmarkets.com
- Google Finance COMEX Gold Continuous Contract: https://www.google.com/finance/quote/GCW00:COMEX
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) daily settlement/close price is above $3,900.00 per troy ounce on at least 15 trading days between November 3, 2025 and November 28, 2025 (inclusive). The resolution window is from 2025-10-31 (start_date) to 2025-11-30 (end_date), but only trading days within November 2025 count toward the tally. The data source is the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract as reported on Google Finance (https://www.google.com/finance/quote/GCW00:COMEX) or, as a fallback, COMEX settlement data from CME Group (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.quotes.html). A 'trading day' is any day the COMEX is open and a settlement price is published. If the data source becomes unavailable, Kitco's historical gold price chart (https://www.kitco.com/charts/livegold.html) may be used as a secondary source. If fewer than 15 trading days occur in November 2025 (e.g., due to extended market closures), the question resolves Yes if gold closes above $3,900 on all available trading days. The question resolves No otherwise.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether gold closes in the narrow $3,900–$4,000 band at end of 2025. Tracking how consistently gold stays above $3,900 during November provides critical evidence about the price trajectory heading into year-end. If gold consistently trades above $3,900 (and especially above $4,000) throughout November, it suggests the $3,900–$4,000 band is either being used as support or has been left behind — both informative for the ultimate question. If gold fails to maintain $3,900 for most of November, the $3,900–$4,000 year-end close becomes less likely from below. This subquestion captures the momentum and price level dynamics one month before resolution without simply restating the ultimate question.

question: Will Sam Altman get OpenAI equity in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Sam Altman formally takes equity in OpenAI by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI and Microsoft publicly announce a finalized restructuring agreement (converting OpenAI's capped-profit structure to a for-profit entity with equity ownership) by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI has been pursuing a major corporate restructuring from its unusual hybrid nonprofit/capped-profit structure to a more conventional for-profit entity. This restructuring is widely seen as a prerequisite for Sam Altman to receive equity in OpenAI, as his current compensation is limited to a $76,001 salary with no ownership stake. As of late August 2025, OpenAI and Microsoft were actively negotiating terms for the restructuring, including Microsoft's future equity stake (expected to settle between 30-35%), cloud hosting rights, intellectual property access, and the controversial 'AGI clause.' The restructuring also faces regulatory hurdles, including independent valuations and approvals from Delaware and California attorneys general, as well as potential complications from Elon Musk's lawsuit. Reuters has reported that Altman would receive equity after the nonprofit-to-for-profit restructuring, though CNBC noted Altman told staff he would not receive a 'giant equity stake.' The restructuring was originally targeted for 2026 but negotiations could accelerate or delay the timeline.

Sources:
- Benzinga (2025-08-27): What's Going On With Microsoft Stock Wednesday? https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/08/41508283/whats-going-on-with-microsoft-stock-wednesday
- Benzinga (2025-08-30): Here's Why Sam Altman Won't Make A Fortune From OpenAI https://www.benzinga.com/general/25/08/41544408/heres-why-sam-altman-wont-make-a-fortune-from-openai
- Fortune (2025-08-21): OpenAI may soon be the world's most valuable private company https://fortune.com/2025/08/21/openai-worlds-most-valuable-private-company-sam-altman-no-equity/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), OpenAI and Microsoft publicly announce (via official press releases, SEC filings, or confirmed reporting by at least two major credible news outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, the Wall Street Journal, the New York Times, or CNBC) that they have reached a finalized agreement to restructure OpenAI from its current capped-profit/nonprofit hybrid structure into a for-profit corporation with equity ownership for investors. A 'finalized agreement' means a binding deal has been signed, not merely that negotiations are ongoing or that a term sheet has been agreed in principle. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2025, this question resolves No. Resolution sources include official OpenAI and Microsoft communications (https://openai.com/blog, https://blogs.microsoft.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), and the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com).
subquestions.rationale: The corporate restructuring from nonprofit/capped-profit to for-profit is widely reported as the key prerequisite for Sam Altman to receive equity in OpenAI. If the restructuring deal is finalized in October, it would strongly increase the probability that Altman receives equity before year-end 2025, as the equity grants would likely follow shortly after. Conversely, if the deal remains unfinalized by end of October, the window for Altman to receive equity by December 31 narrows significantly given the additional regulatory approvals needed. This question tracks a concrete, observable precursor event rather than simply asking the ultimate question earlier.

question: Will Kim Keon Hee be sentenced to prison by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kim Keon Hee is sentenced to any time in jail/prison for any charges, including but not limited to allegations of stock price manipulation, bribery, election interference, abuse of power, or criminal acts related to Yoon Suk Yeol’s martial law declaration and related subsequent actions, by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will remain open through March 31, 2026 or until Kim Keon Hee is sentenced to time in jail/prison, regardless of any initial sentencing that does not include prison. Any sentencing will qualify, regardless of subsequent appeals or changes to the sentence.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean government and law enforcement; however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court schedule a sentencing hearing date for Kim Keon Hee's corruption trial before January 2, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Kim Keon Hee, the former first lady of South Korea, was indicted on August 29, 2025, on charges including stock manipulation, bribery, and election interference. Her trial opened on September 24, 2025, at the Seoul Central District Court. South Korean corruption trials typically involve multiple hearings over several months, with evidence presentation, witness testimony, and prosecution/defense arguments before a sentencing hearing can be scheduled. As of early December 2025, the trial is still in its relatively early stages, having begun only about two months prior. The charges include violations of the Capital Markets Act, the Political Funds Act, and laws prohibiting acceptance of bribes for mediation. If convicted, Kim could face prison sentences of 5 years or longer. The pace at which the court moves through the trial proceedings is a key indicator of whether a sentence could be handed down before the end of March 2026.

For context, her husband Yoon Suk Yeol's insurrection trial began in mid-April 2025, and as of late 2025, it is still ongoing without a verdict. South Korean high-profile political trials can sometimes move quickly under special counsel mandates but sentencing typically takes many months.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald, "Kim Keon Hee trial begins" (2025-09-24): https://www.koreaherald.com/article/arti_detail.php?cid=10424441
- The Korea Herald, "Kim Keon Hee becomes 1st former first lady to be indicted" (2025-08-29): https://www.koreaherald.com/article/arti_detail.php?cid=10419835
- The Independent, "South Korea indicts former first lady Kim Keon Hee on criminal charges" (2025-08-29): https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/south-korea-indicts-former-first-lady-kim-keon-hee-b2606123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02 (inclusive), a South Korean court officially schedules or announces a specific date for a sentencing hearing (also known as a verdict/judgment hearing) in Kim Keon Hee's corruption trial. This includes any announcement by the Seoul Central District Court or other relevant court indicating that trial proceedings have concluded and a date for the pronouncement of a verdict and sentence has been set. The scheduling must be reported by credible South Korean media outlets such as The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), or JoongAng Ilbo (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/). If no such scheduling is reported by January 2, 2026, the question resolves No. Note: this question asks about the scheduling of a sentencing date, not the sentencing itself. The scheduled sentencing date itself may fall after January 2, 2026.
subquestions.rationale: Whether a sentencing hearing date has been scheduled is a strong leading indicator of whether Kim Keon Hee will actually be sentenced by March 31, 2026. South Korean criminal trials must complete evidence presentation, witness examination, and closing arguments before a court can schedule a sentencing date. If by early January 2026 no sentencing date has been set, it becomes much less likely that the trial will conclude with a sentence before the end of March 2026. Conversely, if a sentencing date is announced, it strongly signals an imminent verdict. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question (the actual sentencing) and serves as a meaningful procedural milestone that forecasters can use to update their beliefs.

question: Pepe ETF in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any spot Pepe (https://etherscan.io/token/0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933) ETF receives approval from the SEC by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Approval under Rule 19-4b will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, even if there has not been an S-1 approval. Similarly, an S-1 approval without a 19-4b approval will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the SEC, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the SEC declare effective (approve) any S-1 registration statement for a spot crypto ETF covering a token other than Bitcoin or Ethereum between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 18, 2025, the SEC adopted generic listing standards for commodity-based trust shares, eliminating the need for case-by-case 19b-4 exchange rule filings for crypto spot ETFs. On September 29, 2025, the SEC instructed issuers of spot ETFs for Litecoin, XRP, Solana, Cardano, Dogecoin, and other tokens to withdraw their 19b-4 filings, since only an S-1 registration statement is now required for approval. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas stated that the approval odds for the 16 pending spot crypto ETFs are now '100%' and that the SEC can approve them 'at any time.' Analyst James Seyffart noted the SEC could 'move absurdly fast if they really want to,' potentially approving S-1s in days, though he cautioned there is no guarantee on timing. Multiple S-1 filings are already pending for tokens including Solana, XRP, Litecoin, Dogecoin, and Cardano. The SEC had previously set decision deadlines for several of these applications in October 2025. The first product approved under the new framework was Grayscale's Digital Large Cap Fund (GDLC), approved on September 18, 2025, which holds exposure to Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Solana, and Cardano. Pepe (PEPE) is a meme token on Ethereum that does not currently have a pending spot ETF application and does not have a regulated futures market with six months of trading history — a key eligibility criterion under the new generic listing standards. As of late September 2025, no issuer has filed an S-1 for a Pepe spot ETF. The tokens most likely to receive early approvals are those with existing futures markets and pending S-1 filings, such as Solana, XRP, and Litecoin.

Sources:
- Yahoo Finance, 'SEC's Approval Odds for 16 Spot Crypto ETFs Now 100%' (Sep 30, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/secs-approval-odds-16-spot-100000456.html
- CoinDesk, 'SEC Tells Issuers to Pull 19b-4s; ETFs Could Be Approved Absurdly Fast' (Sep 29, 2025): https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2025/09/29/sec-tells-issuers-to-pull-19b-4s-etfs-could-be-approved-absurdly-fast/
- The Crypto Basic, 'SEC Adopts Generic Listing Standards' (Sep 18, 2025): https://thecryptobasic.com/2025/09/18/sec-adopts-generic-listing-standards-to-accelerate-spot-crypto-etf-approvals/
- Yahoo Finance, 'SEC Backs Nasdaq, CBOE, NYSE Push to Simplify Crypto ETF Rules' (Sep 18, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/sec-backs-nasdaq-cboe-nyse-push-to-simplify-crypto-etf-rules/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission declares effective at least one S-1 registration statement for a spot cryptocurrency ETF that holds a token other than Bitcoin (BTC) or Ethereum (ETH) as its primary underlying asset. This includes ETFs for tokens such as Solana, XRP, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Cardano, or any other altcoin. Multi-asset ETFs (like Grayscale's GDLC, already approved) do not count unless a new single-asset altcoin spot ETF is approved in this window. Resolution will be determined by SEC EDGAR filings (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&type=S-1&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany) and official SEC press releases (https://www.sec.gov/news/pressreleases), supplemented by credible reporting from Bloomberg, CoinDesk, or similar financial outlets. If no such S-1 is declared effective by 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a strong early indicator for whether a Pepe ETF could be approved by end of 2025. If the SEC approves S-1s for altcoin spot ETFs in October — starting with tokens like Solana, XRP, and Litecoin that have pending applications and meet the generic listing criteria — it establishes both the regulatory precedent and the speed of the new approval process. However, Pepe currently lacks both a pending ETF application and a qualifying futures market, so even if other altcoin ETFs are approved in October, Pepe faces additional barriers. If the SEC does NOT approve any altcoin spot ETFs in October despite the streamlined framework, it would strongly signal that a Pepe ETF by year-end is virtually impossible, since Pepe would need an issuer to file, a qualifying futures market to exist, and the SEC to act — all within roughly two months. Conversely, rapid October approvals of other altcoins would at least leave open the theoretical possibility of a Pepe ETF filing and fast-track approval, though it would remain very unlikely.

question: Will Michael Anton be next National Security Advisor?
description:
This market will resolve according to the next person Donald Trump appoints to the National Security Advisor position by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on Trump's first announcement - if Trump announces another person to this position first, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

This market refers to the first permanent National Security Advisor following Mike Waltz's departure from the role; any acting advisor or otherwise temporary advisor will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly mention or be credibly reported as considering Michael Anton for a senior national security role between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-22?
subquestions.background_information:
Since Mike Waltz was removed as National Security Advisor in May 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been serving in a dual role as Acting National Security Advisor. As of late November 2025, no permanent replacement has been announced. Michael Anton is a conservative intellectual who served as a spokesman for Trump's National Security Council during the first Trump administration (2017-2018) and is known for his 2016 essay 'The Flight 93 Election.' He has remained in conservative policy circles and has been mentioned in some speculation about national security roles. However, other names — including Steve Witkoff — have received more public advocacy for the position (see American Thinker, October 2025). The fact that the NSA role has remained unfilled for over six months suggests Trump may not be in a rush, or may be deliberating among multiple candidates. Any credible reporting linking Anton to the role would be a strong signal that he is the frontrunner.

Sources:
- American Thinker, 'It's Time To Appoint Steve Witkoff National Security Advisor' (October 16, 2025): https://www.americanthinker.com/articles/2025/10/its_time_to_appoint_steve_witkoff_national_security_advisor.html
- The Hill, 'Trump's non-security council is another ticking time bomb' (July 14, 2025): https://thehill.com/opinion/national-security/5047123-trumps-non-security-council-is-another-ticking-time-bomb/
- Outside the Beltway, 'Trump's National Security Non-Process' (September 9, 2025): https://www.outsidethebeltway.com/trumps-national-security-non-process/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-22 (inclusive), at least one credible major news outlet (e.g., Reuters, AP, New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Axios, Politico, CNN, Fox News, NBC News) publishes a report stating that Donald Trump is considering, interviewing, or has met with Michael Anton specifically regarding the National Security Advisor position, OR if Trump or an official White House spokesperson publicly mentions Anton in connection with the NSA role. The report must specifically name Michael Anton and the National Security Advisor role. Opinion pieces, speculation by outside commentators, or social media posts by non-official accounts do not count. If no such credible report appears by 2025-12-22, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Trump is publicly considering Anton for the NSA role is a strong leading indicator of whether he will ultimately appoint Anton. If two forecasters disagree on the ultimate question — one thinks Anton will be named NSA, the other doesn't — they would likely update significantly upon learning whether credible reports link Anton to the role. The absence of any such reporting in the weeks before the December 31 deadline would strongly suggest Anton is not the pick, while the presence of such reporting would be a major positive signal. This is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks a precursor event (being publicly considered) rather than the final announcement itself.

question: U.S. forces in Gaza in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if active regular US military personnel physically enter Gaza at any point between July 28, 2025, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. 

US military personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

US military personnel entering buffer zones under control of Israel will not qualify.

High ranking U.S. service members entering Gaza for diplomatic purposes (and their accompanying entourage), military contractors, military advisors, and special operation forces will not qualify. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a multinational stabilization force (excluding U.S. combat troops) physically enter the Gaza Strip by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Following the Gaza ceasefire that took effect on October 10, 2025, the U.S. deployed approximately 200 troops to Hatzor Air Base in southern Israel to establish a coordination center for monitoring ceasefire implementation. U.S. officials have repeatedly stated that no American troops will enter Gaza itself. However, the broader peace plan envisions a multinational stabilization force — potentially including troops from Egypt, Turkey, Indonesia, Azerbaijan, and Gulf Arab states — deploying between Gaza's urban zones and its border with Israel. Egyptian military forces and heavy equipment entered Gaza on October 26, 2025, to assist in the search for hostages. Israel's Channel 12 reported that Israel will not carry out further withdrawals until the international force enters Gaza. Israeli PM Netanyahu stated on October 26 that Israel will retain control over which foreign troops may enter. A UN Security Council resolution to authorize the force is under discussion in Qatar, and the force's mandate was discussed at the Sharm el-Sheikh summit on October 12. The deployment of this multinational force is a key precursor to any potential change in the U.S. military posture regarding Gaza — if the multinational force successfully deploys and encounters operational challenges, it could increase pressure for U.S. troops to enter Gaza in a supporting role.

Sources:
- The Times of Israel, Oct 26: https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/egyptians-enter-gaza-as-us-drones-fly-above-strip/
- Saudi Gazette, Oct 12: https://www.saudigazette.com.sa/article/647123
- News18, Oct 26: https://www.news18.com/world/we-are-in-control-netanyahu-says-israel-will-choose-which-foreign-troops-can-enter-gaza-ws-9228234.html
- Ynetnews, Oct 18: https://www.ynetnews.com/article/rkg11bg9jx
- TASS, Oct 10: https://tass.com/world/1917123
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel) confirms that military personnel from a multinational stabilization force — excluding U.S. regular military combat troops — have physically entered the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip (not merely Israeli-controlled buffer zones, maritime areas, or airspace). The force must be part of the internationally agreed stabilization plan discussed at the Sharm el-Sheikh summit or authorized by a UN Security Council resolution. Egyptian forces that entered before October 31, 2025, do not count; only new deployments or entries of non-Egyptian multinational force contingents after October 31 qualify, OR additional Egyptian force entries as part of the formally constituted multinational stabilization force (as distinct from the hostage search operation). If reporting is ambiguous about whether forces entered Gaza proper versus buffer zones, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The deployment of a multinational stabilization force in Gaza is a critical precursor and indicator for whether U.S. troops might eventually enter Gaza. If the multinational force deploys successfully without U.S. ground presence, it reduces the likelihood that U.S. forces will need to enter. Conversely, if the multinational force fails to deploy, encounters significant obstacles, or if the security situation deteriorates, pressure could mount for a more direct U.S. military role — potentially including ground troops entering Gaza. The multinational force's progress is the most important near-term observable that would update forecasts on whether active regular U.S. military personnel will physically enter Gaza before December 31, 2025.

question: Will TIME's Person of the Year for 2025 be a human?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any human is named TIME's Person of the Year for 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, any person or group of people will count as “humans.” This includes explicitly named individuals and their titles such as "Taylor Swift" or "Bad Bunny", general public designations such as “You” (i.e., internet users), and collective entities such as “The Protester” or “The Silence Breakers.”

In the event that multiple entities are named TIME's 2025 Person of the Year, this market will resolve to "No" if at least one of them is not a human.

If, for any reason, the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a non-human entity (e.g., an AI system, a concept, or an organization) be featured on the cover of TIME magazine between October 3, 2025 and November 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME magazine's Person of the Year is typically announced in December, but TIME's regular cover stories throughout the year often signal cultural and political trends that influence the final selection. In recent years, AI systems and technologies have received extraordinary media attention—OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman was named on TIME's 2023 list of most influential people, and AI has been a dominant topic across major media outlets. If TIME devotes a cover story to a non-human entity such as an AI system, a movement, or a concept (rather than a specific person) in the weeks leading up to the Person of the Year decision, it could signal that the editorial team views a non-human entity as a serious contender for the 2025 Person of the Year. Historically, TIME has selected non-human entities on rare occasions: 'The Computer' was Machine of the Year in 1982, 'The Endangered Earth' was Planet of the Year in 1988, and 'Ebola Fighters' (a collective concept) was selected in 2014. However, the vast majority of selections have been individual humans or groups of humans. In 2024, Donald Trump was named Person of the Year for the second time. As of October 2025, no strong reporting suggests a non-human entity is the frontrunner for 2025.

Sources:
- TIME Person of the Year history: https://time.com/person-of-the-year/
- TIME 2024 Person of the Year (Trump): https://time.com/7203697/donald-trump-person-of-the-year-2024/
- TIME's 1982 Machine of the Year: https://time.com/vault/issue/1983-01-03/page/1/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 (inclusive), at least one cover of TIME magazine (U.S. edition) prominently features a non-human entity as its primary subject. A 'non-human entity' includes an AI system (e.g., ChatGPT, an AI agent), a concept (e.g., 'Artificial Intelligence,' 'Climate Change'), a non-human organism, or an abstract idea—but NOT a named individual person, a named group of specific people, or a collective human designation (e.g., 'The Protester'). Resolution will be based on the covers published on TIME's official website at https://time.com/vault/ during this period. If TIME's website is unavailable, consensus reporting from credible outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, NYT) about TIME covers during this window may be used instead.
subquestions.rationale: TIME's cover choices in the months leading up to the Person of the Year announcement reflect the editorial priorities and cultural narratives the magazine is tracking. If TIME features a non-human entity (such as AI) prominently on a cover in October 2025, it could indicate the magazine views non-human forces as defining the year—raising the probability that the Person of the Year could be non-human. Conversely, if all October covers focus on individual humans or human groups, this would be consistent with the historical pattern of selecting a human, keeping the base rate high for a human selection. This is a meaningful early indicator because it captures editorial direction at TIME itself, rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Trump release more Epstein files in 2025?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only files which were created prior to the start of the Trump Administration (January 20, 2025, 12:00 PM ET) will qualify. 

Announcements of declassifications or releases that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives hold a floor vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act (or a substantially similar bill compelling release of Epstein files) between October 1 and October 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Throughout 2025, bipartisan pressure has been building in Congress for the full release of Jeffrey Epstein-related files. Representatives Thomas Massie (R-KY) and Ro Khanna (D-CA) introduced a bipartisan resolution to compel the Trump administration to release all Epstein files within 30 days. A discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act was reported in early September 2025 to be only two signatures short of forcing a House floor vote, despite House Speaker Mike Johnson's efforts to block the measure (https://franknez.com/trump-administration-now-asks-judge-to-keep-two-names-private-in-the-epstein-files/). The House Oversight Committee released 33,295 pages of Epstein-related documents on September 2, 2025, but critics noted many were already public or heavily redacted (https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/epstein-files-us-house-panel-releases-first-batch-33000-investigation-documents-made-public/articleshow/113042044.cms). The Trump administration has resisted broader releases, with President Trump dismissing the issue as a 'Democrat hoax' (https://franknez.com/trump-now-continues-to-dismiss-epstein-files-as-a-hoax/). A successful floor vote would dramatically increase the likelihood of additional file releases before year-end, as it would create a formal congressional mandate.

Sources:
- FrankNez Media, Sept 6 2025: https://franknez.com/trump-administration-now-asks-judge-to-keep-two-names-private-in-the-epstein-files/
- Times of India, Sept 2 2025: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/epstein-files-us-house-panel-releases-first-batch-33000-investigation-documents-made-public/articleshow/113042044.cms
- FrankNez Media, Sept 3 2025: https://franknez.com/trump-now-continues-to-dismiss-epstein-files-as-a-hoax/
- We Got This Covered, Aug 29 2025: https://wegotthiscovered.com/news/can-she-be-counted-on-to-tell-the-truth-speaker-johnson-questions-whether-convicted-epstein-co-conspirator-maxwell-is-credible-witness/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives holds a floor vote (whether it passes or fails) on the Epstein Files Transparency Act, or any substantially similar standalone bill or resolution that would compel the executive branch to release or declassify documents related to Jeffrey Epstein's criminal activities, between October 1, 2025 and October 29, 2025 (inclusive). A 'floor vote' means a recorded vote of the full House chamber, not merely a committee vote. Resolution will be based on the official congressional record available at https://www.congress.gov/ and https://clerk.house.gov/Votes, supplemented by credible reporting from major outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, PBS, C-SPAN). If the vote is scheduled within this window but postponed beyond October 29, 2025, this question resolves No. Procedural votes (e.g., on a discharge petition motion) that directly concern bringing such a bill to the floor also count.
subquestions.rationale: The discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act was reported to be just two signatures short in early September 2025. If the petition succeeds and a floor vote occurs, it would create strong legislative pressure—and potentially a legal mandate—for the Trump administration to release additional Epstein files before the end of 2025. Conversely, if Speaker Johnson continues to successfully block a floor vote, the administration faces less institutional pressure to act. This is a meaningful leading indicator because the ultimate question asks whether files are released between August 25 and December 31, 2025, and congressional action (or inaction) in October would significantly influence whether that happens. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely differ on whether Congress will force the administration's hand.

question: Trump imposes tariff on semiconductors by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action enacting a tariff on imports of semiconductors into the United States by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only tariffs specifically targeting semiconductors will qualify. For example, a general tariff (tariffs on all imports into the U.S.) or country-specific tariff (tariffs on all imports from China) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs on semiconductors from a specific country will qualify.

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publish or leak a specific proposed tariff rate and timeline for semiconductor-specific tariffs between October 24 and November 23, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Trump has repeatedly signaled his intent to impose tariffs specifically on semiconductor imports. On August 6, 2025, he announced a planned 100% tariff on imported chips, with exemptions for companies manufacturing in the U.S. (https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/us-to-impose-100-tariff-on-semiconductor-imports-says-trump-7058157). On September 5, 2025, Trump softened this to a 'fairly substantial' tariff without specifying a rate or timeline (https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2025/09/05/brace-for-impact-trump-to-slap-fairly-substantial-tariffs-on-semiconductor-imports/). On September 26–27, 2025, reports emerged that the administration was considering a 25% tariff on chip-related imports (with lower rates for allied nations) and a 1:1 domestic-to-imported chip production ratio requirement (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-plans-to-require-a-11-ratio-of-domestically-made-to-imported-chips-wsj-reports/articleshow/113687345.cms; https://www.econotimes.com/Trump-Administration-Weighs-Tariffs-on-Electronics-Based-on-Chip-Content-1685891). As of late October 2025, no formal executive order, proclamation, or Federal Register notice has been issued establishing a semiconductor-specific tariff rate or effective date. The progression from vague announcements to more concrete policy proposals (like the 1:1 ratio and 25% rate) suggests the administration is refining its approach, but the exact rate, structure, and timeline remain unannounced.

Sources:
- NDTV: https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/us-to-impose-100-tariff-on-semiconductor-imports-says-trump-7058157
- Malay Mail: https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2025/09/05/brace-for-impact-trump-to-slap-fairly-substantial-tariffs-on-semiconductor-imports/
- Economic Times: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-plans-to-require-a-11-ratio-of-domestically-made-to-imported-chips-wsj-reports/articleshow/113687345.cms
- EconoTimes: https://www.econotimes.com/Trump-Administration-Weighs-Tariffs-on-Electronics-Based-on-Chip-Content-1685891
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive), the Trump administration or a senior administration official (President, Commerce Secretary, USTR, or White House spokesperson) publicly announces, or credible major news outlets (e.g., Wall Street Journal, Reuters, Bloomberg, New York Times, Washington Post) report based on official documents or named sources, a specific proposed tariff rate (a numerical percentage) AND a proposed timeline or effective date for a tariff that specifically targets semiconductor imports. Both a specific rate and a specific timeline/effective date must be disclosed. Vague statements like 'fairly substantial' or 'very shortly' without a numerical rate and date do not qualify. The announcement does not need to be a final enacted tariff — a formal proposed rule, executive order draft, or official policy announcement with both elements qualifies. Resolution will be based on reporting from major news outlets including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com), and official White House communications (https://www.whitehouse.gov).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Trump will formally enact a semiconductor-specific tariff by December 31, 2025. A key precursor to formal enactment is the announcement of a concrete policy with a specific rate and timeline. As of late October, Trump has made multiple statements about semiconductor tariffs but without firm details sufficient to constitute a formal policy. If the administration publishes a specific rate and implementation date in the next month, this strongly signals that formal enactment before year-end is likely. Conversely, if the administration continues to speak in vague terms without concrete details through late November, it becomes much less likely that a formal tariff could be enacted by December 31, given the typical regulatory and legal process required. This subquestion measures policy concreteness rather than just repeating the ultimate question with an earlier date.

question: US Treasury transactions on blockchain in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Department of the Treasury sends any funds or assets via a blockchain between February 4, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes", the payment must be a publicly announced, official transaction involving the sending of assets or funds; exploratory or experimental transactions will not count toward the resolution of this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of the Treasury publicly announce a pilot, program, or initiative to send funds or settle payments via blockchain by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. Department of the Treasury will send any funds or assets via a blockchain by end of 2025. As of September 2025, several federal agencies have moved toward blockchain adoption, but the Treasury itself has not yet executed an official on-chain payment. The U.S. Commerce Department announced on August 28, 2025 that it would publish GDP data on nine public blockchains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc.) in partnership with Chainlink, Pyth, Coinbase, Gemini, and Kraken (https://www.decrypt.co/283000/us-commerce-dept-puts-gdp-data-on-bitcoin-ethereum-and-solana-blockchains). Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said the program would eventually make blockchain data distribution available to the entire government. However, publishing data on-chain is fundamentally different from sending funds or assets on-chain.

The Treasury has been active in the broader crypto/blockchain policy space: it issued a request for comment on the GENIUS Act stablecoin legislation (comments due October 17, 2025), published a primer on stablecoins, and OFAC has sanctioned blockchain addresses (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-4-5765498/). New Treasury regulations on August 15, 2025 increased oversight of stablecoins (https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/08/blockchain-trilemma-cryptocurrency-platforms-could-scale-while-ensuring-adequate-security-and-decentralization-analysis/). The Deploying American Blockchains Act passed the House in June 2025 and awaits Senate approval, which would authorize Commerce to lead federal blockchain policy.

While the broader Trump administration is crypto-friendly — creating a Bitcoin reserve, stockpiling ETH and SOL, signing a stablecoin law, and appointing crypto-friendly agency heads — the Treasury specifically sending funds on-chain would be a distinct escalation. An announcement of such a program or pilot in September 2025 would be a strong leading indicator that an actual transaction could occur before year-end.

Sources:
- Decrypt, "US Commerce Dept. Puts GDP Data on Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana Blockchains" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.decrypt.co/283000/us-commerce-dept-puts-gdp-data-on-bitcoin-ethereum-and-solana-blockchains
- JD Supra, "Weekly Blockchain Blog - August 2025 #4" (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-4-5765498/
- Business Standard, "US govt puts GDP data on the public blockchain in Trump's crypto push" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.business-standard.com/technology/tech-news/us-government-puts-gdp-data-on-blockchain-trump-crypto-push-125082800550_1.html
- Crowdfund Insider, "Blockchain Trilemma" (Aug 28, 2025): https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/08/blockchain-trilemma-cryptocurrency-platforms-could-scale-while-ensuring-adequate-security-and-decentralization-analysis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of the Treasury (including sub-agencies such as the Bureau of the Fiscal Service, but excluding OFAC sanctions actions and excluding the Commerce Department or other non-Treasury agencies) publicly announces a program, pilot, or initiative specifically designed to send, disburse, or settle government funds or financial assets using blockchain technology. The announcement must come from an official Treasury source (e.g., press release on https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases, official statements by the Treasury Secretary or other senior Treasury officials) or be confirmed by a consensus of at least two credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, Wall Street Journal). Merely publishing data on-chain, issuing regulatory guidance about blockchain, or sanctioning blockchain addresses does not count. The announcement must describe a program intended to move actual funds or financial assets (not just data or hashes) on a blockchain. If no such announcement is made by October 1, 2025, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Treasury will actually send funds on blockchain by end of 2025. A Treasury announcement of a blockchain payments program or pilot in September would be the strongest near-term leading indicator, since any actual transaction would almost certainly be preceded by a public announcement. The broader federal government's rapid adoption of blockchain (Commerce publishing GDP data on-chain, the Deploying American Blockchains Act, crypto-friendly executive actions) creates a plausible pathway, but Treasury sending funds is a distinct and higher bar. If forecasters disagree on the ultimate question, learning whether Treasury has announced such a program by early October would significantly update their estimates — an announcement would make a year-end transaction much more likely, while silence would suggest the ultimate question is less likely to resolve Yes.

question: Will Trump establish a Gaza “Board of Peace” by March 31?

question: Will Pope Leo visit another country first?

subquestions.question: Will the Vatican officially announce a specific date for Pope Leo XIV's visit to Turkey (for the Council of Nicaea anniversary) before October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

Cardinal Bechara Boutros Rai stated the Lebanon visit would happen 'anytime from now until December,' and several sources have linked Lebanon and Turkey as part of a broader first international tour. As of October 1, 2025, the Vatican has not publicly confirmed exact dates for any of these trips. If the Vatican formally announces a date for the Turkey visit (expected for late November), this would strongly indicate that Turkey — not Lebanon — could be the pope's first foreign visit, since the Nicaea anniversary event has a fixed calendar anchor. Conversely, if no Turkey date is announced by end of October, it may suggest the trip is delayed or that Lebanon could come first.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), the Vatican (via the Holy See Press Office, Vatican News, or an official papal statement) publicly announces a specific date or date range for Pope Leo XIV's visit to Turkey. subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks which country Pope Leo XIV will visit first (outside Italy) before December 2025. Turkey has been a leading candidate because of the fixed 1,700th anniversary of the Council of Nicaea in late November. If the Vatican confirms specific dates for a Turkey trip in October, this is strong evidence that Turkey will be the first country visited — or at minimum that Turkey is on a very near-term schedule that could precede or follow a Lebanon visit. The timing of this announcement is a key early indicator: a confirmed Turkey date by end of October would narrow the possibilities significantly, while absence of confirmation might suggest delays or that Lebanon could come first. This is a genuinely different observable (an official scheduling announcement) rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

question: Will China lift rare earths export ban by December 31?
description:
On April 4, China implemented a series of restrictions on the export of a variety of rare earth metals. You can read more about that here: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/13/business/china-rare-earths-exports.html

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Chinese government officially lifts, removes, or reduces any of the export restrictions placed on rare earth metals on April 4, between July 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The issuance of a qualifying official act by China within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, even if the lifting or reduction of the stated export ban does not come into effect until after this market's resolution date.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and China announce a new bilateral trade agreement or framework that explicitly addresses rare earth export controls between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
China imposed export licensing restrictions on seven rare earth elements (samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium) and related magnets on April 4, 2025, as part of escalating trade tensions with the United States. These restrictions created significant supply chain disruptions globally. A temporary US-China trade deal reached in mid-2025 led to some improvement in shipments, with Beijing promising to resume rare earth exports to the US in exchange for Washington lifting certain tech-export restrictions (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508220340/china-tightens-controls-on-rare-earths). However, in August 2025, China further tightened oversight by issuing new regulations requiring monthly reporting to a government-run tracking system and assigning production quotas, effective July 28 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508220340/china-tightens-controls-on-rare-earths). China's approach has been selective — it reportedly lifted restrictions for India following diplomatic talks in August 2025, though actual shipments have been slow to materialize (https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/world/china-yet-to-resume-rare-earth-exports-to-india-despite-wang-yi-s-assurance-ev-makers-face-crunch-report-13491841.html). The broader US-China trade relationship remains contentious, with tariffs and counter-tariffs still in effect. Any new bilateral agreement addressing rare earths would be a strong signal that China may formally lift or reduce the April 4 export restrictions before December 31, 2025.

Sources:
- Morningstar: China Tightens Controls on Rare Earths (2025-08-22): https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508220340/china-tightens-controls-on-rare-earths
- MoneyControl: China yet to resume rare earth exports to India (2025-09-11): https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/world/china-yet-to-resume-rare-earth-exports-to-india-despite-wang-yi-s-assurance-ev-makers-face-crunch-report-13491841.html
- Down to Earth: Beijing's rare earth weapon (2025-08-21): https://www.downtoearth.org.in/energy/beijing-s-rare-earth-weapon-a-new-oil-shock-for-the-green-age
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025, the United States and China publicly announce a new bilateral trade agreement, trade deal, framework, or joint statement that explicitly mentions rare earth export controls, rare earth licensing, or rare earth trade facilitation. The announcement must come from official US government sources (e.g., the White House, US Trade Representative, US Department of Commerce, or US State Department) or official Chinese government sources (e.g., China's Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or State Council), or be confirmed by a consensus of at least three credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, NYT, WSJ). A mere extension or continuation of an existing temporary deal without new terms specifically addressing rare earths does not qualify. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2025, this question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Office of the US Trade Representative: https://ustr.gov/
- White House statements: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- China Ministry of Commerce: http://english.mofcom.gov.cn/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether China will lift rare earth export restrictions by December 31, 2025. The April 4 restrictions were largely imposed in the context of US-China trade tensions, and the most likely path to a formal lifting of the ban is through a bilateral US-China trade agreement. A new deal or framework announced in October that explicitly addresses rare earths would be a very strong leading indicator that the restrictions will be formally lifted before the end of the year. Conversely, the absence of such an agreement in October — with only two months remaining — would suggest the restrictions are unlikely to be lifted by December 31. This subquestion is meaningfully different from the ultimate question because it asks about the diplomatic precondition (a bilateral agreement) rather than the final regulatory action (lifting the ban).

question: OpenAI becomes a for-profit in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI shifts from its current capped-profit corporation structure to a for-profit model by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Any form of fully for-profit organization—including a Benefit Corporation (B-Corp), Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), or a modification to its existing structure to remove profit caps—will suffice for a "Yes" resolution.

If the OpenAI non-profit relinquishes control over the for-profit business, this will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

An announcement indicating that OpenAI is merely considering the shift will not suffice; the change must officially occur.

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the California or Delaware Attorney General publicly approve or sign off on OpenAI's proposed restructuring into a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) by October 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In May 2025, OpenAI announced it would abandon its original plan to become a fully for-profit entity and instead convert its for-profit arm into a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) while keeping the nonprofit board in control. However, this restructuring requires approval from the Attorneys General of both California (where OpenAI's nonprofit is incorporated) and Delaware (where the for-profit entity is incorporated). As of late September 2025, these approvals have not yet been publicly confirmed. California Attorney General Rob Bonta has been actively scrutinizing the deal, and Delaware's AG has also been involved in discussions. The approval process is a critical gating factor: without AG sign-off, the restructuring cannot be finalized. OpenAI's $30 billion investment from SoftBank and other funding rounds have been tied to completing this corporate restructuring. Reports from May 2025 indicated that OpenAI was in 'constructive dialogue' with both AGs, but no formal public approval had been announced as of the information available.

Sources:
- Investopedia: OpenAI Scraps For-Profit Plans (2025-05-06): https://www.investopedia.com/openai-scraps-for-profit-plans-11734194
- Engadget: OpenAI's new for-profit plan leaves many unanswered questions (2025-05-06): https://www.engadget.com/ai/openais-new-for-profit-plan-leaves-many-unanswered-questions-193048498.html
- TechCrunch: OpenAI expects to cut share of revenue it pays Microsoft by 2030 (2025-05-07): https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/07/openai-expects-to-cut-share-of-revenue-it-pays-microsoft-by-2030/
- Futurism: OpenAI Forced to Abandon Plans to Become For-Profit (2025-05-06): https://futurism.com/openai-forced-abandon-for-profit
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-25 (inclusive), either the California Attorney General or the Delaware Attorney General publicly announces approval of, or formal non-objection to, OpenAI's proposed restructuring of its for-profit arm into a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC). Evidence of such approval may include an official press release from either AG's office, a court filing reflecting the approval, or an official OpenAI announcement citing the AG approval, corroborated by credible reporting from sources such as Reuters, Bloomberg, the New York Times, TechCrunch, or the Wall Street Journal. If no such public approval or sign-off is reported by 11:59 PM ET on October 25, 2025, this question resolves No. If reporting is ambiguous (e.g., 'discussions are ongoing' without a clear approval), this resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- California Attorney General's office: https://oag.ca.gov/
- Delaware Attorney General's office: https://attorneygeneral.delaware.gov/
- OpenAI's official blog: https://openai.com/blog
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
subquestions.rationale: Attorney General approval is the most critical procedural prerequisite for OpenAI's restructuring to be finalized. The ultimate question asks whether OpenAI becomes for-profit by the end of 2025, and the proposed PBC conversion (which removes profit caps and qualifies under the ultimate question's resolution criteria) cannot officially take effect without AG sign-off from California and/or Delaware. If AG approval happens in October, it strongly signals that the full conversion will be completed before the ultimate question's deadline. Conversely, if approval has still not occurred by late October, there is much less time for the restructuring to be finalized by late October 2025 (the ultimate question's end date). This is a genuinely different observable event from the ultimate question itself — it tracks a specific regulatory milestone rather than the corporate conversion itself.

question: Evidence Trump went to Epstein's Island made public in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House Oversight Committee or any other congressional committee publicly release a new batch of Epstein-related documents between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Throughout 2025, U.S. congressional committees have been reviewing and periodically releasing portions of an estimated 100,000+ pages of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein's sex trafficking case. In September 2025, Democrats on the relevant committees released documents that included Epstein's calendar entries mentioning Elon Musk and flight logs naming various public figures (https://in-cyprus.philenews.com/international/leaked-documents-reveal-planned-visit-by-elon-musk-to-jeffrey-epsteins-private-island/). The Department of Justice has been sending tranches of documents to the House Oversight Committee, and the FBI has categorized unreleased evidence including logbooks of visitors to Epstein's Little Saint James Island (https://www.alternet.org/trump-nervous-epstein-release/). New York Times correspondent Maggie Haberman reported in August 2025 that the Trump administration was nervous about upcoming releases, with the DOJ expecting 'unfavorable coverage' (https://www.alternet.org/trump-nervous-epstein-release/). As of late October 2025, not all documents have been made public, and additional releases are anticipated. These document releases are the primary mechanism through which new evidence about Trump's potential visits to Epstein's island could emerge.

Sources:
- Alternet, August 2025: https://www.alternet.org/trump-nervous-epstein-release/
- In-Cyprus / Philenews, September 2025: https://in-cyprus.philenews.com/international/leaked-documents-reveal-planned-visit-by-elon-musk-to-jeffrey-epsteins-private-island/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. House Oversight Committee, the Senate Judiciary Committee, or any other congressional committee publicly releases or makes available to the public a new batch of documents (not previously released) related to Jeffrey Epstein's criminal case, estate, or associated investigations. 'Publicly releases' means the documents are posted on an official government website, shared with the press in a manner that makes them broadly accessible, or officially published through congressional proceedings. Resolution will be based on credible news reporting from major outlets (e.g., New York Times, Washington Post, CNN, AP, Reuters) or official congressional press releases. If no new batch of Epstein-related documents is released by any congressional committee during this window, the question resolves No. Individual leaks or unofficial disclosures do not count unless they originate from a congressional committee's official action.
subquestions.rationale: The primary pathway by which evidence of Trump visiting Epstein's island could become public is through the ongoing congressional document releases. The FBI's categorized evidence reportedly includes visitor logbooks for Little Saint James Island. If a new batch of documents is released in November 2025, it materially increases the probability that evidence placing Trump on the island could emerge before the ultimate question's December 31, 2025 deadline. Conversely, if document releases stall or cease, it becomes less likely that new evidence will surface in time. This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable process variable — the cadence of congressional document releases — that is a leading indicator for whether the ultimate question resolves Yes.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate at its September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has held the federal funds rate steady at 4.25%–4.50% for the first five meetings of 2025 (January, March, May, June, and July). At the July 30, 2025 meeting, two FOMC members (Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and Governor Christopher Waller) dissented, calling for a quarter-point cut, indicating growing internal support for easing. As of early August 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool showed approximately a 60% probability of at least a quarter-point cut at the September meeting. Forbes reported in August 2025 that markets expect a September 17 rate cut, with further cuts possible in October and December. The Invesco Conservative Income Fund Q2 2025 commentary (published September 2, 2025) expected two 0.25% rate cuts beginning in October, implying a pause in September. The September FOMC meeting is the first of the three meetings addressed by the ultimate question ('cut-pause-pause'), and its outcome directly determines whether the 'cut-pause-pause' pattern remains possible.

Sources:
- Barron's, "Stocks Are Steady After Fed Keeps Rates on Pause" (July 30, 2025): https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/fed-meeting-interest-rate-decision-today-july-2025
- Forbes, "What To Expect On Interest Rates For The Remainder Of 2025" (August 3, 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/08/03/what-to-expect-on-interest-rates-for-the-remainder-of-2025/
- Seeking Alpha, "Invesco Conservative Income Fund Q2 2025 Commentary" (September 2, 2025): https://seekingalpha.com/article/4750000-invesco-conservative-income-fund-q2-2025-commentary
- Federal Reserve FOMC Calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
- Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate, as announced in the FOMC statement following the September 16-17, 2025 meeting, is lower than the upper bound prior to that meeting (currently 4.50%). It resolves No if the upper bound remains at 4.50% or is raised. The resolution window is between 2025-09-05 and 2025-09-30. Resolution is based on the official FOMC statement published at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and the federal funds rate target published at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm. If the September 16-17 FOMC meeting is postponed beyond September 30, 2025, or no statement is released by that date, this question resolves No. Emergency rate actions taken outside the regularly scheduled September 16-17 meeting do not count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will follow a 'cut-pause-pause' pattern across its September, October, and December 2025 meetings. The September meeting is the first of these three decisions. If the Fed does NOT cut in September, the 'cut-pause-pause' outcome becomes impossible, and the ultimate question resolves to a different combination. If the Fed DOES cut, the 'cut-pause-pause' pattern remains viable. This makes the September rate decision the most immediate and decisive indicator for the ultimate question. Two forecasters who disagree on whether the ultimate pattern will be 'cut-pause-pause' are very likely to disagree on whether a September cut will happen, making this a strong crux.

question: Will Russia capture Myrnohrad by September 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection between Vatutina Vulytsya and Puhachova Vulytsya located in Myrnohrad by September 30, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection station will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the intersection, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Intersection Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/myrnohrad+intersection+zoom.png

Intersection Location in Myrnohrad: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/myrnohrad+intersection.jpeg

Location on Google maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/qCLFQNiDKN2ABe5Q9

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.
