subquestions.question: Will a majority (at least 3 out of 5) of the Brazilian Supreme Court judges cast their votes in the Bolsonaro coup trial by September 9, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Brazil's Supreme Court has scheduled extraordinary sessions beginning September 2 to deliver its ruling on whether former president Jair Bolsonaro is guilty of plotting a coup after his 2022 electoral defeat. The sessions are scheduled for September 2, 3, 9, 10, and 12, 2025. A panel of five judges will decide the case. In Brazilian Supreme Court proceedings of this nature, each judge (ministro) reads their individual vote, which can take hours or even span multiple sessions. The rapporteur (Justice Alexandre de Moraes) typically votes first, followed by the other judges in order of seniority. The pace at which judges deliver their votes will determine how quickly the trial reaches a verdict. If at least three of the five judges have voted by September 9 — the third scheduled session day — the direction of the verdict would effectively be determined, even if the formal conclusion comes later. Given the complexity of the case and the lengthy nature of individual votes in Brazilian Supreme Court trials, it is uncertain whether three votes will be cast by that date.

Sources:
- AFP: "Brazil court to rule from Sept 2 in Bolsonaro coup trial" (2025-08-15) https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250815-brazil-court-to-rule-from-sept-2-in-bolsonaro-coup-trial
- Newsday: "What to know about Bolsonaro's trial" (2025-06-11) https://www.newsday.com/news/nation/what-to-know-about-bolsonaro-s-trial-now-that-he-has-testified-over-an-alleged-coup-plot-kv6bz2xh
- AFP: "Prosecutor asks Brazil's Supreme Court to find Bolsonaro guilty of coup" (2025-07-15) https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250715-prosecutor-asks-brazil-s-supreme-court-to-find-bolsonaro-guilty-of-coup
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-09 (inclusive), at least 3 out of the 5 judges on the Brazilian Supreme Court panel hearing the Bolsonaro coup trial (STF case related to the alleged January 8, 2023 coup plot) have publicly cast their individual votes (votos) during the scheduled extraordinary sessions. The question resolves No if fewer than 3 judges have cast their votes by the end of September 9, 2025 (23:59 UTC-3, Brasília time). Resolution will be based on official reporting from the Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) website (https://portal.stf.jus.br/) or credible news sources such as Reuters, AFP/France24, Folha de S.Paulo, or G1 Globo. If the sessions scheduled for September 2, 3, and/or 9 are postponed or cancelled entirely such that no voting occurs by September 9, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Bolsonaro will be found guilty by February 28, 2026. The voting sessions begin September 2, and if a majority of judges (3 of 5) have voted by September 9, this strongly indicates the trial is proceeding on schedule toward a verdict. More importantly, if 3 judges have voted, the direction of the verdict (guilty or not guilty) will be effectively determined, since 3 votes constitute a majority on the 5-judge panel. Knowing whether the voting has progressed this far — and early reporting on the direction of individual votes — would be a powerful near-term indicator of whether Bolsonaro will ultimately be found guilty. Conversely, if the trial stalls or is delayed (e.g., due to diplomatic pressure, procedural challenges, or requests for more time), fewer than 3 votes by September 9 would signal uncertainty about whether a verdict will come promptly.

question: Will any of the stolen Louvre jewels be returned by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any of the jewels stolen from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon are officially recovered by the listed date ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

A single item (e.g., one earring) will suffice regardless of if it is missing a diamond or other element; however, recovery of only a fragment or part of an item (for example, a loose stone or a piece of a crown) will not suffice

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Louvre or the French government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will French police publicly identify or arrest at least one suspect in the Louvre crown jewels heist by November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 19, 2025, four masked thieves executed a brazen daylight heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris, stealing eight pieces of historic crown jewelry from the Galerie d'Apollon in under seven minutes. The thieves used a truck-mounted cherry picker to access a second-floor window, smashed display cases with power tools, and fled on motorbikes. A ninth item—Empress Eugénie's crown—was dropped and recovered damaged near the museum.

As of October 20, 2025, no suspects have been arrested. The Paris prosecutor's office has launched a major investigation, with Interpol and neighboring countries alerted. Authorities suspect possible insider knowledge or a former contractor's involvement, and early reports indicate possible links to previous European high-value robberies. Forensic teams found traces of burnt fuel and metal filings near the entry point, and police are reviewing CCTV footage and interviewing staff.

Art recovery experts have warned that the jewels are likely to be dismantled and melted down within 24–48 hours if not recovered quickly. Chris Marinello, CEO of Art Recovery International, stated: 'They may catch the criminals but they won't recover the jewels.' However, art detective Arthur Brand described the recovery as a 'race against time,' suggesting a roughly one-week window before the pieces are destroyed.

Historically, in comparable high-profile European jewel heists—such as the 2019 Dresden Green Vault robbery—arrests came weeks to months after the crime. In that case, suspects were arrested in November 2020, over a year later, though some of the stolen items were eventually recovered as part of a plea deal.

Sources:
- Smithsonian Magazine, "Burglars Just Broke Into the Louvre and Stole Historic Crown Jewels in a Daring Daylight Heist" (2025-10-20): https://www.smithsonianmag.com
- Invezz, "Louvre Museum robbery shocks France as eight crown jewels vanish in minutes" (2025-10-20): https://invezz.com
- PEOPLE.com, "Expert Says Stolen Louvre Jewels Need to Be Recovered in 24-to-48 Hours Or They're 'Long Gone'" (2025-10-20): https://people.com
- CNN International, "Historic jewels stolen in 'national disaster' for France" (2025-10-20): https://www.cnn.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive), French law enforcement or the Paris prosecutor's office publicly confirms the identification by name or the arrest of at least one individual suspected of directly participating in the October 19, 2025 Louvre crown jewels heist. Resolution will be based on official statements from French law enforcement (e.g., Paris prosecutor's office, Police Nationale, or the French Ministry of Justice), or, in the absence of such statements, a consensus of at least two major credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AFP, Le Monde, BBC, CNN). Mere identification of 'persons of interest' without formal suspect designation or arrest does not count. If no suspect is publicly identified or arrested by 2025-11-15 23:59 UTC, this question resolves No.

Sources for resolution:
- Paris prosecutor's office official communications
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- AFP / France 24: https://www.france24.com
- Le Monde: https://www.lemonde.fr
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: Whether police identify or arrest suspects is a strong early indicator of whether the stolen jewels will be recovered by December 31, 2025. Historically, recovery of stolen art and jewels almost always follows the apprehension of suspects, either through seizure during arrest, negotiated returns as part of plea deals, or information extracted during interrogation. If no suspects are identified within the first month—a period when forensic evidence (CCTV, forensics from the abandoned equipment, witness accounts) is freshest—it becomes substantially less likely that the jewels will be recovered before year-end. Conversely, early arrests dramatically increase the probability of recovery, as police can execute search warrants and potentially recover items before they are dismantled. This question thus serves as a meaningful leading indicator that differentiates between a scenario where recovery is plausible and one where the jewels are likely 'long gone.'

question: U.S. x Iran Military Engagement by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Iran between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Iranian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Iranian land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage.

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; the Iranian Law Enforcement Command is a branch of the Iranian Armed Forces; all sub-branches of the Artesh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (including the Basij), and Law Enforcement Command are part of the Iranian Armed forces.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S.–Iran nuclear/diplomatic talks scheduled for early February 2026 fail to produce any agreed framework or joint statement by February 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of February 2026, the U.S. and Iran are engaged in high-stakes diplomatic negotiations over Iran's nuclear program, amid significant military tensions. Nuclear talks were initially scheduled for February 7, 2026, in Istanbul, with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as lead negotiators. Iran requested the venue be moved to Oman and limited to bilateral nuclear discussions only, excluding broader regional issues. The U.S. reportedly demands zero uranium enrichment, curbs on ballistic missiles, and an end to support for regional proxies, while Iran has offered flexibility on enrichment levels and surrendering 400 kg of highly enriched uranium.

These talks are taking place against a backdrop of escalating military confrontations: on February 3–4, 2026, the U.S. shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone near the USS Abraham Lincoln, and Iranian IRGC gunboats harassed a U.S.-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. These incidents followed U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear and military facilities in June 2025. President Trump has warned that military force remains an option if diplomacy fails, while Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei has cautioned that military action could trigger a 'regional war.'

The outcome of these diplomatic efforts is a critical indicator: a diplomatic breakdown would significantly raise the probability of a direct U.S.–Iran military engagement, while a successful framework would reduce tensions.

Sources:
- bne IntelliNews, "US fighter jet downs Iranian drone ahead of diplomatic talks," February 4, 2026: https://www.intellinews.com
- TEMPO.CO, "US Military Claims to Have Shot Down Iranian Drone in Arabian Sea," February 4, 2026: https://en.tempo.co
- defensescoop.com, "F-35C pilot downs Iranian drone to defend USS Abraham Lincoln, Centcom says," February 4, 2026: https://defensescoop.com
- Lloyd's List, "Tension flare as Iranian gunboats threaten to board US-flagged tanker," February 3, 2026: https://www.lloydslist.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-20 (inclusive), U.S.–Iran diplomatic talks (whether held in Oman, Turkey, or any other venue) fail to produce any publicly announced agreed framework, joint statement, or preliminary deal text. Specifically, 'failure to produce any agreed framework or joint statement' means that by 11:59 PM UTC on February 20, 2026, no official document, communiqué, or joint statement has been released by either the U.S. government (e.g., via the White House, State Department, or U.S. envoy) or the Iranian government (e.g., via the Foreign Ministry or official state media) confirming mutual agreement on any set of principles, terms, or next steps regarding nuclear negotiations. Unilateral statements from either side describing talks as 'productive' or 'ongoing' without a joint document do not count.

If talks are postponed entirely beyond February 20, 2026, or are cancelled, the question resolves Yes. If no talks were scheduled or attempted during this window, the question resolves Yes.

Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible international news sources, including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), official U.S. State Department statements (https://www.state.gov), and official Iranian government media (https://en.irna.ir).
subquestions.rationale: The trajectory of U.S.–Iran diplomacy is a critical leading indicator for military engagement. If negotiations collapse or fail to produce any framework, the risk of military confrontation rises substantially—President Trump has explicitly tied the threat of force to the failure of diplomacy, and Iran's Supreme Leader has warned of regional war. Conversely, a successful diplomatic output would signal de-escalation. The recent drone shootdown and maritime harassment incidents make a diplomatic breakdown more plausible and more consequential. Forecasters who disagree on whether a U.S.–Iran military engagement will occur by late February are likely to update significantly based on whether diplomacy yields any tangible output in the near term.

question: Will there be exactly 1 earthquake of magnitude 7.0 or higher worldwide by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 7.0 or higher that occur anywhere on Earth between October 13, 2025, 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will 3 or more earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher occur worldwide between November 13, 2025, and December 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether there will be *exactly* 1 earthquake of M7.0+ worldwide between October 13 and December 31, 2025. The global long-term average is roughly 15 M7.0+ earthquakes per year, or about 1.25 per month, meaning over an ~2.5-month window we'd expect around 3 M7.0+ events. Having exactly 1 would require a below-average period. A useful leading indicator is the rate of M6.0+ earthquakes, since elevated M6.0+ activity often correlates with (or precedes) M7.0+ events. The long-term average for M6.0+ earthquakes is roughly 120–150 per year, or about 6–7 per ~19-day window. If the rate of M6.0+ events is high in the first half of the remaining window, it suggests the seismic environment is active and having only exactly 1 M7.0+ event over the full period becomes less likely. Recent months have seen notable seismic activity: the July 2025 M8.8 Kamchatka earthquake generated thousands of aftershocks including a M7.8 event in September, and October 2025 saw M7.4 and M7.7 events (Philippines/Davao Oriental and South Atlantic). The USGS aftershock forecast for the Kamchatka sequence indicated a 24% chance of another M7+ event in the months ahead, with >99% probability of continued M5+ and M6+ activity (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us7000nkfz/oaf/commentary). The USGS significant earthquakes page (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php) and real-time earthquake map (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/map/) provide continuously updated data.

Sources:
- USGS Earthquake Hazards Program: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php
- USGS Real-time Earthquake Map: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/map/
- Newsweek on Kamchatka aftershock forecast: https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-1982345
- USGS Earthquake Statistics (historical averages): https://www.usgs.gov/programs/earthquake-hazards/lists-maps-and-statistics
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if 3 or more earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or higher are recorded worldwide between November 13, 2025, and December 1, 2025 (inclusive of both dates, using UTC timestamps). The primary data source is the USGS Earthquake Catalog search (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/), using the following parameters: minimum magnitude 6.0, start date 2025-11-13T00:00:00 UTC, end date 2025-12-01T23:59:59 UTC. Only earthquakes listed by the USGS with a final or reviewed magnitude of 6.0 or greater count. If the USGS revises an earthquake's magnitude below 6.0 after initial reporting, it does not count. If the USGS catalog is temporarily unavailable at the time of resolution, the question may wait up to 7 days (until December 8, 2025) for the data to become available. If the USGS catalog remains unavailable, the EMSC (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre, https://www.emsc-csem.org/) will be used as a fallback source. The question resolves No if fewer than 3 such earthquakes are recorded in the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks about exactly 1 M7.0+ earthquake over a ~2.5-month window. M6.0+ seismicity serves as a leading indicator of M7.0+ activity: periods of elevated M6+ activity tend to produce more M7+ events, making 'exactly 1' less probable. If 3+ M6.0+ events occur in just the first ~19 days of the remaining window, it suggests heightened global seismicity and makes it more likely that multiple (not exactly 1) M7.0+ events will occur over the full period. Conversely, if the threshold is not met, it could suggest a quieter seismic period where exactly 1 M7.0+ becomes more plausible. This question is distinct from the ultimate question—it measures a different magnitude band over a different time window—yet is mechanistically related as a real-time barometer of global seismic energy release. The threshold of 3 is set somewhat below the long-term average (~6-7 for this window length) to avoid having a question that almost always resolves Yes, while still being informative.

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any bill with the effect of banning sitting members of the US congress from trading stocks is signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Rep. Anna Paulina Luna's discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) obtain at least 100 signatures by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 29-30, 2025, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) filed a discharge petition to force a House floor vote on the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908), a bill introduced by Rep. Tim Burchett (R-TN) in March 2025 that would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks, bonds, commodities, and other complex investment vehicles. A discharge petition requires 218 signatures to force a bill to the House floor for a vote. Discharge petitions are historically very difficult to complete — only a handful have succeeded in modern congressional history, because members of the majority party face intense pressure from leadership not to sign them. House Speaker Johnson has called the discharge petition a 'tool of the minority.' However, this petition has some notable tailwinds: President Trump has said he would 'absolutely' sign a stock trading ban, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly endorsed the concept in August 2025, and polling shows 86% public support for such a ban. Congress returned from its August recess on September 1, 2025, and faces a packed schedule including a September 30 government funding deadline, which may limit bandwidth for other legislative action. The signature count on the discharge petition in its first month will be a key early indicator of whether this bill has any realistic chance of passing in 2025.

Sources:
- One America News Network, "Rep. Luna introduces resolution to advance the End Congressional Stock Trading Act" (Aug 30, 2025): https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/
- Washington Examiner, "Anna Paulina Luna to force House vote on congressional stock trading ban" (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/congress/3233082/anna-paulina-luna-force-house-vote-congressional-stock-trading-ban/
- AP News, "Government shutdown looms as Congress returns" (Aug 31, 2025): https://apnews.com/article/congress-returns-recess-shutdown-funding-deadline-d5e1c2a3f4b8
- Newsmax, "Rep. Luna Seeks Vote on Congress Stock Trading Ban" (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.newsmax.com/politics/congress-stock-trading-ban-luna/2025/08/29/id/1188890/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the discharge petition filed by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna for H.R. 1908 (End Congressional Stock Trading Act) accumulates at least 100 total signatures from members of the U.S. House of Representatives. The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. House Clerk's record of discharge petitions, available at https://clerk.house.gov/DischargePetition. If the House Clerk's website does not publish a timely count, resolution may rely on a consensus of credible reporting from sources such as the Associated Press, Reuters, The Hill, Politico, or C-SPAN. If the discharge petition is withdrawn or otherwise rendered moot before October 1, 2025, the question resolves No. If no credible source reports a signature count by October 1, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The discharge petition is the most concrete near-term procedural mechanism that could lead to a floor vote on a congressional stock trading ban in 2025. Reaching 100 signatures (roughly 46% of the 218 needed) within the first month would be an unusually strong signal of broad bipartisan support and momentum, suggesting the bill has a realistic path to passage. Historically, discharge petitions that fail to gain significant early traction almost never succeed. Conversely, if the petition stalls well below 100 signatures, it would strongly suggest that House leadership will successfully block the bill and that no stock trading ban will become law in 2025. This subquestion is thus a meaningful early indicator: two forecasters who disagree on whether a ban passes in 2025 likely disagree on whether the petition can build critical mass.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate at the October 28-29, 2025, FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled to meet on October 28-29, 2025. As of mid-October, market expectations assign a 100% probability to a rate cut at this meeting, following the September 2025 rate cut of 25 basis points. The ultimate question resolves 'No' (i.e., something happens) if, among other conditions, the Fed cuts rates twice between September 23 and December 31, 2025. The September cut already counts as one cut. If the Fed cuts again in October, that would constitute the second cut, satisfying one of the 'No' resolution conditions of the ultimate question. The current fed funds rate target range is 4.00%-4.25% after the September cut. Labor market weakness (only 22,000 jobs added in August, jobs falling in June for the first time in over four years) and ongoing government shutdown disruptions to economic data have bolstered the case for further easing, though core PCE inflation remains at 2.9%, above the 2% target. Fed officials are divided, with some favoring further cuts and others concerned about inflation risks from tariffs.

Sources:
- Investopedia, 'Next Fed Meeting: When It Is In October And What To Expect' (Sept 29, 2025): https://www.investopedia.com/next-federal-reserve-meeting-702702
- The Financial Express, 'All eyes on Jerome Powell's speech' (Oct 14, 2025): https://www.financialexpress.com/money/all-eyes-on-jerome-powells-speech-in-his-first-public-appearance-since-the-september-rate-cut-3704123/
- Investing.com, 'Market wagers of Hassett as next Fed Chair' (Oct 2, 2025): https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/market-wagers-of-hassett-as-next-fed-chair-gaining-traction-wolfe-analysts-say-93CH-3871234
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve announces a reduction in the federal funds rate target range at the conclusion of the October 28-29, 2025, FOMC meeting. The resolution window is from 2025-10-27 to 2025-10-30. Resolution will be based on the official FOMC statement published on the Federal Reserve's website at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm. The statement is typically released at 2:00 p.m. ET on the second day of the meeting (October 29, 2025). If the FOMC meeting is delayed or postponed beyond October 31, 2025, this question resolves No. A rate cut of any size (25 bps, 50 bps, etc.) counts. If the Fed holds rates steady or raises rates, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This is a direct indicator for one of the four 'No' resolution conditions of the ultimate question. The September 2025 cut already counts as the first cut. If the Fed cuts again at the October meeting, two of the required two cuts will have occurred, triggering the 'Fed cuts twice' condition and resolving the ultimate question to 'No.' Market pricing strongly implies a cut is coming, but confirming it is still informative because if the Fed surprisingly holds, the probability of 'Yes' on the ultimate question increases significantly (the remaining conditions—Trump announcing a Fed Chair pick, Powell saying 'Trump' at the October press conference, or Lisa Cook departing—would each need to be assessed independently). This subquestion is decidable within days and provides the single highest-information-value early signal for the ultimate question.

question: Will there be at least 500 measles cases in the U.S. in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter (see: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) at the resolution time. If the counter becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

Note: Only cases reported by the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter will qualify, regardless of reports from U.S. State agencies or other sources.

subquestions.question: Will the CDC measles case count for 2025 exceed 1,800 confirmed cases by December 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States is experiencing its largest measles outbreak in over three decades. As of November 13, 2025, the CDC reported 1,723 confirmed measles cases nationwide, with 87% linked to 45 outbreaks across 41 states. By November 21, 2025, the count had risen to 1,753. Active outbreaks continue in Utah, Arizona, South Carolina, and other states. The rate of new cases in late 2025 reflects the ongoing susceptibility of under-vaccinated communities and the effectiveness (or lack thereof) of containment efforts. The CDC's measles data page (https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) is the authoritative source for confirmed case counts.

The trajectory of the 2025 case count heading into the end of the year is a strong indicator of the outbreak momentum that will carry into 2026. If cases continue to accumulate rapidly through December 2025, it signals that transmission chains remain active and that the conditions for reaching 500 cases in 2026 are more favorable. Conversely, if the case count plateaus near 1,753, it would suggest containment efforts are succeeding and new outbreaks are less likely to emerge in early 2026.

Sources:
- CDC Measles Data Research: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
- The Boston Globe, Nov 18 2025: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/18/nation/cdc-links-measles-outbreaks-multiple-states/
- SheKnows, Nov 21 2025: https://www.sheknows.com/health-and-wellness/articles/measles-outbreak-2025-states/
- Scientific American, Nov 3 2025: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CDC Measles (Rubeola) case counter at https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html shows 1,801 or more confirmed measles cases for the year 2025 at any point between December 2, 2025 (start_date) and December 31, 2025 (end_date), inclusive. The CDC counter may update with a delay, so the relevant figure is the 2025 cumulative case count as displayed on the CDC page on or before December 31, 2025. If the CDC counter becomes unavailable, alternative credible sources such as state health department aggregations or the Johns Hopkins measles tracker (https://publichealth.jhu.edu/) may be used. If no reliable source can confirm the 2025 case count by December 31, 2025, the question resolves ambiguously.
subquestions.rationale: The momentum of measles cases at the end of 2025 is a direct indicator of whether the conditions exist for 500+ cases in 2026. With 1,753 cases as of late November 2025, reaching 1,800 by year-end would indicate that active transmission chains persist heading into 2026, that containment efforts are insufficient, and that under-vaccinated populations remain exposed. This ongoing outbreak activity—including active clusters in Utah, Arizona, and South Carolina—would carry directly into January 2026 and beyond. Additionally, the U.S. is on the verge of losing its measles elimination status (deadline ~January 20, 2026), and whether transmission continues unabated through December is a key indicator of 2026 outbreak risk. If the case count stalls well below 1,800, it suggests outbreaks are being contained, making 500 new cases in 2026 less likely.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025, still be in effect on October 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government entered a partial shutdown on October 1, 2025, after Congress failed to pass a spending bill. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) suspended all operations, including the release of the September Employment Situation report originally scheduled for October 3, 2025. The BLS confirmed it would halt all data collection, processing, and dissemination activities during the shutdown. Historical shutdowns have varied in duration: the 2013 shutdown lasted 16 days, and the 2018-2019 shutdown lasted 35 days. As of October 8, 2025, the shutdown is in its 8th day with no resolution in sight. The longer the shutdown persists, the less likely it is that BLS can resume operations, collect/process data, and release the Employment Situation report before the shutdown ends. Conversely, if the shutdown ends quickly, BLS would resume operations and might release the report after the shutdown concludes (resolving the ultimate question 'No'). If the shutdown drags on for weeks, there is a greater chance that Congress or the administration may find a way to authorize the release of already-collected data during the shutdown, or that BLS might release the report as part of a resumption that overlaps with continued shutdown conditions.

Sources:
- AFP: "US delays key jobs report due to government shutdown" (2025-10-03) https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251003-us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-to-government-shutdown
- Yahoo Finance: "The government shutdown is putting Friday's jobs report in jeopardy" (2025-10-01) https://finance.yahoo.com/news/the-government-shutdown-is-putting-fridays-jobs-report-in-jeopardy-174508556.html
- U.S. News: "Missing Data Leaves Economy 'Flying Blind'" (2025-10-06) https://www.usnews.com/news/economy/articles/2025-10-06/missing-data-leaves-economy-flying-blind
- OPM Operating Status page: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025, is still in effect (i.e., no appropriations legislation has been enacted to fund the affected agencies, and OPM has not announced the end of shutdown conditions) at any point during October 20, 2025 (Eastern Time). It resolves No if the shutdown has fully ended before the start of October 20, 2025 (i.e., funding has been restored and OPM has announced normal operations before midnight ET on October 19, 2025). A partial shutdown still counts as a shutdown being in effect. Resolution will be determined by checking the OPM Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/) and corroborated by credible news sources. If OPM's page is unavailable, a consensus of credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, major U.S. newspapers) reporting on the shutdown status as of October 20, 2025, will be used. The resolution window for determining the answer is between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-20.
subquestions.rationale: The duration of the shutdown is the key determinant of whether BLS releases the Employment Situation report during or after the shutdown. If the shutdown is still ongoing by October 20 (nearly three weeks in), it increases the probability that political or public pressure leads to some mechanism for releasing the jobs data while the government remains shut down (resolving the ultimate question Yes). Alternatively, a very long shutdown might mean BLS simply cannot release the report at all during the shutdown. If the shutdown ends quickly (before October 20), BLS would likely resume operations and release the report shortly after funding is restored, meaning the report comes out after the shutdown ends (resolving the ultimate question No). This subquestion about shutdown duration is a meaningful leading indicator because it differentiates between scenarios where the report is released during vs. after the shutdown, which is the crux of the ultimate question.

question: Lee Jun-seok in jail in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court issue an arrest warrant for Lee Jun-seok between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Lee Jun-seok (이준석) is a prominent South Korean conservative politician who formerly led the People Power Party (PPP) and later founded the Reform Party (개혁신당). Following the political upheaval surrounding former President Yoon Suk-yeol's martial law declaration in December 2024, South Korean prosecutors have been aggressively investigating political figures associated with the former administration and conservative opposition. Special counsel investigations have expanded significantly in 2025, with former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo indicted on August 29, 2025, former First Lady Kim Keon-hee arrested and indicted on corruption charges, and raids conducted on the Justice Ministry and Supreme Prosecutors' Office on August 25, 2025 (https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10422895). Lee Jun-seok has been a controversial figure in South Korean politics, having clashed with both the ruling Democratic Party and factions within his own conservative camp. As of late August 2025, the political environment in South Korea is marked by extensive judicial proceedings against conservative politicians linked to the Yoon administration, with President Trump publicly criticizing what he called 'ruthless political persecution' of the opposition (https://www.theblaze.com/news/trump-warns-revolution-south-korea-summit). Whether prosecutors seek an arrest warrant for Lee Jun-seok would be a key precursor to any imprisonment.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald, "Special counsel raids Justice Ministry, Supreme Prosecutors' Office" (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10422895
- Al Jazeera, "South Korea indicts former first lady for bribery, ex-PM over martial law" (Aug 29, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/29/south-korea-indicts-former-first-lady-for-bribery-ex-pm-over-martial-law
- TheBlaze, "Trump warns of 'revolution' in South Korea" (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.theblaze.com/news/trump-warns-revolution-south-korea-summit
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), a South Korean court issues an arrest warrant for Lee Jun-seok (이준석, the politician who formerly led the People Power Party and founded the Reform Party) on any criminal charges. Resolution will be based on official reporting from Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), or other major South Korean English-language news outlets confirming that a warrant has been issued. If no credible reports of an arrest warrant emerge by October 1, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No. An arrest warrant that is requested by prosecutors but denied by the court does not count. Only a warrant that is formally issued (approved) by a court qualifies.
subquestions.rationale: An arrest warrant is the most immediate legal precursor to imprisonment. If Lee Jun-seok is to serve any time in custody before December 31, 2025, prosecutors would likely need to secure a warrant in the near term, given the typical timeline of South Korean criminal proceedings. The current political environment features aggressive prosecution of conservative figures, so monitoring whether Lee Jun-seok specifically becomes a target of arrest proceedings in September 2025 is a highly informative early indicator. If a warrant is issued in September, the probability of him being in jail before year-end increases substantially; if no warrant materializes, it significantly reduces the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy be in the top 5 of the overall medal count at the 2026 Winter Olympics as of the end of events on February 16, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Italy is the host nation of the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics (February 6–22, 2026). Historically, host nations often perform better than their baseline, benefiting from home-crowd support, familiarity with venues, and additional qualification spots. As of February 7, 2026, Italy had already won 1 gold, 1 silver, and 1 bronze, placing it among the early leaders (GEO TV, 2026-02-07). However, pre-Games projections from Bleacher Report and prediction markets gave Italy only about a 2% chance of leading the overall medal table, with Norway, the United States, and Germany considered the top three contenders (Bleacher Report, 2026-02-05; sportsbookreview.com, 2026-01-29). In the 2022 Beijing Olympics, Italy won 17 total medals (2 gold, 7 silver, 8 bronze), finishing 8th overall. For Italy to finish second overall in the 2026 Games, it would likely need to sustain a top-5 pace through the middle of the Games. Italy's strongest events include alpine skiing, short track speed skating, speed skating, biathlon, and luge. By February 16, roughly two-thirds of the 116 medal events will have been contested, providing a strong signal about Italy's trajectory.

Sources:
- GEO TV, "Which country has most medals in 2026 Winter Olympics medal race?" (2026-02-07): https://www.geo.tv/latest/588491-which-country-has-most-medals-in-2026-winter-olympics-medal-race
- Bleacher Report, "Medal Tally Olympics 2026 Predictions" (2026-02-05): https://www.bleacherreport.com/articles/10147474-medal-tally-olympics-2026-predictions-for-milano-cortinas-final-winter-medal-count
- sportsbookreview.com, "Winter Olympics Medal Odds 2026" (2026-01-29): https://www.sportsbookreview.com/predictions/winter-olympics/medal-odds/
- AP, "Italians collect medals on a feel-good first day" (2026-02-07): https://apnews.com/article/2026-olympics-italy-medals-day-one
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Italy is ranked 5th or higher in total medal count (gold + silver + bronze) among all nations at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, based on results from all medal events completed between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-16 (inclusive). The ranking is determined by total medals; in case of a tie in total medals, the nation with more gold medals is ranked higher (consistent with the ultimate question's tiebreaker rules). Resolution will be based on the official medal standings published by the International Olympic Committee at https://www.olympics.com/ as they stand at the end of the competition day on February 16, 2026. If the IOC website is unavailable, the medal count reported by CBS Sports (https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/medal-count/) or NBC Olympics (https://www.nbcolympics.com/medals) may be used as a fallback. If the Games are cancelled or suspended before February 16, 2026, this question resolves based on medals awarded in completed events up to that point; if no events have been completed, the question resolves as No.
subquestions.rationale: Italy finishing second in the overall medal count is a relatively unlikely outcome based on pre-Games projections; the favorites are Norway, the US, and Germany. For Italy to achieve second place by the end of the Games on Feb 22, it would almost certainly need to be in the top 5 through the midpoint of the Games (Feb 16). This subquestion tracks whether Italy is on a medal-winning pace consistent with a potential second-place finish. If Italy is not in the top 5 by Feb 16, it is very unlikely to leapfrog multiple powerhouse nations in the final week. Conversely, a top-5 position at the midpoint would significantly raise the probability of a second-place finish. This is a meaningfully different question from the ultimate question because it asks about a broader threshold (top 5 vs. exactly 2nd) at an earlier date, providing an intermediate signal.

question: James Comey indicted before October?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any Federal or State jurisdiction of the United States formally charges or otherwise announces a criminal indictment of James Comey between July 8 and September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purposes of this market the District of Columbia and any county, municipality, or other subdivision of a State shall be included within the definition of a State.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from US governmental sources, however a wide consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury in a jurisdiction outside of Washington, D.C. (such as the Southern District of Florida) be reported to have convened or be convening to hear evidence related to James Comey before September 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Former FBI Director James Comey has been reportedly under criminal investigation by the Trump DOJ for alleged wrongdoing related to the Steele dossier and the Russiagate investigation. As of mid-2025, multiple reports indicate that the DOJ is considering bringing a criminal conspiracy case against Comey and former CIA Director John Brennan. A key strategic question is venue: Fox News legal analyst Gregg Jarrett argued in July 2025 that seeking an indictment from a D.C. grand jury would be 'a fool's errand' due to the political leanings of D.C. jurors, and separate reporting from July 2025 indicated that the DOJ may attempt to use Florida jurisdiction to obtain a more favorable jury pool. The failure of a D.C. grand jury to indict Sean Charles Dunn on felony charges for throwing a sandwich at a federal agent in August 2025 further highlighted the challenge of obtaining indictments in D.C. for cases perceived as politically charged. If a grand jury outside D.C. is convened to hear evidence against Comey, it would be a strong leading indicator that an indictment is imminent.

Sources:
- Gregg Jarrett on DC jury challenges: https://conservativenewstoday.com/gregg-jarrett-explains-why-a-dc-jury-handling-comey-or-brennan-case-might-be-a-fools-errand/
- Trump DOJ criminal conspiracy case report: https://therussophile.org/a-new-age-of-accountability-trump-doj-preps-criminal-conspiracy-case-against-russiagate-architects.html
- DC grand jury declines sandwich thrower indictment: https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/27/grand-jury-wont-indict-alleged-dc-sub-sandwich-thrower/75434567007/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-20 (inclusive), at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., Associated Press, Reuters, New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Fox News, CNN, NBC News, ABC News, CBS News) report that a federal grand jury in a U.S. judicial district outside of the District of Columbia has been convened, is hearing evidence, or has heard evidence specifically related to potential criminal charges against James Comey (the former FBI Director). Reports citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter are sufficient, provided at least two independent outlets corroborate the claim. The question resolves No if no such reporting emerges by end of day (11:59 PM ET) on September 20, 2025. If the reporting is ambiguous about whether the grand jury is specifically hearing evidence related to Comey (as opposed to a broader investigation not targeting him), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The venue choice for a potential Comey indictment is a critical procedural step that must precede any indictment. Reports suggest the DOJ may avoid D.C. in favor of Florida or another jurisdiction. Confirmation that a grand jury outside D.C. is hearing evidence against Comey would be a strong leading indicator that an indictment is forthcoming within the ultimate question's timeframe. This is a distinct observable event from the indictment itself — it tracks the prosecutorial machinery rather than the final charging decision — and would significantly update forecasters' beliefs about whether an indictment will occur before the September 30 deadline.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool show a probability of 50% or higher for a 'no change' (pause) outcome at the December 9–10, 2025 FOMC meeting as of December 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
After the October 29, 2025 FOMC meeting, the Federal Reserve cut rates by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75%–4.00%. However, Chair Jerome Powell explicitly warned that a December rate cut is 'not a foregone conclusion—far from it,' noting a 'growing chorus' within the FOMC supporting a pause. The vote was 10-2, with dissents in both directions (one for a larger cut, one for no change), revealing unusual internal division. Following Powell's remarks, Fed funds futures shifted sharply, with the implied probability of a December cut dropping significantly and Treasury yields rising above 4% on the 10-year note (Yahoo Finance, October 30, 2025). The CME FedWatch Tool, which derives probabilities from federal funds futures contracts, is the standard market-based gauge for upcoming FOMC rate decisions. As of late October 2025, the tool showed reduced expectations for a December cut compared to pre-meeting levels. The key question for the ultimate 'Pause-Pause-Pause' scenario is whether the first meeting (December 9–10) will indeed be a pause, and market-implied probabilities in the days leading up to that meeting are a strong leading indicator.

Sources:
- Yahoo Finance, 'Powell's December Warning Exposes Hardening Divisions at Fed' (October 30, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powell-december-warning-exposes-hardening-divisions-fed-211500123.html
- Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, 'Federal Reserve Cuts Rate for Second Month, Ends Quantitative Tightening' (October 30, 2025): https://www.chosun.com/english/
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
- FOMC calendar and statements: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, on December 5, 2025, the CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) shows a probability of 50% or higher that the FOMC will keep the federal funds rate target range unchanged (i.e., at 3.75%–4.00%) at the December 9–10, 2025 meeting. The probability should be read from the CME FedWatch Tool's main page for the December 2025 FOMC meeting at any point during the trading day on December 5, 2025 (Eastern Time). If the CME FedWatch Tool is unavailable on December 5, 2025, a screenshot or archived version from a reliable financial news outlet (e.g., CNBC, Bloomberg, Reuters) reporting the same Fed funds futures-implied probabilities for the December meeting on that date may be used instead. The resolution window is between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05. The specific check date is December 5, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will pause at all three upcoming meetings (December, January, March). The first and most imminent test is the December 9–10 meeting. Market-implied probabilities from federal funds futures, as displayed by the CME FedWatch Tool, are the best real-time indicator of what the FOMC will do. If markets assign a ≥50% probability to a pause just days before the December meeting, this is a strong signal that a pause is likely, which is a necessary (though not sufficient) condition for the 'Pause-Pause-Pause' scenario. Conversely, if markets price in a cut with high probability, the Pause-Pause-Pause outcome becomes much less likely. This subquestion thus serves as a high-value early indicator that would meaningfully update forecasters' beliefs about the ultimate question, without simply restating the ultimate question itself.

question: Progressive Cities Parlay
description:
The 2025 mayoral elections in New York City, Minneapolis, and Seattle will be held on November 4, 2025, to elect the mayors of those cities.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if all of the following conditions are met:

- Zohran Mamdani wins New York City Mayoral Election
- Omar Fateh wins Minneapolis Mayoral Election
- Katie Wilson wins Seattle Mayoral Election

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will remain open until the official results of the listed elections are published.

The full rules for this market can be found here:
https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/pc1.png

subquestions.question: Will Omar Fateh be within 5 percentage points of Jacob Frey in the final publicly released pre-election poll of the 2025 Minneapolis mayoral race?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question ('Progressive Cities Parlay') requires all three progressive candidates—Zohran Mamdani (NYC), Omar Fateh (Minneapolis), and Katie Wilson (Seattle)—to win their respective mayoral elections on November 4, 2025. The weakest link in this parlay is widely considered to be Omar Fateh's challenge to incumbent Jacob Frey in Minneapolis. As of early October 2025, Fateh trailed Frey by approximately 5 points in polls, making Minneapolis the most uncertain of the three races. Mamdani leads his NYC race by roughly 18–20 points and Wilson defeated Harrell in Seattle's August primary, making both of those races more favorable for the progressive candidates. Whether Fateh can close the gap with Frey in the final days is the key swing factor for this parlay.

A report from October 4, 2025, noted Fateh was 'just five points behind Frey in the polls' (https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/the-next-mamdani-meet-minneapolis-muslim-socialist-mayoral-candidate). DSA-affiliated candidates like Fateh have been buoyed by the 'Mamdani bump' in progressive organizing (https://localnews8.com/news/national-world/ap-national-news/2025/10/19/democratic-socialists-see-their-moment-in-zohran-mamdanis-rise/). However, incumbent Frey has significant structural advantages in Minneapolis.

Sources:
- Donald J. Trump (news site): https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/the-next-mamdani-meet-minneapolis-muslim-socialist-mayoral-candidate
- LocalNews8 (AP): https://localnews8.com/news/national-world/ap-national-news/2025/10/19/democratic-socialists-see-their-moment-in-zohran-mamdanis-rise/
- Yahoo News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/believe-not-election-next-month-090025498.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, in the last publicly released poll of the 2025 Minneapolis mayoral race conducted and/or published between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03 (inclusive), Omar Fateh is within 5 percentage points of Jacob Frey (i.e., Frey's share minus Fateh's share is ≤ 5 points, or Fateh is ahead). The poll must be conducted by a recognized polling firm (e.g., one listed on FiveThirtyEight's pollster ratings or a major local/national news outlet-commissioned poll). If multiple polls are released on the same final date, the question resolves based on the average of those polls' margins. If no publicly released poll meeting these criteria is published between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A. Sources to check include FiveThirtyEight (https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/), RealClearPolitics, 538/Silver Bulletin, Star Tribune polling, and other major outlets covering the Minneapolis mayoral race.
subquestions.rationale: The Minneapolis race is the most competitive and uncertain of the three races in the parlay. Mamdani holds a commanding lead in NYC and Wilson is favored in Seattle, so the parlay's outcome hinges most heavily on whether Fateh can beat the incumbent Frey. A late poll showing Fateh within striking distance (≤5 points) would be a strong indicator that the parlay has a realistic chance of hitting. Conversely, if Fateh falls further behind, the parlay is very unlikely to resolve Yes regardless of the other two races. This subquestion thus serves as the most informative early indicator for the ultimate question.

question: Ahmed al-Sharaa out as leader of Syria in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ahmed al-Sharaa, the President of Syria, is removed from power for any length of time between July 15,, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Al-Sharaa will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, is officially dismissed, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as leader of Syria within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ahmed al-Sharaa deliver a speech at the UN General Assembly high-level week (September 22–30, 2025)?
subquestions.background_information:
Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syria's interim president since December 2024, is scheduled to speak at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) high-level week in New York, set for September 22–30, 2025. A Syrian foreign ministry official confirmed this plan, noting he would be 'the first Syrian president to speak at the United Nations since former president Nureddin al-Atassi (in 1967)' (Firstpost, August 25, 2025). Al-Sharaa remains under UN sanctions and a travel ban due to his past as a designated jihadist, meaning he must request a sanctions exemption for each foreign trip. The United States has been pushing for his delisting from the UN Security Council terrorism sanctions list (bne IntelliNews, August 7, 2025). His ability to attend and speak at UNGA would be a strong signal that he remains firmly in power, retains international backing, and faces no immediate domestic threat to his rule. Conversely, failure to appear could indicate a crisis—whether a travel ban not being lifted, domestic instability preventing his departure, or a loss of power.

Sources:
- Firstpost (2025-08-25): https://www.firstpost.com/world/al-sharaa-to-speak-at-unga-next-month-first-syrian-leader-to-do-so-in-decades-13838291.html
- bne IntelliNews (2025-08-07): https://www.intellinews.com/us-pushes-to-remove-syrian-officials-from-un-terrorism-sanctions-list-366029/
- Asharq Al-Awsat (2025-08-31): https://english.aawsat.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Ahmed al-Sharaa delivers a speech (in person or via a live video address as head of the Syrian delegation) at the UN General Assembly high-level segment between September 22 and September 30, 2025. It resolves No if, by September 30, 2025 (23:59 UTC), he has not delivered such a speech. The resolution window is September 1, 2025 to September 30, 2025. Primary resolution sources will be official UN General Assembly records (https://gadebate.un.org/), UN Web TV (https://media.un.org/), and a consensus of credible international news reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP). If the high-level week is postponed beyond September 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Al-Sharaa's UNGA appearance is a strong near-term observable indicator of his continued hold on power. To travel to New York, he must (1) still be Syria's recognized leader, (2) maintain enough domestic stability to leave the country, (3) receive a UN sanctions exemption, and (4) retain sufficient international support. If any of these conditions fail—particularly if he is removed from power, faces a coup, or domestic unrest prevents his departure—he would not appear. Thus, his UNGA speech is a meaningful early indicator for the ultimate question of whether he remains Syria's leader through 2025. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely also disagree on whether he can successfully make this trip, making it a useful crux.

question: Will Venezuela invade Guyana in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Venezuela commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Guyana between January 29 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be will be official confirmation by Venezuela, Guyana, the United Nations, or any permanent member of the UN Security Council, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Venezuela conduct a new armed incursion or cross-border firing incident targeting Guyanese military, police, or civilian personnel in the Essequibo or border region between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Venezuela has been steadily escalating provocations against Guyana over the disputed Essequibo region throughout 2025. In March 2025, a Venezuelan naval gunboat intercepted ExxonMobil operations in Guyanese waters. On May 15, 2025, Guyana's military reported three armed attacks on its patrols along the Cuyuni River, believed to be carried out by Venezuelan operatives or proxies. On August 31, 2025, a Joint Services patrol escorting ballot boxes along the Upper Cuyuni River was fired upon from the Venezuelan side. Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López warned in September 2025 that Venezuela would respond in 'legitimate defense' to any attack launched from Guyanese or Trinidadian territory, accusing both nations of collaborating with the United States. The U.S. has deployed a major naval presence in the Southern Caribbean, including seven warships, a nuclear-powered submarine, and over 4,500 service members. Trinidad and Tobago has offered the U.S. military access to its territory in the event of Venezuelan aggression against Guyana. The pattern of escalating cross-border armed incidents — from naval interceptions to proxy attacks to direct fire on patrols — serves as a leading indicator of whether Venezuela is moving toward a full military offensive. A further escalation in October 2025 would signal heightened risk of an invasion before year-end.

Sources:
- Zero Hedge, 'Venezuela's Shadow War Over Oil-Rich Essequibo Is Escalating' (May 29, 2025): https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/venezuelas-shadow-war-over-oil-rich-essequibo-escalating
- BNO News, 'Guyana says patrol came under fire from Venezuela; no injuries reported' (Aug 31, 2025): https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/08/guyana-says-patrol-came-under-fire-from-venezuela/
- Latin Times, 'Venezuela Warns Neighbors of Retaliation Over Support for U.S. Military Operations' (Sep 15, 2025): https://www.latintimes.com/venezuela-warns-neighbors-retaliation-over-support-us-military-operations-well-act-legitimate-578641
- bne IntelliNews, 'Trinidad backs US access in case of Venezuelan escalation over Essequibo' (Aug 25, 2025): https://www.intellinews.com/trinidad-backs-us-access-in-case-of-venezuelan-escalation-over-essequibo-370123/
- Newsroom Guyana, 'Guyana on high alert as Venezuela threatens international peace and order' (May 25, 2025): https://newsroom.gy/2025/05/25/guyana-on-high-alert-as-venezuela-threatens-international-peace-and-order/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), there is at least one credible report — from Guyana's government (e.g., the Guyana Defence Force, Ministry of Foreign Affairs), Reuters, AP, BBC, or the Associated Press — of a new armed incident in which Venezuelan military personnel, Venezuelan-flagged vessels or aircraft, or armed actors operating from Venezuelan territory fire upon, attack, or physically engage Guyanese military, police, or civilian personnel, or Guyanese-licensed commercial operations (e.g., ExxonMobil), within Guyana's internationally recognized territory or territorial waters (including the Essequibo region and its maritime zone). The incident must involve the use of firearms, explosives, or other lethal weaponry. Verbal threats, diplomatic protests, troop movements within Venezuelan territory, or overflights that do not involve the use of weapons do not count. If no such incident is reported by credible sources by November 5, 2025, the question resolves No. If reports are ambiguous regarding the origin of fire (i.e., it is not confirmed that the fire came from Venezuelan territory or Venezuelan-affiliated actors), the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The pattern of escalating armed incidents in 2025 — from naval interceptions in March, to armed attacks on patrols in May, to cross-border fire during elections in August — forms a clear escalation ladder. Whether this pattern continues or accelerates in October is a strong leading indicator of whether Venezuela will move from shadow-war provocations to an outright military offensive by year-end. If armed incidents intensify, the probability of invasion increases significantly; if they cease or de-escalate (perhaps due to U.S. naval deterrence or diplomatic pressure), invasion becomes much less likely. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely update substantially based on whether October sees further armed provocations.

question: Will Samsung release a trifold phone by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Samsung releases a phone with three foldable screens by the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Samsung. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Samsung's trifold phone become available for purchase by the general public in at least one market (e.g., South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, or UAE) by December 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Samsung officially unveiled its trifold smartphone at the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea on October 31–November 1, 2025. Samsung confirmed in an official statement to SamMobile that it plans to bring the device to users 'within this year.' The initial launch is expected to be limited to select Asian markets — South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, and possibly the UAE — with an initial production run reportedly of only 50,000 units. Multiple reports from September–November 2025 indicated the device was already in mass production and could go on sale shortly after the APEC unveiling, potentially in November 2025. However, as of November 12, 2025, no confirmed on-sale date has been publicly announced by Samsung, and the device has not yet been made available for purchase by the general public.

Sources:
- Forbes (Nov 1, 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/jaymcgregor/2025/11/01/samsung-galaxy-trifold-unveil-release-date/
- TechStory (Oct 27, 2025): https://techstory.in/the-galaxy-trifold-set-for-ultra-limited-debut/
- Mashable ME (Sep 3, 2025): https://me.mashable.com/tech/50093/samsung-galaxy-z-trifold-tipped-to-launch-in-october-with-limited-availability
- TechRadar (Oct 28, 2025): https://www.techradar.com/phones/samsung-galaxy-phones/the-samsung-galaxy-tri-fold-just-got-officially-shown-off
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-12 and 2025-12-01 (inclusive), Samsung's trifold phone becomes available for purchase by the general public in at least one country. 'Available for purchase' means individual consumers can order or buy the device through Samsung's official website, Samsung retail stores, or authorized retailers in at least one market (e.g., South Korea, China, Singapore, Taiwan, UAE, or any other country). An announcement, unveiling, pre-registration, or waitlist without the ability to complete a purchase does not count. Resolution will be based on official Samsung announcements (https://news.samsung.com/ or samsung.com), credible tech publication reporting (e.g., The Verge, Forbes, TechRadar, SamMobile), or evidence of the product being listed for sale on Samsung's official online store in any market. If no credible evidence of the device being available for purchase by the general public emerges by end of day December 1, 2025 (UTC), this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Samsung will release a trifold phone available for public purchase by December 12, 2025. This subquestion asks whether the phone goes on sale by December 1, which is a strong early indicator. Samsung has unveiled the device and stated it will arrive 'within this year,' with multiple reports suggesting a November launch in limited markets. If the phone is purchasable by December 1, it almost certainly resolves the ultimate question. If it is NOT purchasable by December 1, the remaining 11-day window becomes very tight, making a 'No' resolution on the ultimate question more likely (though still possible). This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable milestone — actual retail availability — that is distinct from the ultimate question's deadline and provides strong directional evidence.

question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publish or release the text of a new executive order targeting mail-in voting, voting machines, or voter ID requirements between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump announced on August 18, 2025, that his administration was drafting an executive order to ban mail-in voting and voting machines ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. On August 30-31, he further announced plans for an executive order mandating voter ID for every vote and limiting mail-in voting to the very ill and overseas military. As of late November 2025, Trump has made multiple public statements and Truth Social posts about these intentions but the key question is whether a formal executive order has been or will be signed.

Trump previously signed an executive order in March 2025 requiring documentary proof of citizenship for federal elections and that all ballots be received by Election Day; a federal judge blocked the citizenship-proof requirement in April 2025, citing that election regulation is a state and congressional power. Legal experts have consistently noted that the Constitution's Article I, Section 4 grants states authority over election administration, making executive orders in this area legally vulnerable.

Despite months of announcements, no executive order specifically banning mail-in voting or voting machines has been publicly signed as of late November 2025. The question is whether one will materialize before the end of December 2025.

Sources:
- USA Today, "Trump says he will issue executive order mandating voter ID requirement" (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/08/31/trump-voter-id-executive-order/75487291007/
- Al Jazeera, "Trump to order voter ID for every vote, 'no exceptions'" (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/31/trump-to-order-voter-id-for-every-vote-no-exceptions
- KOMO, "Election officials speak out as Trump pushes to eliminate mail-in voting" (Aug 24, 2025): https://komonews.com/news/nation-world/election-officials-speak-out-as-trump-pushes-to-eliminate-mail-in-voting
- USAfricaOnline, "Trump pushes to end mail-in voting ahead of 2026 elections" (Aug 19, 2025): https://usafricaonline.com/2025/08/19/trump-pushes-to-end-mail-in-voting-ahead-of-2026-elections/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025 (inclusive), the Trump administration officially publishes, signs, or releases the text of a new executive order (distinct from the March 2025 order on proof of citizenship) that specifically targets mail-in voting, voting machines, or imposes new voter ID requirements for federal elections. The executive order must be published on the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/) or announced via official White House communications (https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/). If no such executive order text is published or signed during this window, the question resolves No. Draft announcements, Truth Social posts promising future action, or verbal statements alone do not count — the order must be formally signed or officially released.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Trump will 'act' to ban mail-in voting or voting machines by signing legislation or performing executive action by December 31, 2025. The most likely pathway is an executive order, which Trump has repeatedly promised since August 2025. Tracking whether an actual executive order is signed and published in December 2025 is a direct leading indicator: if one appears by December 29, it is almost certain the ultimate question resolves Yes. If no order materializes by then, only two days remain, making a No resolution highly likely. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it focuses specifically on the observable event of an executive order being formally released (not just announced or promised), and its window ends slightly before the ultimate deadline, providing early signal.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q3 of 2025 scheduled for October 30, 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlanta Fed GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP growth be between 2.0% and 3.0% as of its last update on or before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
