subquestions.question: Will the CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release Natality Dashboard show a Q2 2025 general fertility rate data point by September 16, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. general fertility rate in Q2 2025 exceeds 54.5 births per 1,000 women aged 15–44, as reported by the CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) Natality Dashboard. The CDC updates this dashboard on a rolling basis, typically with a lag of several months. The Q1 2025 figure (54.5) is already available as of August 2025. The Q2 2025 data would cover April–June 2025 births. The CDC's VSRR Natality Dashboard (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm) is the authoritative source. However, there is uncertainty about whether Q2 2025 data will be posted before the ultimate question's resolution deadline of September 19, 2025. Historically, VSRR provisional data appears with roughly a 2–4 month lag, meaning Q2 data (through June 2025) could plausibly appear in August or September 2025, but it is not guaranteed. If the data is not yet published, the ultimate question cannot resolve Yes (it would resolve No by default per the question's rules). Whether the data appears in time is therefore a key crux: if forecasters believe the data won't be published before September 19, the ultimate question trivially resolves No regardless of the underlying fertility trend.

Sources:
- CDC VSRR Natality Dashboard: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm
- CDC Vital Statistics Rapid Release overview: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16 (inclusive), the CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release Natality Dashboard (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/vsrr/natality-dashboard.htm) displays a general fertility rate estimate specifically labeled as covering Q2 2025 (i.e., April–June 2025, or any monthly data within that quarter that would allow computation of a Q2 2025 rate). The data must be publicly accessible on the dashboard. If no Q2 2025 general fertility rate data is available on the dashboard by 11:59 PM ET on September 16, 2025, this question resolves No. Note: if the dashboard is temporarily unavailable due to technical issues but the data was confirmed published before September 16, it still counts as Yes. If the CDC restructures or removes the dashboard entirely and no equivalent VSRR provisional natality data source publishes Q2 2025 data by September 16, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is a critical crux for the ultimate question because if the CDC does not publish Q2 2025 data before the resolution deadline, the ultimate question resolves No by default regardless of the actual fertility rate. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question may partly disagree on whether data will be available in time. This is an observable, different event from the fertility rate itself — it concerns data publication timing rather than the underlying demographic trend. If the data is confirmed available, forecasters can then focus entirely on whether the rate exceeds 54.5. If the data won't be available, the ultimate question is settled.

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed or nominated by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

Nominations will qualify even if the individual is not confirmed.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Eric Adams officially suspend or end his 2025 New York City mayoral campaign by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of September 5, 2025, New York City Mayor Eric Adams is running as an independent candidate in the 2025 mayoral race. However, multiple credible reports indicate that top Trump advisers — including special envoy Steve Witkoff and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles — have been in active discussions with Adams' team about offering him a federal position, reportedly the ambassadorship to Saudi Arabia, in exchange for dropping out of the mayoral race. The strategy is aimed at clearing the field to help defeat Democratic front-runner Zohran Mamdani. Adams was expected to make an 'important campaign announcement' on September 5, 2025, amid these reports. Trump reportedly set a deadline of the following week (around September 8-12) for Adams to drop out. Adams has publicly denied wanting a Trump administration job and has said he intends to finish his first term, but sources close to his team say they have been pushing him to accept a federal 'golden parachute.'

Sources:
- New York Post, 'Top Trump adviser floats Eric Adams for Saudi Arabia ambassadorship' (Sep 5, 2025): https://nypost.com/2025/09/05/us-news/top-trump-adviser-floats-eric-adams-for-saudi-arabia-ambassadorship/
- CNBC, 'New York Mayor Eric Adams to make important campaign announcement as Trump nomination floated' (Sep 5, 2025): https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/05/eric-adams-campaign-announcement-trump-nomination.html
- New York Post, 'Eric Adams, White House in talks over potential Trump admin job' (Sep 3, 2025): https://nypost.com/2025/09/03/us-news/eric-adams-white-house-in-talks-over-potential-trump-admin-job/
- The Times of Israel, 'Trump advisers offer job to Adams to quit NYC mayoral race' (Sep 4, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com/trump-advisers-offer-job-to-adams-to-quit-nyc-mayoral-race-clear-path-for-mamdani-cuomo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Eric Adams publicly announces the suspension, termination, or withdrawal of his 2025 New York City mayoral campaign between 2025-09-06 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The announcement must be made by Adams himself or by an authorized campaign spokesperson, and must be reported by at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., New York Times, New York Post, CNBC, Associated Press, Reuters). Merely saying he is 'considering' dropping out does not count — there must be a definitive statement that he is no longer actively running. If Adams suspends his campaign but his name remains on the ballot, this still resolves Yes as long as the campaign is officially suspended or ended. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on October 1, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- New York Post: https://nypost.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- CNBC: https://www.cnbc.com
subquestions.rationale: Adams dropping out of the mayoral race is a critical precondition for him joining the Trump administration. The reported negotiations explicitly link a federal appointment to Adams' withdrawal from the race. If Adams suspends his campaign in the near term, it is a very strong signal that a deal has been reached and a Trump nomination or appointment is forthcoming. Conversely, if Adams stays in the race through early October, it significantly reduces the likelihood of him joining the Trump administration by year-end, since the political calculus driving the offer (clearing the mayoral field before the November election) would lose urgency. This subquestion captures a distinct, observable near-term event that is a leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

question: Apple AirTags 2 priced below $30 USD at release?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the standard edition of the AirTag 2 launches at $29.99 or less. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the AirTag 2 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations, this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard AirTag 2 model with no additional features, accessories, or services.

A qualifying product must be named "AirTag" and be recognized as a successor to the original AirTag product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 14 and iPhone 15. A new AirTag product released without a number, under a designation other than AirTag 2 will qualify if it retains the original functions of the AirTag and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

If the AirTag 2 is not released by June 30, 2026, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Apple officially announce the AirTag 2 (or its successor) at its September 2025 event with a US retail price of $29 or less for a single unit?
subquestions.background_information:
Apple is widely expected to unveil the AirTag 2 at its September 9, 2025 'Awe Dropping' event alongside the iPhone 17 series. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that the new AirTag is 'nearly ready' for launch (https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/27/new-airtag-2-is-coming-very-soon-with-these-rumored-features/). The current first-generation AirTag has a US list price of $29 for a single unit and $99 for a four-pack (https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/apple-airtag-2-rumors-new-features-and-possible-release-date-leaked/). Some analysts and commentators have speculated the AirTag 2 could be priced slightly higher due to its upgraded ultra-wideband chip, tamper-proof speaker, and extended precision finding range (up to 60 meters vs. the current ~15 meters). Tom's Guide Australia noted that 'the upcoming AirTag 2 is expected to be more expensive' (https://www.tomsguide.com/deals/apple-airtag-4-packs-are-back-down-to-just-au-dollar104-close-to-their-all-time-low-and-only-au-dollar26-per-tag). However, Apple has historically been aggressive about keeping accessory pricing stable—the AirTag launched at $29 in 2021 and has never had a list price increase. Apple is also currently clearing out existing AirTag inventory at steep discounts on Amazon (https://gizmodo.com/apple-is-sitting-on-millions-of-airtags-and-is-clearing-them-out-on-amazon-with-zero-profit-2000609055), which could signal confidence in a competitively priced successor. The announced pricing at the event would be the strongest near-term indicator of whether the final retail price will be below $30.

Sources:
- 9to5Mac: https://9to5mac.com/2025/08/27/new-airtag-2-is-coming-very-soon-with-these-rumored-features/
- CNET: https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/apple-airtag-2-rumors-new-features-and-possible-release-date-leaked/
- Tom's Guide: https://www.tomsguide.com/deals/apple-airtag-4-packs-are-back-down-to-just-au-dollar104-close-to-their-all-time-low-and-only-au-dollar26-per-tag
- Gizmodo: https://gizmodo.com/apple-is-sitting-on-millions-of-airtags-and-is-clearing-them-out-on-amazon-with-zero-profit-2000609055
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, Apple officially announces (at a keynote, press release, or on apple.com) a successor to the AirTag—whether called 'AirTag 2' or another name that clearly identifies it as the next-generation AirTag—with a stated US single-unit retail price of $29.99 or less (pre-tax). The announcement must include an explicit price; if Apple announces the product but does not disclose pricing during this window, this question resolves No. If no such announcement occurs during this window, this question also resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Apple's official event page and press releases: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/
- Apple Store product listings: https://www.apple.com/shop/
- Credible reporting from outlets such as The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/), CNET (https://www.cnet.com/), and 9to5Mac (https://9to5mac.com/) may be used to confirm announcement details if the Apple Newsroom or Apple Store page is temporarily unavailable or ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the AirTag 2 will be priced below $30 at release. The most informative near-term indicator is the price Apple announces at its September 2025 event. Apple almost always announces pricing at the same time it reveals new products, and the announced price virtually never changes before the product ships. If Apple announces the AirTag 2 at $29 (matching the original), that is an extremely strong signal the ultimate question resolves Yes. If the announced price is $35 or higher, the ultimate question almost certainly resolves No. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it concerns the announcement and stated price, not the actual availability for purchase, and it captures the key information—pricing—within a much earlier and tighter window.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025 last longer than 21 consecutive days?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 1, 2025, the U.S. federal government entered a partial shutdown after Congress failed to pass a funding bill before the fiscal year deadline. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) has announced it will 'suspend all operations' during the lapse, ceasing all data collection and publication activities. According to the Department of Labor's 73-page contingency plan, the BLS workforce would shrink from 2,055 employees to just 1 during a shutdown. Key economic releases at risk include the September jobs report (originally due October 3), the Consumer Price Index (October 15), the Producer Price Index (October 16), and JOLTS data.

The duration of the shutdown is a critical variable for whether BLS could miss three consecutive scheduled releases of any report — one of the triggers for the ultimate question's resolution. Historical shutdowns have varied in length: the 2018-19 shutdown lasted 34 days, the 2013 shutdown lasted 16 days, and the 1995-96 shutdown lasted 21 days. A shutdown exceeding 21 days would encompass multiple scheduled BLS release dates and increase the risk that the BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of at least one report series, potentially triggering resolution of the ultimate question.

President Trump was scheduled to meet with congressional leaders on September 29 to negotiate, but no deal was reached before the deadline. Senate Republicans rejected a House-passed short-term funding bill.

Sources:
- Fortune: https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts/
- FinanzNachrichten.de: https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2025-09/63876543-bureau-of-labor-statistics-to-cease-operations-if-govt-shuts-down.htm
- Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/partisan-standoff-threatens-crucial-economic-data-leaving-fed-families-dark
- UPI: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/bls-jobs-report-government-shutdown/3451727618432/
- EconoTimes: https://www.econotimes.com/US-Government-Shutdown-Threatens-Release-of-Key-Economic-Data-1720345
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. federal government shutdown that began on or around October 1, 2025 continues without interruption for more than 21 consecutive calendar days — i.e., the government has not been funded and reopened by October 22, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. The resolution window is between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31.

If the government does not shut down (i.e., Congress passes funding before operations cease on October 1), this question resolves No.

If the government shuts down but reopens on or before October 22, 2025, this question resolves No.

If the government shuts down, briefly reopens (for less than 48 hours), and then shuts down again, the days are counted cumulatively toward the 21-day threshold.

Resolution sources: Official announcements from the Office of Management and Budget (https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/), reporting from major news outlets (Reuters, AP, Bloomberg), and the BLS release calendar (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/). If there is ambiguity about the exact reopening time, credible reporting from at least two major news outlets will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The duration of the current government shutdown is the single most important near-term indicator for whether BLS will 'cease regular publication' of payroll data. The ultimate question resolves Yes if BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of any covered report without providing data within 30 days. BLS has confirmed it will suspend all operations during a shutdown. A shutdown lasting more than 21 days would span multiple scheduled release dates for jobs reports, CPI, PPI, and JOLTS, making it increasingly likely that three consecutive releases of at least one series are missed — directly threatening the ultimate question's Yes resolution. Conversely, a short shutdown (under 21 days) would likely result in only temporary delays followed by publication, which explicitly does not count as cessation under the ultimate question's criteria. This question thus serves as a meaningful early indicator: forecasters who believe the shutdown will be prolonged should assign higher probability to BLS ceasing publication, while those expecting a quick resolution should assign lower probability.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Senate formally accept or initiate proceedings on any impeachment request against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, there have been approximately 30 impeachment requests filed against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, but none have advanced to a formal vote in the Brazilian Senate. The process requires the President of the Senate (currently Davi Alcolumbre) to accept and forward an impeachment request before any vote can take place. Senate President Alcolumbre has so far declined to advance impeachment proceedings against Moraes, despite mounting political pressure from right-wing parties.

On July 30, 2025, the U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned Moraes under the Global Magnitsky Act for alleged 'serious human rights abuses and arbitrary detentions' (https://home.treasury.gov/). Following the sanctions, five senators from the Liberal Party filed the 30th impeachment request against Moraes in early August 2025 (https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/). Right-wing groups have planned mass protests for September 7, 2025 (Brazil's Independence Day) to demand Moraes' impeachment (https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/). A Quaest poll found 46% of Brazilians support impeaching Moraes while 43% oppose it.

The impeachment of a Supreme Court minister requires a two-thirds majority vote in the Senate (54 of 81 senators). However, the critical gateway is the Senate President's decision to formally accept and initiate proceedings on any of the filed requests.

Sources:
- Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/
- NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/
- U.S. Treasury sanctions announcement: https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases
- Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/politics/3299123-high-stakes-diplomacy-brazilian-judge-in-trumps-crosshairs
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), the President of the Brazilian Federal Senate (Senado Federal) formally accepts, forwards to a committee, or otherwise initiates official proceedings on any impeachment request against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. This includes publishing an official dispatch (despacho), referring the request to the relevant Senate committee, or scheduling a formal session to consider the impeachment request. Mere filing of new impeachment requests by senators does NOT count — the Senate President must take affirmative procedural action to advance the process.

This question resolves No if no such action is taken by October 1, 2025.

Primary resolution sources will be official communications from the Brazilian Senate (https://www.senado.leg.br/), the Senate's official gazette (Diário do Senado Federal), and a consensus of credible Brazilian news outlets such as Folha de S.Paulo (https://www.folha.uol.com.br/), O Globo (https://oglobo.globo.com/), and G1 (https://g1.globo.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The Senate President's decision to formally accept and initiate impeachment proceedings is the essential procedural prerequisite for any impeachment vote. Without this step, no vote can occur and the ultimate question must resolve No. If the Senate President takes this action in September 2025, it would be a strong signal that impeachment proceedings will advance to a vote before year-end. Conversely, if September passes — a period of heightened pressure due to the September 7 protests and U.S. sanctions — without the Senate President acting, it significantly reduces the probability of an impeachment vote occurring by December 31, 2025. This subquestion tracks a distinct, observable procedural event rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US conduct a qualifying aerial strike (drone, missile, or air strike) on a third distinct country's territory between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
As of January 13, 2026, the US has already conducted qualifying strikes on at least two distinct countries' territories in 2026:

1. **Venezuela**: On January 3, 2026, the US launched Operation Absolute Resolve, involving over 150 aircraft including F-18s, F-35s, F-22s, B-1 bombers, and drones, conducting offensive strikes on Venezuelan government infrastructure and air defenses in Caracas (https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/pentagon-official-on-venezuela-war/).

2. **Syria**: On January 10, 2026, the US conducted large-scale airstrikes across Syria targeting at least 35 Islamic State locations, involving approximately 20 aircraft and over 90 bombs and missiles (https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/).

For the ultimate question to resolve Yes at 'exactly 3 countries,' the US would need to strike exactly one more country (but not more). Historically, the US has conducted strikes in countries such as Yemen (against Houthi targets), Somalia (against al-Shabaab), Iraq, Libya, Pakistan, and Afghanistan. The US currently maintains counterterrorism operations in several regions, and the Trump administration has shown willingness to use force aggressively. The Council on Foreign Relations has warned of potential India-Pakistan conflict in 2026, and various global flashpoints remain active.

Sources:
- The Intercept, Pentagon Official on Venezuela War: https://theintercept.com/2026/01/05/pentagon-official-on-venezuela-war/
- OpIndia, US airstrikes hit Islamic State targets across Syria: https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/
- Next Big Future, USA Stealth Drones and Special Operations: https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2026/01/usa-stealth-drones-and-special-operations-give-military-domination.html
- India TV News, India-Pakistan conflict warning: https://www.indiatvnews.com/news/world/india-pakistan-likely-to-engage-in-conflict-in-2026-warns-us-think-tank-cites-terror-activities-2025-12-31-971057
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between January 13, 2026 and February 12, 2026 (inclusive), the United States conducts at least one qualifying aerial strike (defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles launched by US military forces that impact ground territory) on the soil of a country other than Venezuela and Syria — i.e., a third distinct country struck by the US in 2026. The strike must be officially acknowledged by the US government or confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., from Reuters, AP, BBC, or US Central Command press releases at https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/). Intercepted missiles or drones that do not impact ground territory do not count. Artillery, small arms, ground operations, cyberattacks, and naval shelling do not count. If no such strike on a third country occurs in this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the US will strike exactly 3 countries in 2026. As of January 13, 2026, the US has already struck two countries (Venezuela and Syria). Whether the US strikes a third country in the near term is the key crux: the US has ongoing counterterrorism operations in Yemen, Somalia, and Iraq where strikes are plausible but not certain. If a third country is struck by mid-February, forecasters would significantly update upward on the probability that 3+ countries will be struck by year-end. Conversely, if no third-country strike occurs in this window despite active global tensions, it may suggest restraint. This subquestion is a direct early indicator without merely restating the ultimate question, because it focuses on the marginal next strike rather than the total count, and the time window is much shorter.

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing another Fed Governor before their term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request between August 25 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling that permits President Trump to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 25, 2025, President Trump announced the firing of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing alleged mortgage fraud as 'cause' for removal. Cook has refused to resign and filed a lawsuit challenging the removal in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., before Judge Jia Cobb. A hearing on whether to block the removal was scheduled for August 30, 2025. The legal question centers on whether the Federal Reserve Act's 'for cause' removal provision (Section 10) permits a president to dismiss a Fed governor based on conduct alleged to have occurred before the governor's Senate confirmation, and whether such conduct constitutes the statutory grounds of 'inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance in office.' In May 2025, the Supreme Court issued an order distinguishing the Fed as a unique institution with a 'distinct historical tradition' of independence, suggesting Fed governors may have stronger removal protections than officials at other agencies. If the court blocks Cook's removal, Trump's ability to secure a 4-3 majority on the Fed Board is stalled, making it less likely he would attempt to fire another governor (since the legal avenue would appear closed). Conversely, if a court permits the removal, it establishes precedent that could embolden further dismissals.

Sources:
- CNN: 'We just jumped into the unknown: Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed' (Aug 28, 2025) https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/politics/trump-fed-lisa-cook/index.html
- Yahoo Finance: 'Trump's firing of Fed Governor Cook could be blocked by US judge' (Aug 29, 2025) https://www.yahoo.com/finance/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-blocked-judge/
- The Straits Times: 'Trump fires Lisa Cook, escalating his war on the Federal Reserve' (Aug 27, 2025) https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trump-fires-lisa-cook-escalating-his-war-on-the-federal-reserve
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court (district court, appeals court, or the Supreme Court) issues a ruling, order, or decision that permits President Trump's removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to proceed — meaning no injunction or restraining order blocking the removal is in effect as of the ruling, OR a previously issued injunction blocking the removal is vacated or overturned. The question resolves No if, as of 2025-09-30, a court order blocking Cook's removal remains in effect, or if no court has ruled to permit the removal. Resolution will be based on official court filings available through PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or the court's public docket, supplemented by credible reporting from major news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/). If the lawsuit is withdrawn or dismissed (e.g., because Cook resigns), the question resolves Yes, since no court order would be blocking the removal. If no ruling has been issued by September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The outcome of the Lisa Cook litigation is a critical leading indicator for whether Trump will attempt to fire another Fed governor. If courts uphold Trump's authority to remove a Fed governor for cause, it substantially lowers the legal and political barriers to firing additional governors, making a second firing attempt much more likely before October 31. If courts block the removal, Trump faces a clear legal obstacle that would likely deter additional firing attempts. Two forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would likely update significantly upon learning the court outcome — one of the strongest cruxes for this prediction.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Canada announce the start of formal bilateral trade negotiations (or a new trade framework/deal) between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late October 2025, U.S.-Canada trade relations remain strained. President Trump raised tariffs on Canadian goods not covered by CUSMA to 35% in August 2025 (https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-countries-delayed/63492181), and eliminated the de minimis exemption for all imports effective August 29, 2025 (https://www.globalnews.ca/news/11045678/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses/). Canada has removed retaliatory tariffs on CUSMA-covered goods but maintains steel, aluminum, and auto tariffs. Unlike with Mexico, where Trump agreed to a 90-day negotiating period in August 2025, no equivalent formal negotiation framework has been publicly announced with Canada. The ultimate question asks whether Trump will lower, pause, delay, or remove tariffs specifically targeting Canada by December 31, 2025. A formal announcement of bilateral trade negotiations or a new trade deal framework would be a strong leading indicator that tariff relief is imminent, as such negotiations typically precede any executive action on tariff reduction. Conversely, the absence of any formal negotiation track in November would suggest that the status quo of elevated tariffs is likely to persist through year-end.

Sources:
- Pittsburgh's Action News 4, "New tariffs on Canada take effect Friday; Dozens of other countries delayed" (2025-08-01): https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-countries-delayed/63492181
- Global News, "Duty-free shipping to U.S. ends Friday. Canadian businesses are 'fearful'" (2025-08-27): https://www.globalnews.ca/news/11045678/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. government (via the White House, USTR, State Department, or President Trump) and the Canadian government (via the Prime Minister's Office, Foreign Affairs Ministry, or Trade Ministry) jointly or separately announce the commencement of formal bilateral trade negotiations, a new trade deal or framework agreement, or a formal negotiating period aimed at resolving tariff disputes between the two countries. The announcement must be confirmed by at least two major credible news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, CBC, Globe and Mail, Wall Street Journal, New York Times) or by official government press releases from either the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the Prime Minister of Canada's office (https://www.pm.gc.ca/). Informal or background-level discussions, or statements of willingness to negotiate without a concrete announcement, do not qualify. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Formal trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada are a necessary precursor to any voluntary tariff reduction by the Trump administration. Trump's pattern has been to use tariffs as leverage and then negotiate reductions (as seen with the 90-day negotiating period offered to Mexico in August 2025). If formal negotiations are announced in November, it significantly increases the probability that Trump will lower tariffs on Canada before December 31. If no negotiations materialize by the end of November, the two-month window remaining would be very tight for any tariff relief to occur, making it a strong negative indicator. This question thus serves as a meaningful early signal that distinguishes between scenarios where tariff relief is plausible versus unlikely.

question: Julie Masino out as Cracker Barrel CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Julie Masino ceases to be CEO of Cracker Barrel for any length of time between August 24 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Julie Masino's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Cracker Barrel and/or Julie Masino, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Cracker Barrel's board of directors announce any significant leadership or governance changes (e.g., new board members, committee restructuring, or executive departures other than the CEO) between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Cracker Barrel has been under intense pressure throughout 2025 following a botched logo redesign and broader rebranding effort led by CEO Julie Felss Masino. The company reverted to its original logo in August 2025 and suspended its remodel program in September 2025. In early October 2025, Cracker Barrel ended its relationship with Prophet, the consultancy behind the rebrand, and announced organizational changes to 'streamline leadership' and support field operations (https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company). Activist investor Sardar Biglari has waged a long-running campaign against Cracker Barrel's management, having launched seven proxy solicitations in 14 years and securing a board seat in 2022 under a standstill agreement that expired in October 2024. After the standstill expired, Biglari released a 7-page open letter attacking the board's strategic transformation plan (https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/cracker-barrel-hits-back-self-interested-steak-n-shake-ceos-poor-leadership-after-online-attacks). Public calls for Masino's resignation have been widespread, with conservative influencers, customers, and even former President Trump weighing in (https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-pressure-resign-logo-1948340). At a late October 2025 investor summit, Masino publicly defended the logo change as a visibility improvement rather than an ideological decision (https://thehill.com/blogs/in-the-know/5057191-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/). Cracker Barrel's fiscal year Q1 2026 earnings report is typically released in November, which often serves as a catalyst for governance changes.

Sources:
- Nation's Restaurant News: https://www.nrn.com/quick-service/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company
- Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/lifestyle/cracker-barrel-hits-back-self-interested-steak-n-shake-ceos-poor-leadership-after-online-attacks
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-pressure-resign-logo-1948340
- The Hill: https://thehill.com/blogs/in-the-know/5057191-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), Cracker Barrel Old Country Store Inc. announces any of the following through official SEC filings (8-K, DEF 14A, or proxy statements), press releases, or confirmed credible reporting: (1) the appointment or departure of one or more members of the board of directors; (2) the departure of any C-suite executive other than the CEO (e.g., CFO, COO, CMO); or (3) any formal restructuring of board committees. Routine operational hires below the C-suite level do not count. The primary resolution sources will be Cracker Barrel's SEC filings available at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001067294&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40 and official press releases at https://investor.crackerbarrel.com/. A consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Reuters, Wall Street Journal, Nation's Restaurant News) will serve as a fallback source. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Board and senior leadership changes at Cracker Barrel are a strong leading indicator of whether the CEO herself will be ousted. Companies under activist investor pressure and public backlash typically see governance changes—board reshuffles, executive departures, committee restructurings—before or simultaneously with a CEO departure. Cracker Barrel already announced organizational streamlining in early October 2025 and ended its consultancy relationship. If additional leadership changes occur in November (especially around an earnings report), it would signal escalating internal pressure that makes a CEO departure by year-end significantly more likely. Conversely, if the board holds steady, it suggests the company is rallying behind Masino through the holiday season. This subquestion captures an observable, distinct event that is different from the ultimate question but highly informative about its outcome.

question: Will Microstrategy's mNAV dip to 1.00 by December 31?
description:
This market will immediately resolve to "Yes" if Microstrategy's mNAV is equal to or lower than the value specified in the title on any day by December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Resolution will be based on StrategyTracker's "NAV Premium & Performance" chart available at https://strategytracker.com/mstr/, with "1M" and "Diluted Shares" selected.

NAV data for any given date will be considered finalized once the data point for the following calendar day is published on the chart.

This market will resolve based on the specified StrategyTracker chart, not according to other sources or spot markets.

subquestions.question: Will Bitcoin's price fall below $75,000 at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
MicroStrategy's mNAV (market-cap-to-net-asset-value ratio) is fundamentally driven by two factors: the price of MSTR stock and the value of Bitcoin held on its balance sheet. As of late September 2025, Bitcoin trades around $63,000–$65,000 (per recent market data), and MSTR's mNAV sits at approximately 1.5×. Strategy holds roughly 638,460 BTC with an average purchase price of ~$73,880 per BTC (per a September 8, 2025 SEC filing). For mNAV to reach 1.00, MSTR's market capitalization would need to fall to equal the net value of its Bitcoin holdings minus liabilities. A sharp Bitcoin price decline is the most direct mechanism that could collapse mNAV toward 1.0, because it simultaneously reduces the value of the underlying asset while also pressuring MSTR's stock price (which historically trades at a premium or discount to BTC). If Bitcoin drops below $75,000 — roughly a 15–20% decline from recent levels — this would significantly erode the value of Strategy's holdings and likely cause MSTR stock to decline proportionally or more, compressing mNAV. Conversely, if Bitcoin remains above $75,000, it becomes much harder for mNAV to reach 1.00 by year-end.

Sources:
- CoinDesk, 'MSTR News: Strategy Acquires Another 1,955 BTC for $217M': https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/08/strategy-acquires-another-1955-btc-for-217m/
- CoinGecko Bitcoin Price: https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin
- StrategyTracker MSTR NAV Premium & Performance: https://strategytracker.com/mstr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Bitcoin's daily closing price (UTC) falls below $75,000 according to CoinGecko's Bitcoin price page (https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). The 'daily closing price' is defined as the price at 00:00 UTC as reported by CoinGecko. If CoinGecko is unavailable, CoinMarketCap (https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/bitcoin/) may be used as a fallback. If Bitcoin's daily closing price remains at or above $75,000 on every day in this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Bitcoin's price is the single largest driver of MicroStrategy's net asset value. Strategy holds over 638,000 BTC, meaning a significant Bitcoin decline would directly reduce the denominator of mNAV (BTC value) while also cratering MSTR stock. A drop below $75,000 would bring BTC close to or below Strategy's average cost basis (~$73,880), dramatically increasing the probability that mNAV compresses to 1.0 or below. Forecasters who disagree on whether mNAV will hit 1.0 by December likely disagree on whether Bitcoin will experience a major selloff. Tracking whether BTC breaches $75,000 in October provides an early, concrete signal about the trajectory of mNAV compression.

question: Will Drake's next album debut No.1 on Billboard 200?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Drake’s next officially released album debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart for its first charted week following release. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Drake does not release a new album by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will Drake officially announce a release date for his solo album 'Iceman' (or any new solo album) before November 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Drake has been teasing his upcoming solo album, tentatively titled 'Iceman,' throughout 2025. As of early October 2025, no official release date has been confirmed, though Drake has described the album as 'coming soon' and hinted it would drop later in 2025. He has been touring Europe with PARTYNEXTDOOR and releasing singles like 'Which One' (feat. Central Cee) and 'What Did I Miss?' to build momentum. His most recent project, the collaborative album '$ome $exy $ongs 4 U' with PARTYNEXTDOOR, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with approximately 246,000 first-week units (https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/). Drake was also named Billboard's No. 1 Hip-Hop/R&B artist of the 21st century in August 2025. The ultimate question asks whether Drake's next album will debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 by the end of 2025; if the album is not released by then, the market resolves 'No.' Whether Drake announces a concrete release date in the near term is a key indicator of whether the album will come out in time and under what promotional conditions — both of which affect its likelihood of debuting at No. 1.

Sources:
- HotNewHipHop, 'Drake Sends Odd Message About Good Times Amid Iceman Rollout' (Sep 18, 2025): https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/
- HotNewHipHop, 'Drake & Central Cee Which One Heads For Huge Chart Debut' (Jul 28, 2025): https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), Drake officially announces a specific release date for a new solo studio album (whether titled 'Iceman' or otherwise). An 'official announcement' means a public statement from Drake, his management, his record label (OVO Sound / Republic Records / Universal Music Group), or a verified social media post by Drake himself that names a specific calendar date for the album's release. Mere hints, 'coming soon' statements, or unofficial leaks do not count. The announcement must be reported or confirmable via at least one major music news outlet such as Billboard (https://www.billboard.com/), Pitchfork (https://pitchfork.com/), Complex (https://www.complex.com/), or HotNewHipHop (https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/). If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM ET on November 8, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Drake announces a concrete release date for 'Iceman' in the next month is a strong early indicator of whether the album will actually drop before December 31, 2025 — which is a prerequisite for the ultimate question resolving Yes. Major albums typically have release dates announced 2-6 weeks in advance, so an announcement by early November would put the album on track for a late 2025 release. Additionally, the nature and timing of the rollout (promotional strategy, single releases, pre-order availability) heavily influence first-week sales and thus the likelihood of a No. 1 debut. If no release date is announced by November 8, it becomes significantly less likely the album drops in 2025 with enough promotional runway to debut at No. 1. Forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely disagree on whether the album will actually come out in time and how well-promoted it will be — this subquestion directly addresses that crux.

question: Half-Life 3 released in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Half-Life 3 or a differently titled game continuing the Half-Life series is officially released in the US by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release.
