subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury return an indictment against John Bolton between October 1 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, senior Department of Justice officials have been pushing for swift charges against former National Security Adviser John Bolton. According to Reuters and CNN reporting from September 25-26, 2025, prosecutors were expected to present the Bolton case to a grand jury as early as the first week of October 2025. However, there is internal tension: prosecutors in the Maryland U.S. Attorney's Office and the DOJ's National Security Division have reportedly resisted pressure from Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche's office, arguing that more investigation is needed to build a stronger case. The FBI raided Bolton's Bethesda, Maryland home and Washington, D.C. office on August 22, 2025, seizing computers, phones, USB drives, and classified documents. The investigation centers on allegations that Bolton emailed highly sensitive classified documents to his wife and daughter via a private email server while serving as National Security Adviser, as well as potential Espionage Act violations related to his 2020 memoir. Court filings indicate Bolton could face charges under two sections of the Espionage Act and a statute against hoarding classified files. Bolton's attorney, Abbe Lowell, has said the records are ordinary and that Bolton did nothing wrong. The push for charges intensified after Virginia's top federal prosecutor was dismissed for being too slow to prosecute Trump critics.

Sources:
- Reuters via KSL.com (2025-09-26): https://www.ksl.com/article/51316892/justice-department-pushing-for-swift-charges-against-bolton-people-familiar-say
- CNN report on DOJ push (2025-09-25): https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/25/politics/bolton-charges-doj/index.html
- Devdiscourse on DOJ pressure (2025-09-25): https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3289410-escalating-tensions-doj-pressures-charges-against-bolton-amid-internal-dissent
- Times of India on Espionage Act charges (2025-09-04): https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/espionage-probe-fbi-investigates-former-nsa-john-bolton/articleshow/113035678.cms
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a federal grand jury returns a sealed or unsealed indictment against John Bolton between October 1, 2025 and October 10, 2025 (inclusive), as confirmed by official U.S. Department of Justice announcements, federal court docket filings (e.g., via PACER), or a wide consensus of credible news reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, CNN, NYT). The indictment must be a formal criminal charging document returned by a grand jury in any U.S. federal district court. If no indictment is returned or publicly reported by end of day October 10, 2025 ET, the question resolves No. If an indictment is sealed and only becomes publicly known after October 10 but was returned on or before October 10, the question still resolves Yes once confirmed. Sources for resolution include PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) and official DOJ press releases (https://www.justice.gov/news).
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly tracks the most critical near-term precursor to Bolton being federally charged: the grand jury indictment itself. Reports from late September indicated that prosecutors were expected to present the case to a grand jury in early October. If a grand jury indictment is returned by October 10, it is almost certain the ultimate question resolves Yes. If no indictment materializes in this window despite the reported pressure, it suggests that prosecutors successfully pushed back against the rush to charge, making it less likely charges come before October 17. This question captures a different observable event — the grand jury action — rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, because an indictment could be returned but formal charges/announcement could follow days later.

question: Will Kamala Harris endorse Mamdani?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for Zohran Mamdani or endorses Mamdani for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 26, and November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Kamala Harris or one of her representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Kamala Harris's endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will Chuck Schumer or Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorse Zohran Mamdani for NYC Mayor between September 1, 2025 and September 18, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Zohran Mamdani won the 2025 NYC Democratic mayoral primary in June by a commanding margin and is the party's nominee for the November general election. However, top national Democratic leaders have been notably slow to endorse him. As of late August 2025, neither Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer nor House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has endorsed Mamdani. Jeffries met with Mamdani in July but declined to endorse, and multiple reports have noted the reluctance of establishment Democrats to back the self-described socialist candidate. Disgraced former congressman Anthony Weiner predicted in August 2025 that Schumer and Jeffries would 'inevitably' endorse Mamdani as the party nominee, but noted they were holding back to protect moderate Democrats ahead of the 2026 midterms. Meanwhile, several Democratic members of Congress — including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jerrold Nadler, Nydia Velázquez, and Adriano Espaillat — have already endorsed Mamdani. Kamala Harris, as a former Democratic presidential nominee and current political figure, would likely follow rather than lead establishment Democratic endorsements; if Schumer and Jeffries have not endorsed Mamdani, it would be highly unusual for Harris to do so first. Their endorsement (or continued refusal) would be a strong signal about whether other top Democrats, including Harris, will follow suit.

Sources:
- "Hakeem Jeffries meets with Zohran Mamdani, but no endorsement yet for NYC mayor" (Yahoo, 2025-07-18): https://www.yahoo.com/news/hakeem-jeffries-meets-zohran-mamdani-222517498.html
- "Anthony Weiner Predicts Zohran Mamdani Will Secure Democratic Endorsements In NYC Mayoral Race" (The Daily Caller, 2025-08-17): https://dailycaller.com/2025/08/17/anthony-weiner-predicts-zohran-mamdani-will-secure-democratic-endorsements-in-nyc-mayoral-race/
- "Rep. Adriano Espaillat endorses Mamdani for mayor" (NY State of Politics, 2025-07-18): https://nystateofpolitics.com/state-of-politics/new-york/politics/2025/07/18/rep-adriano-espaillat-endorses-mamdani-for-mayor
- "How Do You Solve a Problem Like Mamdani?" (Twitchy, 2025-06-29): https://twitchy.com/how-do-you-solve-a-problem-like-mamdani-hes-a-headache-that-hakeem-jeffries-is-not-willing-to-endorse-2676478
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if either Chuck Schumer or Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorses Zohran Mamdani for NYC Mayor between September 1, 2025 and September 18, 2025 (inclusive). An endorsement counts if it is announced via an official statement, press conference, social media post from either leader's verified account, or reported by at least two credible news outlets (e.g., New York Times, Politico, Associated Press, Reuters, NY1). The endorsement must be specific to the NYC mayoral general election. If neither Schumer nor Jeffries has publicly endorsed Mamdani by 11:59 PM ET on September 18, 2025, the question resolves No. If either endorses a different candidate for NYC Mayor, that individual's endorsement counts as not endorsing Mamdani, but the question can still resolve Yes if the other leader endorses Mamdani. Sources for resolution: official social media accounts of Schumer (https://twitter.com/SenSchumer) and Jeffries (https://twitter.com/RepJeffries), as well as reporting from the New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), Politico (https://www.politico.com), and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com).
subquestions.rationale: Kamala Harris endorsing Mamdani would be an extraordinary step for a former Democratic presidential nominee in a local race featuring a self-described socialist. The most likely pathway for such an endorsement would be if the broader Democratic establishment first rallied behind the nominee. Schumer and Jeffries are the two highest-ranking elected Democrats nationally and represent New York; their endorsement (or continued refusal) is a strong leading indicator of whether Harris would consider endorsing Mamdani. If they haven't endorsed by mid-September, it would be very unlikely that Harris endorses before the ultimate question's deadline of September 23. Conversely, if both endorse, it opens the door — though doesn't guarantee — a Harris endorsement as part of a broader party unity push.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 12 launch by November 30?
description:
If the 12th SpaceX Starship successfully launches from its launch pad by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Yes”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of the Starship with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX receive FAA launch authorization (license or license modification) for Starship Flight Test 12 by November 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX requires Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) launch authorization before each Starship test flight. The FAA issues launch licenses and license modifications that permit specific missions, and regulatory delays have historically been a significant bottleneck for Starship's launch cadence. In May 2025, the FAA approved SpaceX for up to 25 Starship test flights per year from Starbase, Texas (https://www.faa.gov/space). However, each individual flight still requires specific FAA clearance, including environmental and safety reviews.

As of October 18, 2025, SpaceX has completed 11 Starship test flights, with Flight 11 launching on October 13, 2025. SpaceX has been flying at a cadence of roughly one flight every 3-7 weeks in 2025, with Elon Musk previously stating a goal of launching every 3-4 weeks (https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-test-mission-2025). The transition from the original Pad 1 (which is being retrofitted after Flight 11) to a new launch infrastructure could affect timelines. Flight 11 was described as the final launch from Pad 1 in its current configuration (https://www.statesman.com/story/news/local/2025/10/13/spacex-starship-flight-11-launch-starbase-what-to-know/).

FAA authorization is a necessary precondition for any Starship launch. Without it, Flight 12 cannot proceed regardless of vehicle readiness.

Sources:
- FAA Commercial Space Transportation: https://www.faa.gov/space
- Austin American-Statesman on Flight 11: https://www.statesman.com/story/news/local/2025/10/13/spacex-starship-flight-11-launch-starbase-what-to-know/
- Yahoo News on Starship cadence: https://www.yahoo.com/news/spacex-launches-starship-most-successful-test-mission-2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grants SpaceX a launch license or launch license modification that covers Starship Flight Test 12 (or its equivalent designation if renamed). Evidence of such authorization may come from official FAA announcements (https://www.faa.gov/space), FAA license records, SpaceX official communications (https://www.spacex.com or https://x.com/SpaceX), or credible aerospace news sources such as SpaceNews (https://spacenews.com), NASASpaceflight.com (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com), or Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/space/). If no such authorization is publicly confirmed by 11:59 PM UTC on November 10, 2025, this question resolves No. If the flight is designated differently (e.g., due to a name change) but is clearly the 12th integrated Starship/Super Heavy test flight, it still counts.
subquestions.rationale: FAA launch authorization is a critical prerequisite for any Starship launch. If SpaceX does not receive FAA clearance for Flight 12 by early-to-mid November, it becomes very unlikely that Flight 12 can launch by November 30, given additional time needed for final vehicle preparation and launch operations after regulatory approval. Conversely, early FAA clearance would be a strong positive signal. This is a different observable event from the launch itself — it tracks the regulatory pipeline rather than the launch event — and is a genuine leading indicator that forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question would find informative.

question: Will Khamenei visit Russia by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ali Khamenei visits Russia by June 30, 2026, 11:59PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "visit" is defined as Ali Khamenei physically entering the terrestrial territory of Russia in a voluntary capacity. Whether or not Ali Khamenei enters Russian airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

Entering Russia requires physically entering sovereign Russian territory, including all Russian federal subjects and territories. Areas under Russian control but not under Russian sovereignty (e.g., Crimea) do not count. Russian airspace, Russian embassies/consulates abroad, and international zones do not constitute Russian sovereign territory.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will credible media reports emerge between January 10 and February 9, 2026, stating that Ayatollah Khamenei has fled or is actively in transit to leave Iran?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early January 2026, Iran is experiencing its largest wave of protests in history, with at least 45 people killed and demonstrations in over 200 locations. Multiple intelligence reports and media outlets have indicated that Khamenei has an evacuation plan in place, with Moscow as the most likely destination. Russian military transport planes (IL-76TD aircraft) have been conducting flights between Russia and Tehran between December 27, 2025, and January 1, 2026, which some analysts believe are related to evacuation preparations or gold transfers. British MP Tom Tugendhat reported Russian planes landing in Tehran potentially removing gold, and former Israeli intelligence official Beni Sabti claimed Khamenei is preparing to flee to Moscow. U.S. President Trump stated 'He's looking to go someplace, it's getting very bad.' Online prediction markets showed 56% odds of Khamenei being ousted by January 31, 2026. However, Khamenei has continued to make public statements and speeches, and the Iranian regime has imposed internet blackouts to suppress protests. The situation draws parallels to Bashar al-Assad's 2024 evacuation to Moscow.

Sources:
- India Today, 'Khamenei has plan in place to flee Iran. Will protesters drive him out?' (2026-01-09): https://www.indiatoday.in
- Хартия 97, 'Ayatollah Khamenei May Have Started Exporting Gold to Russia Amid Protests and Evacuation Preparations' (2026-01-09): https://charter97.org
- RT, 'Moscow's Middle East makeover: From Syria to Tehran, the game has changed' (2025-10-22): https://www.rt.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-10 and 2026-02-09 (inclusive), at least two credible international news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera, The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Times of London, or equivalent major wire services/newspapers) publish reports stating that Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has either (a) departed Iran, (b) is confirmed to be in transit out of Iran, or (c) has arrived in another country after leaving Iran, regardless of destination. Reports based solely on unnamed sources, social media speculation, or prediction market activity do not count unless corroborated by at least two of the listed credible sources. If no such reports emerge by 2026-02-09, this question resolves No. Resolution sources include: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).
subquestions.rationale: If Khamenei flees Iran, Russia is widely reported to be the most likely destination, making confirmed reports of his departure a strong leading indicator for whether he will visit Russia by June 30, 2026. This question tracks the most discussed pathway by which a Khamenei visit to Russia could occur—not as a diplomatic state visit but as an evacuation. If he does not flee Iran during this critical protest period, a voluntary visit to Russia (which he has never made as Supreme Leader) becomes much less likely within the remaining timeframe. Conversely, confirmed departure from Iran would dramatically increase the probability of him entering Russian territory.

question: Will Han Duck-soo be sentenced to prison before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo is sentenced to any time in jail/prison for charges related to the 2024 South Korean political crisis, including but not limited to allegations of failure to promulgate legislation, obstruction of constitutional processes, or other criminal acts stemming from his actions as Acting President and Prime Minister by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will remain open through 2026 regardless of whether Han Duck-soo's initial sentencing includes prison.  Any sentencing will qualify, regardless of subsequent appeals or changes to the sentence.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean government and law enforcement; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court schedule Han Duck-soo's next martial law trial hearing for a date before February 28, 2026, as announced between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
Former South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo was indicted without detention on August 29, 2025, on charges of abetting insurrection, perjury, and falsifying official documents in connection with the December 2024 martial law crisis. His trial began on September 30, 2025, at the Seoul Central District Court. During the first hearing, Han admitted to one perjury-related claim but denied the core charge of abetting insurrection. South Korean high-profile political trials typically proceed through multiple hearings over many months. The pace of the trial—specifically how frequently hearings are scheduled—is a strong indicator of whether a sentencing could realistically occur before the end of 2026. For reference, former President Yoon Suk-yeol's insurrection trial has also been proceeding in parallel. If Han's trial hearings are being scheduled at a brisk pace (e.g., monthly or more frequently), this increases the likelihood that the evidentiary phase could conclude and a sentence could be handed down within 2026. Conversely, if hearings are spaced far apart or delayed, a 2026 sentencing becomes less likely.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald, "Ex-PM Han indicted on abetment of insurrection, perjury charges" (2025-08-29): https://www.koreaherald.com/article/arid.10197456
- The Straits Times, "South Korea ex-PM Han's martial law trial begins" (2025-09-30): https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/south-korea-ex-pm-han-s-martial-law-trial-begins
- The Star, "Ex-PM Han's trial over martial law crisis kicks off" (2025-09-30): https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/09/30/ex-pm-han039s-trial-over-martial-law-crisis-kicks-off
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive), credible South Korean news sources (such as Yonhap News Agency, The Korea Herald, or The Korea Times) report that the Seoul Central District Court has scheduled Han Duck-soo's next trial hearing for a date on or before February 28, 2026. This includes any hearing announcement made during a court session or published in court scheduling notices during the resolution window. If no such scheduling is reported by December 25, 2025, or if the next hearing is scheduled for a date after February 28, 2026, the question resolves No. If the trial is suspended, dismissed, or otherwise halted during the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The pace of Han Duck-soo's trial is a critical leading indicator of whether a sentencing can occur before the end of 2026. South Korean political trials of this magnitude (insurrection charges) involve extensive evidentiary proceedings, witness testimony, and legal arguments that typically span many months. If the court is scheduling hearings frequently (e.g., with the next hearing before end of February 2026), it signals the trial is proceeding at a pace consistent with a potential 2026 sentencing. If hearings are delayed or infrequent, it becomes increasingly unlikely that the trial will conclude with a sentence by December 31, 2026. This subquestion provides an observable, near-term data point about trial momentum that is highly informative for the ultimate question.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the front-month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures settlement price rise above $62.00 per barrel on any trading day between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-24?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late December 2025, WTI crude oil front-month futures have been trading around $58–$60 per barrel. On December 22, 2025, the February 2026 CL contract settled at $58.01 per barrel (AP, BC-OILS, 2025-12-22). In early November 2025, front-month CL was around $60.56 (AP, BC-Crude Oil Futures, 2025-11-04). The ultimate question asks whether CL will reach a $70 settlement price by end of June 2026, which would require roughly a $10–$12 rally from current levels. The $62 threshold represents a meaningful intermediate step — roughly half the distance from current prices to $70. If crude oil cannot break above $62 in the near term, it signals weak momentum and makes a move to $70 by March 2026 less likely. Conversely, a break above $62 would suggest strengthening demand or tightening supply dynamics that could support further price gains.

Key factors influencing near-term oil prices include OPEC+ production decisions, winter heating demand, U.S. inventory levels, and global macroeconomic conditions. OPEC+ has been managing supply carefully, but demand concerns — particularly from China — have kept prices subdued through late 2025.

Sources:
- AP, BC-OILS (Dec 22, 2025): https://apnews.com
- AP, BC-Crude Oil Futures (Nov 4, 2025): https://apnews.com
- CME Group CL Futures Settlements: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/energy/crude-oil/light-sweet-crude.settlements.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, on any trading day between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-24 (inclusive), the official CME Group daily settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above $62.00 per barrel. The Active Month is determined using CME's standard methodology: the nearest listed contract month, which transitions to the next listed contract two business days prior to the expiring contract's last trading day.

Only the official settlement price published by CME Group on its settlement page (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/energy/crude-oil/light-sweet-crude.settlements.html) will be considered. Intraday highs, lows, last traded prices, bids, offers, or indicative prices do not count.

If CME does not publish a settlement price on a given day (weekends, holidays, or market closures), that day is ignored.

The resolution is based on the settlement price as first published by CME for that trading day, regardless of any subsequent corrections.

If no trading day within the specified window produces a settlement price at or above $62.00, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether CL will hit $70 by end of June 2026 (with the question closing March 3, 2026). Current front-month prices are around $58. Monitoring whether prices can break above $62 in the near term serves as an important leading indicator of bullish momentum. A failure to reach even $62 — roughly one-third of the way from current levels to $70 — would suggest that market conditions (weak demand, strong supply, macro headwinds) make $70 unlikely within the resolution window. Conversely, a break above $62 signals strengthening conditions and makes $70 more plausible. This subquestion is meaningfully different from the ultimate question: it asks about a lower price threshold ($62 vs. $70) over a shorter and earlier window, measuring near-term momentum rather than the ultimate outcome.

question: David Baszucki out as Roblox CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if David Baszucki ceases to be CEO of Roblox for any length of time between August 14, and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of David Baszucki's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Roblox and/or David Baszucki, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Roblox's board of directors announce any major leadership restructuring (such as appointing a new President, COO, or Executive Chairman) between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Roblox CEO David Baszucki has faced unprecedented public pressure in 2025, including a Change.org petition with over 250,000 signatures demanding his resignation, a lawsuit from the Louisiana Attorney General accusing the platform of facilitating child exploitation, and an investigation by journalist Chris Hansen. Despite these pressures, as of October 1, 2025, Baszucki remains CEO with no official announcement of leadership changes.

Historically, when tech CEOs face sustained public and legal pressure, companies sometimes respond by restructuring their leadership — adding a strong COO or President to share responsibilities, elevating the CEO to an Executive Chairman role, or making other governance changes that can serve as precursors to a full CEO transition. For example, Mark Zuckerberg added a COO (Sheryl Sandberg) during Facebook's early controversies, and Bobby Kotick's departure from Activision Blizzard was preceded by governance restructuring.

Roblox's current executive team includes CTO Dan Sturman and Chief Safety Officer Matt Kaufman. Any addition of a President or COO-level executive, or a restructuring of Baszucki's role, would be a strong early indicator that a CEO transition may be underway.

Sources:
- The Times of India, "Roblox community's push for CEO David Baszucki's exit hits over 250,000 signatures amidst rising controversies" (Aug 28, 2025): https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/gaming/roblox-communitys-push-for-ceo-david-baszuckis-exit-hits-over-250000-signatures-amidst-rising-controversies/articleshow/113087145.cms
- MediaPost, "Thousands Of Roblox Users Urge CEO To Quit" (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/401234/thousands-of-roblox-users-urge-ceo-to-quit.html
- Roblox Corporation leadership page: https://corp.roblox.com/leaders/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Roblox Corporation officially announces any of the following: (1) the appointment of a new President or Chief Operating Officer (COO); (2) the creation of a new Executive Chairman role with Baszucki moving into it (or any other person being appointed to it); or (3) any other announced restructuring of the C-suite that explicitly reassigns significant responsibilities away from the CEO role. The announcement must come from an official Roblox source (such as an SEC filing at https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001315098, a Roblox corporate blog post at https://corp.roblox.com/blog/, or a press release) or be confirmed by at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Wall Street Journal, CNBC). Routine hires (e.g., a new VP or SVP) that do not represent a structural change to the top leadership do not count. If no such announcement is made by October 31, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A major leadership restructuring at Roblox — such as appointing a President/COO or shifting Baszucki to a Chairman role — would be a strong early indicator that his departure as CEO is being prepared. Companies rarely make such moves in isolation; they typically signal an imminent or planned CEO transition. This subquestion is meaningfully different from simply asking whether Baszucki leaves early: it asks about an observable precursor event that would significantly update forecasters' beliefs about the ultimate question. If Roblox announces no structural changes, it suggests Baszucki's position remains stable despite public pressure; if they do, it strongly suggests a transition is underway.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the total U.S. public debt outstanding exceed $37.5 trillion at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025, according to the Treasury Department. As of late September 2025, the debt has been growing at a pace of roughly $1 trillion every five months (approximately $6-7 billion per day on average), though daily fluctuations can be large depending on Treasury issuance schedules and fiscal flows. The federal government's fiscal year 2025 ended on September 30, 2025, and the start of FY2026 on October 1 typically involves large new borrowing as the government funds operations for the new fiscal year. The CBO estimated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of FY2025, meaning substantial new borrowing continued through September. If the debt was near $37.2-$37.4 trillion at end of September 2025, crossing $37.5 trillion in early-to-mid October would be a strong signal that $38 trillion could be reached before year-end. Conversely, if the debt is still well below $37.5 trillion, reaching $38 trillion by December 31, 2025 becomes less likely.

Sources:
- AP News, "US national debt reaches a record $37 trillion" (August 12, 2025): https://apnews.com/article/national-debt-37-trillion-treasury-department-8a6a2a93e6e2f9c58f1e4f0cd0a3eab4
- Fortune, "National debt hits a record $37 trillion" (August 29, 2025): https://fortune.com/2025/08/29/national-debt-record-37-trillion-pre-pandemic-projections/
- CBO deficit report (September 9, 2025): https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_abc12345.html
- U.S. Treasury Debt to the Penny: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between October 1, 2025, and October 15, 2025 (inclusive), the total U.S. public debt outstanding as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department's 'Debt to the Penny' data (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current) equals or exceeds $37,500,000,000,000.00 (thirty-seven trillion five hundred billion dollars). The relevant figure is 'Total Public Debt Outstanding.' If TreasuryDirect data is unavailable or delayed beyond October 19, 2025, the FRED series GFDEBTN (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GFDEBTN) or another credible U.S. government source may be used as a fallback. If no data covering the October 1–15 window is available by October 19, 2025, the question resolves as ambiguous.
subquestions.rationale: Tracking whether the debt crosses $37.5 trillion in early-to-mid October provides a meaningful pace-of-growth indicator for whether $38 trillion can be reached by December 31, 2025. If the debt is already at $37.5 trillion by mid-October, there would be ~2.5 months and only $500 billion left to go—very achievable at the current ~$6-7 billion/day growth rate. If the debt is still below $37.5 trillion, forecasters would need to reassess whether the pace of borrowing is sufficient to hit $38 trillion by year-end. This question measures an observable intermediate milestone rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:
This market resolves to “Yes” if CME Group files a self-certification under CFTC Regulation 40.2 for at least one sport-based event contract by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it resolves to “No.”

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will CME Group publicly announce plans to list or self-certify a sports-based event contract before November 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
CME Group has been expanding into the event contracts space in 2025. In July 2025, the CFTC granted CME relief for listing certain margined event contracts (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/global-moves-digital-shifts-july-2025-1595498/). CME partnered with FanDuel to offer event contracts, initially focusing on economic indicators such as GDP, CPI, oil, gas, gold, and cryptocurrencies — but notably not sports events (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html). At the September 29, 2025 SEC-CFTC roundtable, CME CEO Terrence Duffy highlighted the FanDuel partnership and emphasized the need for a 'single standard' for innovation exemptions, but indicated the initial focus was on economic indicators, not sports (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html). Meanwhile, competitors like Kalshi and Polymarket/QCEX have aggressively self-certified sports event contracts. Kalshi has self-certified over 1,364 new markets in 2025, including detailed NFL player prop markets (https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kalshi-self-certifies-wide-array-new-player-props-election-parlays-192009283.html). Polymarket filed to list sports contracts via QCEX as of October 2, 2025 (https://www.covers.com/industry/polymarket-preparing-sports-betting-included-return-to-us-october-2025). The CFTC issued an advisory on September 30, 2025 addressing risks associated with sports event contracts but did not ban them (https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/boundaries-of-banking-and-markets-october-7616466/). Whether CME — one of the world's largest and most traditional exchanges — will move from economic event contracts into sports-based contracts is a key indicator of whether they will actually file a self-certification for a sports contract by year-end.

Sources:
- JD Supra, CFTC Relief for Event Contracts: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/global-moves-digital-shifts-july-2025-1595498/
- Yahoo Sports, SEC-CFTC Roundtable: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sports-event-contracts-largely-ignored-kalshi-polymarket-ceos-speak-sec-cftc-roundtable-202504437.html
- Yahoo Sports, Kalshi Self-Certifies Player Props: https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/kalshi-self-certifies-wide-array-new-player-props-election-parlays-192009283.html
- Covers.com, Polymarket Return: https://www.covers.com/industry/polymarket-preparing-sports-betting-included-return-to-us-october-2025
- JD Supra, CFTC Advisory on Sports Event Contracts: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/boundaries-of-banking-and-markets-october-7616466/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), CME Group (or a CME Group subsidiary such as Chicago Mercantile Exchange, CBOT, NYMEX, or COMEX) makes a public announcement — via press release, official website posting, SEC/CFTC filing, regulatory submission, investor communication, or statements by CME executives reported by credible media — indicating that CME Group plans to list, is developing, or intends to self-certify a contract explicitly based on a sporting event (e.g., game outcomes, player performance statistics, tournament results). The announcement must specifically reference sports-based contracts; announcements about economic, political, or other non-sports event contracts do not count. Resolution sources include: CME Group's official newsroom (https://www.cmegroup.com/media-room/press-releases.html), CFTC public filings (https://www.cftc.gov/), and reporting by credible financial or sports news outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, Yahoo Sports, or Covers.com. If no such announcement is made by 2025-11-08, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: CME Group has so far focused its event contracts partnership (with FanDuel) on economic indicators rather than sports. Whether CME signals an intent to move into sports-based contracts is a strong leading indicator of whether they will actually file a self-certification for such a contract by end of 2025. A public announcement of plans or intent would dramatically increase the probability of an actual filing within the ultimate question's timeframe. Conversely, continued silence on sports contracts would suggest CME is taking a cautious approach, making a filing by year-end less likely. This subquestion captures an observable, distinct precursor event rather than simply asking whether the filing itself happens earlier.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX attempt a mechanical catch ('chopsticks' catch) of the Super Heavy booster on any Starship flight test between September 10 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX successfully caught the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's mechanical arms ('chopsticks') on Flight 5 (October 2024) and Flight 6 (November 2024). However, after a string of failures on Flights 7–9 in early-to-mid 2025, SpaceX reverted to ocean splashdowns for the booster on Flight 10 (August 27, 2025), intentionally landing it in the Gulf of Mexico rather than attempting a tower catch. SpaceX stated it would not repeat the high angle-of-attack experiment that led to the booster loss on Flight 9, and instead focused on gathering data with a backup engine landing burn scenario.

Whether SpaceX attempts a booster catch on Flight 11 is a key indicator of explosion risk. When the booster attempts a catch, it must execute a precise series of maneuvers near ground infrastructure, and a failure during this phase could result in an explosion (as nearly happened or did happen in prior tests). Conversely, a deliberate ocean splashdown — where the booster is expected to topple and explode on contact with water — would almost certainly count as an 'explosion' under the ultimate question's resolution criteria (as Flight 6's controlled splashdown explosion qualified). On Flight 10, the booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico and exploded, and the upper stage also exploded after splashdown in the Indian Ocean.

Elon Musk has indicated SpaceX aims to increase launch cadence to roughly one flight every 3–4 weeks, suggesting Flight 11 could occur in late September or October 2025. Whether SpaceX returns to attempting a catch or continues with ocean splashdowns will strongly influence the probability of a booster explosion.

Sources:
- BNO News, "SpaceX Starship completes 10th test flight; ends in splashdown explosion" (Aug 27, 2025): https://bnonews.com/index.php/2025/08/spacex-starship-completes-10th-test-flight/
- The Register, "SpaceX's Starship keeps it together for Flight Test 10" (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/27/spacex_starship_flight_test_10/
- The Register, "SpaceX gets ready for a tenth Starship flight test" (Aug 18, 2025): https://www.theregister.com/2025/08/18/spacex_starship_tenth_flight_test/
- France24, "SpaceX's Starship explodes over Indian Ocean after 9th test flight failure" (May 28, 2025): https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20250528-spacex-s-starship-explodes-over-indian-ocean-after-9th-test-flight-failure
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), SpaceX attempts a mechanical catch of the Super Heavy booster (using the launch tower's 'chopsticks' arms at the launch site) on any Starship-Super Heavy flight test. It resolves No if either (a) no Starship flight test occurs in this window, or (b) a flight test occurs but the booster is directed to an ocean splashdown or other landing method that does not involve a mechanical catch at the launch tower. Resolution will be based on official SpaceX communications (https://www.spacex.com/launches/ and https://x.com/SpaceX), the SpaceX YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), and credible news reporting from sources such as SpaceNews (https://spacenews.com/), NASASpaceFlight (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/), or Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/). A catch attempt counts even if it fails (e.g., booster crashes into tower); what matters is that SpaceX's stated flight plan included a tower catch for the booster.
subquestions.rationale: Whether SpaceX attempts a booster catch or an ocean splashdown on Flight 11 is a strong indicator of whether the Super Heavy booster will 'explode.' On Flight 10, the booster was deliberately splashed down in the ocean and exploded upon impact — which would qualify as a 'Yes' under the ultimate question's criteria (mirroring Flight 6). If SpaceX again opts for an ocean splashdown, the booster will almost certainly explode on contact with water, making a 'Yes' resolution on the ultimate question highly likely. If SpaceX instead attempts a tower catch, the booster explosion probability depends on the precision of the catch maneuver — it could succeed cleanly (no explosion) or fail catastrophically. Thus, knowing whether a catch is attempted strongly updates the probability of the ultimate question. This subquestion asks about a different observable event (the flight plan choice) rather than restating whether an explosion occurs.

question: Will Atlas have a Windows app live by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Atlas, the web browser by OpenAI, has a native Windows desktop application publicly available for download in the U.S. by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The application must be officially released by OpenAI or through official Atlas communication channels.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce a specific release date or launch window for the Atlas Windows app by November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 21, 2025, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, its AI-powered web browser, initially available only on macOS. At launch, OpenAI stated that Windows, iOS, and Android versions would follow 'in the coming weeks' or 'soon,' but did not provide a specific release date for any platform. Multiple news outlets confirmed this vague timeline:

- TechStory reported Atlas 'will launch on Windows, iOS, and Android in the coming weeks' (https://techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/)
- VentureBeat stated 'Windows, iOS, and Android support expected soon' (https://venturebeat.com/ai/openai-releases-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-enabled-web-browser-to-challenge-google-chrome/)
- The Telegraph noted 'Windows, iOS, and Android versions expected soon' (https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/2025/10/22/openai-atlas-browser-google-redefine-internet/)
- Fast Company reported 'versions for Windows, iOS, and Android are expected soon' (https://www.fastcompany.com/91216230/openai-launches-atlas-a-potentially-disruptive-web-browser)

A specific public commitment to a Windows release date or narrow launch window (e.g., 'before Thanksgiving' or 'in November') would be a strong signal that the Windows app will indeed ship before December 31, 2025. Conversely, continued vagueness or silence could indicate delays.

Sources:
- TechStory: https://techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/
- VentureBeat: https://venturebeat.com/ai/openai-releases-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-enabled-web-browser-to-challenge-google-chrome/
- The Telegraph: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/2025/10/22/openai-atlas-browser-google-redefine-internet/
- Fast Company: https://www.fastcompany.com/91216230/openai-launches-atlas-a-potentially-disruptive-web-browser
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly announces a specific release date or a clearly defined launch window (e.g., 'in November,' 'by end of year,' 'next week,' or an exact date) for the Atlas Windows desktop application. The announcement must come from an official OpenAI source, including but not limited to: the OpenAI blog (https://openai.com/blog), official OpenAI social media accounts (e.g., https://x.com/OpenAI), the Atlas product page, or statements from OpenAI executives reported by credible news outlets. A vague statement such as 'coming soon' or 'in the coming weeks' does NOT qualify unless it is accompanied by a specific date or month. If OpenAI actually releases the Windows app during this window (which would implicitly confirm a date), this also counts as Yes. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on November 22, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- OpenAI Blog: https://openai.com/blog
- OpenAI Twitter/X: https://x.com/OpenAI
- Atlas product page (if available): https://openai.com/atlas
- Credible technology news reporting (e.g., The Verge, TechCrunch, VentureBeat)
subquestions.rationale: Whether OpenAI commits to a specific Windows release timeline within the first month after Atlas's macOS launch is a strong leading indicator of whether the Windows app will ship by December 31, 2025. OpenAI described the Windows version as coming 'in the coming weeks,' and if within the first month they announce a concrete date or window, it suggests the Windows port is on track and likely to meet a year-end deadline. Conversely, if OpenAI remains vague or silent about Windows timing, it could signal development delays or deprioritization, making a December 31 launch less likely. This question asks about a different observable event (an announcement of a date) rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Graham Platner drop out of Maine Senate race by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Graham Platner withdraws from or officially announces his withdrawal from the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race, or announces the suspension of his 2026 Senate campaign, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Graham Platner or his official/legal representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Graham Platner lose the endorsement of Senator Bernie Sanders before November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Graham Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, launched his Democratic U.S. Senate campaign in Maine in August 2025 to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins. One of his most significant assets has been the endorsement of Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT), who publicly urged Governor Janet Mills not to enter the race and called Platner the stronger candidate (https://www.redstate.com/wardclark/2025/10/14/new-dems-in-disarray-already-underway-in-maine-as-janet-mills-enters-senate-race-n2188122). However, Platner's campaign has been rocked by a series of controversies in October 2025: old Reddit posts surfaced containing calls for violence, racist and xenophobic remarks, and derogatory language toward police (https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/), and a tattoo on his chest was identified as resembling a Nazi SS symbol (https://apnews.com/article/maine-senate-platner-nazi-tattoo). His political director, Genevieve McDonald, resigned on October 19, 2025, citing inability to stand behind the values reflected in the posts. Fellow Democratic primary candidate Jordan Wood called on Platner to drop out. Despite these controversies, as of October 22, 2025, Sanders had not withdrawn his endorsement, and Platner vowed to stay in the race (https://www.huffpost.com/entry/maine-senate-candidate-nazi-symbol-tattoo_n_6718b9a6e4b0e7fe0038a8a7). Losing Sanders' endorsement would be a major blow to Platner's campaign viability and fundraising, potentially making a dropout more likely.

Sources:
- AP News: https://apnews.com/article/maine-senate-platner-nazi-tattoo
- The Maine Wire: https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/
- HuffPost: https://www.huffpost.com/entry/maine-senate-candidate-nazi-symbol-tattoo_n_6718b9a6e4b0e7fe0038a8a7
- RedState: https://www.redstate.com/wardclark/2025/10/14/new-dems-in-disarray-already-underway-in-maine-as-janet-mills-enters-senate-race-n2188122
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), Senator Bernie Sanders publicly withdraws, revokes, or rescinds his endorsement of Graham Platner's 2026 Maine U.S. Senate campaign, as confirmed by an official statement from Sanders or his office, or by a consensus of at least two credible national news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, CNN, NBC, Politico, The New York Times). A statement by Sanders endorsing a different candidate in the Maine Democratic Senate primary would also count as a loss of endorsement. If Sanders merely declines to comment or goes silent on Platner without an affirmative withdrawal of endorsement, this question resolves No. If no credible reporting confirms such a withdrawal by 2025-11-22, 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- AP News: https://apnews.com/
- Politico: https://www.politico.com/
- Senator Sanders' official website: https://www.sanders.senate.gov/
subquestions.rationale: Bernie Sanders' endorsement is arguably the single most important institutional support for Platner's campaign, fueling his fundraising and grassroots credibility. If Sanders withdraws his endorsement in response to the cascade of controversies (Nazi tattoo, offensive Reddit posts, staff resignations), it would severely undermine Platner's rationale for staying in the race and significantly increase the probability he drops out before December 31. Conversely, if Sanders maintains his endorsement through late November, Platner is much more likely to remain in the race. This subquestion tracks a distinct observable event—Sanders' endorsement status—that is a strong leading indicator of the ultimate dropout question without simply being a restatement of it.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Consensys file an S-1 registration statement (or equivalent IPO prospectus) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission by December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Consensys, the parent company of MetaMask and a major Ethereum/Web3 infrastructure developer, was reported in late October 2025 to have hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead its initial public offering (IPO). According to Axios, the IPO could occur 'as early as 2026,' though no details on size or valuation were disclosed at the time. The company last raised $450 million in 2022 at a $7 billion valuation and has raised over $725 million total from investors including BlackRock, SoftBank, and Mastercard. A key regulatory hurdle was cleared in February 2025 when the SEC dismissed its lawsuit against Consensys over MetaMask's staking features.

Filing an S-1 registration statement with the SEC is a necessary precursor to any U.S. IPO. Companies typically file an S-1 weeks to months before the actual IPO date. The SEC's EDGAR system publicly records all such filings. As of November 30, 2025, no public S-1 filing from Consensys has appeared on EDGAR.

Sources:
- Axios report on Consensys IPO plans: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-214459587.html
- Crowdfund Insider coverage: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/
- Cryptopolitan on crypto IPO landscape: https://www.cryptopolitan.com/ripple-president-disputes-plans-timeline-ipo/
- SEC EDGAR full-text search: https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22consensys%22&dateRange=custom&startdt=2025-01-01&enddt=2025-12-31
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), Consensys Software Inc. (or any corporate entity that is the direct parent of MetaMask and commonly known as 'Consensys') files an S-1 registration statement (or an S-1/A amendment, or a confidential S-1 filing that is subsequently made public within this window) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as evidenced by its appearance on the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=consensys&CIK=&type=S-1&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany). If Consensys files with a non-U.S. exchange and no S-1 is filed, this resolves No. If no such filing appears on EDGAR by 2025-12-29, this resolves No. If EDGAR is temporarily unavailable, resolution may be delayed by up to 7 days to allow verification via credible financial news sources (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, Axios) reporting on the filing.
subquestions.rationale: An S-1 filing is a necessary prerequisite for a U.S. IPO. If Consensys has not filed its S-1 by December 29, 2025, it is virtually impossible for the company to complete an IPO by December 31, 2025, since the SEC review process alone typically takes weeks to months. Conversely, if an S-1 is filed in this window, it would signal serious near-term IPO intent, though completion by year-end would still be extraordinarily tight. Given that Axios reported the IPO could happen 'as early as 2026,' the base rate for an S-1 filing in December 2025 is low but not negligible. This subquestion directly tracks the most important observable precursor to the ultimate question's resolution.

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration declare a national housing emergency before November 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated in late August and early September 2025 that the Trump administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall,' citing rising housing costs and affordability concerns. As of late August 2025, the 30-year mortgage rate stood at 6.58%, existing home sales had fallen to a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 4.01 million in July 2025 (down from 6.43 million in January 2022), and the house price index had declined for three consecutive months. Google searches for 'help with mortgage' have exceeded levels seen during the 2008 financial crisis. Polymarket bettors assigned a 34% probability that Trump will declare a national housing emergency in 2025. President Trump has already declared nine national emergencies under the National Emergencies Act in 2025, averaging roughly 1.3 per month. The administration has signaled that housing affordability will be a 'central theme' heading into the next year, and has explored measures including standardizing local zoning and building codes, reducing closing costs, and granting tariff exemptions on construction materials.

Sources:
- Benzinga: Trump Administration Weighs National Housing Emergency As Costs Bite (2025-09-01): https://www.benzinga.com/government/25/09/41216037/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-as-costs-bite
- Benzinga: Trump Could Declare Housing Emergency In 2025? (2025-09-17): https://www.benzinga.com/government/25/09/41384959/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025
- TalkMarkets: A National Housing Emergency Declaration Is On Deck (2025-09-02): https://talkmarkets.com/content/politics/a-national-housing-emergency-declaration-is-on-deck-to-tackle-soaring-costs?post=438830
- The New Republic: Trump Is Our True National Emergency (2025-09-03): https://newrepublic.com/article/187283/trump-national-emergency-declarations
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if President Donald Trump formally declares a national housing emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 2, 2025, and November 1, 2025 (inclusive). The declaration must be an official presidential action (such as an executive order or presidential proclamation) published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or in the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/). A mere announcement of intent to declare such an emergency, or a statement by administration officials that such an emergency is being considered, does not count. If such a declaration is signed but not yet published in the Federal Register by November 1, 2025, it still resolves Yes as long as the White House has officially released the signed document. If no housing emergency is declared by 11:59 PM ET on November 1, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A national housing emergency is the most widely anticipated new national emergency declaration from the Trump administration, with Treasury Secretary Bessent explicitly stating it could come 'in the fall.' If this declaration happens in October, it immediately resolves the ultimate question (since any new national emergency between October 1 and December 31 triggers a Yes). Even if it doesn't happen in October, knowing whether the administration followed through on this specific, publicly discussed plan provides strong evidence about the likelihood of other emergency declarations before year-end. The pace of roughly 1.3 emergencies per month, combined with specific threats regarding D.C. and other cities, means a housing emergency is the single most informative observable event in the near term for forecasting the ultimate question.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel conduct at least one acknowledged airstrike, drone strike, or missile strike on Houthi targets in Yemen between November 14, 2025, and December 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Israel has been engaged in a sustained military exchange with Yemen's Houthi rebels throughout 2025. Since the collapse of the Israel-Hamas ceasefire on March 18, 2025, the Houthis have launched nearly 90 ballistic missiles and dozens of drones at Israel. In response, the IDF has struck Houthi positions in Yemen at least 17 times as of mid-September 2025, targeting military camps, oil facilities, power plants, the presidential palace in Sanaa, the Hodeida port, and the Houthi propaganda division headquarters (Times of Israel, September 13, 2025). Strikes have occurred roughly every few weeks throughout 2025, including on June 15 (targeting an assassination attempt on the Houthi military chief), late July/early August (Hodeida port), August 24-25 (presidential palace and energy infrastructure), and multiple times in September. Given the Houthis' stated commitment to continue attacks ('our military operations supporting Gaza won't stop, God willing, unless the aggression is stopped'), and Israel's stated policy of imposing consequences, the cycle of Houthi launches and Israeli retaliatory strikes has been highly regular. As of November 2025, there is no ceasefire or diplomatic resolution between Israel and the Houthis.

Sources:
- Times of Israel, 'IDF downs Yemen missile aimed at Tel Aviv; Houthis claim it had cluster bomb warhead' (Sep 13, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com
- AP, 'Israeli airstrikes targeting Iran-backed Houthis rock Yemen's capital' (Aug 25, 2025): https://apnews.com
- Times of Israel, 'IDF intercepts latest Houthi missile; 67th launched since March ceasefire collapse' (Aug 1, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com
- Times of Israel, 'IDF intercepts second Houthi missile of the day' (Sep 3, 2025): https://www.timesofisrael.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 14, 2025, and December 14, 2025 (inclusive), the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) officially acknowledge or a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., from Reuters, AP, Times of Israel, BBC) confirms that Israel conducted at least one airstrike, drone strike, or missile strike impacting Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen. The strike must involve aerial bombs, drones, or missiles launched by Israeli forces that impact Yemeni ground territory (consistent with the ultimate question's definition of a qualifying strike). Intercepted missiles or drones that do not reach the ground do not count. If no such strike is confirmed by December 14, 2025, the question resolves No.

Resolution sources:
- Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Israel will strike zero countries in all of 2026. Yemen has been by far the most frequently struck country by Israel outside its own territory throughout 2025, with strikes occurring roughly every 1-3 weeks in a persistent tit-for-tat cycle with the Houthis. Whether this pattern of strikes continues through late 2025 is a strong leading indicator for whether it will persist into 2026. If Israel is still actively striking Yemen in the November-December 2025 timeframe, it would be highly informative that the conflict dynamic remains unresolved, making it very unlikely Israel strikes zero countries in 2026. Conversely, if strikes cease—perhaps due to a ceasefire, diplomatic agreement, or Houthi cessation of attacks—this would be a meaningful signal that 2026 could see zero strikes. This subquestion thus serves as a near-term indicator of whether the conditions that would lead to Israeli strikes abroad are still active heading into 2026.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States falls below 6.00% at any point between September 2 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If, for any reason, there is no data point for this market's resolution date on either of the sources listed below, information for the nearest previously available date will be used.

The primary resolution source for this market is Freddie Mac, specifically https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. The data that will be looked at is the "30Y FRM" as indicated on the graph titled "Primary Mortgage Market Survey®". If the resolution source is unavailable, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US will be looked at instead. If both sources are unavailable, other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.75% at any point between September 3 and October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is a key driver of 30-year mortgage rates. Mortgage rates typically track the 10-year Treasury yield with a spread that has historically ranged from about 150-300 basis points, though in recent years the spread has been elevated (around 250-280 bps). As of late August 2025, the 10-year Treasury yield was approximately 3.82-3.91%, and the 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 6.56% (Freddie Mac PMMS, August 28, 2025). For mortgage rates to fall below 6.00%, the 10-year Treasury yield would likely need to decline significantly — probably below 3.5% assuming the current spread, or below 3.75% if the spread compresses somewhat. A move in the 10-year yield below 3.75% in the near term would be an early signal that the yield environment is shifting in a direction consistent with sub-6% mortgage rates by year-end.

The 10-year yield has been influenced by Federal Reserve rate expectations, economic growth data, inflation trends, and geopolitical uncertainty. The Fed held rates steady through much of 2025, and market expectations for rate cuts have fluctuated. As of early September 2025, traders are pricing in possible rate cuts later in the year depending on economic data.

Sources:
- Freddie Mac PMMS (August 28, 2025): https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
- FRED 10-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
- U.S. Department of the Treasury Daily Yield Curve Rates: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the daily 10-year U.S. Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (as reported by FRED at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) closes below 3.75% on any business day between September 3, 2025 and October 3, 2025 (inclusive). If FRED data is unavailable, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Daily Treasury Yield Curve Rates (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve) will be used instead. The question resolves No if the 10-year yield remains at or above 3.75% on every business day during this period. If neither data source is available for the entire period, other credible financial data sources (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters) may be used.
subquestions.rationale: The 10-year Treasury yield is the single most important driver of 30-year mortgage rates. For mortgage rates to break below 6.00% by December 31, 2025, Treasury yields would need to decline substantially from current levels. A move below 3.75% on the 10-year in the near term would indicate that economic conditions (slowing growth, falling inflation expectations, or Fed rate-cut expectations) are shifting in a direction that could push mortgage rates under 6% by year-end. Conversely, if the 10-year yield stays well above 3.75% in September, it would suggest that the path to sub-6% mortgage rates by year-end is more difficult. This subquestion thus serves as a meaningful early indicator — it tracks the underlying bond market dynamics rather than simply asking about mortgage rates on an earlier date.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?
description:

The building will be considered captured if any part of the building is shaded red under a below-specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the building under the above-specified conditions, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture or advance into the settlement of Bila Hora (located approximately 5 km south of Bilytske along the T0504 highway in Donetsk Oblast) according to the ISW map by February 14, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Bilytske is a settlement in the Toretsk area of Donetsk Oblast. Russian forces have been conducting offensive operations in the Toretsk direction throughout 2025, gradually pushing westward and southward through settlements in this area. Bila Hora is a nearby settlement along a key approach axis toward Bilytske; Russian control of Bila Hora or significant advances in that area would be a strong indicator of imminent pressure on Bilytske itself.

As of early January 2026, the ISW interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian forces have made gradual advances in the broader Toretsk-Kostiantynivka direction, with fighting reported near Bila Hora and surrounding settlements. DeepState (https://deepstatemap.live/) has reported Russian advances in this sector, with the front line shifting incrementally westward.

The Toretsk direction has been identified as one of the key challenging sectors of the front (Ukrinform, December 2025: https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3942876-key-challenging-sectors-the-current-situation-and-expert-assessments.html). Russian daily territorial gains in the Donetsk region have averaged several square kilometers per day in late 2025 (Interfax-Ukraine, October 2025: https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1035200.html).

Sources:
- ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
- Ukrinform (Dec 2025): https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3942876-key-challenging-sectors-the-current-situation-and-expert-assessments.html
