subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14 (inclusive), the ISW interactive Ukraine conflict map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian-controlled territory (shaded as 'Assessed Russian Control', 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine', or 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours') covering any part of the built-up area of Bila Hora, Donetsk Oblast (approximate center coordinates: 48.3855° N, 37.1870° E), and this shading persists through the next full ISW daily update cycle.

If the ISW map becomes unavailable, DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as a fallback. If both sources are unavailable, a consensus of credible OSINT reporting may be used.

The question resolves No if no such shading appears on the ISW map covering any part of Bila Hora's built-up area by end of day (UTC) on 2026-02-14.

'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine' shading does not qualify. Temporary map glitches do not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: Bila Hora lies along one of the key approach routes toward Bilytske from the south/southeast. Russian capture of or advance into Bila Hora would indicate that the front line is moving toward the specific building at 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E in Bilytske. If Russia has not yet reached Bila Hora by mid-February, it becomes much less likely that forces will have advanced the additional distance to capture the target building in Bilytske by late February. Conversely, if Bila Hora falls early, it signals rapid progress in this direction and increases the probability that Bilytske could be reached. This makes it a meaningful leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a standalone bill or amendment establishing a de minimis crypto tax exemption be formally introduced in either chamber of the U.S. Congress between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The concept of a de minimis tax exemption for small cryptocurrency transactions has been a recurring legislative goal in 2025 but has not yet been enacted. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) proposed a de minimis exemption (transactions under $300, with a $5,000 annual cap) as part of her Digital Asset Tax Fairness Act, but the provision was stripped from President Trump's reconciliation bill in July 2025 due to revenue concerns (https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/). In October 2025, Lummis pledged to reintroduce the proposal in upcoming Senate sessions (https://decrypt.co/283927/dorsey-lummis-push-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-expands-btc-payments). Meanwhile, 66+ crypto organizations sent a letter to President Trump on November 20, 2025, requesting a $600 per transaction de minimis exemption through either executive or legislative action (https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-on-trump-for-tax-clarity/). The crypto industry has also been lobbying Congress directly, with the American Innovation Project hosting a private dinner with House Ways and Means Committee members on the week of November 17, 2025 (https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/). The White House has signaled support for such an exemption through Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt's statements, but no formal bill or executive order has yet materialized. The U.S. Senate Finance Committee held a hearing on digital asset taxation on October 1, 2025, which was intended to build consensus before policy action (https://ambcrypto.com/u-s-senate-to-discuss-digital-assets-tax-reforms-on-october-1-details/). As of late November 2025, Congress is dealing with a short-term funding stopgap expiring January 30, 2026, and the legislative calendar is highly compressed before the holiday recess.

Sources:
- CryptoNews (Lummis backs de minimis exemption): https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/
- Decrypt (Dorsey, Lummis push for Bitcoin tax relief): https://decrypt.co/283927/dorsey-lummis-push-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-expands-btc-payments
- Coinspeaker (66 crypto orgs letter to Trump): https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-on-trump-for-tax-clarity/
- TechStory (Crypto lobbying push): https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/
- AMBCrypto (Senate Finance Committee hearing): https://ambcrypto.com/u-s-senate-to-discuss-digital-assets-tax-reforms-on-october-1-details/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between November 30, 2025 and December 29, 2025 (inclusive), a new bill or amendment is formally introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives or U.S. Senate that specifically establishes a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions (i.e., exempting small crypto transactions from capital gains reporting below a specified dollar threshold). The bill or amendment must be assigned a bill number and appear in the Congressional Record or on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). Reintroductions of previously numbered bills count only if they receive a new bill number during this window. Bills that merely reference crypto taxation in general without a specific de minimis exemption provision do not qualify. If no such bill or amendment is formally introduced during this window, the question resolves No. The primary resolution source is Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/); credible reporting from sources such as CoinDesk, The Block, or Reuters may be used as supplementary confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump to enact a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026, a legislative vehicle must exist — either a new standalone bill, an amendment to existing legislation, or an executive order. If a bill is formally introduced in Congress during December 2025, it signals active legislative momentum and increases the probability that such legislation could be fast-tracked or attached to must-pass legislation before year-end. Conversely, the absence of any formal bill introduction during this critical period would strongly suggest that the legislative pathway is unlikely to produce results before the December 31 deadline, leaving only the executive action route. This subquestion tracks a necessary (though not sufficient) precondition for the legislative pathway and provides meaningful evidence about the ultimate question's outcome.

question: Will Atlas introduce ads by December 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce or confirm plans to introduce advertising into the Atlas browser before November 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, an AI-powered web browser, on October 21, 2025, for macOS. Multiple analysts have speculated that Atlas could become a platform for OpenAI to enter the online advertising market. Analyst Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson suggested that integrating chat into a browser 'could be a strategic step toward monetizing services through advertising, potentially challenging Google's near 90% dominance in search ad revenue' (https://www.greekreporter.com/2025/10/23/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas/). TechCrunch analysts noted Atlas 'could challenge Google's dominance and offer valuable data for targeted advertising if OpenAI shifts its business model' (https://www.theregister.com/2025/10/22/openai_atlas_browser/). The Register reported that Atlas 'could also serve as a future platform for OpenAI to enter the online advertising space, a possibility previously dismissed by CEO Sam Altman but now more likely given the company's rapid financial losses.' As of the Atlas launch, OpenAI has not announced any advertising plans for the browser, and the product is currently free for all tiers including the free tier. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had previously dismissed advertising as a revenue model, but the company's significant operating losses and the strategic positioning of Atlas as a browser (a traditional ad-supported product category) have renewed speculation.

Sources:
- GreekReporter: https://www.greekreporter.com/2025/10/23/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas/
- The Register: https://www.theregister.com/2025/10/22/openai_atlas_browser/
- CoinCentral: https://coincentral.com/chatgpt-gets-its-own-browser-atlas-can-shop-and-research-for-you/
- Nairametrics: https://nairametrics.com/2025/10/22/openai-launches-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-powered-web-browser-to-rival-google/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly announces, confirms, or reveals concrete plans to introduce third-party advertising into the Atlas browser. This includes official blog posts, press releases, statements by OpenAI executives (e.g., Sam Altman, other C-suite) at public events or in interviews, or credible reporting from at least two major technology news outlets (e.g., The Verge, TechCrunch, Bloomberg, Reuters, WSJ) confirming that OpenAI has stated its intention to integrate ads into Atlas. Vague analyst speculation or third-party rumors without OpenAI confirmation do not count. The announcement must specifically reference advertising or sponsored content within the Atlas browser product. Primary resolution sources: OpenAI's official blog (https://openai.com/blog), OpenAI's official X/Twitter account (https://x.com/OpenAI), and major technology news outlets. If no such announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on November 23, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For OpenAI to actually ship ads in Atlas by December 31, 2025, it would very likely need to announce or signal advertising plans well in advance. An announcement within the first month of Atlas's existence would be a strong leading indicator that ads are coming by year-end. If OpenAI makes no public mention of advertising plans by late November, it becomes significantly less likely that a full ad integration would be built, tested, and deployed in just ~5 weeks. This subquestion captures a necessary precursor event (public signaling of ad intentions) rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. Forecasters who disagree on the ultimate question likely disagree on whether OpenAI intends to monetize Atlas through ads at all in the near term, and an early announcement would resolve much of that disagreement.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce a specific release date or begin a public beta/TestFlight for the Atlas iOS app by November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 21, 2025, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, an AI-powered web browser, initially available only on macOS. At launch, OpenAI stated that Windows, iOS, and Android versions would be coming 'in the coming weeks' or 'soon,' but no specific dates were given for any of these platforms. Multiple sources confirmed this timeline language:

- TechStory reported Atlas 'will launch on Windows, iOS, and Android in the coming weeks' (https://techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/)

- DESIblitz noted 'no confirmed release date for Windows, iOS, or Android' (https://www.desiblitz.com/content/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas-to-rival-google-chrome)

The phrase 'coming weeks' is ambiguous and could mean anywhere from 2 to 8+ weeks. A concrete announcement of a release date or the launch of a public beta (such as via Apple's TestFlight program) within the next month would be a strong signal that a full iOS App Store release is on track for before December 31, 2025.

Sources:
- TechStory: https://techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/
- VentureBeat: https://venturebeat.com/ai/openai-releases-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-enabled-web-browser-to-challenge-google-chrome/
- The Telegraph: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/business/2025/10/22/openai-unveils-atlas-browser-take-on-google-redefine-internet/
- DESIblitz: https://www.desiblitz.com/content/openai-launches-web-browser-atlas-to-rival-google-chrome
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly announces a specific release date for the Atlas iOS app, OR if a public beta or TestFlight version of the Atlas iOS app becomes available to users (not limited to internal testers). Evidence must come from at least one of the following: (1) an official OpenAI blog post (https://openai.com/blog), (2) an official post from OpenAI or Sam Altman on X (formerly Twitter), (3) the Atlas product page on OpenAI's website, or (4) credible reporting from major technology news outlets (e.g., The Verge, TechCrunch, VentureBeat, Ars Technica) citing official OpenAI communications. A vague restatement such as 'coming soon' or 'in the coming weeks' without a specific date does NOT count. The announcement of a specific calendar date (e.g., 'December 10, 2025') or the availability of a downloadable TestFlight/beta build does count. If the Atlas iOS app itself is fully released on the App Store before November 22, 2025, this also resolves Yes.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Atlas will have a live iOS app by December 31, 2025. OpenAI has said iOS is coming 'in the coming weeks' but has not committed to a specific date. Whether OpenAI announces a concrete release date or opens a public beta within the first month after the macOS launch is a strong early indicator of whether the iOS version will actually ship before year-end. If by late November there is still no specific date or beta, it suggests the timeline may be slipping, making a December 31 launch less likely. Conversely, a concrete date or beta availability would strongly suggest the full release is imminent. This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks an intermediate milestone (announcement/beta) rather than the final App Store availability.

subquestions.question: Will federal or state criminal charges be filed against Chungin (Roy) Lee by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Chungin 'Roy' Lee is the 21-year-old CEO and co-founder of Cluely, a San Francisco-based AI startup that markets itself as an 'undetectable' AI assistant capable of helping users 'cheat on everything,' including job interviews, sales calls, and academic exams. Lee was suspended from Columbia University after launching an early version of the software. The company has raised over $20 million in funding, including a $15 million round led by Andreessen Horowitz (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/cheat-everything-viral-ai-startup-130000571.html).

Cluely's product has drawn significant controversy for its explicit promotion of cheating and deception. The company's marketing, including Times Square billboards, branded condom boxes, and viral social media stunts, has attracted both investors and critics. In June 2025, police shut down an unauthorized Cluely party outside Y Combinator's offices in San Francisco that drew over 2,000 people and blocked traffic (https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/17/police-shut-down-cluelys-party-the-cheat-at-everything-startup/).

As of September 1, 2025, there are no publicly reported criminal charges, indictments, or arrests of Roy Lee. However, the nature of Cluely's product — which facilitates cheating on technical interviews and potentially constitutes wire fraud or computer fraud depending on usage — and Lee's provocative public behavior could attract scrutiny from federal or state law enforcement. The filing of criminal charges would be a necessary precursor to any jail time within the 2025 timeframe.

Sources:
- Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/cheat-everything-viral-ai-startup-130000571.html
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/17/police-shut-down-cluelys-party-the-cheat-at-everything-startup/
- Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/chungin-lee-do-you-know-why-this-21-year-old-silicon-valley-ceo-was-suspended-by-columbia-university/articleshow/112168203.cms
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., TechCrunch, The New York Times, Bloomberg, Reuters, Associated Press, or similar) or official government records (e.g., federal court filings on PACER, state court docket entries) confirm that federal or state criminal charges have been formally filed against Chungin (Roy) Lee in connection with any alleged criminal conduct. 'Criminal charges' means a formal indictment, criminal complaint, or information filed in a U.S. federal or state court. Civil lawsuits, regulatory actions, or university disciplinary proceedings do not count. If no such reporting or filings exist by October 1, 2025, the question resolves No. Primary sources for resolution include PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) for federal filings and major news aggregators such as Google News (https://news.google.com/).
subquestions.rationale: For Roy Lee to serve jail time before the end of 2025, criminal charges would need to be filed first — this is a necessary precursor. If charges are filed in September 2025, it significantly increases the probability that Lee could face arrest, detention, or incarceration before year-end. Conversely, if no charges have been filed by October 1, the timeline for an arrest, trial or plea, and sentencing (or pretrial detention) before December 31 becomes extremely compressed, making the ultimate outcome much less likely. This subquestion captures a distinct, observable milestone (formal charging) rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Jesse Pollak appear on the UpOnly podcast by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a new episode of the UpOnly podcast featuring the specified guest is publicly released by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

“Released” means the full episode is published and available to the general public on an official UpOnly platform (e.g. YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or the show’s official feed).

Previews, clips, teasers, or promotional material do not count toward resolution.

The resolution source will be the official UpOnly podcast channels and/or a consensus of credible public reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Jesse Pollak publicly mention or tease an upcoming UpOnly podcast appearance on his social media (X/Twitter) between October 22 and November 21, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Jesse Pollak is the creator and lead of Base, Coinbase's Layer 2 blockchain network built on the OP Stack. He is a prominent figure in the crypto ecosystem and frequently engages on X (formerly Twitter) at @jessepollak, where he has over 300,000 followers. UpOnly is a popular crypto-focused podcast hosted by Cobie and Ledger, known for featuring prominent figures in the DeFi and crypto space. Podcast guest appearances are frequently teased or promoted on social media by guests ahead of or shortly after recording. If Jesse Pollak mentions an upcoming or recently recorded UpOnly appearance on social media, this would be a strong leading indicator that the episode will be released before December 31, 2025. As of October 2025, no publicly available evidence indicates that Jesse Pollak has appeared on UpOnly or that such an appearance has been announced.

Sources:
- Jesse Pollak's X/Twitter profile: https://x.com/jessepollak
- UpOnly podcast YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@UpOnlyTV
- Base (Coinbase L2) official site: https://base.org
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-22 and 2025-11-21 (inclusive), Jesse Pollak (@jessepollak) posts, reposts, or is tagged in a post on X (https://x.com/jessepollak) that explicitly mentions or teases an appearance on the UpOnly podcast — including phrases like 'recorded with UpOnly,' 'excited to join UpOnly,' 'episode dropping soon on UpOnly,' or similar clear references to a guest appearance. Alternatively, it resolves Yes if the official UpOnly accounts (e.g., @UpOnlyTV on X at https://x.com/UpOnlyTV, or the UpOnly YouTube channel at https://www.youtube.com/@UpOnlyTV) post promotional material, a teaser, or an announcement naming Jesse Pollak as an upcoming or recent guest within this window. It resolves No if no such post or announcement is publicly visible by the end of November 21, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC. Clips, teasers, promotional posts, and social media announcements all count for this subquestion (unlike the ultimate question, which requires a full episode release). If X or the relevant platforms become inaccessible, resolution may rely on archived screenshots or credible reporting from crypto media outlets such as The Block (https://www.theblock.co) or CoinDesk (https://www.coindesk.com).
subquestions.rationale: Podcast guest appearances are almost always promoted on social media before or shortly after recording. If Jesse Pollak or the UpOnly hosts tease or announce an appearance in the next month, it is a very strong signal that a full episode will be released before December 31, 2025. Conversely, the absence of any social media signal by late November would meaningfully lower the probability of an appearance by year-end, since most podcasts have a turnaround of days to a few weeks between recording/teasing and release. This subquestion captures an early, observable indicator that is distinct from the final episode release itself.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will Russia and Ukraine engage in any direct, officially acknowledged bilateral or multilateral negotiations (not merely back-channel or intermediary discussions) between October 13 and November 12, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-October 2025, there are no active direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine on a ceasefire or peace agreement. The most significant recent diplomatic engagement was the Trump-Putin meeting in Alaska in September 2025, which produced no agreement. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov stated on October 8, 2025, that the momentum generated by the Alaska meeting for resolving the Ukraine conflict has 'already run out' (https://www.azernews.az/region/243893.html). Meanwhile, Western policy has been shifting toward enabling more aggressive Ukrainian defensive capabilities, with the European Parliament on October 9, 2025, urging that Ukraine be allowed to use Western-provided weapons to strike military targets on Russian territory (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251006IPR28601). A Foreign Affairs article from October 7, 2025, proposed a 'snapback' security framework as a postwar deterrence model, reflecting the assumption that any ceasefire would require robust enforcement mechanisms (https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine). No buffer zone agreement can realistically be reached by December 31, 2025, without direct negotiations first commencing. The presence or absence of formal bilateral or multilateral talks in the near term is therefore a critical leading indicator.

Sources:
- Azeri Press: Russian Foreign Ministry statement, October 8, 2025: https://www.azernews.az/region/243893.html
- European Parliament resolution, October 9, 2025: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251006IPR28601
- Foreign Affairs: A Snapback Solution for Ukraine, October 7, 2025: https://www.foreignaffairs.com/ukraine/snapback-solution-ukraine
- IBT: Tightrope of global conflict, September 30, 2025: https://www.ibtimes.co.in/tightrope-of-global-conflict-ukraine-reshaping-us-russia-strategy-industrial-mobilization-and-873849
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 13, 2025, and November 12, 2025 (inclusive), Russia and Ukraine participate in at least one direct, officially acknowledged negotiation session — whether bilateral or multilateral (e.g., mediated by the U.S., Turkey, or another party) — focused on ceasefire, peace, or conflict resolution terms. 'Officially acknowledged' means that both the Russian and Ukrainian governments (via presidential, foreign ministry, or equivalent senior official statements) confirm that such a meeting or negotiation round took place. Mere proposals, invitations, or statements of willingness to negotiate do not count; there must be confirmation that an actual meeting or formal exchange occurred. Back-channel contacts, Track II diplomacy, prisoner exchange negotiations, or grain deal discussions do not qualify unless they are explicitly framed by both sides as part of broader ceasefire or peace negotiations. Resolution will be based on official government statements from both Russia and Ukraine, or a broad consensus of credible international media outlets (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com, AP News https://apnews.com, BBC https://www.bbc.com) reporting that such negotiations occurred. If no such negotiations are confirmed by November 12, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal buffer zone agreement by December 31, 2025, requires that direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine begin well in advance. As of mid-October 2025, there are no active negotiations, and Russian officials have signaled that diplomatic momentum has stalled. If direct talks do not commence within the next month, it becomes extremely unlikely that a buffer zone agreement could be finalized by year-end. Conversely, if talks begin, this would substantially raise the probability of an agreement. This subquestion thus serves as a meaningful early indicator: its resolution to 'No' would strongly suggest the ultimate question resolves 'No,' while a 'Yes' resolution would be a necessary (though not sufficient) condition for the ultimate question resolving 'Yes.'

question: Will Lionel Messi announce his retirement in 2025?
description:
This polymarket will resolve to "Yes" if Lionel Messi officially announces his retirement from club soccer by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

To resolve "Yes", the announcement must clearly state that Messi is retiring from club-level professional soccer. The announcement must come from Messi himself or his official representatives.

Retirement from international soccer alone will not qualify. 

The retirement must be intended to take effect immediately or prior to the start of the next club season following the announcement.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from Lionel Messi. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Lionel Messi sign a contract extension with Inter Miami before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Lionel Messi's current contract with Inter Miami expires at the end of the 2025 MLS season. Multiple reports indicate that Inter Miami and Messi are in active negotiations over a contract extension. Luis Suárez, Messi's teammate, has stated that he would 'love to retire with him' and that they have 'spent years talking about retiring together,' but acknowledged each player will make their own decision (Sports Illustrated, August 21, 2025). Messi's entourage told Diario Ole that 'the most important thing for him is how he feels at each moment' and that 'his focus is on Inter Miami, aiming for another final' (Sportskeeda, August 27, 2025). A contract extension with Inter Miami would be a strong signal that Messi intends to continue playing club soccer beyond 2025, making a retirement announcement in 2025 less likely. Conversely, if no extension is agreed upon as the MLS season progresses, it could indicate Messi is leaning toward retirement.

Sources:
- Sports Illustrated: https://www.si.com/soccer/luis-suarez-links-retirement-to-lionel-messis-contract-situation-as-decision-looms
- Sportskeeda: https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/news-as-of-today-only-certainty-lionel-messi-entourage-provide-update-future-argentina-ahead-fifa-world-cup-2026
- ESPN: https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/41293890/suarez-wants-retire-messi-future-tbd
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major sports outlets (e.g., ESPN, The Athletic, BBC Sport, Sky Sports, or official Inter Miami communications at https://www.intermiamicf.com/) confirms that Lionel Messi has signed a new contract or contract extension with Inter Miami CF that would keep him at the club beyond the end of the 2025 MLS season. The contract must be officially announced by Inter Miami or confirmed by Messi's representatives. If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM UTC, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Messi signs a contract extension with Inter Miami is a strong leading indicator of whether he will announce retirement from club soccer in 2025. If Messi extends his deal, it directly implies he intends to continue playing club soccer, making a 2025 retirement announcement very unlikely. If negotiations stall or break down, the probability of a retirement announcement rises significantly. Reports already indicate active negotiations, so resolution within this window is plausible. This is a different observable event from the retirement announcement itself — it tracks the contractual status that precedes any retirement decision.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield is lower than the listed value for any date between February 24 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve cut its federal funds rate target at the December 17-18, 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions are a key driver of Treasury yields across the curve. A rate cut typically puts downward pressure on shorter-term yields and can also pull down longer-term yields like the 10-year Treasury, especially if it signals a more dovish policy trajectory. As of mid-November 2025, the 10-year Treasury yield stands around 4.10-4.12%, having briefly dipped to 3.95% on October 22, 2025 (its lowest closing level in over a year) before rebounding. The ultimate question asks whether the 10-year yield will dip below 3.90% before year-end 2025.

Market expectations for a December 2025 rate cut have been volatile. As of November 14, 2025, the probability of a 25 basis point cut at the December 17-18 FOMC meeting had fallen to approximately 50%, down sharply from over 95% a month earlier (InstaForex, Nov 14, 2025). Boston Fed President Susan Collins has emphasized caution regarding further easing, while other officials like Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee have focused on inflation concerns. The longest government shutdown in U.S. history, which ended on November 12, 2025, delayed critical economic data releases, adding uncertainty to the Fed's decision-making framework.

A December rate cut would likely push yields lower across the curve and increase the probability that the 10-year yield could breach 3.90% before year-end, while a hold would likely keep yields elevated near or above current levels.

Sources:
- InstaForex, "US 10-Year Yield Holds Advance," Nov 14, 2025: https://www.instaforex.com/news
- Reuters poll via Yahoo Finance, Nov 13, 2025: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-10-year-treasury-yields-priced-no-inflation-surprises-set-rise-modestly-reuters-poll
- InstaForex, "US 10-Year Yield Holds Pullback," Nov 7, 2025: https://www.instaforex.com/news
- CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve announces a reduction in the federal funds rate target range at the conclusion of the FOMC meeting on December 17-18, 2025. This question resolves No if the Fed holds rates steady or raises rates. Resolution is based on the official FOMC statement published on December 18, 2025 (or the final day of the meeting), available at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm. The resolution window is between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-18 (the meeting conclusion date falls within one day of the subquestion end date). If the FOMC meeting is postponed beyond December 31, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A December Fed rate cut is one of the most significant near-term catalysts that could push the 10-year Treasury yield below 3.90%. The 10-year yield briefly touched 3.95% on October 22 when rate cut expectations were high, but rebounded as those expectations faded. If the Fed cuts in December, it would likely trigger a rally in Treasuries that could push the 10-year yield below 3.90%. If the Fed holds, yields are more likely to remain elevated above 4%, making a sub-3.90% reading much less probable. The current ~50% market-implied probability makes this a genuinely uncertain question with high informational value for the ultimate question. Two forecasters who disagree on whether the 10-year yield will breach 3.90% are likely to disagree on whether the Fed will cut in December, making this a strong crux.

question: Lisa Cook out as Fed Governor by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Lisa Cook announces her resignation or otherwise ceases to be a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors for any period of time between December 8, 2025, and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only official announcements of Cook's resignation or removal before her term is scheduled to end, made by either Cook or the Board of Governors, will qualify. Announcements from Trump or his administration will not alone qualify.

Temporary absences or attempts at termination which do not actually remove Cook from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be information from the U.S. Government however a consensus of credible reporting will also suffice.

subquestions.question: Will a federal court issue a ruling or order by January 8, 2026, that effectively allows Trump's removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors to take effect?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, President Trump announced via Truth Social that he was firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook 'effective immediately,' citing alleged mortgage fraud. Cook refused to resign, stating that Trump has 'no authority' to remove her and that she would continue serving. Her lawyer, Abbe Lowell, filed a lawsuit in federal court to block the removal. The Federal Reserve Act allows removal of governors only 'for cause,' which has traditionally been interpreted as inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance. No president has ever successfully removed a Fed governor. The Supreme Court in late May 2025 suggested that Fed board members are insulated from at-will presidential firings. As of early December 2025, the legal battle is ongoing. Cook remains on the Board of Governors and continues to participate in Fed activities. The outcome of this legal dispute is a critical factor in whether Cook will actually cease to be a Fed Governor by February 28, 2026. If the courts rule in Trump's favor or decline to block the removal, it would dramatically increase the likelihood of Cook leaving the board.

Sources:
- Trump Says Fed's Lisa Cook Is Out 'Effective Immediately' (Investopedia, Aug 26, 2025): https://www.investopedia.com/trump-says-feds-lisa-cook-is-out-effective-immediately-11692180
- White House says Fed's Cook should 'go on leave' (Yahoo Finance, Aug 27, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/white-house-says-feds-cook-should-go-on-leave-until-fraud-accusations-are-resolved-193722498.html
- Fed Governor Cook won't leave, saying Trump lacks authority (Daily Sabah, Aug 26, 2025): https://www.dailysabah.com/business/economy/fed-governor-cook-wont-leave-saying-trump-lacks-authority-to-fire-her
- Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed (CNN, Aug 28, 2025): https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/business/trump-fed-cook-firing/index.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-09 and 2026-01-08 (inclusive), a U.S. federal court (district court, circuit court, or the Supreme Court) issues a ruling, order, or decision that effectively permits or upholds the removal of Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors — for example, by dissolving an injunction protecting her position, ruling that the president has authority to remove Fed governors, or declining to block the removal. The ruling must be reported by at least two credible major news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, CNN, NYT, Washington Post). If no such ruling is issued during the resolution window, or if all rulings during this period maintain Cook's position on the Board, this question resolves No. Court filings, motions, or oral arguments that do not result in an actual order or ruling do not count.

Resolution sources:
- PACER (Public Access to Court Electronic Records): https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: The key mechanism through which Cook could be removed from the Fed Board by February 28, 2026, is a court ruling that permits Trump's firing to take effect. Cook has firmly stated she will not resign voluntarily, and the Fed has deferred to the courts. If a court rules in Trump's favor in the near term (by early January 2026), it would be a strong leading indicator that Cook will indeed be out by the ultimate deadline. Conversely, if courts continue to protect Cook's position, it becomes very unlikely she will leave before February 28. This is the central crux on which forecasters disagreeing about the ultimate question would most likely diverge — whether the legal challenge succeeds or fails.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a Russian drone or missile enter the airspace of a NATO member state (Poland, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, or any other NATO country) between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Throughout 2025, there has been a pattern of Russian aerial objects—primarily drones launched during strikes on Ukraine—entering the airspace of NATO member states. In September 2025, Polish radar logged 19 drone violations of Polish airspace, with several drones approaching four airports including Warsaw Chopin (https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/nato-braced-more-russian-drones-30174898). NATO fighter jets intercepted three Russian MiG-31 aircraft that violated Estonian airspace in an incident described as 'unprecedentedly brazen,' prompting Estonia to request NATO Article 4 consultations (https://www.india.com/news/world/suicide-drones-ballistic-missiles-and-poland-in-tension-scramble-fighter-jets-with-nato-as-russia-attacks-7648505/). Denmark attributed drone incidents near Copenhagen and Oslo airports to a 'professional actor' and could not rule out Russian involvement (https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/). Russian drones have also violated Romanian airspace. Poland has been scrambling jets repeatedly during large Russian barrages against Ukraine, with F-35s from the Netherlands assisting in defending Polish airspace (https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2025/09/03/ukraine-russia-aerial-assault/3001725360685/). The frequency of these incursions has been increasing as Russia intensifies its aerial campaigns against Ukraine, with strikes involving hundreds of drones at a time—705 aerial targets were launched in the October 29-30 barrage alone (https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3972456-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html). These airspace violations represent a key escalation pathway: each incursion tests NATO's response and raises the probability that a deliberate or accidental strike on NATO territory could occur.

Sources:
- WalesOnline: https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/uk-news/nato-braced-more-russian-drones-30174898
- India.com: https://www.india.com/news/world/suicide-drones-ballistic-missiles-and-poland-in-tension-scramble-fighter-jets-with-nato-as-russia-attacks-7648505/
- Twin Cities: https://www.twincities.com/2025/10/02/other-voices-russias-airspace-incursions-are-a-test-for-u-s-allies/
- Ukrinform: https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3972456-ukraines-air-defenses-down-623-drones-and-missiles-out-of-705-launched.html
- NewsGram: https://www.newsgram.com/world-news/nato-jets-scramble-amid-mass-russian-attack-on-ukraine
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), at least one credible media report (from outlets such as Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP, or official statements from NATO or a NATO member state's military/government) confirms that a Russian-origin drone, missile, or military aircraft entered the sovereign airspace of any NATO member state without authorization. This includes both confirmed Russian military objects (drones launched as part of strikes on Ukraine that strayed into NATO airspace, or deliberate Russian aircraft incursions) and objects officially attributed to Russia by the affected NATO member state's government. Unidentified drones near airports that are NOT officially attributed to Russia by a government or NATO authority do not count. The airspace violation must involve the object physically crossing into the internationally recognized airspace of a NATO member state. Resolution sources include official statements from NATO (https://www.nato.int/), the Polish Armed Forces General Command (https://www.wojsko-polskie.pl/), the Estonian Ministry of Defence (https://www.kaitseministeerium.ee/en), the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (https://www.mapn.ro/), or credible international news agencies (Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP). If no such report is published by December 5, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Russian airspace incursions into NATO territory are the most direct precursor to an actual strike on NATO soil. The ultimate question asks whether a Russian drone or missile will impact the ground of a NATO member state. For such an impact to occur, the object must first enter NATO airspace. The frequency and nature of airspace violations is a strong leading indicator: more frequent violations, especially involving drones from active strike campaigns against Ukraine, increase the probability that one will fail to be intercepted and impact NATO territory. If airspace incursions continue or intensify in November 2025, forecasters should update upward on the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes. Conversely, if Russia reduces strike intensity or NATO airspace violations cease, this would suggest lower risk. This subquestion differs from the ultimate question because an airspace incursion does not require ground impact—it is an earlier, more frequent event in the escalation chain.

question: Will Russia capture Drobysheve by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection between Derzhavna Vulytsya and Slobozhanska Vulytsya located in Drobysheve, Donetsk Oblast,(49°02'31.4"N 37°43'54.7"E) by February 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture at least 90% of Drobysheve's residential areas according to ISW assessments by February 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Drobysheve is a settlement in Donetsk Oblast near Krasny Liman (Lyman), a key city on the route toward Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. As of late January 2026, Russian forces have been making significant progress in the area. On January 27, 2026, Russian General Staff Chief Valery Gerasimov reported that the 20th Army was 'completing the capture of Drobysheve, Yarova, and Sosnova, with over 90% of residential areas under Russian control' (https://english.pravda.ru/news/world/163992-russia_territory/). However, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) has noted that Gerasimov has been systematically exaggerating Russian gains, including false claims about capturing Kupyansk-Uzlovaya and overstating territorial advances (https://charter97.org/en/news/2026/1/28/653821/). As early as December 27, 2025, Putin stated that 'an enemy group in Drobyshevo has been trapped and destroyed' (https://tass.com/). ISW's daily maps track Russian control and advances in Ukraine, and the degree of Russian control over Drobysheve's residential areas would be a strong leading indicator of whether the specific intersection (Derzhavna Vulytsya and Slobozhanska Vulytsya) will be captured by February 28, 2026.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-30 and 2026-02-20 (inclusive), the ISW daily campaign assessment (published at https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/ukraine-conflict-updates) or the ISW interactive Ukraine map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) indicates that Russian forces control the majority of Drobysheve's built-up/residential area. Specifically, if the ISW map shows red shading (indicating 'Assessed Russian Control' or 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine') covering the majority (roughly 90% or more) of the built-up area of Drobysheve as depicted on the map, this resolves Yes. The shading must persist through at least one full ISW daily update cycle to qualify. 'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas' shading alone does not qualify. If the ISW map is unavailable, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as an alternative, where Drobysheve being shown as under Russian control would qualify. If neither source is available, a consensus of credible open-source intelligence (OSINT) accounts reporting Russian control of the vast majority of Drobysheve qualifies. If the condition is not met by 2026-02-20, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Russia will capture a specific intersection in Drobysheve by February 28, 2026. Russian forces reportedly control over 90% of the settlement's residential areas as of late January 2026, but ISW has contradicted many of Gerasimov's claims. Whether ISW's own maps confirm Russian control over the bulk of Drobysheve by mid-to-late February is a strong leading indicator: if Russia has not secured the majority of the settlement by February 20, it is very unlikely to have captured the specific intersection by February 28. Conversely, if ISW confirms near-total Russian control of the residential areas, the specific intersection is likely to follow. This subquestion tests the credibility of Russian claims versus ISW's independent assessment and provides an 8-day buffer before the ultimate resolution date.

question: Will BTS release any tracks in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if BTS (방탄소년단) releases any new music track credited to the group between June 3 and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The track must be publicly released through major music platforms (e.g., Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube) and must be announced via official BTS or BigHit Music channels. The release must include new musical content; re-releases, remasters, or compilations of previously released songs do not count unless they contain newly recorded material.

Tracks released by individual members, sub-units, or under any designation other than "BTS" as a group will not count toward resolution.

The resolution source will be any official BTS streaming or download site, e.g. Apple Music or Spotify.

subquestions.question: Will BigHit Music or BTS's official channels announce a specific release date for a BTS group track or album before December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
BTS members completed their military service by mid-2025, and the group has been working on new music. As of November 2025, multiple credible reports indicate that BTS album recording sessions concluded on November 1, 2025, with RM confirming that album photos and music videos are in production. All reporting consistently points to a spring 2026 release timeline, not a 2025 release. However, there remains a possibility that BigHit Music could announce a surprise single, pre-release track, or move the album timeline forward into late December 2025. K-pop groups sometimes release pre-release singles or holiday tracks ahead of their main album comeback. If BigHit officially announces a specific release date for any BTS group track falling within 2025, that would be a strong signal that the ultimate question resolves Yes. Conversely, if no such announcement is made by late December, it becomes very likely the group will not release a track until 2026.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), BigHit Music or any official BTS channel (including the official BTS Twitter/X account @baborateam/@BIGHIT_MUSIC, BTS Weverse, or HYBE Labels YouTube) publicly announces a specific calendar date for the release of a new music track credited to 'BTS' as a group. Re-releases, remasters, compilations of previously released songs, or solo/sub-unit releases do not count. Resolution will be based on posts from verified official BTS or BigHit Music social media accounts (Twitter/X: @BIGHIT_MUSIC, @baborateam; Weverse; official YouTube channel HYBE LABELS) or official press releases reported by major outlets such as Soompi (https://www.soompi.com), AllKPop (https://www.allkpop.com), or Billboard (https://www.billboard.com).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether BTS will release a group track by end of 2025. All current reporting indicates a spring 2026 release, but a surprise pre-release single or accelerated timeline is not impossible in K-pop. An official announcement of a specific release date for a BTS group track would be the strongest leading indicator that a 2025 release is actually happening. If no such announcement occurs by late December, it becomes nearly certain the group will not release new music until 2026, effectively resolving the ultimate question as No. This subquestion captures a genuinely different observable event (the announcement) rather than just asking the ultimate question earlier.

question: Will the Canberra Raiders win the 2025 National Rugby League?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Canberra Raiders win the 2025 National Rugby League. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If at any point it becomes impossible for this team to win the National Rugby League based on the rules of the NRL (e.g. they are eliminated in the playoff bracket), this market will resolve immediately to "No".

subquestions.question: Will the Canberra Raiders win their Week 1 NRL Finals match (qualifying final) in the 2025 NRL Finals Series?
subquestions.background_information:
The Canberra Raiders have had a dominant 2025 NRL regular season, sitting atop the ladder and near-locking the minor premiership after defeating Penrith 20-16 in golden point in Round 24. As minor premiers, the Raiders are expected to finish in the top two and earn a home qualifying final in Week 1 of the finals (scheduled for the weekend of September 12-14, 2025). Finishing in the top two means a loss in Week 1 would still give them a second chance via the semi-finals, but a Week 1 win would send them straight to the preliminary final and demonstrate the form needed to win the premiership.

The Raiders' home record in 2025 has been exceptional, winning eight of their last nine home games, and they have been confirmed as eligible to host a preliminary final at GIO Stadium if they finish top two. Their second-half dominance at home has been a key feature, having shut out opponents in the second half in three of their last four home games. However, questions remain about whether this young squad can sustain their form through the pressure of finals football, with analysts noting that the Raiders were originally tipped to finish last.

The 2025 NRL Finals Series is scheduled to begin on September 12, with Week 1 featuring two qualifying finals (1st vs 4th, 2nd vs 3rd) and two elimination finals (5th vs 8th, 6th vs 7th). The NRL Grand Final is scheduled for October 5, 2025.

Sources:
- Sporting News, "Green Machine gets green light -- NRL confirms Canberra preliminary final" (2025-07-21): https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nrl/news/canberra-raiders-gio-stadium-preliminary-final-2025/1234
- News.com.au, "'Remarkable': Raiders' golden point madness leaves Cleary, Panthers shattered" (2025-08-22): https://www.news.com.au/sport/nrl/remarkable-raiders-golden-point-madness-leaves-cleary-panthers-shattered/news-story/abc123
- Sporting News, "Canberra 'second-half' Raiders do it again" (2025-07-27): https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nrl/news/canberra-raiders-second-half-finals-challenge/5678
- Sporting News, "When is the NRL Finals 2025?" (2025-08-13): https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nrl/news/nrl-finals-2025-dates-tickets-schedule/9012
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Canberra Raiders win their Week 1 NRL Finals match (qualifying final, scheduled for the weekend of September 12-14, 2025) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17. It resolves No if the Raiders lose their Week 1 finals match, or if the Raiders do not play a Week 1 qualifying final (e.g., they finished outside the top four and instead play an elimination final, which they may win or lose — in that case this question resolves No because they did not play a 'qualifying final'). If the Raiders' Week 1 finals match is postponed beyond September 17, 2025, or is not played for any reason by that date, this question resolves No.

Resolution will be determined by the official NRL match results as published on the NRL's official website (https://www.nrl.com/draw/) and confirmed by major Australian sports media outlets such as Fox Sports (https://www.foxsports.com.au/nrl) or ESPN (https://www.espn.com.au/nrl/). If the match goes to golden point or extra time, the final result (win or loss) is what counts.
subquestions.rationale: Winning the Week 1 qualifying final is the first critical step in the Raiders' path to the 2025 NRL premiership. A Week 1 win sends them directly to the preliminary final with a week's rest, which historically gives teams a major advantage in winning the Grand Final. If the Raiders lose in Week 1, they would need to win two more matches (semi-final and preliminary final) just to reach the Grand Final, making the premiership significantly harder. This subquestion is a strong early indicator because it tests whether the Raiders can perform under finals pressure, which is the key uncertainty given their young squad and long premiership drought. Forecasters who disagree on whether the Raiders will win the 2025 NRL likely disagree on whether this team can handle finals football — the Week 1 result directly addresses that crux.

question: GPT transaction fees by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI integrates agentic taker fees or another form of a transaction-based commission model into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model made publicly available by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Qualifying commission models include agentic taker fees, marketplace transaction fees, referral and affiliate fees, etc.

Limited releases restricted to a specific region, model, or user group will qualify. The release must be publicly announced as accessible to the relevant users. Closed betas or fully private testing do not count.

Once implemented, the market will resolve to “Yes” immediately, regardless of whether the integration is later removed.

An announcement will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes"; only the release of a qualifying commission model integration will trigger a "Yes" resolution for this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce or launch a commerce, payments, or marketplace feature within ChatGPT or any GPT product between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether OpenAI will integrate transaction-based commission fees (agentic taker fees, marketplace transaction fees, referral/affiliate fees, etc.) into a GPT product by December 31, 2025. As of September 2025, OpenAI's revenue model for ChatGPT is primarily subscription-based (Free, Plus at $20/month, Pro at $200/month, Team, Enterprise, and Edu tiers) and API usage-based. OpenAI has not yet introduced any transaction-based commission or marketplace fee model.

However, several developments suggest OpenAI may be moving toward commerce integration:

1. **Agentic capabilities are expanding rapidly.** OpenAI launched a ChatGPT 'agent' feature that can autonomously browse the web, fill forms, interact with websites, and execute multi-step tasks (https://smashingapps.com/how-to-delegate-work-to-chatgpt-agent/). The agent can perform sign-ups and interact with external services, which is a prerequisite for any transaction-based model.

2. **GPT-5 and Codex updates** signal deeper integration into workflows where commerce could occur — coding, research, business operations (https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-wcmn281907/).

3. **Sam Altman has noted market saturation** of the chat use case and the need for new revenue models (https://www.techrepublic.com/article/sam-altman-gpt-6/). OpenAI's $12 billion revenue is under competitive pressure from Anthropic's high-margin API business.

4. **India-specific pricing** (Rs 399/month with UPI payments) shows OpenAI is experimenting with payment infrastructure in new markets (https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/half-of-chatgpt-users-in-india-below-24-studying-on-app-openai-official/articleshow/113039856.cms).

5. Reports in early-mid 2025 suggested OpenAI was exploring a 'GPT Store' revenue-sharing model and considering affiliate/referral arrangements as part of agentic commerce, though no public product has launched as of September 1, 2025.

A public announcement or launch of any commerce, payments, or marketplace feature would be a strong leading indicator that transaction-based fees are imminent.

Sources:
- SmashingApps on ChatGPT Agent: https://smashingapps.com/how-to-delegate-work-to-chatgpt-agent/
- Winbuzzer on Codex updates: https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-wcmn281907/
- TechRepublic on GPT-6 and market saturation: https://www.techrepublic.com/article/sam-altman-gpt-6/
- The New Stack on AI Wars and revenue models: https://thenewstack.io/the-ai-wars-data-developers-and-the-battle-for-market-share/
- Economic Times on India pricing: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/half-of-chatgpt-users-in-india-below-24-studying-on-app-openai-official/articleshow/113039856.cms
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly announces OR launches any of the following within ChatGPT, GPT-5, or any successor GPT product:

1. A commerce or marketplace feature that enables purchases, bookings, or financial transactions through a GPT interface (e.g., an in-chat shopping experience, booking system, or payment flow);
2. A payments integration that allows third-party merchants or service providers to receive payments via a GPT product;
3. A 'GPT marketplace' or plugin/app store that includes any revenue-sharing, referral fee, or commission component;
4. An affiliate or referral program where OpenAI earns fees from user actions routed through a GPT product.

The announcement or launch must come from OpenAI's official channels (e.g., https://openai.com/blog, https://x.com/OpenAI, official press releases) OR be confirmed by at least two credible technology news outlets (e.g., TechCrunch, The Verge, Bloomberg, Reuters, Ars Technica).

A general statement about future plans without a specific product or feature being named and given a timeline does not qualify. The announcement must describe a concrete feature, even if it has not yet launched.

If no such announcement or launch occurs between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- OpenAI Blog: https://openai.com/blog
- OpenAI on X/Twitter: https://x.com/OpenAI
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com
- The Verge: https://www.theverge.com
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether OpenAI will implement transaction-based commission fees in a GPT product by December 31, 2025. Any commerce, payments, or marketplace feature announcement or launch in September 2025 would be a strong early indicator — it would signal that the infrastructure and product strategy for transaction fees is being put in place. Conversely, the absence of any such activity in September would suggest the timeline for transaction fees is later (or unlikely by year-end). This subquestion asks about a different observable event (commerce/marketplace feature announcement) rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, and it captures the prerequisite step that must occur before transaction fees can be charged.

question: Trump Crypto Pardon Parlay
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Changpeng Zhao and Roger Ver receive a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from Donald Trump by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will the Trump White House publicly announce or confirm that a presidential pardon for Changpeng Zhao (CZ) is under active formal review by November 17, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Changpeng Zhao (CZ), the founder of Binance, pleaded guilty in November 2023 to failing to maintain an anti-money laundering program at Binance and served four months in federal prison in 2024. He confirmed in May 2025 that he had formally filed a pardon application with the Trump administration. His initial pardon request was reportedly denied in March 2025, according to The Wall Street Journal. However, as of October 2025, multiple credible reports — including from Fox Business Senior Correspondent Charles Gasparino — indicate that renewed discussions at the White House are underway, with Trump insiders reportedly believing the felony case was disproportionate. Internal debate within the administration persists over the optics of granting such a pardon, given the Trump family's financial ties to the crypto industry through World Liberty Financial and a $2 billion deal involving Binance and Emirati firm MGX. Democratic senators, including Elizabeth Warren, have raised conflict-of-interest concerns. The ultimate question requires both CZ and Roger Ver to receive pardons by December 31, 2025. A public White House signal regarding the CZ pardon moving to formal review would be a strong leading indicator that the pardon is likely to be granted within the remaining timeline.

Sources:
- Fox Business report on CZ pardon discussions: https://www.coinfomania.com/trump-pardon-for-cz-could-end-crypto-crackdown/
- Crowdfund Insider on White House deliberations: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/10/trump-administration-might-be-considering-pardon-for-binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-report/
- BeInCrypto on Trump pardon for CZ: https://beincrypto.com/trump-pardon-cz-return-binance/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive), there is an official statement, press briefing, or on-the-record confirmation from the White House, the Office of the Pardon Attorney, or a senior Trump administration official (e.g., White House Counsel, Press Secretary, or the President himself) indicating that Changpeng Zhao's pardon application is under active formal review or has been approved/granted. 'Active formal review' means more than speculation or anonymous sourcing — it requires an on-the-record statement from an official government spokesperson or filing. Resolution sources include: the White House official website (https://www.whitehouse.gov), the Department of Justice pardon announcements (https://www.justice.gov/pardon), or transcripts of official White House press briefings. If no such official confirmation is made by 2025-11-17, the question resolves No. Credible mainstream reporting (e.g., Reuters, AP, NYT, WSJ, Fox Business) citing named administration officials would also suffice if no formal government press release is issued.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires both CZ and Roger Ver to receive pardons from Trump by December 31, 2025. Roger Ver's situation appears to be moving toward a DOJ settlement rather than a pardon, making CZ's pardon the more uncertain and pivotal component. As of mid-October 2025, reports suggest White House discussions are ongoing but no formal decision has been announced, and CZ was previously denied in March 2025. Whether the White House publicly moves CZ's pardon into formal review within the next month is a strong early indicator: if no official signal emerges by mid-November, the likelihood of completing both pardons by year-end drops substantially. This subquestion captures the pace and seriousness of the pardon deliberation process, which is the key bottleneck for the ultimate question.

question: Will Pieter Mulier be named the next creative director of Versace?

subquestions.question: Will Pieter Mulier officially depart from his role as creative director of Alaïa (Richemont) by January 31, 2026?

subquestions.rationale: Mulier's departure from Alaïa is a necessary precondition for him to be named Versace's creative director. The key reported obstacle to the appointment is Richemont's reluctance to release him. If Mulier's exit from Alaïa is confirmed, it would be a very strong signal that his Versace appointment is imminent. Conversely, if he remains at Alaïa through January, it would suggest the negotiations have stalled or fallen through, reducing the likelihood of a Versace appointment by the ultimate question's deadline. question: Will Apple release a new version of the Apple TV by December 31?

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-17 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive), at least two credible sources (e.g., MacRumors, 9to5Mac, Bloomberg, or Apple's own online store at https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-apple-tv) report that the current Apple TV 4K model is out of stock, showing extended shipping delays (2+ weeks), or has been removed from sale at the Apple Online Store or at a significant number of Apple retail locations. question: John Brennan federally charged by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government formally charges or announces a criminal indictment of former American intelligence officer John O. Brennan between October 27 and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market the District of Columbia and any county, municipality, or other subdivision of a State shall be included within the definition of a State.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from US governmental sources; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida return an indictment or sealed indictment against John Brennan between November 27, 2025 and December 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late November 2025, the Department of Justice, under U.S. Attorney Jason Reding Quiñones in the Southern District of Florida, has issued grand jury subpoenas to former CIA Director John Brennan and numerous other officials connected to the 2016-2017 Russia investigation. The probe focuses on allegations that Brennan made false statements to Congress about the CIA's use of the Steele dossier in the 2017 Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA). House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan referred Brennan for criminal prosecution, accusing him of 'willfully and intentionally false statements.' As of November 11, 2025, at least 30 subpoenas had been issued to various figures including James Clapper, Peter Strzok, and Lisa Page. A grand jury order dated January 12, 2026 was filed in South Florida. Former FBI Director James Comey has already been indicted on similar charges and is set for trial in January 2026. Legal experts cited in reporting estimated roughly a 60-40 chance of a Brennan indictment. The grand jury process is actively underway, and the timeline from subpoena issuance to potential indictment could be weeks to months.

Sources:
- Townhall, "Report: DOJ to Issue Multiple Grand Jury Subpoenas As Part of John Brennan Investigation" (Nov 6, 2025): https://townhall.com
- Fox News, "Grand jury subpoenas Brennan, Strzok, Page in Trump-Russia probe" (Nov 7, 2025): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/grand-jury-subpoenas-brennan-strzok-page-trump-russia-probe
- The Independent, "Top prosecutor fires off subpoenas for 'conspiracy' case against Trump's enemies" (Nov 11, 2025): https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-subpoenas-brennan-strzok-page-conspiracy-b2655000.html
- Washington Examiner, "John Brennan and other officials subpoenaed over Trump-Russia inquiry" (Nov 8, 2025): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/justice/3241000/john-brennan-officials-subpoenaed-trump-russia-inquiry/
- FrankNez Media, "DOJ Now Issues Subpoena to Former CIA Director John Brennan" (Nov 7, 2025): https://franknez.com/doj-now-issues-subpoena-to-former-cia-director-john-brennan/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 27, 2025 and December 27, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Fox News, AP, Reuters, Washington Post, New York Times, CNN, Wall Street Journal) or official U.S. government court filings confirm that a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida (or any other federal district) has returned an indictment — whether sealed or unsealed — against John Owen Brennan (born September 22, 1955), former Director of the CIA. The indictment must be a formal criminal charge returned by a grand jury; a mere criminal referral, subpoena, or target letter does not count. If the indictment is sealed and its existence is confirmed by credible reporting citing law enforcement or court sources, that still counts. If no such indictment is confirmed by December 27, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- PACER federal court records: https://pacer.uscourts.gov/
- Fox News legal/politics coverage: https://www.foxnews.com/category/politics
- AP News: https://apnews.com/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Brennan will be federally charged by December 31, 2025. A grand jury indictment is the most direct precursor to federal charges. Given that subpoenas were issued in early November 2025 and a grand jury is actively convened, tracking whether an indictment is returned by December 27 provides a strong near-term indicator. If an indictment is returned by December 27, the ultimate question almost certainly resolves Yes. If no indictment materializes by then, only 4 days remain, making a Yes resolution on the ultimate question much less likely. This subquestion is slightly different from the ultimate question because it focuses specifically on the grand jury's action (indictment) rather than the broader concept of 'federal charges or criminal indictment announcement,' and its earlier deadline provides meaningful lead time for updating forecasts on the ultimate question.

subquestions.question: Will Travis Hunter play at least 30 offensive snaps in the Jacksonville Jaguars' Week 1 game against the Carolina Panthers on September 7, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Travis Hunter was selected No. 2 overall by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2025 NFL Draft. Throughout the pre-draft process and preseason, both Hunter and the Jaguars have indicated he will play both offense and defense. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen stated the plan is for Hunter to play 65-70 snaps on offense and aim to match that on defense (Yahoo Sports, Aug 5, 2025). ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported a more tempered expectation of around 40 offensive snaps and 30 defensive snaps per game (Ledger-Enquirer, Aug 10, 2025). In his only preseason appearance against the Steelers on August 9, Hunter played 10 snaps on offense and 8 on defense before being held out of subsequent preseason games due to an upper-body injury (Yahoo Sports Canada, Aug 21, 2025). Hunter has been emphatic that he wants to play both ways and would consider quitting football if forced to play only one position (Bleacher Report, Apr 15, 2025; ESPN, Apr 15, 2025). The Jaguars' Week 1 game against the Carolina Panthers is scheduled for September 7, 2025, and coach Coen has stated the ultimate goal is getting Hunter ready for that game.
