subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Travis Hunter records at least 30 offensive snaps (excluding special teams punt snaps) in the Jacksonville Jaguars' Week 1 regular season game against the Carolina Panthers, scheduled for September 7, 2025. This question covers the period from 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-08. Resolution will be based on official NFL snap count data as reported by NFL.com's gamebook/box score (https://www.nfl.com/stats/), ESPN's snap count reports (https://www.espn.com/nfl/), or Pro Football Reference (https://www.pro-football-reference.com/). If the game is postponed beyond September 14, 2025, this question resolves No. If Hunter does not play in the game (zero snaps), this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Travis Hunter will only play defense across his first 4 NFL games (≥20 defensive snaps and ≤19 offensive snaps). If Hunter plays 30+ offensive snaps in his very first NFL game, it would be an extremely strong early indicator that the Jaguars are deploying him as a two-way player, making a 'defense-only' outcome across 4 games essentially impossible. Conversely, if he plays very few or zero offensive snaps in Week 1, it could signal a shift toward a defense-only role. This subquestion directly measures the Jaguars' actual offensive deployment plan for Hunter in his first regular-season game, which is the single most informative early data point for the ultimate question.

subquestions.question: Will Attorney General Pam Bondi publicly release or declassify previously sealed Jeffrey Epstein investigation files between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Attorney General Pam Bondi has faced pressure from both conservative activists and congressional Republicans to release Jeffrey Epstein investigation files held by the Department of Justice. As of October 2025, Bondi has refused to release these files despite demands. During her October 7, 2025 Senate Judiciary Committee testimony, the handling of Epstein investigation files was raised as a topic of discussion (https://www.dailybulletin.com/2025/10/07/watch-live-attorney-general-bondi-faces-senate-questions-over-political-pressure-on-justice-department/). Trump previously promised during his 2024 campaign to release the Epstein files, but as of late October 2025, no major release has occurred. Whether the DOJ takes concrete action on the Epstein files — such as a public release or declassification — could signal whether the administration is building toward a special prosecutor appointment or instead handling the matter through existing DOJ channels.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Justice, Attorney General Pam Bondi, or the Trump White House announces a public release, declassification, or unsealing of previously non-public Jeffrey Epstein investigation files (including but not limited to grand jury materials, witness interview records, or internal DOJ memoranda related to the Epstein case). The release must consist of substantive investigative documents, not merely a press statement or summary. Resolution will be based on official DOJ announcements, White House statements, or a consensus of at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, NYT, Washington Post, CNN, Fox News) reporting on such a release. If no such release or declassification is announced within this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The release of Epstein files is a meaningful leading indicator for whether the Trump administration will appoint a special prosecutor. If Bondi releases the files, it could indicate the administration is moving toward more aggressive action on the Epstein case, potentially including a special prosecutor appointment. Conversely, continued refusal to release files suggests the administration is unlikely to escalate to a special prosecutor appointment. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question — it tracks DOJ engagement with the Epstein matter rather than directly asking about a prosecutor appointment — and would update forecasters' beliefs about the likelihood of a special prosecutor being named by year-end.

question: Will the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025 (S.1241) be signed into law by December 31 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate hold a floor vote on the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025 (S.1241) or a legislative vehicle containing its core provisions between October 22, 2025 and November 21, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025 (S.1241) was introduced by Senators Lindsey Graham and Richard Blumenthal with broad bipartisan support — reportedly 84-85 Senate co-sponsors and around 100 House co-sponsors as of September 2025. Despite this strong backing, the bill has faced repeated delays. As of mid-2025, sponsors discussed attaching the bill to a continuing resolution or other must-pass legislation to accelerate passage (https://medium.com/@nickylee_82870/the-us-congress-has-made-a-major-move-a-bill-to-sanction-russia-may-pass-within-the-month-0ec9e65f2a23). However, the bill's progress has been complicated by President Trump's desire to use sanctions as leverage in Russia-Ukraine peace negotiations, and the White House has not given clear informal approval for a vote (https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/7/10/651035/). Senate Majority Leader John Thune expressed hope for a floor vote before the August 2025 recess, but that deadline passed without action (https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2025/07/15/us-senate-weighs-sanctions-bill-as-russia-stalls-peace-talks/). As of October 2025, the bill has not received a Senate floor vote. For the bill to be signed into law by December 31, 2025, it would need to clear both chambers and reach the President's desk — making a Senate floor vote in the coming weeks an essential precursor.

Sources:
- JD Supra, "Congress Threatens Putin with Sanctions Bill" (June 4, 2025): https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/congress-threatens-putin-with-sanctions-8412066/
- Charter97, "Graham's Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025" (July 10, 2025): https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/7/10/651035/
- Medium, "The US Congress has made a major move" (September 16, 2025): https://medium.com/@nickylee_82870/the-us-congress-has-made-a-major-move-a-bill-to-sanction-russia-may-pass-within-the-month-0ec9e65f2a23
- Forbes, "U.S. Senate Weighs Sanctions Bill As Russia Stalls Peace Talks" (July 15, 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2025/07/15/us-senate-weighs-sanctions-bill-as-russia-stalls-peace-talks/
- WSIU, "Congress hopes to raise heat on Russia" (July 18, 2025): https://www.wsiu.org/2025-07-18/congress-hopes-to-raise-heat-on-russia-amid-souring-relations-between-trump-and-putin
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 22, 2025 and November 21, 2025 (inclusive), the U.S. Senate holds a recorded floor vote (roll call or voice vote) on S.1241 (the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2025) as a standalone bill, OR on any other legislative vehicle (e.g., a continuing resolution, appropriations bill, or National Defense Authorization Act) that contains the core sanctions provisions of S.1241 (specifically the 500% tariff on Russian-origin goods and secondary sanctions on purchasers of Russian energy). The primary resolution source is Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1241) and the Senate roll call vote records (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm). If Congress.gov is unavailable, credible reporting from at least two major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, The Hill, Politico) confirming such a vote will suffice. The question resolves No if no such floor vote occurs by 11:59 PM ET on November 21, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: A Senate floor vote is a necessary precursor to the bill becoming law. If the Senate does not vote on S.1241 or a vehicle containing its provisions by late November, the remaining legislative calendar before December 31, 2025 becomes extremely compressed, making enactment far less likely. Conversely, a Senate vote (especially passage) in this window would be a strong positive indicator. This is a genuinely different observable event from the ultimate question — it asks about a specific procedural step rather than final enactment — and it is a crux on which forecasters who disagree about the ultimate outcome would likely differ.

subquestions.question: Will the Atlas browser appear as a separately listed browser on StatCounter's global daily browser market share data with at least 0.5% share on any single day between October 24 and November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, its first AI-powered web browser, on October 21–22, 2025. The browser is initially available on macOS only, with Windows, iOS, and Android versions expected later. As of September 2025, Google Chrome held approximately 71.9% of global browser market share according to StatCounter, with Safari at ~13.9%, Edge at ~4.67%, Firefox at ~2.17%, Samsung Internet at ~1.86%, and Opera at ~1.74%. For NG-3 to launch by January 31, 2026, Blue Origin would likely need to either reuse the recovered NG-2 booster or have a new booster ready. The pace of booster refurbishment is a strong indicator of whether NG-3 can meet that timeline. SpaceX's early Falcon 9 booster turnaround times were measured in months; Blue Origin's first-ever refurbishment could take longer. If Blue Origin publicly confirms the NG-2 booster has been refurbished and is ready for re-flight (or confirms a new booster is ready), this is a strong signal that NG-3 is on track for a late January 2026 launch.

If no such public confirmation is made by 11:59 PM UTC on January 11, 2026, the question resolves No. If Blue Origin's official communications channels become unavailable, credible reporting from major space news outlets (e.g., SpaceNews at https://spacenews.com/, Ars Technica at https://arstechnica.com/space/, or NASASpaceflight.com at https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/) may serve as alternative resolution sources.
subquestions.rationale: The readiness of a New Glenn booster for NG-3 is a critical prerequisite for the flight to occur by January 31, 2026. If by January 11, 2026, Blue Origin has not confirmed booster readiness for NG-3, it becomes very unlikely the mission will launch within the remaining ~20 days. Conversely, if booster integration or readiness is confirmed by that date, it significantly increases the probability of an on-time NG-3 launch. This is a different observable event from the launch itself—it tracks vehicle preparation progress rather than the launch outcome—and serves as a meaningful leading indicator. question: Will Trump send the national guard to Boston by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump or his administration takes a formal action or makes an official announcement directing the deployment of National Guard troops to the listed city by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No.”
A qualifying announcement or action will count, regardless of if/when the deployment actually occurs, or if the deployment is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

Qualifying actions include but are not limited to:
- A Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order, Presidential Memorandum) that directs or announces National Guard deployment to the listed city.
- An official White House/DoD/National Guard Bureau press release, fact sheet, or order explicitly stating that National Guard troops will be deployed to the listed city.
- A Secretary of Defense or NGB directive/order that calls up or assigns National Guard forces to the listed city, including under Title 32 (state control with federal funding) or Title 10 (federalized).
- An official federal announcement that specific state Guard units (including the listed city National Guard or out-of-state Guard) are being sent to the listed city.

Non-qualifying actions include:
- Informal announcements/social media posts which do not constitute a formal policy announcement 
- Ambiguous remarks, “we’re considering it,” broad statements like “ready to go anywhere,” or contingent plans without a clear directive to the listed city.
- Generic posture changes (e.g., standing up quick-reaction forces “nationwide”) that do not explicitly name the listed city as a deployment location.
- A state-only activation by the listed city's state Governor without any official Trump administration action or announcement about sending the Guard to the listed city.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

For context, Tesla China wholesale figures in recent months have varied significantly. In September 2025, Tesla China wholesale sales were reportedly strong as part of the Q3 record. Historically, Tesla China monthly wholesale figures have ranged from roughly 40,000 to over 90,000 units depending on the month and export cycles, with October often being a transition month as new-quarter production ramps. If October China sales exceed 75,000 units, it would suggest Tesla is on pace for a strong Q4 globally. Album rollouts in the modern era typically involve some form of public announcement — a social media post, a press release through a label, or at minimum, pre-save links appearing on streaming platforms — weeks before release. Major artists occasionally drop albums with no advance notice ('surprise drops'), but even these are typically preceded by increased social media activity or cryptic teasers. Frank Ocean's primary public communication channels include his Instagram (@blfrankocean), his Tumblr, and his website (blfrankocean.com).
