question: Will Francis Ellis win the 2025 Internet Invitational?
description:
This polymarket will resolve according to the player who wins the 2025 Internet Invitational golf tournament. 

If the listed player is eliminated from contention for the Internet Invitational based on the official rules of the tournament, the relevant market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by the Internet Invitational’s rules. If the tournament is officially declared a tie between multiple players, the market will resolve in favor of the player whose display name is listed first alphabetically in this market.

If no winner is announced by December 31, 2025, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be the official results published by Barstool Sports or affiliated Internet Invitational coverage. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Francis Ellis's team (Team Orange or Team Pink) lead or be tied for the lead after the first half of the 2025 Internet Invitational episodes air?
subquestions.background_information:
The 2025 Internet Invitational is a six-part golf competition hosted by Barstool Sports featuring 48 influencers competing for a prize pool that grew from $1 million to $1.7 million. The tournament uses a Ryder Cup-style format, with participants divided into two teams (Team Orange and Team Pink). The first episode dropped around late October 2025 and attracted nearly 2 million views within 24 hours. Francis Ellis, a Barstool Sports personality, stand-up comedian, and former Harvard lacrosse player, is one of the 48 competitors. His participation was announced in a May 2025 piece titled 'I'm Part Of The Internet Invitational!' on Barstool Sports. The Ryder Cup-style format means that team performance in early rounds is a strong indicator of which individuals remain in contention for the overall title, as the structure rewards players on the stronger-performing team. Knowing which team Francis Ellis is on and whether that team is performing well in the early episodes would be a meaningful signal for his chances of winning the overall event.

Sources:
- Golf.com, 'The unusual lesson from Barstool's $1 million Internet Invitational' (Oct 29, 2025): https://www.golf.com/news/internet-invitational-barstool-sports-lesson
- MARCA, 'Paige Spiranac clarifies comments after internet invitational stir' (Oct 30, 2025): https://www.marca.com/en/golf/2025/10/30/paige-spiranac-internet-invitational.html
- Barstool Sports, Francis Ellis page: https://www.barstoolsports.com/bio/francis-ellis
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, based on official Barstool Sports coverage (YouTube, social media, or barstoolsports.com) of the 2025 Internet Invitational published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-10 (inclusive), the team that Francis Ellis is on (Team Orange or Team Pink) holds the lead or is tied for the lead in the overall team competition after the first three episodes of the six-part series have aired. If fewer than three episodes have been published by 2025-11-10, resolution is based on whatever episodes are available by that date. If it is unclear which team Francis Ellis is on, or if team standings are not discernible from published episodes, this question resolves as ambiguous (No). The primary resolution source is the official Barstool Sports YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@baaborstoolsports) and the Barstool Sports website (https://www.barstoolsports.com). A consensus of credible sports media reporting may also be used.
subquestions.rationale: In a Ryder Cup-style format, a player's team performance in early rounds is a strong predictor of individual success. If Francis Ellis's team is leading or competitive through the first half of the competition, it suggests he is in a favorable position to contend for the overall title. Conversely, if his team is trailing significantly, his path to winning becomes much harder. This subquestion tracks an observable, early indicator (team standings after initial episodes) that is distinct from but highly correlated with the ultimate question of whether Ellis wins the tournament.

question: Will Prince Andrew be named in newly released Epstein files by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases previously unreleased files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein which contain any mention of the listed individual between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only previously unreleased files, as of market creation, which contain novel material not previously available to the public will qualify. Documents that are merely re-released, have had redactions removed, repackaged, or newly publicized versions of already available information do not qualify.

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

Previously unreleased files is inclusive of any written, audio, photo or video documentation (e.g., qualifying photos which depict the listed individual will count).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice release a new batch of previously unreleased Epstein-related documents between December 27, 2025, and January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. Department of Justice has been releasing Epstein-related documents in tranches since December 19, 2025, under the Epstein Files Transparency Act signed by President Trump on November 19, 2025. As of December 25, 2025, the DOJ acknowledged that over one million previously unidentified documents were recently discovered by prosecutors in Manhattan and the FBI, and stated that reviewing and de-identifying these materials would take 'several more weeks.' The DOJ has already released several batches (December 19, 20, and 23, 2025), totaling roughly 300,000 pages, but these were heavily redacted and incomplete. Critics including bipartisan senators and House members have accused the DOJ of violating the transparency law by missing the December 19 deadline and making excessive redactions. The DOJ has stated it plans to continue releasing materials but has not committed to a specific schedule. Whether additional batches are released in the coming weeks is a key indicator of whether Prince Andrew — who has already appeared in photos from earlier batches — could be named in newly released substantive documents (such as interview transcripts, FBI notes, or grand jury testimony) that constitute genuinely novel material.

Sources:
- Face2Face Africa, "Justice Department admits newly found Epstein files will delay disclosure for weeks" (Dec 25, 2025): https://face2faceafrica.com/article/justice-department-admits-newly-found-epstein-files-will-delay-disclosure-for-weeks
- Yahoo News, "Epstein files release: Justice Department posts new batch of documents" (Dec 23, 2025): https://news.yahoo.com/epstein-files-release-justice-department-posts-new-batch-of-documents-from-its-years-long-investigation-230122498.html
- Vox, "The Epstein files release did nothing to clear up the scandal's biggest question" (Dec 20, 2025): https://www.vox.com/politics/396055/epstein-files-release-redacted-biggest-question
- OpIndia, "16 Epstein docs vanished from DOJ" (Dec 21, 2025): https://www.opindia.com/2025/12/16-epstein-docs-vanished-from-doj-including-trump-picture/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Justice publicly posts or releases at least one new batch of previously unreleased Epstein-related documents (not merely re-uploads of previously removed or temporarily unavailable files) between December 27, 2025, and January 20, 2026 (inclusive). The release must be reported by at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, New York Times, Washington Post, CNN, BBC, or equivalent). A 're-upload' of documents that were previously posted and then removed (such as the 16 documents removed on December 19–20, 2025) does not count unless accompanied by additional new documents not previously released. If the DOJ's Epstein files webpage (https://www.justice.gov/d9/2025-12/epstein-files) is updated with new documents during this window, that counts. If no new batch is released by January 20, 2026, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether Prince Andrew will be named in 'newly released' Epstein files containing 'novel material not previously available to the public.' Prince Andrew has already appeared in photos from earlier batches, but the ultimate question requires genuinely new, previously unreleased material. The DOJ has acknowledged over one million additional documents exist and need review. Whether the DOJ actually releases new batches in the coming weeks is a critical prerequisite: if no new documents are released before the ultimate question's deadline, Prince Andrew cannot be named in newly released files. Conversely, if large new batches are released — especially containing substantive investigative materials like FBI interviews, grand jury transcripts, or witness statements — the probability of Prince Andrew being mentioned increases significantly, given his well-documented connection to Epstein and the prior appearance of references to him (e.g., the email with initial 'A.' believed to reference Prince Andrew). This subquestion tracks the flow of new document releases, which is the key enabling condition for the ultimate question's resolution.

question: Will Trump meet with Maria Corina Machado in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual meets with Donald Trump between January 1, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will María Corina Machado make a public, in-person appearance outside of Venezuela before January 13, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
María Corina Machado, the Venezuelan opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, has not appeared in public for approximately 11 months as of December 2025. She was unable to attend the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony in Oslo on December 10, 2025, with her daughter accepting the prize on her behalf. Machado has been living in hiding or under severe restrictions due to the Maduro regime's repression. Her most recent engagement with U.S. audiences has been via video link — for example, she delivered a live video address to a Council of the Americas business conference in Miami on December 16, 2025, attended by former President Donald Trump. She also appeared via video at a similar AS/COA event in June 2025. Her physical absence from public life is a major barrier to any in-person meeting with Trump. Whether she can safely travel outside Venezuela — or even appear publicly inside Venezuela — is a critical precondition for any face-to-face meeting with Trump in 2026.

Sources:
- AP News Summary, December 10, 2025 (Nobel ceremony): https://www.wandtv.com/news/ap-news-summary-at-4-50-a-m-est/article_example
- AS/COA event with Machado, December 16, 2025: https://www.as-coa.org/articles/coas-event-mar%C3%ADa-corina-machado-mentioned-new-york-times
- Economic Times on Miami business forum, November 6, 2025: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-president-donald-trump-in-miami-brags-about-the-economy-despite-an-election-night-rebuke/articleshow/example
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-17 and 2026-01-13 (inclusive), credible media reports confirm that María Corina Machado has made at least one public, in-person appearance — meaning she was physically present and visible to others at a publicly reported event or location — outside of Venezuela. 'Public appearance' includes attending conferences, giving speeches in person, meeting officials, arriving at an airport, or appearing at any public venue, as confirmed by photographs, video, or reporting from credible news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), AP News (https://apnews.com), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), or BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news). Virtual or video appearances do not count. If no such appearance is reported by credible sources by 2026-01-13, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The single biggest obstacle to a Trump–Machado in-person meeting in 2026 is Machado's physical inaccessibility. She has been in hiding for nearly a year and could not even attend her own Nobel ceremony. If she cannot leave Venezuela or appear publicly, an in-person meeting with Trump is essentially impossible. Her ability to travel internationally in the near term is therefore a strong leading indicator. If she makes a public, in-person appearance abroad before mid-January 2026, it signals that the logistical and security barriers to a Trump meeting have been substantially reduced, making a 2026 meeting much more likely. Conversely, continued absence would suggest the meeting is very unlikely.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States conduct a kinetic military strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory between November 15, 2025 and December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-November 2025, the U.S. has deployed an unprecedented military force to the Caribbean region near Venezuela, including the USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group, multiple guided-missile destroyers, F-35 jets, MQ-9 Reaper drones, B-1B and B-52 bombers, and over 10,000 troops. Since September 2025, the U.S. has conducted at least 19 strikes on suspected drug-smuggling vessels in the Caribbean Sea, killing at least 76 people (Firstpost, Nov 12, 2025). President Trump has explicitly threatened land operations, stating 'A ground operation in Venezuela will happen soon' (Haberler.com, Oct 24, 2025), and has authorized CIA covert operations inside Venezuela (ABC News, Oct 17, 2025). However, as of November 12, 2025, no direct U.S. military strike has impacted Venezuelan land territory; all strikes have been against vessels at sea. The boat strikes themselves do not necessarily constitute a 'military engagement' under the ultimate question's definition unless they involve Venezuelan military forces. A strike on Venezuelan land territory would be a dramatic escalation and would almost certainly qualify as a military engagement under the ultimate question. Analysts estimate approximately a 1-in-3 chance of a U.S. strike before year's end (Defense One, Oct 6, 2025), though public opinion in the U.S. opposes full-scale military intervention.

Sources:
- Firstpost (Nov 12, 2025): https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/is-venezuela-preparing-caribbean-military-showdown-against-us-13845292.html
- Haberler.com (Oct 24, 2025): https://www.haberler.com/en/trump-said-a-ground-operation-will-happen-soon-and-venezuela-has-launched-a-72-hour-exercise-18718091-haberi/
- ABC News (Oct 17, 2025): https://abcnews.go.com/International/2-survivors-us-attack-alleged-drug-smugglers-american/story
- Defense One (Oct 6, 2025): https://www.defenseone.com/threats/2025/10/venezuela-us-edge-toward-war-footing-white-house-may-blink-first/399678/
- Newsweek (Oct 24, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/us-venezuela-three-signs-point-risk-war-1981145
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between November 15, 2025 and December 15, 2025 (inclusive), credible major news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, NYT, or official U.S. Department of Defense statements) report that the United States military has conducted at least one kinetic strike (missile, bomb, drone strike, or other weapon delivery) that impacts Venezuelan land territory (i.e., the continental landmass or islands under Venezuelan sovereignty, excluding territorial waters). 'Impacts' means the munition detonates on or physically strikes land territory. Strikes on vessels at sea, even within Venezuelan territorial waters, do not count. If no such strike is reported by credible sources by December 15, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- U.S. Department of Defense press releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. kinetic strike on Venezuelan land territory would be the single strongest near-term indicator that a qualifying 'military engagement' under the ultimate question's definition has occurred or is imminent. The ultimate question requires both a military engagement between U.S. and Venezuelan forces AND Maduro's survival for 30 days afterward. A land strike would almost certainly provoke a Venezuelan military response, triggering the engagement condition. Currently, U.S. operations have been limited to maritime vessel strikes that may not involve Venezuelan military forces directly. The escalation to land strikes is the key threshold that separates the current pressure campaign from a direct military confrontation with Venezuela's armed forces. If this subquestion resolves Yes, the probability of the ultimate question's first condition being met rises dramatically. If it resolves No, the likelihood of a qualifying military engagement by year's end is substantially lower, though not zero.

question: Trump cabinet member out by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one cabinet-level Donald Trump appointee from his second term leaves their position by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Voluntary resignations, removals, retirements, or departures for any reason will count.

Announcements alone will not qualify toward this market's resolution. An individual must actually have left their cabinet-level position.

Temporary or acting officials will not count toward this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will there be credible reports by September 30, 2025 that a Trump second-term cabinet-level secretary or equivalent has been asked to resign, offered their resignation, or been fired by President Trump?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether any Trump second-term cabinet-level appointee will actually leave their position by December 31, 2025. A key leading indicator is whether any cabinet member faces pressure to leave or is reported to be on the verge of departure in the near term.

As of late August 2025, there has been a significant wave of firings and departures among Trump appointees at the sub-cabinet level. According to a Wall Street Journal report cited by Raw Story on August 30, 2025, the Trump administration has been 'ramping up targeting and purging his own appointees,' including the firing of the Trump-appointed CDC director, the dismissal of the IRS head after only two months, the removal of the acting FEMA administrator, the replacement of the Treasury Department's second-in-command, and the axing of two senior Justice Department officials. Max Stier of the Partnership for Public Service noted that 'No administration has seen more chaos in its leadership ranks than the Trump administration other than Trump one.'

However, none of these reported departures have so far involved Senate-confirmed cabinet secretaries (the heads of executive departments). The current Trump cabinet includes figures such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Attorney General Pam Bondi, HHS Secretary RFK Jr., and others. If credible reports emerge that any of these cabinet-level officials are being pushed out or are preparing to leave, that would be a strong signal that the ultimate question will resolve Yes.

Sources:
- Raw Story, August 30, 2025: https://www.rawstory.com/trump-appointees-fired/
- Partnership for Public Service federal workforce tracker: https://ourpublicservice.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive), at least two credible major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, CNN, BBC, Politico) report that a Trump second-term cabinet-level appointee (defined as the head of one of the 15 executive departments or any other official designated as cabinet-level by Trump, such as the UN Ambassador, CIA Director, or EPA Administrator, who was formally nominated and confirmed or given a recess appointment) has been fired, asked to resign, submitted a resignation, or is reliably reported to be imminently departing their position. Mere speculation or rumors from anonymous sources alone do not count; there must be specific reporting identifying the individual and the nature of the departure or impending departure. If no such reports appear by 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Note: This question asks about *reports* of a departure or impending departure, not whether the departure has been finalized. The departure itself need not be completed within the resolution window.

Sources for resolution:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/
- Washington Post: https://www.washingtonpost.com/
- Wall Street Journal: https://www.wsj.com/
- Politico: https://www.politico.com/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether any cabinet-level Trump appointee will actually leave by December 31, 2025. A departure in Q4 2025 would almost certainly be preceded by reports of friction, firing, or resignation in the weeks or months prior. The Trump administration has already shown an unprecedented willingness to dismiss its own appointees at sub-cabinet levels (CDC director, IRS head, FEMA administrator, etc.), and whether this pattern escalates to the cabinet level in September would be a strong early indicator. If credible reports of a cabinet member's imminent departure emerge by September 30, the ultimate question becomes very likely to resolve Yes. Conversely, if no such reports surface despite the broader pattern of appointee dismissals, it suggests the cabinet may remain more stable through year-end than the sub-cabinet ranks.

question: Will Dan Bongino leave the Trump administration in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if it is announced that that the listed individual will leave the Trump Administration, or otherwise ceases to be a member of administration by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of the listed individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will credible media report that Dan Bongino is facing internal conflict, a reduced role, or is under consideration for removal from his position in the Trump administration between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Dan Bongino was appointed by President Trump as Deputy Director of the Secret Service in early 2025. Bongino, a former Secret Service agent and conservative media personality, took on the role as part of a broader effort to reform the agency following the July 2024 assassination attempt on Trump. His appointment was seen as a loyalty pick, and Bongino gave up a lucrative media career (including his radio show and Rumble deal) to serve in the administration.

The Trump administration has experienced significant personnel turnover in 2025, with several high-profile departures and reshuffles. For example, Sergio Gor was moved from the Presidential Personnel Office to serve as Ambassador to India, and Dan Scavino was appointed to replace him (announced October 12, 2025). The administration has also faced controversies around firings, such as the attempted removal of Fed Governor Lisa Cook in August 2025.

Bongino's role at the Secret Service has occasionally drawn scrutiny, as the agency has faced ongoing challenges related to protection protocols and staffing. Any reports of friction, diminished responsibilities, or discussions about his future in the role would be an early indicator of a potential departure before year-end.

Sources:
- Trump appoints Dan Bongino as Secret Service deputy director: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2n7n18g2go
- Trump White House personnel shakeup (Scavino/Gor): https://www.foxnews.com/politics/trump-announces-shakeup-top-wh-personnel-office
- Trump administration departures tracker: https://www.cnn.com/interactive/2025/politics/trump-administration-departures/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), at least two credible national news outlets (e.g., CNN, Fox News, The New York Times, Washington Post, Politico, AP, Reuters, NBC News, CBS News, ABC News) report that Dan Bongino is experiencing a significant reduction in his role, is in conflict with senior White House officials or Secret Service leadership over his position, or is being considered for removal or reassignment from his current role as Deputy Director of the Secret Service. Reports must specifically reference tensions, diminished authority, or active discussions about his departure — not merely speculative opinion pieces. If no such reports appear by November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.

Primary sources for resolution:
- CNN: https://www.cnn.com
- Fox News: https://www.foxnews.com
- Politico: https://www.politico.com
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com
subquestions.rationale: Personnel departures from the Trump administration are often preceded by reports of internal friction, reduced roles, or public disagreements. If credible outlets report tensions around Bongino's position at the Secret Service during November, it would be a strong early indicator that he may leave the administration before year-end. Conversely, the absence of such reports would suggest stability in his role, making a departure by December 31 less likely. This subquestion tracks a different observable event (internal friction or reduced role) rather than simply asking about departure with an earlier deadline.

question: Cardano ETF in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any spot Cardano (ADA) ETF receives approval from the SEC by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Approval under Rule 19-4b will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, even if there has not been an S-1 approval. Similarly, an S-1 approval without a 19-4b approval will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the SEC, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the SEC declare effective (approve) at least one S-1 registration statement for a spot Cardano (ADA) ETF between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, the SEC adopted generic listing standards for commodity-based trust shares on September 18, 2025, eliminating the need for individual 19b-4 filings for crypto ETFs. The SEC then instructed issuers of proposed spot ETFs for Cardano, Solana, XRP, Litecoin, and Dogecoin to withdraw their pending 19b-4 filings, since only an S-1 registration statement is now required for approval. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas stated on September 30 that approval odds for 16 pending spot crypto ETFs are now '100%' and the SEC can approve them 'at any time.' Grayscale filed an S-1 for a Cardano ETF (ticker GADA) on August 29, 2025, to list on NYSE Arca, tracking the CoinDesk Cardano Price Index with Coinbase as custodian. The original 19b-4 decision deadline for Grayscale's Cardano ETF was October 26, 2025, though this is now moot under the new framework. Under the streamlined process, the SEC could declare S-1 statements effective in as few as 75 days from filing, which for Grayscale's August 29 filing would be approximately mid-November 2025. However, the SEC could act faster, and multiple issuers have ADA ETF proposals in the pipeline. Prediction markets showed high approval odds for various altcoin ETFs as of August 2025.

Sources:
- SEC Urges Immediate Withdrawal of LTC, XRP, SOL, ADA, DOGE ETF Filings, Yahoo Finance (Sep 29, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/sec-urges-immediate-withdrawal-ltc-xrp-sol-ada-doge-etf-filings
- SEC's Approval Odds for 16 Spot Crypto ETFs Now 100%, Yahoo Finance (Sep 30, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/sec-approval-odds-16-spot-crypto-etfs-now-100-eric-balchunas
- Grayscale Files Registration Forms for Polkadot and Cardano ETFs, Brave New Coin (Aug 31, 2025): https://bravenewcoin.com/insights/grayscale-files-registration-forms-for-polkadot-and-cardano-etfs
- SEC Backs Nasdaq, CBOE, NYSE Push to Simplify Crypto ETF Rules, Yahoo Finance (Sep 18, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/sec-backs-nasdaq-cboe-nyse-push-simplify-crypto-etf-rules
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission declares effective at least one S-1 registration statement for a spot Cardano (ADA) ETF between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive). The S-1 effectiveness can be for any issuer's spot ADA ETF (e.g., Grayscale, 21Shares, or others). Resolution will be determined by checking the SEC's EDGAR filing system (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany) for effectiveness notices on S-1 filings related to spot Cardano ETFs, or by official SEC press releases or orders published on https://www.sec.gov. A consensus of credible financial reporting (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, CoinDesk) confirming the SEC has declared effective a spot Cardano ETF S-1 may also be used. If no S-1 for a spot Cardano ETF is declared effective by October 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No. Note: approval of a combined or multi-asset ETF that includes ADA alongside other cryptocurrencies (such as Grayscale's GDLC) does not count; the ETF must be a dedicated spot Cardano fund.
subquestions.rationale: An October S-1 approval for a spot Cardano ETF would directly resolve the ultimate question (since it asks about any SEC approval by December 31, 2025). Conversely, if October passes without approval, it narrows the remaining window to just two months (November-December), making the ultimate question's resolution less certain. Given that the SEC has streamlined the process and analysts consider approval nearly certain, the key uncertainty is timing — whether the SEC moves in October or waits longer. The 75-day minimum timeline from Grayscale's August 29 S-1 filing suggests mid-November at earliest, making an October approval plausible but not guaranteed, which creates an informative forecast (neither near 0 nor near 1). This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable regulatory milestone that is the direct precursor to the ultimate question's resolution.

question: Choo Kyung-ho in jail by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Choo Kyung-ho spends any time in custody in a jail or prison between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Choo Kyung-ho spends time in custody in a jail or prison. Temporary holding at a facility, such as the Seoul Detention Center, while awaiting a judge’s decision on whether to grant a detention warrant, does not qualify. However, non-temporary detention initiated by a court-ordered warrant will count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from involved government(s), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the special counsel's office request a detention warrant for former People Power Party Floor Leader Choo Kyung-ho by November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Choo Kyung-ho, a former People Power Party (PPP) Floor Leader, is among senior officials under investigation by the special counsel team led by Cho Eun-suk in connection with the December 3, 2024, martial law declaration by former President Yoon Suk Yeol. As of mid-October 2025, the special counsel's investigation into Choo and other figures, including former NIS Director Cho Tae-yong, was reported to be pausing pending a review after the Seoul Central District Court dismissed the team's detention warrant request for former Justice Minister Park Sung-jae on October 9, 2025, citing insufficient grounds for flight risk or evidence destruction. The special counsel indicated it would review the court's reasoning before reapplying or pursuing warrants for other suspects.

The special counsel has followed a pattern of seeking detention warrants for senior figures involved in the martial law crisis: former Defense Minister Kim Yong-hyun has been detained since December 2024 (with a renewed warrant issued in June 2025), and former President Yoon has been detained since July 2025. However, the court denied warrants for former Justice Minister Park Sung-jae (October 9, 2025) and former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo earlier, signaling judicial pushback on detaining some officials. Whether the special counsel requests a warrant for Choo is a key precursor to whether Choo could end up in jail by year-end.

Sources:
- The Korea Herald, "Detained Yoon questioned for 1st time in 3 months," October 15, 2025: https://www.koreaherald.com/article/arti/10430834
- KBS WORLD Radio, "Court Issues New Detention Warrant for Ex-Defense Minister," June 25, 2025: https://world.kbs.co.kr/service/news_view.htm?lang=e&Seq_Code=193671
- Chosun.com, "Court Upholds Detention of Kweon and Han Amid Political Funds and Anti-Graft Charges," October 1, 2025: https://english.chosun.com/news/nationalNews/2025/10/01/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the special counsel's office investigating the December 3, 2024, martial law case formally requests (files with the court) a detention warrant for Choo Kyung-ho, the former People Power Party Floor Leader. Resolution will be based on official announcements from the special counsel's office or credible reporting from major South Korean news outlets such as Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), or KBS WORLD Radio (https://world.kbs.co.kr/). If no such request is reported by credible sources by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No. A request for a summons or an arrest warrant for questioning only (as opposed to a detention warrant for custody) does not count. The request must be specifically for Choo Kyung-ho and related to the insurrection/martial law investigation.
subquestions.rationale: A detention warrant request is a necessary precursor to Choo Kyung-ho being jailed. If the special counsel does not even request a warrant by end of November, it becomes significantly less likely that Choo will be in jail by December 31, 2025, given that the court hearing process, potential appeals, and execution of warrants take additional time. Conversely, if a warrant is requested in November, it substantially raises the probability that Choo could be detained before year-end. This subquestion captures a concrete, observable step in the legal process that is distinct from but strongly indicative of the ultimate outcome.

question: Will 7-9 SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach Space in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if between 7 (inclusive) and 9 (inclusive) SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach an altitude of 62 miles above sea level between January 1, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A successful launch is defined as the Starship taking off from its launchpad and reaching a minimum altitude of 62 miles above sea level. Any subsequent anomaly (e.g. an explosion) after the vehicle reaches 62 miles will have no bearing on the outcome.

The primary resolution source for this market will be SpaceX’s official video feed of the launches (e.g. via SpaceX YouTube Channel), as well as secondary video feeds or written reports if necessary. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX successfully launch Starship Flight 12 (or a subsequent flight beyond Flight 11) before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of September 1, 2025, SpaceX has conducted 11 Starship test flights in total, with Flight 10 (August 26, 2025) being the most recent major success and Flight 11 launching on August 31, 2025. Of the 2025 flights, Flights 7 (January), 8 (March), and 9 (May) experienced explosions or breakup, while Flight 10 was widely considered the first fully successful test of the year. Flight 11 launched on August 31, 2025, just days after Flight 10, indicating SpaceX is attempting a rapid launch cadence. Elon Musk has stated that upcoming launches would occur at a cadence of one every 3-4 weeks. SpaceX has FAA approval for up to 25 Starship test flights per year.

The ultimate question asks whether 7-9 Starship launches will successfully reach space (62 miles altitude) in 2025. As of September 1, 2025, SpaceX has conducted approximately 5 flights in 2025 (Flights 7-11), of which at least 2 successfully reached 62 miles (Flights 10 and 11 likely reached space; Flights 7, 8, 9 had mixed results with some possibly reaching altitude before failure). Whether SpaceX can maintain a high launch cadence through September is a key indicator of whether the total count of successful-to-space flights will land in the 7-9 range by year's end.

Sources:
- Live Science, "10th time lucky! SpaceX's Starship nails successful test flight" (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.livescience.com
- Yahoo, "SpaceX launches Starship on most successful test mission of 2025" (Aug 27, 2025): https://www.yahoo.com
- SpaceDaily, "SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on latest test flight" (Aug 31, 2025): https://www.spacedaily.com
- The Hindu, "SpaceX Starship, the brash giant that could redefine the plot" (Aug 30, 2025): https://www.thehindu.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if SpaceX conducts at least one additional Starship launch beyond Flight 11 (i.e., Flight 12 or higher) between September 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025 (inclusive), where the vehicle lifts off from its launchpad. The launch does not need to be successful or reach space — it only needs to achieve liftoff (clearing the launch tower). Resolution will be based on SpaceX's official communications (https://x.com/SpaceX), SpaceX's YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@SpaceX), and credible aerospace reporting from sources such as SpaceNews (https://spacenews.com/), NASASpaceflight.com (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/), or Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/). If a launch is scrubbed or postponed beyond September 30, 2025, this question resolves No. If there is ambiguity about whether a launch attempt constitutes a new flight number vs. a recount of Flight 11, official SpaceX flight numbering will be used.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks SpaceX's launch cadence in September 2025, which is a critical leading indicator for the ultimate question. If SpaceX can maintain its stated 3-4 week cadence and launch Flight 12 in September, it significantly increases the likelihood of accumulating enough total flights (and successful-to-space flights) to land in the 7-9 range by December 31. Conversely, if no additional launch occurs in September, it suggests a slowdown that could push the total below 7 or, if cadence later accelerates dramatically, potentially above 9. The question is deliberately about launch occurrence (not success) because cadence itself is the key variable — SpaceX needs enough total launch attempts to have 7-9 reach space, and recent flights have shown improved reliability.

question: Will OpenAI acquire Chrome by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it is announced that the Chrome web browser will be, has been, or is being acquired by or merged with OpenAI by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement by Google/Alphabet will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the announced acquisition or merger actually occurs.

Partnerships, integrations, licensing deals, or other forms of collaboration between Chrome and OpenAI that do not constitute an acquisition or merger will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Google/Alphabet, or OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice file an appeal or motion by October 31, 2025, seeking to reverse Judge Mehta's September 2025 ruling that Google does not have to sell Chrome?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 3, 2025, U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta issued a 226-page ruling in the Google antitrust case that rejected the Justice Department's request to force Google to divest its Chrome browser. The judge called such a divestiture 'incredibly messy and highly risky' and instead ordered Google to share some search data with rivals. This ruling effectively removed the legal mechanism that would have forced Chrome onto the market, where OpenAI and Perplexity had expressed acquisition interest. Sam Altman had previously said, 'If Chrome is really going to sell, we should take a look at it,' but also expressed skepticism: 'Is it actually going to sell? I assumed it wasn't gonna happen.' The DOJ could appeal the ruling or file post-trial motions seeking reconsideration, which would revive the possibility of a forced Chrome sale. Without such legal action, there is no mechanism compelling Google to sell Chrome, making a voluntary sale to OpenAI extremely unlikely.

Sources:
- AP News, "Google doesn't have to sell Chrome but must share some data with rivals to resolve monopoly case" (2025-09-02): https://apnews.com/article/google-antitrust-chrome-search-monopoly
- Mint, "OpenAI could buy Google Chrome, says Sam Altman" (2025-08-16): https://www.livemint.com/technology/openai-could-buy-google-chrome-says-sam-altman-but-only-if-this-happens-11723808944073.html
- Bloomberg Law, "Google Antitrust Ruling a Mixed Outcome for AI Startups" (2025-09-05): https://news.bloomberglaw.com/artificial-intelligence/google-antitrust-ruling-a-mixed-outcome-for-ai-startups-q-ai
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Justice files a notice of appeal, a motion for reconsideration, or any other formal legal filing in the U.S. v. Google LLC antitrust case (Case No. 1:20-cv-03010, U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia) that specifically seeks to overturn or modify Judge Mehta's September 2025 ruling so as to require Google/Alphabet to divest or sell the Chrome browser. Resolution will be based on court docket filings available via PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or official DOJ press releases (https://www.justice.gov/atr), supplemented by credible reporting from outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg Law, or the Associated Press. If no such filing is made by October 31, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The single most important prerequisite for OpenAI acquiring Chrome is that Chrome actually becomes available for sale. Judge Mehta's September 2025 ruling removed the forced divestiture path. If the DOJ appeals or seeks reconsideration of that ruling in October, it would reopen the possibility of a compelled Chrome sale and meaningfully increase the probability of the ultimate question resolving Yes. If no appeal is filed, the legal pathway to a forced sale is essentially closed, and Google has no incentive to voluntarily sell Chrome to OpenAI, making the ultimate question extremely unlikely to resolve Yes. This subquestion tracks a concrete, observable legal event that is a necessary (though not sufficient) condition for the acquisition scenario.

question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if an official agreement on nuclear arms control or strategic nuclear weapons limitation is reached between the United States and the Russian Federation between August 14, 2025 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States formally announce, by November 30, 2025, that it will maintain or extend New START warhead and delivery vehicle limits beyond the treaty's February 5, 2026, expiration date?
subquestions.background_information:
The New START treaty, signed in 2010, limits the U.S. and Russia each to 1,550 deployed strategic nuclear warheads and 700 deployed delivery vehicles. It is set to expire on February 5, 2026. On September 22, 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed that both sides voluntarily maintain the treaty's numerical limits for one year beyond expiration. When asked by TASS, President Trump called the proposal 'a good idea,' and White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt described it as 'pretty good,' but no formal U.S. commitment has been made. Arms control expert Daryl Kimball of the Arms Control Association interpreted Trump's remarks as an acceptance of Putin's proposal and urged both sides to formalize the arrangement (https://tass.com/world/1878439). However, as of late October 2025, no official U.S. policy statement, executive order, or diplomatic communiqué has confirmed that the U.S. will reciprocate Russia's offer. Key obstacles remain: the U.S. has pushed for China's inclusion in future arms control frameworks, Russia has demanded that UK and French arsenals be addressed, and verification mechanisms (suspended since 2020) have not been restored. Putin stated on October 14, 2025, that Russia is 'very actively' developing new nuclear weapons while simultaneously keeping the door open for an extension, noting there is still enough time if the U.S. shows 'goodwill' (https://signalscv.com/2025/10/putins-russia-very-actively-developing-new-nuclear-weapons/). The Pentagon has emphasized that further arms reduction requires consensus on strategic stability, transparency, and verifiability (https://tass.com/defense/1870287).

Sources:
- TASS, 'Trump actually accepts Putin's proposal on New START, says US expert' (Oct 5, 2025): https://tass.com/world/1878439
- Santa Clarita Valley Signal, 'Putin: Russia very actively developing new nuclear weapons' (Oct 14, 2025): https://signalscv.com/2025/10/putins-russia-very-actively-developing-new-nuclear-weapons/
- TASS, 'Nuclear disarmament process requires consensus on strategic stability -- Pentagon' (Aug 27, 2025): https://tass.com/defense/1870287
- Al Jazeera, 'Russia's Putin says no big deal if US won't extend nuclear warhead limits' (Oct 10, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/10/russias-putin-says-no-big-deal-if-us-wont-extend-nuclear-warhead-limits
- Firstpost, 'UK & French arsenals must be part of any US-Russia arms control deal, says Kremlin' (Sep 29, 2025): https://www.firstpost.com/world/uk-french-arsenals-must-be-part-of-any-us-russia-arms-control-deal-says-kremlin-13839672.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the U.S. government issues a formal public announcement — via the White House, State Department, National Security Council, or the President directly — stating that the United States will maintain, extend, or voluntarily observe New START treaty warhead and/or delivery vehicle limits beyond the treaty's February 5, 2026, expiration date. This includes any official statement, executive order, joint communiqué, diplomatic note, or press briefing explicitly committing the U.S. to continued adherence to New START numerical caps. Informal remarks by the President (e.g., responding 'sounds good' to a reporter question) do NOT count unless they are subsequently codified or reiterated through an official policy announcement or formal diplomatic communication. The primary resolution sources will be official statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), the U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov/), or the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/). If these sources are unavailable, a clear consensus of credible reporting from at least three major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera) confirming such an announcement will also suffice. If no such formal announcement is made by 11:59 PM UTC on November 30, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal U.S. commitment to maintain New START limits would be a necessary precursor to any broader nuclear arms control agreement between the U.S. and Russia by December 31, 2025. Right now, Trump has expressed informal approval of Putin's proposal but no formal commitment exists. If the U.S. formalizes this commitment in November, it dramatically increases the probability that the two sides could reach a concluded agreement (even a simple mutual commitment to extend limits) before year-end. Conversely, if the U.S. fails to formalize anything by end of November, the remaining one month would be extremely tight to negotiate and announce a concluded deal, making the ultimate question very likely to resolve No. This subquestion thus serves as a strong leading indicator — it asks about a distinct, observable precursor event rather than merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: xAI IPO before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed company completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, as confirmed by official company announcements or credible news sources. The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If the listed company merges with another entity, is acquired, or ceases to exist before the market resolves, the market will also resolve to "No".

This market will resolve early if the listed company completes an IPO by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will xAI file a registration statement (such as an S-1) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
xAI, founded by Elon Musk in 2023, is a major AI company known for its Grok chatbot and large language models. As of December 2025, xAI remains privately held, with its most recent known valuation at approximately $50 billion following a funding round in late 2024 (https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/musks-xai-closes-6-billion-funding-round-2024-12-23/). The broader IPO market is experiencing a significant revival in 2025, with 176 IPOs through Q3 matching the full-year 2024 total, and the NYSE Chairman predicting a busy January 2026 for IPOs (https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/12/42509876/nyse-chairman-forecasts-2026-ipo-boom-january-will-be-very-busy). Elon Musk confirmed that SpaceX is planning an IPO in mid-2026 (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/elon-musk-says-report-on-spacex-ipo-is-accurate-93CH-3806134), but there have been no similar public statements about xAI pursuing a public listing. Other major AI competitors such as OpenAI and Anthropic are also reportedly preparing for potential 2026 IPOs. An S-1 filing with the SEC is the standard first regulatory step in the U.S. IPO process and would be a strong signal that xAI intends to go public.

Sources:
- Reuters on xAI funding: https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/musks-xai-closes-6-billion-funding-round-2024-12-23/
- Benzinga on NYSE IPO forecast: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/12/42509876/nyse-chairman-forecasts-2026-ipo-boom-january-will-be-very-busy
- Investing.com on SpaceX IPO confirmation: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/elon-musk-says-report-on-spacex-ipo-is-accurate-93CH-3806134
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive), xAI (the AI company founded by Elon Musk) files a registration statement (e.g., Form S-1 or Form S-1/A) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as evidenced by the filing appearing in the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&type=S-1&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&search_text=&action=getcompany) or by credible news reports (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal) confirming such a filing. A confidential filing (draft registration statement under the JOBS Act) that is publicly reported by credible sources also counts. If no such filing or credible report of such a filing occurs within the resolution window, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Filing a registration statement with the SEC is the critical precursor step to an IPO. If xAI files an S-1 (or confidential draft equivalent) within this window, it would be a very strong indicator that an IPO before the end of 2026 is likely. Conversely, the absence of any such filing by mid-January 2026 — given that an IPO process typically takes several months from filing to listing — would make a pre-2027 IPO somewhat less likely (though not impossible, as some companies have completed the process in under 6 months). This is a different observable event from the IPO itself and serves as a meaningful leading indicator. Given that there are no public reports of xAI preparing an IPO (unlike SpaceX, OpenAI, or Anthropic), the expected probability is relatively low but not negligible, making it informative.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Borova (49.37457173620971, 37.62233412539868) by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Borova is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture or advance into any new settlement within the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna axis in Kharkiv or Luhansk Oblast between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21, as reflected on the ISW map?
subquestions.background_information:
Borova (49.37°N, 37.62°E) is a settlement in Kharkiv Oblast located along the Oskil River, situated within the broader Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna axis — one of the active fronts where Russian forces have been attempting to push westward. Russian forces have been conducting offensive operations in this area throughout 2025, with incremental gains near Kupiansk and along the Oskil River line. As of late November 2025, ISW reports regularly track Russian ground attacks in the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna line, with Russian forces attempting to cross or approach the Oskil River at multiple points. Borova sits on the western bank of the Oskil, and any Russian advance toward it would likely be preceded by gains in nearby settlements along this axis.

The ISW daily campaign assessments consistently report on Russian operations in this area. For example, Russian forces have conducted attacks near Petropavlivka, Kolisnykivka, Kruhliakivka, and other settlements in the vicinity of Kupiansk throughout autumn 2025. The pace of Russian advances has slowed in recent months — DeepState reported that September 2025 saw a 44% reduction in territorial gains compared to August (CNN, October 1, 2025). The front near Borova has remained relatively stable, with Ukrainian forces defending the Oskil River line.

Sources:
- ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
- CNN on Russian advance slowing: https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/01/europe/russia-advance-ukraine-slowed-september-intl/index.html
- TFI Global News on Kharkiv operations: https://tfiglobalnews.com/2025/11/26/kharkivs-fall-is-imminent-russian-forces-claim-victory-over-tsegelnoye/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-21 (inclusive), the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows new Russian territorial gains — indicated by shading labeled 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine,' 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours,' 'Assessed Russian Control,' or 'Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine' — in any settlement located within 25 km of Borova (49.37°N, 37.62°E) along the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna axis that was not already shaded under those categories as of 2025-11-27. The new shading must persist through at least one full subsequent ISW daily update cycle. Qualifying settlements include but are not limited to: Petropavlivka, Kolisnykivka, Kruhliakivka, Pishchane, Dvorichna, Kupyansk-Vuzlovyi, Kindrashivka, or any other settlement within that 25 km radius. If the ISW map becomes unavailable, DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used as an alternative. This question resolves No if no such new gains are reflected by 2025-12-21.
subquestions.rationale: Borova is located on the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna front line, and any Russian entry into Borova would almost certainly be preceded by advances in nearby settlements along this axis. Tracking whether Russia makes new territorial gains within 25 km of Borova in the weeks before the ultimate question's deadline provides a meaningful leading indicator. If Russian forces are actively capturing settlements near Borova, the probability of them reaching Borova itself by December 31 increases significantly. Conversely, if the front remains static or Ukraine is successfully defending, it becomes very unlikely Russia would reach Borova. This subquestion measures the operational momentum on the specific front relevant to Borova, rather than simply asking about Borova itself with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Ukraine and Russia announce the start of formal, direct bilateral peace negotiations (or negotiations mediated by a third party with both sides at the table) between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
For Ukraine to agree to cede territory to Russia by end of 2025, a necessary precursor is that some form of structured negotiations between the two sides must be underway or announced. As of late September 2025, no formal bilateral peace talks have been announced. Diplomatic activity has been intense but indirect: the US has been engaging Russia and Ukraine separately, European allies held a 26-nation meeting in Paris on September 4, 2025, to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine (https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine), and various proposals for territorial arrangements have been floated in the media. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy reversed his earlier openness to ceding Russian-held territory in late September 2025, stating 'We will never recognize these territories that are temporarily occupied by Russia' (https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/). Russia has maintained maximalist demands, insisting Ukraine cede five regions and halt mobilization (https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70507839). The Kremlin has also signaled interest in claiming Odesa and Mykolaiv regions based on a map seen in a briefing by General Staff chief Valery Gerasimov in August 2025 (https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine). Without formal negotiations beginning, a territorial agreement by year-end is essentially impossible.

Sources:
- Telangana Today: https://www.telanganatoday.com/russia-has-provided-fresh-evidence-of-its-territorial-ambitions-in-ukraine
- Deutsche Welle: https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-which-territorial-concessions-are-being-discussed/a-70507839
- InfoWars (Zelensky reversal): https://www.infowars.com/posts/zelensky-flip-flops-will-not-cede-territory-to-russia/
- Investing.com (peace plan): https://za.investing.com/news/world-news/ukraine-may-cede-russianheld-territory-in-peace-plan--telegraph-93CH-3873457
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Ukraine and Russia publicly announce or confirm that they have agreed to begin formal bilateral peace negotiations (either direct talks or talks mediated by a third party such as the US, Turkey, or another country, where both Ukrainian and Russian delegations participate or are confirmed to participate in the same structured negotiation process). The announcement must come from official Ukrainian and/or Russian government sources, or be confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, AFP). Informal back-channel communications, shuttle diplomacy where a mediator meets each side separately, or unilateral statements of willingness to negotiate do not count. The negotiations need not have actually commenced by October 31 — a confirmed, mutual announcement that formal talks will take place is sufficient. If no such announcement is made by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
- AP News: https://apnews.com
- BBC News: https://www.bbc.com/news
- Official Ukrainian Presidential website: https://www.president.gov.ua/en
- Kremlin official website: http://en.kremlin.ru
subquestions.rationale: Formal bilateral negotiations are a necessary precondition for any territorial agreement by end of 2025. If no structured talks are announced or confirmed in October, it becomes extremely unlikely that Ukraine would agree to cede territory within the remaining two months of the year, given the complexity of such negotiations and the need for constitutional/political processes on the Ukrainian side. Conversely, if formal talks are announced, it would significantly raise the probability of a deal — or at least a framework agreement — by year-end. This subquestion is a strong leading indicator because it tracks a concrete, observable precursor event rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. Two forecasters who disagree on whether Ukraine will cede territory by year-end are very likely to update their positions based on whether formal negotiations have been announced.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) report that 2025's global average temperature anomaly (relative to 1991–2020) is higher than 2023's when it publishes its annual climate summary in January 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) typically publishes its annual global climate summary in early January of the following year. As of the January-to-November 2025 data, C3S reported that 2025 is currently tied with 2023 as the second-warmest year on record, with a global average temperature anomaly of 0.60°C above the 1991–2020 average (https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-2025-track-be-second-or-third-warmest-year-record). For context, 2023's full-year anomaly was 0.60°C and 2024's was 0.72°C above the 1991–2020 average according to C3S. Whether December 2025 tips the annual average above or below 2023's level will determine whether 2025 finishes as the second- or third-warmest year. This is a leading indicator because C3S data and NASA GISS data are highly correlated but C3S publishes its annual result earlier (typically in the first week of January). If C3S ranks 2025 above 2023, it strongly suggests NASA GISS will also rank 2025 as second-warmest.

Sources:
- Copernicus Climate Change Service, December 2025 bulletin: https://climate.copernicus.eu/copernicus-2025-track-be-second-or-third-warmest-year-record
- News18 reporting on C3S data (Dec 9, 2025): https://www.news18.com/world/2025-set-to-become-2nd-or-3rd-warmest-year-on-record-copernicus-9167955.html
- MoneyControl (Dec 10, 2025): https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/world/european-scientists-warn-2025-may-rank-second-or-third-hottest-year-in-history-12890095.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) publishes its official annual global climate summary for 2025 (typically available at https://climate.copernicus.eu/global-climate-highlights or their monthly/annual bulletin pages) and reports that the 2025 full-year global average surface air temperature anomaly relative to the 1991–2020 baseline is strictly greater than the corresponding 2023 full-year anomaly (which was 0.60°C). If C3S reports 2025 as exactly equal to 2023's anomaly (to the reported precision), this resolves No. If C3S does not publish the full-year 2025 summary by 2026-01-11, this question resolves as ambiguous/N/A.

Primary source: Copernicus Climate Change Service annual bulletin at https://climate.copernicus.eu/global-climate-highlights
Alternative: C3S press releases or data pages at https://climate.copernicus.eu/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether 2025 will be the second-hottest year on record per NASA GISS. The C3S annual summary, published in early January (before NASA GISS typically releases its data in mid-January), uses an independent but highly correlated temperature dataset. Whether C3S ranks 2025 above 2023 is a strong leading indicator of whether NASA GISS will also rank 2025 as second-warmest. As of November 2025, 2025 and 2023 are essentially tied in the C3S dataset, making this a genuinely uncertain indicator question (not near 0 or 1 probability). If 2025 edges out 2023 in C3S data, it substantially increases confidence that 2025 will be second-hottest in NASA GISS as well; if it doesn't, 2025 may end up third.

question: Will Trump talk to Nicolás Maduro by December 31?
