Kallas indicated that concrete measures would be proposed the following week (early September 2025). The next formal EU Foreign Affairs Council meeting is expected in mid-September 2025, which would be the earliest opportunity for a formal decision.

Sources:
- Euronews, 'EU Member States divided over Gaza at their Copenhagen meeting' (2025-08-30): https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/08/30/eu-member-states-divided-over-gaza-at-their-copenhagen-meeting
- Europa press remarks by Kaja Kallas (2025-08-30): https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/informal-meeting-foreign-affairs-ministers-press-remarks-high-representative-kaja-kallas-after_en
- Anadolu Agency, 'EU prepares sanctions options as pressure on Israel grows' (2025-07-05): https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-prepares-sanctions-options-as-pressure-on-israel-grows/3388123
- Euractiv, 'EU to Examine Possible Measures Against Israel Over Gaza Situation' (2025-07-06): https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/eu-to-examine-possible-measures-against-israel-over-gaza-situation/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive), the Council of the European Union (Foreign Affairs Council or European Council) formally adopts a legal act imposing sanctions that directly target the Israeli state, Israeli government members, or Israeli military officials. 'Formally adopts' means a Council Decision or Regulation is published in the Official Journal of the European Union or announced via an official EU Council press release. Sanctions targeting only individual settlers or non-governmental entities do not count — the sanctions must target the Israeli government, its members, or Israeli military officials in their official capacity. If no such formal adoption occurs by 2025-10-03, the question resolves No. The primary resolution sources are: (1) the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html), (2) the EU Council's press releases page (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/), and (3) a consensus of credible international media reporting.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion directly tracks whether the EU can overcome its internal divisions and move from discussion to formal adoption of sanctions against Israel within the next month. The key obstacle to the ultimate question resolving Yes is the unanimity requirement for CFSP sanctions and the known opposition from Germany and Hungary. If the EU manages to adopt formal sanctions by early October — just weeks after Kallas promised 'concrete measures' — it would be a very strong indicator that the ultimate question resolves Yes. Conversely, if no formal decision is reached by October 3 despite the momentum from late August, it suggests the divisions are too deep for action by year-end, making the ultimate question more likely to resolve No. This subquestion captures the critical near-term decision point without merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, as it focuses specifically on the formal Council adoption process rather than the broader category of any EU sanctions action.

question: Trump eliminates capital gains tax on crypto in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to eliminate capital gains tax on any cryptocurrency assets by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If capital gains is eliminated only for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any member of Congress formally introduce a standalone bill or amendment specifically to eliminate or substantially reduce federal capital gains tax on cryptocurrency between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks whether Trump will eliminate capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025. For this to happen, a bill or amendment would need to be introduced, pass both chambers of Congress, and be signed by the President — or Trump would need to take executive action. As of late 2025, no such legislation has been enacted. The closest legislative effort was a 'Hail Mary' push in late June 2025 to include a crypto tax exemption (specifically a de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions) in Trump's 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB), but a full elimination of capital gains tax on crypto was not part of that effort (Decrypt, June 30, 2025: https://decrypt.co/news-flash/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption). The GENIUS Act, signed into law on July 18, 2025, regulated stablecoins but did not address capital gains taxation (Invezz, July 18, 2025: https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/). Trump's executive actions so far have focused on regulatory frameworks, strategic crypto reserves, and 401(k) access for crypto — none have addressed capital gains tax elimination (ValueWalk, August 8, 2025: https://www.valuewalk.com/trump-signs-order-to-broaden-access-to-crypto-private-equity-in-401ks/). A de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions has been discussed but is distinct from a full elimination of capital gains tax. For a full elimination to occur by year-end, legislative activity would need to materialize very quickly. Tracking whether any bill or amendment is formally introduced in October is a meaningful leading indicator.

Sources:
- Decrypt (June 30, 2025): https://decrypt.co/news-flash/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption
- Invezz (July 18, 2025): https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/
- ValueWalk (August 8, 2025): https://www.valuewalk.com/trump-signs-order-to-broaden-access-to-crypto-private-equity-in-401ks/
- Crowdfund Insider (July 29, 2025): https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/07/crypto-policy-under-the-trump-administration-could-enhance-adoption-of-digital-assets-analysis/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), at least one member of the U.S. Congress (House or Senate) formally introduces a standalone bill or floor amendment that specifically proposes to eliminate federal capital gains tax on cryptocurrency assets (either all crypto or a defined subset such as Bitcoin), as recorded in the Congressional Record or on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). A 'de minimis' exemption for small transactions does NOT count unless it effectively eliminates capital gains tax on all crypto transactions regardless of size. The bill or amendment must be formally introduced (i.e., assigned a bill number or recorded as a filed amendment); mere public statements of intent, press releases, or draft proposals without formal introduction do not qualify. If Congress.gov is unavailable, resolution may rely on official records from the House Clerk (https://clerk.house.gov/) or Senate (https://www.senate.gov/) or a consensus of at least three credible news sources (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, Politico, CoinDesk). This question resolves No if no such bill or amendment is formally introduced during the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: For Trump to eliminate capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025, either Congress must pass legislation or Trump must take executive action. Executive action to change tax law faces severe legal constraints (the taxing power belongs to Congress), making legislation the most plausible path. If no bill or amendment is even introduced in October 2025, the legislative timeline to pass such a major tax change through both chambers by year-end becomes extremely compressed — making the ultimate question's resolution as 'Yes' very unlikely. Conversely, if a bill is introduced with apparent momentum, it would significantly update the probability upward. This subquestion tracks a necessary precursor to the legislative path without simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla receive a Texas Department of Motor Vehicles permit to operate autonomous vehicles without a human driver by September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Texas House Bill 4500, signed by Governor Greg Abbott on June 22, 2025, requires autonomous vehicle operators to obtain a permit from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) before operating self-driving vehicles on public streets without a human driver. This law takes effect on September 1, 2025. Tesla currently operates a limited robotaxi trial in Austin, Texas, with 'safety monitors' riding in the front passenger seat — meaning the service does not qualify as fully driverless. For Tesla to launch a truly driverless robotaxi service (as defined by the ultimate question), it would need to operate without a safety driver or monitor actively positioned to control the vehicle. In Texas, this now requires a TxDMV permit under the new law. Whether Tesla applies for and receives this permit in the first week of September is a critical gating factor for any driverless launch in Austin.

Sources:
- CNA: "Texas enacts robotaxi rules on the eve of Tesla's Austin rollout" (2025-06-22) https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-teslas-austin-rollout-5191171
- The Express Tribune: "Tesla's robotaxi won't be driverless, set to launch with 'human monitors'" (2025-06-21) https://tribune.com.pk/story/2539123/teslas-robotaxi-wont-be-driverless-set-to-launch-with-human-monitors
- TechRadar: "I'm not buying the Tesla robotaxi hype" (2025-06-23) https://www.techradar.com/vehicle-tech/hybrid-electric-vehicles/im-not-buying-the-tesla-robotaxi-hype-heres-why-its-still-miles-behind-waymo
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between September 1, 2025, and September 8, 2025 (inclusive), credible reporting or an official announcement from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles confirms that Tesla has been granted a permit under Texas HB 4500 (or equivalent regulation effective September 1, 2025) to operate autonomous vehicles on public roads without a human driver present or actively controlling the vehicle. The permit must specifically authorize operation without a safety driver in the driver's seat. Sources for resolution include official TxDMV announcements (https://www.txdmv.gov/), Tesla's official communications, or a consensus of credible news reporting from outlets such as Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, or major automotive/technology news sources. If no such permit is confirmed by September 8, 2025, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The Texas autonomous vehicle permit law (HB 4500) takes effect on September 1, 2025 — the exact start of our resolution window. Tesla's Austin robotaxi trial has been its most advanced public-facing service, but it currently operates with human safety monitors. For Tesla to launch a truly driverless robotaxi service (as required by the ultimate question), obtaining a Texas permit is a necessary regulatory prerequisite for its Austin operations. If Tesla does not secure this permit in the first week of September, it is extremely unlikely to launch a fully driverless service anywhere by September 11. Conversely, if Tesla does obtain the permit, it signals serious regulatory progress toward a driverless launch. This is a concrete, observable regulatory milestone that serves as a strong early indicator.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass at least two 'minibus' spending packages (collections of full-year appropriations bills) between January 9, 2026 and January 24, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Congress faces a January 30, 2026 deadline to fund the nine remaining federal agencies operating under a stopgap continuing resolution. A failure to pass spending bills by that date would trigger a partial government shutdown. As of early January 2026, House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole (R-OK) announced a plan to pass the remaining nine bills in three 'minibus' packages, one per week in January. The first package—covering Commerce, Justice, Science, Energy & Water, and Interior & EPA—was unveiled on January 6 and a House floor vote was expected around January 9, 2026. Two additional packages covering the remaining six bills (Defense, Labor-HHS-Education, Transportation-HUD, Financial Services, Legislative Branch, and State-Foreign Operations) would need to follow in rapid succession.

The House Republican majority is extremely narrow (Speaker Johnson has only a two-vote margin after Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene's early retirement), making passage of each package uncertain. House conservatives like Rep. Chip Roy (R-TX) are insisting on flat or reduced spending, while some bills—particularly foreign aid and DHS—are politically contentious. Senate Democrats also retain leverage due to the 60-vote threshold in the Senate.

Polymarket odds of a shutdown by January 31 dropped from ~40% in mid-December to ~28% by January 3, suggesting growing but incomplete confidence that Congress will avoid a shutdown. Passing at least two of the three planned minibus packages through the House by January 24 would be a strong indicator that Congress is on track to avert a shutdown.

Sources:
- One America News Network, "Congress debuts $174B spending package as Jan. 30 govt shutdown deadline looms" (Jan 6, 2026): https://www.oann.com/newsroom/congress-debuts-174b-spending-package-as-jan-30-govt-shutdown-deadline-looms/
- NYMag, "Odds Are Dropping for a January Government Shutdown" (Jan 6, 2026): https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/odds-are-dropping-for-a-january-government-shutdown.html
- Agri-Pulse, "Washington Week Ahead: Congress returns amid uncertainty, mid-term politics" (Jan 4, 2026): https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/21500-washington-week-ahead-congress-returns-amid-uncertainty-mid-term-politics
- Washington Times, "Stalled spending bills put Congress in catch-up mode" (Dec 26, 2025): https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-catch-up-mode/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes (by recorded floor vote) at least two separate minibus or omnibus spending packages containing full-year fiscal year 2026 appropriations bills between January 9, 2026 and January 24, 2026 (inclusive). A 'minibus' is defined as a legislative package combining two or more of the twelve annual appropriations bills into a single measure for floor consideration. Passage of a single appropriations bill standing alone does not count as a 'minibus' unless it is bundled with at least one other appropriations bill. Passage of a continuing resolution or stopgap measure does not count. Resolution will be determined by the official roll call vote records published by the Office of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes). If the House passes only one minibus package, or passes none, by January 24, 2026, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is a conjunction: no shutdown by January 31 AND Republicans win the House in 2026. The shutdown component is the near-term uncertainty. The House's ability to pass multiple spending packages in quick succession is a leading indicator of whether Congress can meet the January 30 deadline and avoid a shutdown. If the House fails to pass at least two packages by January 24, there is very little time to conference with the Senate and get bills signed, making a partial shutdown much more likely. Additionally, Republican ability to govern effectively and pass spending bills with their narrow majority is relevant to their brand heading into the 2026 midterms — repeated dysfunction or shutdowns could hurt Republican House candidates. This subquestion thus provides evidence for both components of the ultimate question.

question: Negative GDP growth in Q4 2025?
description:
"This market will resolve to 'Yes' if the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP 'Advance Estimate' for Q4 2025, scheduled for release by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on January 29, 2026, reports a growth rate below 0. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'.

The GDP release will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Advance Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered."

subquestions.question: Will the ISM Manufacturing PMI for October 2025 (released in early November 2025) be below 50?
subquestions.background_information:
The ISM Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) is a widely watched leading indicator of economic activity. A reading below 50 indicates contraction in the manufacturing sector, while a reading above 50 indicates expansion. Manufacturing weakness in Q4 2025 would be an early signal of broader economic softness that could contribute to negative GDP growth.

As of recent months, U.S. manufacturing has been mixed. The ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2025 came in at 47.2, indicating continued contraction in the manufacturing sector. The index has been below 50 for most of the past two years, though it briefly touched expansion territory earlier in 2025. Tariff-related uncertainty and front-loading of imports in Q1 2025 (which depressed Q1 GDP) have created volatile economic conditions. The October reading, covering the first month of Q4 2025, provides an early signal about Q4 economic momentum.

Sources:
- ISM Manufacturing Report on Business: https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-report-on-business/pmi/
- Trading Economics ISM Manufacturing PMI: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/business-confidence
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the ISM Manufacturing PMI for October 2025, as published by the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-29, reports a headline PMI reading below 50.0. The October 2025 ISM Manufacturing Report on Business is scheduled for release on November 3, 2025. The resolution will use the first published headline PMI figure from the ISM's official report, available at https://www.ismworld.org/supply-management-news-and-reports/reports/ism-report-on-business/pmi/. If the ISM report is delayed beyond 2025-11-29, this question resolves as ambiguous. Only the initial release is used; subsequent revisions are not considered.
subquestions.rationale: The ISM Manufacturing PMI is a key leading indicator of economic activity and is released at the start of Q4 2025. A reading below 50 signals manufacturing contraction, which would be an early warning sign for potential negative GDP growth in Q4 2025. Manufacturing has been weak for much of the tariff period, and continued contraction would increase the likelihood of overall GDP contraction. Conversely, a reading above 50 would suggest the economy has some underlying strength heading into Q4, making negative GDP growth less likely. This is a concrete, early-in-the-quarter indicator that forecasters who disagree about Q4 GDP might update on differently.

question: Will Russia capture Pokrovsk train station by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the Pokrovsk train station (48.284816377539386, 37.180016843748454) by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The train station will be considered captured if any part of the train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by October 31, 2025, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces advance to within 5 km of Pokrovsk city center (as measured from coordinate 48.2848°N, 37.1800°E) according to the ISW map by October 18, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Pokrovsk is a key logistics hub in Donetsk Oblast, and its train station (at 48.2848°N, 37.1800°E) is near the city center. As of late September 2025, Russian forces have reached the outskirts of Pokrovsk but have failed to secure the city itself. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported that Russian forces reached the approaches to Pokrovsk but the advance stalled, and a Ukrainian counteroffensive in the Dobropillia area partially rolled back Russian gains in the region. According to ISW's September 17, 2025 assessment, Russia has not captured any major Ukrainian city during the summer 2025 offensive, and the Pokrovsk axis remains one of the most intense battle zones. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated on September 20, 2025, that Russian propaganda claims about capturing Pokrovsk and the east by November are false, and that about 330 km of territory in the Dobropillia-Pokrovsk area remains under Ukrainian control. Reports from early September noted Russia redeployed marines and paratroopers from Sumy to Donetsk, possibly preparing a renewed push toward Pokrovsk. The closest confirmed Russian positions to the train station are approximately 7-10 km to the south and southeast, based on ISW and DeepState maps from late September 2025.

Sources:
- ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
- DeepState Map: https://deepstatemap.live/
- The Moscow Times, "Russia Inflates Battlefield Gains After a Costly Summer Offensive" (Sep 17, 2025): https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive
- Al Jazeera, "Ukraine knocks out Russian refineries as Russia kills dozens in Kyiv" (Sep 4, 2025): https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/4/ukraine-knocks-out-russian-refineries-as-russia-kills-dozens-in-kyiv
- Ukrainska Pravda, "Zelenskyy: Seized maps show Russians deceive their own command" (Sep 20, 2025): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/20/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive), the ISW interactive Ukraine map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shows Russian-controlled territory (shaded red) within 5 km of the Pokrovsk train station at coordinates 48.2848°N, 37.1800°E. The 5 km distance is measured from the nearest edge of any red-shaded area to the train station coordinates. If the ISW map is unavailable, the DeepState Map (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as a fallback. The question resolves No if no red-shaded Russian-controlled territory comes within 5 km of the train station coordinates on either map during the resolution window. Temporary map glitches lasting less than 24 hours do not count. The measurement should be based on the closest point of contiguous Russian-controlled territory (not isolated pockets or errors).
subquestions.rationale: Capturing the Pokrovsk train station requires Russian forces to first close the remaining distance to the city center. If Russian forces cannot advance to within 5 km of the train station by October 18, it is extremely unlikely they could capture the station itself by October 24-31. This subquestion tracks a necessary precondition — geographic proximity — rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. The current front line is roughly 7-10 km from the station, so a 5 km threshold represents meaningful but not complete progress. Forecasters who disagree on whether Russia will capture the station would likely update significantly based on whether Russia can even close to within 5 km, as the rate of advance in urban/suburban areas near Pokrovsk has been very slow.

question: Brazil unemployment below 6.3% for Q4 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Brazil's unemployment rate for Q4 2025 is below 6.3% when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve according to IBGE's (https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego) public release of the Q4 2025 figure unemployment, expected in January 2026. If the publication of this figure is delayed beyond February 28, 2026 ET, this market will resolve according to the last published figure. 

Because this market's resolution source reports quarterly unemployment to one decimal point (e.g. 4.5%), this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will IBGE's monthly PNAD Contínua release published in October 2025 report a three-month moving average unemployment rate of 6.0% or below for the quarter ending in August 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Brazil's unemployment rate has been on a sustained downward trend in 2025. The IBGE publishes monthly releases of the PNAD Contínua (Continuous National Household Survey), which reports a rolling three-month average unemployment rate. The most recent data (for the May–July 2025 quarter) showed unemployment at 6.2%, a record low for the series that began in 2012. In July 2025 alone, the monthly rate was estimated at 5.6%. Analyst Bruno Imaizumi of 4intelligence projected unemployment would fall to 5.5% in August 2025 (https://exame.com/economia/brasil-atinge-pleno-emprego-com-baixa-informalidade-e-renda-recorde-do-trabalhador/). The next PNAD Contínua release, expected around late October 2025, will cover the June–August 2025 quarter. If the rolling three-month average drops to 6.0% or below, it would strongly suggest that Q4 2025 (October–December) unemployment — which historically benefits from seasonal hiring — will come in below 6.3%.

Historically, Q4 unemployment in Brazil tends to be lower than Q2 and Q3 because of end-of-year hiring in retail, services, and agriculture. In Q4 2024, unemployment reached 6.2%. Given that 2025 has consistently posted lower unemployment than the equivalent periods in 2024, a June–August 2025 reading at or below 6.0% would be a strong leading indicator that Q4 2025 unemployment will be below 6.3%.

Sources:
- IBGE PNAD Contínua indicators page: https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego
- Agência Brasil, "Unemployment Falls to 5.6%": https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-09/unemployment-falls-56-lowest-2012-shows-ibge
- Exame, "Brazil reaches full employment": https://exame.com/economia/brasil-atinge-pleno-emprego-com-baixa-informalidade-e-renda-recorde-do-trabalhador/
- Agência Brasil, "Brazil's unemployment falls to 5.8%": https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-08/brazils-unemployment-falls-58-lowest-record
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, IBGE publishes its PNAD Contínua monthly release covering the June–August 2025 quarter and the reported unemployment rate is 6.0% or below (to one decimal place). This question resolves No if the reported rate is 6.1% or higher. If IBGE does not publish the June–August 2025 quarter data by 2025-10-31 (e.g., due to technical delays like the 18-day delay experienced in September 2025), this question resolves No. The resolution source is IBGE's official PNAD Contínua release available at https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego.
subquestions.rationale: The June–August 2025 rolling unemployment figure is the most recent pre-Q4 data point and serves as a direct leading indicator for Q4 2025 unemployment. Brazil's labor market has been on a strong downward trajectory, and the June–August figure will capture the momentum heading into the Q4 period. If the three-month average is already at or below 6.0%, the seasonal Q4 hiring effect (retail, services, year-end agriculture) makes it very likely that Q4 2025 unemployment will be well below 6.3%. Conversely, if the figure stalls above 6.0%, it would indicate the labor market's momentum may be fading, making sub-6.3% Q4 unemployment less certain. This question is a genuine leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question, since it measures a different time period and the relationship between mid-year and Q4 unemployment involves seasonal dynamics.

question: Will Trump pardon Sam Bankman-Fried in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual receives a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from Donald Trump by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for whether the individual is pardoned or not will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Sam Bankman-Fried's parents or legal representatives publicly confirm direct communication with the Trump White House or Trump's pardon office regarding clemency for SBF between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Sam Bankman-Fried is serving a 25-year prison sentence after being convicted in 2023 on seven felony counts related to the collapse of the FTX cryptocurrency exchange. His parents, Stanford Law professors Joseph Bankman and Barbara Fried, have reportedly been actively seeking a presidential pardon from President Donald Trump. According to multiple reports from mid-2025, SBF's parents have been consulting with legal experts and individuals connected to Trump's inner circle about obtaining clemency (Coinspeaker, May 2025: https://www.coinspeaker.com/ftx-founder-sam-bankman-fried-to-leave-jail-earlier/; Decrypt, May 2025: https://decrypt.co/resources/which-crypto-founders-are-seeking-pardons-from-president-trump). Trump has already pardoned several crypto-related figures, including Ross Ulbricht (Silk Road founder) and BitMEX co-founders, establishing a precedent that some crypto offenders may receive executive clemency (Forbes, May 2025: https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons-and-commutations/). SBF's appeal is scheduled for oral arguments on November 4, 2025, before the Second Circuit Court of Appeals (Cointelegraph, Sept 2025: https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-court-to-hear-arguments-for-sam-bankman-fried-s-appeal-on-nov-4). The existence and formality of pardon discussions with the Trump administration would be a strong early indicator of whether a pardon is forthcoming in 2025.

Sources:
- Coinspeaker (May 2025): https://www.coinspeaker.com/ftx-founder-sam-bankman-fried-to-leave-jail-earlier/
- Decrypt (May 2025): https://decrypt.co/resources/which-crypto-founders-are-seeking-pardons-from-president-trump
- Forbes (May 2025): https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons-and-commutations/
- Cointelegraph (Sept 2025): https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-court-to-hear-arguments-for-sam-bankman-fried-s-appeal-on-nov-4
- The Financial Express (July 2025): https://www.financialexpress.com/life/technology/sam-bankman-fried-pardoned-by-donald-trump-who-he-is-and-what-did-he-do/3969384/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), any of the following individuals — Joseph Bankman, Barbara Fried, or an attorney publicly identified as representing Sam Bankman-Fried in pardon/clemency matters — publicly confirm (via on-the-record statements to credible news outlets, court filings, social media posts, or press releases) that they have had direct communication with the Trump White House, the Office of the Pardon Attorney, or officials acting on behalf of President Trump specifically regarding clemency (pardon, commutation, or reprieve) for Sam Bankman-Fried. 'Direct communication' means actual exchanges (meetings, calls, written correspondence, or formal submissions) — not merely consulting with intermediaries or 'people close to Trump's inner circles.' Reports based solely on anonymous sources do not count; the confirmation must come from an on-the-record statement by one of the named parties or their identified legal representative. Resolution will be based on reporting from major credible outlets such as the New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com), Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), or the White House official website (https://www.whitehouse.gov). If no such public confirmation is reported by October 31, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Whether SBF receives a Trump pardon in 2025 depends critically on whether his family and legal team have established meaningful, direct contact with the Trump administration about clemency. As of mid-2025, reports indicate pardon-seeking efforts are underway but remain at the level of consulting intermediaries. Confirmation of direct White House engagement would be a strong signal that a pardon is being seriously considered, while the absence of such contact would suggest a pardon is unlikely in the near term. This subquestion is especially relevant because SBF's appeal hearing is on November 4 — the Trump administration's posture on clemency before the appeal would be highly informative about whether a pardon is forthcoming by year-end.

question: Will Claude 5 be released by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Anthropic's Claude 5 model is made available to the general public by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Claude 5 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Anthropic as being accessible to the general public.

Claude 5 refers to a product explicitly named Claude 5 (e.g. Claude 5.0 would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Claude 4, similar to the progression from Claude 2 to Claude 3. Products labeled as Claude 4.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Anthropic, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Anthropic publicly announce or release a model explicitly named 'Claude 5' or describe a model as the successor to Claude 4 (not Claude 4.5) between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4.5 on September 29, 2025, less than two months after Claude Opus 4.1. The company has been on a rapid release cadence, with multiple model updates within the Claude 4 family (Sonnet 4, Opus 4, Opus 4.1, and now Sonnet 4.5). However, no Claude 5 model has been announced or even hinted at in public communications. The naming convention suggests Anthropic is still iterating within the Claude 4 generation. TechCrunch noted that 'the rapid release cycle—Claude Sonnet 4.5 launches less than two months after Claude Opus 4.1—makes it difficult for any firm to maintain a lasting lead in the competitive AI market.' For Anthropic to release Claude 5 by December 31, 2025, some kind of announcement, teaser, or pre-release signal would very likely need to appear by October 2025, given that major model launches typically involve advance notice, safety evaluations, and staged rollouts.

Sources:
- TechCrunch: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 4.5: https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/29/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-its-best-ai-model-for-coding/
- Anthropic blog (Claude Sonnet 4.5 announcement): https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-4-5
- Analytics India Magazine: https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-touts-it-as-best-coding-model-in-the-world/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), Anthropic makes any official public announcement—via blog post, press release, social media, or official website—that explicitly references a model named 'Claude 5' (e.g., Claude 5, Claude 5.0, Claude 5 Sonnet, Claude 5 Opus) or describes a forthcoming model as the next generation successor to the Claude 4 family (i.e., not a Claude 4.x variant). The announcement does not need to constitute a full public release; it can be a teaser, preview announcement, or confirmation of an upcoming release. Models labeled Claude 4.5, Claude 4.6, or any other Claude 4.x variant do not count. The primary resolution source will be Anthropic's official blog at https://www.anthropic.com/news and their official X/Twitter account at https://x.com/AnthropicAI. Secondary sources include credible tech news outlets such as TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com), The Verge (https://www.theverge.com), and Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com). If Anthropic's blog is unavailable, a consensus of at least two credible news outlets reporting the announcement will suffice.
subquestions.rationale: For Claude 5 to be publicly released by December 31, 2025, Anthropic would almost certainly need to announce or signal the model's existence well in advance. Major frontier model releases involve safety evaluations, red-teaming, and staged rollouts that typically span weeks to months. If no announcement or reference to Claude 5 appears by the end of October, it becomes significantly less likely that a full public release could occur within the remaining two months of 2025. Conversely, if Anthropic does announce Claude 5 in October, this would be a very strong positive indicator. This subquestion captures an early, observable signal that is distinct from the ultimate question (which requires a full public release) while being highly informative about its likelihood.

question: Will Russia capture Huliaipole by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will Russian forces capture or contest (grey zone or Russian-controlled) the village of Nove in Zaporizhzhia Oblast by December 15, 2025, according to DeepState map?
subquestions.background_information:
Huliaipole is a key city in Zaporizhzhia Oblast that Russian forces have been advancing toward from multiple directions. As of mid-November 2025, Russian forces have captured several villages north and northeast of Huliaipole, including Rivnopillia (~10 km north), Uspenivka, Solodke, and Pryvilne. DeepState reported on November 10 that Russian forces were actively advancing toward the villages of Nove and Novouspenivske, which lie along the northern approach corridor to Huliaipole. The Finnish OSINT group Black Bird assessed that Russia may attempt to flank Huliaipole from the north while pinning down Ukrainian defenders from the east and south. Nove is a settlement situated between the recently captured Rivnopillia and Huliaipole, making it a critical waypoint on the northern approach. If Russian forces capture or contest Nove, it would indicate that the advance toward Huliaipole is continuing at a pace that could threaten the city itself before year-end. Conversely, if Ukrainian forces hold Nove, it would suggest the advance has stalled, making capture of Huliaipole by December 31 much less likely. As of November 22, 2025, Nove appears to remain under Ukrainian control but is under active pressure from advancing Russian forces.

Sources:
- Українська правда, 'DeepState Reports Worsening Situation in Zaporizhzhia Oblast' (Nov 10, 2025): https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/
- Kyiv Independent, 'Russia likely captured over 15 villages in Zaporizhzhia Oblast since September' (Nov 22, 2025): https://kyivindependent.com/russia-likely-captured-over-15-villages-in-zaporizhzhia-oblast-since-september-osint-group-says/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-23 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive), the village of Nove (Zaporizhzhia Oblast, located between Rivnopillia and Huliaipole on the northern approach) is shown as either Russian-controlled (red shading) or within a grey zone (contested area) on the DeepState map (https://deepstatemap.live/) at any point during this window. The village of Nove can be identified on DeepState map at approximate coordinates 47.65°N, 36.22°E, situated south of Rivnopillia and north of Huliaipole. If the DeepState map shows the settlement as fully Ukrainian-controlled (no red or grey shading covering the settlement itself) throughout the entire resolution window, this question resolves No. If DeepState map becomes permanently unavailable, the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) may be used as an alternative, with equivalent criteria (any Russian presence or contested shading over Nove). Temporary map glitches are excluded.
subquestions.rationale: Nove lies directly on the northern approach corridor to Huliaipole, between the recently captured Rivnopillia and Huliaipole itself. Russian capture or contestation of Nove would be a strong leading indicator that the advance toward Huliaipole is proceeding at a pace consistent with potentially reaching the city center by December 31. If Nove remains firmly in Ukrainian hands through mid-December, it would suggest the Russian advance has stalled well short of Huliaipole, making capture of the city's central intersection highly unlikely within the ultimate question's timeframe. This is a meaningfully different question from the ultimate question because it asks about an intermediate waypoint rather than the city itself, and it resolves earlier, providing an actionable signal.

question: Will Azerbaijan join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed country formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Azerbaijan and Israel issue a joint official statement or communiqué announcing progress toward Azerbaijan joining the Abraham Accords between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Azerbaijan and Israel have long maintained close diplomatic, military, and economic ties, even though Azerbaijan has not formally joined the Abraham Accords. In August 2025, US Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed the US was 'negotiating multiple entries' of countries into the Abraham Accords, with Azerbaijan specifically named as a candidate (https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/404378). On August 7, 2025, Armenia and Azerbaijan signed a US-brokered peace framework at the White House, which US officials described as a potential gateway for Azerbaijan to join the Abraham Accords (https://en.amwalalghad.com/armenia-azerbaijan-to-sign-us-brokered-peace-deal-granting-us-exclusive-corridor-rights/). President Trump explicitly called for Middle Eastern countries to join the Accords in August 2025 (https://www.dawn.com/news/1853449). A News Ghana opinion piece from September 18, 2025, described a scenario in which Saudi Arabia and Azerbaijan join the Accords as part of a broader regional realignment (https://newsghana.com.gh/the-big-bang-in-the-middle-east-new-peace-agreements-changing-the-rules-of-the-game-saudi-arabia-syria-and-lebanon/). However, regional complications—including Israel's September 2025 airstrikes on Qatar and UAE warnings against West Bank annexation—may slow progress. As of October 1, 2025, no joint Azerbaijan-Israel statement on Abraham Accords accession has been made public.

Sources:
- Arutz Sheva: https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/404378
- Amwal Al Ghad: https://en.amwalalghad.com/armenia-azerbaijan-to-sign-us-brokered-peace-deal-granting-us-exclusive-corridor-rights/
- Dawn: https://www.dawn.com/news/1853449
- News Ghana: https://newsghana.com.gh/the-big-bang-in-the-middle-east-new-peace-agreements-changing-the-rules-of-the-game-saudi-arabia-syria-and-lebanon/
- Yahoo (Factbox): https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-what-are-abraham-accords-093416545.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025 (inclusive), the governments of Azerbaijan and Israel issue a joint official statement, communiqué, or memorandum of understanding that explicitly references Azerbaijan's progress toward joining or intent to join the Abraham Accords. The statement must be published or acknowledged on official government websites (e.g., the Azerbaijani Ministry of Foreign Affairs at https://www.mfa.gov.az/en or the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs at https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_foreign_affairs) or reported by at least two credible international news agencies (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP). A statement by only one side, or informal remarks by officials at press conferences without a corresponding formal document, does not count. If no such joint statement is issued by 11:59 PM UTC on October 31, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Azerbaijan to formally join the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, there would almost certainly need to be visible diplomatic momentum in October—joint statements, frameworks, or memoranda of understanding signaling imminent accession. This subquestion tracks whether the necessary precursor diplomatic activity is occurring in October. If no joint statement emerges in October, it becomes much less likely that a full formal signing could occur in the remaining two months of 2025. Conversely, a joint statement in October would be a strong leading indicator that formal accession is imminent.

question: Will Trump visit Gaza by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. President Donald Trump visits the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. Whether or not Trump enters the Gaza Strip's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on this market's resolution.

A visit to any area within the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip, including visits to buffer zones, counts.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, or official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government officially announce or confirm plans for Trump to visit Gaza before November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of mid-October 2025, Trump is actively engaged in Middle East peace diplomacy. On October 8, 2025, Trump publicly stated he might visit Gaza, saying 'I may go there sometime toward the end of the week' (https://www.lindaikejisblog.com/2025/10/i-might-visit-gaza-soon-us-president-donald-trump-declares.html). On October 11, 2025, Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff visited an IDF base in northern Gaza (https://www.newsweek.com/trumps-envoy-enters-gaza-israel-hamas-ceasefire-holds-2043567). Trump visited Israel on October 13, 2025, addressing the Knesset, and attended a peace ceremony in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt (https://dailypost.ng/2025/10/13/trump-visits-israel-egypt-for-gaza-peace-deal/). A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took hold on October 10-11, 2025, as the first phase of Trump's 20-point peace plan. While Trump has expressed interest in visiting Gaza, no official confirmation of such a visit has been made. The security, logistical, and political complexities of a sitting U.S. president entering an active or recently active conflict zone are enormous. The last U.S. presidential visit to Gaza was Bill Clinton's in 1998, under far more stable conditions.

Sources:
- Linda Ikeji Blog: https://www.lindaikejisblog.com/2025/10/i-might-visit-gaza-soon-us-president-donald-trump-declares.html
- Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/trumps-envoy-enters-gaza-israel-hamas-ceasefire-holds-2043567
- Daily Post Nigeria: https://dailypost.ng/2025/10/13/trump-visits-israel-egypt-for-gaza-peace-deal/
- TASS: https://tass.com/world/1890123
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive), the U.S. government, the White House, or Trump himself (via official statements, press briefings, or verified social media accounts such as https://twitter.com/POTUS or https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump) officially announces or confirms concrete plans for Trump to physically visit the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip, including specifying an approximate date or timeframe for such a visit. Vague statements of possibility (e.g., 'I might visit Gaza') do NOT count — the announcement must indicate a firm intention or scheduled plan. If no such official announcement or confirmation is made by 11:59 PM UTC on November 13, 2025, the question resolves No. Primary resolution sources include White House press briefings (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), Trump's verified social media accounts, and credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters, AP, BBC, CNN, Fox News).
subquestions.rationale: A confirmed, scheduled plan to visit Gaza is a necessary precursor to Trump actually visiting Gaza. If by mid-November there is no official announcement of such a visit, it becomes substantially less likely that Trump would visit Gaza by December 31, 2025, given the extensive advance planning required for a presidential visit to a conflict zone. Conversely, an official announcement would be a very strong signal that the visit will occur. This is a meaningful leading indicator that is distinct from the ultimate question — it asks about the announcement of plans, not the visit itself.

question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran formally notifies the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), pursuant to Article X of the treaty by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the Iranian government must issue an official written notice that explicitly states its intention to withdraw under Article X of the NPT.

The resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Iranian parliament (Majles) vote to approve a bill mandating Iran's withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 28–29, 2025, multiple credible sources reported that the Iranian parliament began drafting an emergency bill to withdraw from the NPT in response to the UK, France, and Germany formally activating the UN sanctions 'snapback' mechanism. Lawmaker Hossein Ali Haji Deligani announced that the three-part emergency plan — which also includes suspending nuclear negotiations with the US and E3, and ending IAEA monitoring cooperation — would be uploaded to the parliament's internal system on August 29 and placed on the agenda for open sessions the following week (i.e., early September 2025). Earlier, on August 13, lawmaker Manouchehr Mottaki had warned that parliament was 'ready to withdraw from the NPT should international sanctions be reimposed.' On August 20, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that while Iran planned to stay in the NPT, withdrawal was 'not ruled out' and could become a matter of formal discussion. However, it is important to note that under Iran's political system, parliamentary approval alone does not constitute a formal withdrawal from the NPT — that would require action by the executive branch (the president and/or Supreme Leader), and the actual NPT withdrawal process under Article X requires 90 days' notice to all parties and the UN Security Council. Thus, a parliamentary vote is a necessary precursor and strong indicator, but not identical to, a formal withdrawal.

Sources:
- Mehr News Agency, "Iran's parl. launches emergency plan to exit NPT" (2025-08-28): https://en.mehrnews.com
- Times of Israel, "Iranian lawmaker says Tehran will withdraw from Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty due to snapback sanctions" (2025-08-29): https://www.timesofisrael.com
- Anadolu Agency, "Iran says it may 'reach point of discussion' on withdrawing from nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty" (2025-08-20): https://www.aa.com.tr/en
- Middle East Monitor, "Iran drafts urgent bill to withdraw from nuclear treaty" (2025-08-29): https://www.middleeastmonitor.com
- Ynetnews, "Iran moves to exit nuclear treaty as Europe triggers UN sanctions snapback" (2025-08-29): https://www.ynetnews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the Iranian parliament (Islamic Consultative Assembly / Majles) holds a floor vote and passes (by simple majority or any required threshold) a bill or resolution that explicitly mandates, authorizes, or directs the Iranian government to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT). The vote must be reported by at least two credible English-language or Farsi-language news sources (e.g., Reuters, AP, AFP, Tasnim News Agency, IRNA, Mehr News Agency, Al Jazeera, BBC Persian). Preliminary committee approvals or drafts that have not yet received a full parliamentary floor vote do not count. If the bill is introduced but the vote is postponed beyond October 1, 2025, this question resolves No. Resolution sources include: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), Tasnim News Agency (https://www.tasnimnews.com/en), IRNA (https://en.irna.ir), Mehr News Agency (https://en.mehrnews.com), and Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).
subquestions.rationale: A parliamentary vote approving NPT withdrawal is the most significant observable precursor to Iran's formal withdrawal from the treaty. Under Iran's system, such a vote would create enormous political momentum and domestic legal authorization for the executive to issue the formal Article X notification. If this bill passes in September 2025, the probability of Iran formally notifying the UN of withdrawal before December 31, 2025 increases dramatically. Conversely, if the bill stalls, is watered down, or fails to reach a vote, it suggests that Iran's NPT withdrawal threats are more likely rhetorical or bargaining tactics rather than a committed course of action. This subquestion captures a concrete, near-term legislative event that is distinct from the ultimate question (which requires formal executive notification to the UN) but is a strong leading indicator of it.

question: Will less than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season?
description:
The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will take place over a period lasting from June 1 to November 30.

This market will resolve according to the number of storms NOAA names during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season.

Storms that form before the designated period but which are active during it will count towards this market's resolution.

If a number of storms exceeding a bracket's number are named within this market's timeframe, that bracket may immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be NOAA’s list of named storms during the Atlantic hurricane season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) and/or their data on individual storms.

If there is a potential named storm that has not yet been classified by Nov 30, 11:59 PM ET, the market may remain open until Dec 1, 12:00 PM ET to determine if a classification was made prior to midnight.

subquestions.question: Will at least one new named storm form in the Atlantic basin between October 1 and October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late September 2025, the Atlantic hurricane season has been relatively slow compared to preseason forecasts. NOAA predicted 13–19 named storms for 2025 (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov), and Colorado State University predicted 17 named storms (https://tropical.colostate.edu/). However, as of late August 2025, only a handful of named storms had formed, with Hurricane Erin being a notable early-season storm. The article from August 31, 2025, mentioned that only one storm (Erin) had formed up to that point, with the next name on the list being Gabrielle (the seventh name, implying six names had been allocated but not all necessarily became storms). October is historically an active month in the Atlantic basin — it is the second-most-active month after September. The climatological average is about 2 named storms forming in October. Given that the ultimate question asks whether fewer than 12 named storms will occur in the entire 2025 season, tracking whether new storms form in early October is a key indicator of whether the season's total will stay below 12.

Sources:
- NOAA 2025 Hurricane Season Outlook: https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/2025/noaa-predicts-above-normal-2025-atlantic-hurricane-season
- National Hurricane Center Active Storms: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/
- Colorado State University Tropical Forecast: https://tropical.colostate.edu/
- Historical October hurricane statistics: https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/climo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least one new tropical or subtropical storm is officially named by the National Hurricane Center (NHC) in the Atlantic basin between October 1, 2025 (00:00 UTC) and October 10, 2025 (23:59 UTC), inclusive. The storm must receive an official name from the NHC during this window; storms named before October 1 that are still active do not count. Resolution will be based on NHC advisories and the official list of named storms at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/ and storm-specific data at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/. If the NHC website is unavailable, alternative sources such as the Weather Prediction Center (https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/) or reliable secondary sources citing NHC data may be used.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether fewer than 12 named storms will form during the entire 2025 Atlantic hurricane season. October is historically the second-most-active month. If new storms form in early October, it increases the likelihood that the season total will reach or exceed 12, making it more likely the ultimate question resolves No. Conversely, if no storms form in early October, it suggests the season may remain quiet enough to stay below 12. This subquestion is a direct, near-term observable indicator — it doesn't simply restate the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, but rather asks about a specific period's storm formation activity that is highly informative for the season total.

question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration may declare a national housing emergency this fall to address high housing costs.(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) primarily addressing housing by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will a draft executive order or presidential memorandum on a national housing emergency be reported as circulating within the Trump administration by December 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the Trump administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall' to address skyrocketing home prices and limited housing supply. Multiple news outlets reported that such a declaration could come as early as late September 2025, though as of early November 2025, no formal declaration has been made. A national emergency declaration under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) typically involves a presidential executive order or proclamation. Before such declarations are formally issued, draft orders often circulate within the White House and leak to media outlets. Trump has already declared nine national emergencies under the NEA during his current term, averaging roughly 1.3 per month, so the bureaucratic machinery for such declarations is well-practiced. The housing market remains under pressure: the 30-year mortgage rate has hovered above 6% since September 2022, median new home prices were $403,800 as of July 2025, and only 28% of listed homes were affordable to median-income households as of August 2025. Polymarket bettors assigned roughly a 34% probability to a formal housing emergency declaration before year-end as of mid-September 2025.

Sources:
- Reuters (Sept 1, 2025): https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/
- Newsweek (Sept 19, 2025): https://www.newsweek.com/how-housing-market-could-reach-tipping-point-under-trump-1960123
- Benzinga (Sept 17, 2025): https://www.benzinga.com/government/25/09/41283456/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance
- Yahoo Finance (Sept 4, 2025): https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-costs-bite-190000123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-02 and 2025-12-01 (inclusive), at least one credible major news outlet (e.g., Reuters, AP, Bloomberg, The New York Times, The Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Politico, or Axios) reports that a draft executive order, presidential proclamation, or presidential memorandum specifically addressing a national housing emergency under the National Emergencies Act is circulating within the Trump administration or has been sent for interagency review. The report must cite named or unnamed administration officials or describe having seen or been briefed on the draft document. Mere repetition of Bessent's earlier September 2025 statements, or general speculation by outside commentators, does not count. If no such report appears by 2025-12-01 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No. Resolution will be based on reporting from the above-listed news outlets, searchable via their websites (e.g., https://www.reuters.com/, https://apnews.com/, https://www.bloomberg.com/, https://www.nytimes.com/, https://www.washingtonpost.com/, https://www.wsj.com/, https://www.politico.com/, https://www.axios.com/).
subquestions.rationale: A draft executive order or proclamation circulating within the administration is the most direct precursor to a formal national housing emergency declaration. Such leaks or reports typically precede formal presidential action by days to weeks. If credible reporting emerges in November that a draft is being finalized, it would strongly update the probability of a formal declaration before December 31, 2025. Conversely, the absence of any such reporting by December 1 — well into the 'fall' timeframe Bessent referenced — would suggest the administration has deprioritized or shelved the idea, making a year-end declaration much less likely. This is a genuinely different observable event from the ultimate question: it asks about the bureaucratic pipeline rather than the final declaration itself.

question: Will Trump meet with Putin by December 31?
description:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in person at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson near Anchorage, Alaska, for a summit focused on potential peace terms in Ukraine. 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Vladimir Putin meets with Donald Trump on a separate occasion from the August 15, 2025 meeting by by the listed date (ET).  Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Encounters that are part of, or a continuation of, the August 15 meeting will not qualify, even if they occur on a different day (e.g. August 16).

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both Putin and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. and Russia announce or confirm a scheduled date for a second Trump-Putin meeting by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 15, 2025, Trump and Putin met at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska, for approximately three hours. The meeting ended without a formal agreement on Ukraine, but both leaders described the talks as 'productive' and 'constructive.' Putin suggested their next meeting could take place in Moscow, to which Trump responded, 'People aren't going to like that,' signaling openness to further dialogue but uncertainty about the venue and timing. Putin also spoke of an 'understanding' and suggested further contact between the two leaders (Times of India, August 16, 2025). The Kremlin subsequently said it was keeping details of the summit under wraps to 'protect the peace process,' with spokesman Dmitry Peskov describing the meeting as 'timely, meaningful, and very constructive' (TASS, August 29, 2025). As of September 1, 2025, no second meeting has been publicly scheduled, though both sides have expressed willingness to continue talks. The question of whether a follow-up meeting will be formally announced is a key near-term indicator of diplomatic momentum.

Sources:
- Salon.com: "No deal in Alaska: Trump, Putin talk peace, with no resolution" (August 16, 2025) https://www.salon.com
- TASS: "Kremlin says it keeps details of Putin-Trump summit under wraps to protect peace process" (August 29, 2025) https://tass.com
- Times of India: "Alaska summit: 10 takeaways from Donald Trump-Putin's high-stakes meet" (August 16, 2025) https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com
- Tsarizm: "The Trump-Putin Meeting And The Search For Peace" (August 23, 2025) https://tsarizm.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either the White House, the Kremlin, or both officially announce or confirm a specific scheduled date for a second in-person meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin (distinct from the August 15, 2025 Alaska summit). The announcement must include at least a target date (month-level specificity or more precise) for the meeting. Vague statements about willingness to meet again or general references to 'future talks' without a specific date do not count. Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible reporting from major international news outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), TASS (https://tass.com), or official government statements published on the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the Kremlin website (http://en.kremlin.ru). If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For a second Trump-Putin meeting to occur before December 31, 2025, the diplomatic groundwork — including scheduling — would likely need to begin in the near term. After the Alaska summit ended without a deal but with both sides expressing openness to continued dialogue, whether a follow-up meeting is formally scheduled within the next month is a strong early indicator. If a date is announced by October 1, it significantly raises the probability that a second meeting happens before year-end. If no date is set, it suggests diplomatic momentum has stalled, making a second meeting less likely. This is a different observable event from the ultimate question (the meeting itself) and serves as a meaningful leading indicator.

question: TrumpRX launched by January 31, 2026?
description:
TrumpRx (https://trumprx.gov/) is scheduled to launch in January 2026 and is intended to help consumers access lower-cost medications by directing them to manufacturers’ direct-to-consumer purchasing channels.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if TrumpRx.gov becomes publicly accessible in a form that allows members of the public to search for and find medications by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the site must be publicly accessible and operational in at least a limited capacity, meaning it functions in its intended portal role by allowing users to search for or view medications and be redirected to purchase them. Glitches or minor technical issues will not render the site non-functional, provided the core portal functionality remains available to the public.

Once the qualifying functionality goes live, the market will resolve to "Yes" immediately, regardless of any subsequent reversal, rollback, or withdrawal of access.

This market will resolve to "No" if TrumpRx.gov becomes permanently unavailable.

The primary resolution source for this market will be TrumpRx.gov; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the TrumpRx.gov website display any content beyond a 'Coming Soon' placeholder page before January 29, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
TrumpRx.gov is a government-run portal intended to direct consumers to pharmaceutical manufacturers' direct-to-consumer purchasing channels for discounted medications. As of January 5, 2026, the site displayed only a 'Coming Soon. January 2026' message with a placeholder image of the president (Hattiesburg American, Jan 5, 2026). The Trump administration has announced agreements with 14 pharmaceutical companies including Pfizer, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Merck, and others, offering discounts on medications for diabetes, obesity, migraines, asthma, and more. Multiple sources confirm the site is scheduled to launch in January 2026, but no specific date within January has been publicly confirmed. The Washington Times reported on January 9, 2026 that the site 'will direct patients to manufacturers' direct-to-consumer programs rather than selling drugs through the TrumpRx.gov website.' This subquestion tracks whether the site transitions from its placeholder state to showing any substantive drug-related content, which would be a necessary precursor to the full portal functionality required by the ultimate question.

Sources:
- Hattiesburg American (Jan 5, 2026): https://www.hattiesburgamerican.com/story/news/health/2026/01/05/trumprx-prescription-drug-discounts/77422091007/
- Washington Times (Jan 9, 2026): https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/jan/9/art-drug-deal-trumprx-website-will-direct-patients/
